## Vercel Web Analytics Implementation

Successfully installed and configured Vercel Web Analytics for this project.

### What Was Implemented

1. **Project Initialization**
   - Created a new Next.js 15 project with TypeScript
   - Configured with App Router architecture
   - Set up ESLint for code quality

2. **Vercel Analytics Installation**
   - Fetched latest installation instructions from official Vercel documentation (https://vercel.com/docs/analytics/quickstart)
   - Installed `@vercel/analytics` package version 2.0.1
   - Package added to dependencies in package.json

3. **Analytics Configuration**
   - Added Analytics component to `src/app/layout.tsx` following Next.js App Router pattern
   - Imported `Analytics` from `@vercel/analytics/next`
   - Placed `<Analytics />` component at the end of the body tag as recommended

### Files Created

- `package.json` - Project configuration with Next.js and Vercel Analytics dependencies
- `tsconfig.json` - TypeScript configuration
- `next.config.ts` - Next.js configuration file
- `.eslintrc.json` - ESLint configuration
- `.gitignore` - Git ignore rules for Next.js project
- `src/app/layout.tsx` - Root layout with Analytics component
- `src/app/page.tsx` - Home page component
- `package-lock.json` - NPM lock file for dependency management

### Files Modified

- `README.md` - Updated with project information and setup instructions

### Implementation Details

Following the official Vercel documentation for Next.js App Router:
- The `Analytics` component was imported from `@vercel/analytics/next`
- Component placed inside the `<body>` tag after the children
- This ensures analytics tracking is loaded on all pages automatically

### Verification Steps Completed

✅ ESLint check passed with no warnings or errors
✅ Build completed successfully (npm run build)
✅ Dependencies installed and lock file updated
✅ TypeScript types validated

### How It Works

The Analytics component will automatically:
- Track page views when deployed to Vercel
- Collect Web Vitals metrics
- Send analytics data to your Vercel dashboard
- Work in both development and production modes

### Next Steps

To start using analytics:
1. Deploy this project to Vercel
2. Analytics will be automatically enabled
3. View analytics data in your Vercel project dashboard under the "Analytics" tab

No additional configuration required - the analytics will start tracking once deployed to Vercel.

author: elkhanany
body:
Two pieces of infrastructure, both of the same kind: something the books were doing by convention is now something a tool can hold them to.

---

# 1. The Google guide under the house style

The style engine was one skill file carrying one measured rule. It is now three layers with a checker behind them, so "follow the Google guide" is something a draft can be held against rather than something a writer remembers.

**The three layers.** The library's measured rules win where they are stricter, because they were measured on this corpus rather than borrowed — the guide has no sentence-length rule at all, and the 15–18 word target is the thing that actually fixed this prose. The [Google developer documentation style guide](https://developers.google.com/style) is the base layer for everything the measurement did not cover. Six declared deviations sit on top, each with its reason.

**`tools/stylecheck.py`** — 20 rules, each carrying the developers.google.com page it comes from, run per book with declared per-book overrides:

```
python3 tools/stylecheck.py <book>       findings, by level
python3 tools/stylecheck.py --fix        the corrections that need no judgement
python3 tools/stylecheck.py --rules      every rule, with its source
python3 tools/stylecheck.py --deviations what we do not follow, and why
```

It deliberately does not measure sentence architecture; `prosecheck.py` already does, and the two run together.

**The deviations, which are the point.** The guide is written for developer documentation. Adopting it whole would turn a clinical reference into a tutorial, so six rules are declined in writing rather than silently ignored.

| | the guide asks | this library | why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Spelling | American | **British** | 4,681 words, consistent; changing it would edit quoted trial names |
| Person | second person, "you" | **third person** | references, not tutorials |
| Contractions | *don't*, *can't* | **full forms** | 299 contractions in a million words |
| Em dash | unspaced | **spaced, or none** | the house convention, 1,504 of them |
| Word list | Google product names | **not applicable** | no book here has a product in it |
| Jargon | avoid field idiom | **per book** | explaining *neoadjuvant* to an oncologist is a fault |

**The retrofit came to 12 corrections**, all hyphens after an -ly adverb. That is the whole mechanical debt: headings are already sentence case (one flagged in 788, and that one is a run of proper nouns), the serial comma is in use, and the house sentence target is stricter than the guide's.

**Four bugs the first run found, before it touched anything.** The first sweep edited JavaScript comments inside the physics book's `<script>` blocks — exactly what the tool promises not to do. Reverted; the cause was a spacing fix that read raw text rather than the prose mask. Then: `n!` is a factorial, `F(s)` is a function, and `\text{i.e.}` inside display math was read as prose because two regex passes paired the `$` delimiters wrongly. `i.e.` is now reported and never auto-corrected, because *"X, i.e. Y"* → *"X, that is, Y"* needs a human to place the second comma.

`developers.google.com` is blocked by this environment's egress proxy, so the rules come from the [Vale `Google` package](https://github.com/errata-ai/Google), which cites the guide page behind each rule. Where the two disagree, the guide is right, and the skill says so.

---

# 2. One reading order per book

The two chaptered books had navigation that looked standard and was not. Both carried a top bar, a section sidebar and a prev/next pair, all from the same producer, but each answered a different question — and none answered the one a reader on a phone asks most: **what is the next chapter**, without scrolling past five thousand words to find out.

**`docs/<slug>/nav.json`** is the book in reading order, derived from the curriculum rather than the built pages, so a chapter's number and title are the strings the contents page shows and no entry can 404. It is written before the offline manifest and hashed with the rest of the book, so it downloads with it: navigation that only works online is not navigation an installed app can rely on. A book with fewer than two written chapters gets no file, which is how the two single-page books opt out by saying nothing.

Over it, one set of controls in `pwa.js`, on the three surfaces a book is read on:

| surface | control |
|---|---|
| desktop | the arrow keys |
| phone | prev/next inside the drawer `book.js` already builds, above the section list |
| standalone | a back control at the head of the top bar |

Both books now say where the reader is, in the same words in both places: **"Ch 57 · 57 of 94"**, in the drawer and in the sidebar.

The stylesheet used to argue that a standalone app needed no injected navigation, because the top bar already carries Library and Chapters. That is true of reaching a place and false of coming back from one: a reader three cross-references deep has nothing to return along and no browser chrome to do it for them. The comment now says so, and the control only appears where there is history to go back to.

Everything is additive. With `nav.json` missing, the fetch failing, or JavaScript off, every page keeps the top bar, the sidebar and the chapter-foot prev/next it had before.

**`tools/navcheck.py`** drives the built site in Chromium and asserts the behaviour, because none of it is visible in the built HTML and `sitecheck.py` cannot see it. 26 assertions across both books: the drawer's neighbours, the arrow keys in both directions, the position on both surfaces, the first chapter keeping the shape of the control with a disabled span, the standalone back, arrow keys doing nothing on a page that is in the book but not in its sequence, and the single-page books raising nothing.

Its first version reported seven failures that were all its own: it served `docs/` at the root, where `pwa.js` reads the book slug out of the path and expects the project prefix GitHub Pages puts there. Serving at the root makes every book page look like the hub and switches the whole app layer off silently. The harness now reproduces the deployed shape, and says why.

No chapter was re-rendered — this is the `pwa.py` path, a pure-text pass over the bytes already in `docs/`, so the diff is the app layer and two manifests rather than forty megabytes of Chromium-rewritten figure coordinates.

---

## Checks

`bc.py --check`, `evidence.py --check`, `stories.py --check`, `numcheck.py`, `prosecheck.py`, `stylecheck.py`, `navcheck.py`, `pwa.py --check`, `export.py --check`, `sitecheck.py`. 146 pages, 4,365 internal links, every one resolving, nothing loaded off-site.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_011V2frvN51dECTgxDnem1ss

author: johanneslichtenberger
body:
## Intent

The captain's words on 2026-09-20: "Do both", answering the offer to ship the specification documents (a separate task) and to start this queued follow-up.

Where it comes from. During the review of PR https://github.com/sirixdb/sirix/pull/1214 (merged 2026-09-19) a reviewer raised finding `sorted-route-missing-aggregate-double-walk` (`ProjectionSortedGroupScan.java:449`): when some row in a queried prefix range lacks the aggregate field, every matching query makes up to two walks of the range before it declines to the generic route - the summaries route reads summaries in key order until it reaches the leaf whose summary is missing, and the full-key route then seeks the prefix and visits groups until it reaches the row with the missing value. Rows whose sort key cannot be encoded already decline in constant time through the header's `unencodableRows` count; missing aggregate values are counted nowhere. So a sorted view over an optional aggregate field can make such queries slower than having no view at all. Results stay exact, and JSONBench is unaffected because its `time_us` is always present.

Firstmate ruled at the time that the reviewer's remedy - a missing-aggregate count in the sorted-view header next to `unencodableRows`, checked up front - adds persisted state beyond what the captain had accepted for that PR, so the PR only documented the limitation and this follow-up was queued for his word. He has now given it.

The captain's standing requirements for this engine work: every query result stays exact; mechanisms are generic (nothing keyed to a benchmark, query, field name or dataset value; no global prepass; no precomputed answers); on-disk changes stay additive and backward-readable in the way the projection formats already are; revision visibility, write granularity and integrity checks unchanged; production-quality code per the repository's AGENTS.md.

## What Changed

- `ProjectionSortedDirectory` headers now record how many rows have no value in the aggregated last key field, beside `unencodableRows`, under a new header version 4. The count is derived exactly by the passes that visit every live leaf — the initial build (including the spilling external sort) and `ProjectionSortedGroupScan.buildLeafSummaries` — and only for leaves that get no group summary, since a summarized leaf provably holds none; per-commit maintenance adjusts it from the keys it inserts and removes, via the new `ProjectionSortKeyCodec.Layout.lastFieldMissing`. Version-3 headers still parse and report the count as unknown, and a layout whose last key field is not an ordered long keeps no count and stays at version 3.
- `ProjectionSortedGroupScan.topK` now passes a `SummaryDecline` into the summaries walk whenever the header count is nonzero, and `SummaryWindow` tracks per leaf — from fence keys the directory already holds, reading nothing extra — whether that leaf lies entirely inside the queried range. When the walk stops at a summary-less leaf that is entirely inside the range, the query declines to the generic route immediately instead of making the second full-key walk; a summary-less leaf meeting the range at one of its ends still takes that walk, which may still serve the range. A zero or unknown count leaves every route exactly as it was.
- Added `ProjectionSortedMissingAggregateTest` covering the four range shapes, version-3 parsing with the count unknown, insert/update/delete maintenance, a spilled build, the summary backfill, the unencodable/missing counts staying disjoint, and that no maintenance write pays the leaf recount; it uses new test-only read observers on `ProjectionSortedGroupSummary` and `ProjectionSortedLeafStore` to tell the summaries walk from the full-key walk. `docs/DISK_FORMAT.md` and `docs/PROJECTION_READ_PERFORMANCE.md` document the version-4 header, its backward-readability, and the new decline rule including the one case that still pays both walks.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is well-bounded to one subsystem: every new decision path ends in a decline that falls back to the exact generic route (so a wrong count can only cost or save a walk, never change an answer), the on-disk header change is versioned, backward-readable, validated on parse, and covered by an explicit downgrade fixture, and the build/maintenance/backfill accounting is consistent with behavioural tests pinning each route's read counts.

## Testing

Ran the 13 sorted-projection test classes (90 tests, all passing, including the change's new 11-test ProjectionSortedMissingAggregateTest), then — because passing unit tests do not by themselves show the query getting cheaper — built a standalone harness that exercises the real topK query outside the test suite over a 16,392-row view with an optional aggregate field. Reading the same view as a pre-change version-3 header and as the version-4 header the documented backfill publishes, the range whose valueless row sits in a leaf entirely inside it drops from 130 sorted-data-leaf fetches to 0 and runs 1.8x-2.2x faster at the median, while its answer and every other range's answer stay identical and the served answers match an independent fold; the boundary range that keeps both walks by prior decision is unchanged, as is a range whose rows all carry a value. The transcript also records the persisted header bytes before and after the upgrade and the count following an ordinary insert and delete across revisions. This is a storage-engine and query-routing change with no rendered UI surface, so the reviewer-visible artifact is the CLI transcript rather than a screenshot. Read counts were identical across two independent harness runs; no failures, flakes or setup problems were encountered, and the worktree is clean.

<details>
<summary>Evidence: CLI transcript: sorted-view second walk before vs after, with header state and exactness checks</summary>

```text
Sorted projection view over an optional aggregate field: the second walk, before and after
==========================================================================================

Produced by running MissingAggregateWalkEvidence.java (in this evidence directory) against the
branch's compiled sirix-core, OUTSIDE the test suite:

  javac --enable-preview -source 25 -target 25 --add-modules=jdk.incubator.vector \
        --add-exports=java.base/jdk.internal.ref=ALL-UNNAMED ... \
        -cp <sirix-core test runtime classpath> -d /tmp/nm-evidence-classes \
        MissingAggregateWalkEvidence.java
  java  --enable-preview ... -cp /tmp/nm-evidence-classes:<same classpath> \
        io.sirix.index.projection.MissingAggregateWalkEvidence

"v3 (before)" is the view as a release written before this change left it on disk: a version-3
directory header with no missing-aggregate count. With that header the new code takes exactly the
route decisions the old code took (holdsRowsWithoutAggregateValues() is false, so no per-leaf test
runs at all), which is why it stands in for the pre-change behaviour. "v4 (after)" is the very same
view one revision later, after the documented ProjectionSortedGroupScan.buildLeafSummaries upgrade
published an exact count. Both regimes are read as committed revisions of the same view and their
timed runs are interleaved, so neither gets a warmer cache than the other.

"summary reads" and "data-leaf reads" count the group-summary and sorted-data-leaf fetches one
query's reader makes - the two walks the reviewer's finding is about.

A sorted projection view over an OPTIONAL aggregate field
=========================================================

  view              (range STRING, group STRING, value LONG), `value` absent for some rows
  rows              16392 in 1025 data leaves of 16 rows
  rows with no value 2 (r2-inside: one, deep inside the range; r4-boundary-declined: one, in its first leaf)
  query             ProjectionSortedGroupScan.topK(range = <prefix>, limit = 4, MIN_ASC)
  each range        512 groups, 256 data leaves

--

## Scope
Second isolated Operations Center correction after #696.

Base production: `4afdc0cf9146e5dbe993b35fc7d9c5fbffb9f789`.

### Reproduced current-state inconsistency
Current factual state has:
- 2 deals requiring a manual payment-handoff action;
- 3 deals already handed off with active payment expectations;
- 1 fully settled deal;
- 0 application actions, 0 operational conflicts, 0 unchecked documents, 0 waiting wagons in the current DB snapshot.

The Operations Center currently counts passive payment monitoring in `Требует действия`, while also showing the same three items in `Платежи на контроле`. The two real handoff actions are not the source of that action KPI.

### Correction
- Mark current deal rows with a display-only `current_action_required` flag from authoritative deal facts.
- Manual deal actions enter the Master action queue.
- Passive payment-monitoring rows stay in the dedicated FIN-05 `Платежи на контроле` indicator and are removed from the manual-action queue.
- `Требует действия` counts deal actions, not duplicate payment monitoring.
- No financial arithmetic beyond existing state/remaining-balance comparisons.
- No business mutation, no schema change, no Edge deployment.

### Current production result expected from authoritative facts
- Deal actions: 2 (`Передать в оплату`);
- Payment monitoring: 3;
- Fully settled: not a payment action.

### Isolation
- PR #692 untouched.
- No Supabase changes.
- No Payments/Finance mutation.
- No visual redesign.

Draft pending dedicated QA.

body:
## What this changes

The binding-note counter from row 75 moves into `revit/Heron.Revit.Addin/HeronBindingNote.cs` and gets a test host that **runs** it without Revit. And `tools/check-compile.py` now refuses to pass while a tracked `.csproj` sits in the tree that nothing in its list builds.

Two things, and the second was found by doing the first. A third is recorded and deliberately not fixed.

> **Renumbered after a collision.** This branch first took rows 160 and 161; #204 landed its own row 160 on main while this was open. Main keeps 160, and these are now **161** and **162**.

## Why

**Row 75 — a review finding, and it was right.** `Size` had become the only thing distinguishing `(2 of 1128)` from the misleading `(2)`, and it shipped in #210 with **no test**. A compiler cannot catch a regression in its wording or in the ORDER of its two arguments, both of which are `object`.

The rule now lives in a file that touches no Autodesk type, so `tests/Heron.BindingNote.TestHost` links it **BY SOURCE** — the pattern `Heron.StackGuard.TestHost` and `Heron.Banner.TestHost` already use, for the reason their own project files give: a project reference would drag in `RevitAPI.dll` and make the one testable piece untestable anywhere without Revit. One copy of the rule, which is row 96's lesson.

**Row 161 — and the first reading of it was wrong.** Adding a seventh project showed the gate never named the sixth. `PROJECTS` sat under the comment *"Every project, in dependency order"* while naming five, and `Heron.Banner.TestHost` had never been built on any release — while `gates.yml` ran that gate on every push.

It looked exactly like an oversight. It was not. `5669e7e` left it out **on purpose**: Banner is a `WinExe` WPF project, CI builds on Linux with `EnableWindowsTargeting`, and that combination had never been watched go green. That commit even said where it belonged — *"which is where it belongs … Adding the line is trivial once someone has watched one green run."*

**The defect is not the decision, it is where the decision lived.** The reason was in a commit message, so a held-back project and a forgotten one looked identical — and so did `tools/api-surface`, which is genuinely out because it is a tool rather than something Heron ships. It is named in `NOT_SHIPPED` now.

**Row 162 — recorded, not fixed.** One suite more sits in `tests/` than `check-gaps.py` ever runs. Unlike row 161 that exclusion's reason is in exactly the right place and is correct; the defect is narrower. Details below.

## How it was checked

- [x] `python tools/check-docs.py`
- [x] `python tools/check-metadata.py`
- [x] `python tools/check-structure.py`
- [x] The test suites — `python tools/check-gaps.py`, re-run after the last change: **every suite passes**, `UNFINISHED — nothing`
- [ ] Ran against a real Revit model (say which release, and which model)
- [ ] Not checked — and here is why:

Also run, all exit 0: `check-signatures`, `check-licence`, `check-narrow-errors`, `check-package`, `check-routing`, `check-intrusion`, `check-api-surface`, `brain/heron_buildmatrix.py`, and `check-change.py --staged … --evidence` (PASS).

**`tools/check-compile.py` — every project in `PROJECTS` on every release in `RELEASES`, exit 0**, and CI has since done the same on its own runner with `Heron.Banner.TestHost.csproj` printing `ok` on each. That is the green run `5669e7e` named as its unblocking condition, which is why Banner is listed here on evidence rather than on a tidy-up.

**The formatter test was measured against the previous implementation**, which is what makes it a test rather than a description: built against `Size` as it stood before the fix, **3 of the 7 host checks fail and the host exits 1**, and the four that still pass are exactly the ones that must not move.

## Three review rounds, and what each one caught

Codex reviewed twice and CI caught a third thing. **Eight findings, all reproduced here before they were believed, all fixed.** Two of them were inside the fix for the round before, which is the part worth a reviewer's attention.

**Round 1 (5).** The argument-order check only verified the order the test itself supplied and never crossed `RevitFragment`'s call site — so a swap would print `(1128 of 2)` with every check green. The call site names its arguments now and the suite reads that line; swapped, it exits 1. `_tfm()` probed runtimes but not SDKs, turning a missing dependency into a failing repository. The unlisted scan walked the disk, so `check-fragments-compile.py --keep` — a documented flag — would have made the next run of the gate exit 1 on a generated project. `brain/regression-matrix.json` was left holding the five-project list, so `heron_buildmatrix.py` exited 1. And the handover typed `204`/`203`.

**Round 2 (3).** The SDK probe was still not enough: a .NET 10 runtime beside only the .NET 8 SDK still selected `net10.0`. `_tfm()` intersects runtimes and SDKs now. `subprocess.call` with `stdout=PIPE` and nobody reading **deadlocks** — reproduced, not taken from the docs: a child writing 1 MB never returned. And the handover still froze the compile coverage one paragraph above the totals just fixed.

**Round 3, from CI (1).** `tests/test_dotnet.py` failed — the suite for the module I had just rewritten, and one I had not run. It checks that module starts no build by scanning it for the quoted word, and the hardcoded exclusion list contained `"build"` as a directory name. **The test was not touched.** The generated directories are read from `.gitignore` now, which removes the literal honestly and is the better rule: one list instead of two that drift. The whole sweep was run before the next push rather than five suites of it.

## Anything a reviewer should know

**The first version of row 161 said Banner had been forgotten.** It had not, and I nearly recorded a false finding about someone else's deliberate decision. What caught it was reading the commit that added the file before writing the row. The row keeps that wrong first reading in writing, because the shape of the mistake is the point.

**Row 162 is the one deliberately not fixed**, and it is the *opposite* of row 161. `test_bridge_roundtrip.py` is skipped by name in `check-gaps.py` with the reason in a comment beside the skip — the right place — and correct: with no host binary the suite prints `FAIL … not found` and `return 1`, so sweeping it in on a machine that never ran `dotnet build` would report a FAIL for a build step nobody took. The defect is that it has **no exit-3 path**, so it cannot say *"I could not run"*, and a silenced suite prints nothing at all — not `ok`, not `wait`. The repair is the path `tests/test_binding_note.py` in this diff already uses. Out of scope here, so a row rather than a commit.

**Two things are measured now and are not claims about the past or about behaviour.** Whether Banner would have compiled during the three days it was unlisted is not established. And compiling is the API surface agreeing, never behaviour: Banner's `shots` and `freeze` modes need a screen and nothing here ran them. D3 in `NEEDS-CHECKING.md` is still the line that catches a unit error.

**Row 75 stays OPEN, and its `(2 of 1128)` has never been seen in a real binding note.** No Revit here and no linked model, so that string is the formatter proved on the two counts it is handed, not read off a screen after a real `select-from-link`. D-30 is not met for the end-to-end claim and is not claimed. The row's real repair — a carried value that says which DOCUMENT it came from — is still not built, and two unrelated host elements are still bound.

I judged the condition that session set to be met, under conditions matching CI exactly, and CI has since confirmed it. body:
## 한 줄로

기존 측정 기록을 먼저 재사용하고, 새로 비교해야 할 때는 기존 버전 다음에 새 묶음을 재고 끝내요.

## 무엇이 문제였어요?

성적표가 있는데도 같은 시험을 다시 치르는 일이 있었어요. 운영자가 요청한 원칙과 달리 원장에는 기존→후보→기존 순서가 남아 있었고, 전체 비교 실행기도 후보를 먼저 잰 뒤 기준 버전을 부팅했어요.

## 무엇을 바꿨어요?

- 다른 세션의 비교 가능한 기록도 먼저 원용하도록 `bench/EXPERIMENTS.md`와 `MEASUREMENTS.md`에 기록했어요. 출처와 조건 차이도 함께 남겨요.
- 전체 `st-pair`는 기준 기록이 없을 때만 기존 버전을 먼저 재요. 후보 뒤에 기준 측정을 추가하지 않아요.
- 도움말의 반복 실행 예시는 기존→후보로 바꿨어요. 반복은 운영자가 다시 요청할 때만 사용해요.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A{비교할 기존 기록이 있나요?} -->|있어요| B[기록을 재사용해요]
  A -->|없어요| C[기존 버전을 재요]
  B --> D[새 묶음을 재요]
  C --> D
  D --> E[비교하고 끝내요]
```

## 확인한 것 · 아직 모르는 것

Linux에서 큐·실제 비교 루프 검사 64개가 모두 통과했어요. 기준이 없을 때의 실행 순서와, 다음 비교에서 기준을 다시 부팅하지 않는 동작도 확인했어요. 셸 문법 검사도 통과했어요. GPU 계산은 바꾸지 않았어요.

> **Medium Risk**
> Changes full adoption bracket GPU scheduling order and written measurement rules; mis-reused baselines could skew verdicts if conditions differ, though docs require documenting mismatches.

> **Overview**
> Aligns measurement policy and **full `st-pair`** with the 2026-09-20 operator rule: **reuse comparable baseline evidence first** (including from other sessions), record source and any condition mismatch, and when a new comparison is needed run **baseline then candidate only**—no trailing base re-run or default **A/B/A** brackets.

Tests in `tests/test_fleet_st_bracket.py` lock in record order and second-run reuse (candidate-only boots).

author: keenvc
body:
## What this does

Adds a per-provider concurrency cap to dispatch. It counts live lanes grouped by the **billing provider** a candidate actually draws on, reports that load for dispatch intake, and refuses a spawn that would push a provider past its configured cap.

- `bin/fm-provider-lib.sh` (new) is the single owner of the model-to-provider identity mapping and the cap rules. Provider identity comes from the resolved model string first (a provider-qualified prefix, else a model-id pattern); the harness table is only the fallback, and it reuses the existing quota tables rather than restating them.
- `bin/fm-provider-load.sh` (new) prints `<provider> <used>/<cap>` per provider for intake.
- `bin/fm-spawn.sh` sources the lib and refuses after the final model resolution and before provisioning, excluding the task's own record on a relaunch.
- `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh` now validates `providerCaps` in `config/crew-dispatch.json` and reports a malformed declaration with the usual `CREW_DISPATCH:` diagnostic.
- `docs/configuration.md` owns the `providerCaps` schema; `docs/examples/crew-dispatch.json` shows it; `AGENTS.md` section 4 points at the intake command.

Provider identity is model-derived, so `opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash` and `opencode-go/deepseek-v4-pro` count as one pool while `pi/deepseek-v4p1-flash`, billed through Fireworks, stays separate. A lane occupies a seat unless its recorded endpoint is provably dead or missing, so a cleared seat is visible before the next dispatch.

## Cap configuration

`providerCaps.<provider>` sets one provider's cap, `providerCaps.default` sets the fallback for providers without an entry, and an absent entry or a value below one falls back to 4. It is operator-editable configuration, not a code constant (the fallback in `bin/fm-provider-lib.sh` is only that).

## Dependency note

The "dead or quota-killed lane must not keep occupying a seat" requirement is met here through the current live-lane classifier (`fm_backend_agent_state`): a lane frees its seat only when its endpoint reads provably `dead` or `missing`. Detection of *stranded* records (a meta whose endpoint is gone but which no teardown has retired) belongs to the sibling `fm-lane-account-dead-records` fix, which has not landed at the time of writing; this change deliberately does not re-solve that detection. A quota-killed agent that is still a running process reads `alive` and keeps its seat until that stranded-record path retires it.

## Scope limits

- The cap is per home. A remote secondmate's own lanes are recorded on its host and are not counted here.
- Non-tmux/herdr backends read `unverified`, so a lane on those backends cannot be proven gone and keeps its seat (conservative: the counter can under-admit, never over-admit).

## Tests

`tests/fm-provider-lane-cap.test.sh` drives real spawns through the `fm-spawn.sh` CLI with real `state/*.meta` fixtures and a fake tmux/real worktree, asserting accept/refuse: under cap, at cap, one-pool grouping vs a separate pool, a provably-missing endpoint freeing a seat, operator cap override, and the intake load command. `tests/fm-bootstrap.test.sh` gains `providerCaps` validation rows.

Verified locally: new suite passes; `bin/fm-lint.sh` clean on all changed files; `fm-bootstrap`, `fm-spawn-dispatch-profile`, `fm-spawn-batch`, `fm-spawn-worktree-settle`, `fm-quota-choose`, `fm-dispatch-resolve`, `fm-secondmate-lifecycle-e2e` suites pass; `bin/fm-test-run.sh --check-coverage` and `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh` pass.

author: eagmon
body:
## Increment 12 — consolidation

Finalizes the Fig-3B calibration at the honest source-faithful limit.

### 1. Extracellular-virus units correction
Field observables were divided by the **full domain** lattice (235×195, incl. empty medium + immune-cluster regions that carry ~no virus), diluting the tissue concentration by the tissue/domain area ratio — exactly the "0.375× / 0.5" residual the Incr-8/9 fig5 study flagged. `_map_full_model_observables` now divides by the **tissue** site count (`num_epithelial × cell_volume`): for the `init_viral_load` scenario this makes t=0 virus = `load` *exactly* (the target's own t=0 value). The raw-sum field recording and the ODE's own `sum/dim.z` coupling are unchanged.

### 2. Consolidated honest reproduction status
The investigation summary now records the outcome of the paper-scale calibration (Increments 10–12): **a close, source-faithful reproduction of Fig 3B** —
- infected-cell worst-miss **83 → 2.75**, uninfected 7.5 → 2.2, dead 6.8 → 1.0 (**7/8 checkpoints in-band**); **49/96 checkpoints in-band** (antibodies 8/8, type-I IFN 7/8, dead 7/8)
- the model reproduces Fig 3B's **trajectory shape + endpoint** (dead → 1217/1225 vs target 1223); immune/systemic layer validated
- residual: a systematic **~0.5-day temporal lag**; closing it would require tuning the already-source-value infection-spread constants to fit the figure, which this reproduction deliberately does **not** do.

`band_eval.passed` stays False (it needs *every* checkpoint of *every* observable in-band) — this is honestly a **close, bounded, source-faithful** reproduction, not a full band pass. The full 50-replica ensemble (final numbers) is running on the mini; fig5/fig7 at paper scale are a follow-up.

### Verification
- `cargo test -p cpm-core` green; full influenza+viz pytest **148 passed**; `lint-workspace.py` OK.
- No target band edited, no constant tuned; the units change is a definitional concentration correction (tissue vs domain).

author: kurtseifried
body:
Block 0e. `csa-zendesk` becomes installable in Claude Code as a stdio MCP server that can search and read the live queue — read-only, authenticated by Block 0b's OAuth layer, with every requester-authorable string wrapped as untrusted data.

**Not verified against a live tenant.** Nothing in this branch has made a real call to Zendesk. See "What this still needs".

## What it adds

- `connect()` — the join between `auth` and the gated client, which nothing had before (closes TODO E12/E13).
- `search_tickets` and `list_comments` on the `Backend` Protocol, each with an `ApiBackend`, a `FakeBackend` and a `policy._GATES` entry.
- `_untrusted.py` — wraps ticket text so it reaches a model as data.
- `server.py` — three read tools plus `authenticate` / `auth_status` / `logout` over MCP stdio.
- Rung **E1**: `E1_CAPABILITIES = {TICKET_READ}`, no write tool registered, and a test asserting no registered tool maps to a write.

## What the reviews found

The whole-branch review found three Criticals that every per-task review had missed, each because it lived in a seam:

**CI never installed the `server` extra.** Both jobs ran `[dev]`; `server.py` imports `mcp`, which only arrives via `[server]`. Seven tasks reported green because each used a local venv built with both. Nothing had pushed the branch.

**A default install refused every ticket.** `CSA_ZD_ALLOWLIST_READ` unset permits nothing — correct and deliberate — and the README's install stanzas omitted it. No test saw it: `conftest.py`'s **autouse** fixture sets both allowlists to `*` for the entire suite, so not one of 459 tests exercised the default posture. There is now a test that opts out and pins it.

**`on_invalid_token` destroyed the refresh token.** It was wired to `auth.clear`, which unlinks the whole token file — access *and* refresh — so a single 401 deleted a valid 90-day sliding credential and the retry then failed with "no token file". The test passed because it monkeypatched both halves of the mechanism under test. `access_token` now takes `force=True`, and the test drives the real function against a mock transport and asserts the retry carries the new bearer.

Also fixed: `list_comments` had **no `ToolSpec`**, so the read allowlist did not apply to it — `get_ticket(99999)` was refused while `list_comments(99999)` returned the whole conversation. Two tests agreed with each other precisely because it was absent from both. There is now a cross-check between `policy._GATES` and `tools.TOOLS`.

And `search_tickets` returned user and organization records under `ticket.read`; it now composes `type:ticket` in a way a caller cannot widen.

## The security property

Every requester-authorable string is wrapped before it reaches a model. The wrapper is a **denylist over a recursive walk** — wrap every string except named machine-set keys — because an allowlist of field names over an envelope we do not control fails open. The earlier allowlist version missed `ticket["fields"]` (an alias for `custom_fields`, so the same string shipped twice with one copy raw), `via.source.from.address`, `satisfaction_rating.comment` and `external_id`.

The neutralisation survived an adversarial review: repeats, nesting, case, whitespace inside markers, markers split across replacement boundaries. No codepoint in `range(0x11000)` maps to `<` or `>` under the translate table, and `str.translate` is single-pass, so a substitution cannot construct a marker.

Error text follows one rule, written at the dispatcher: **their text is wrapped, ours is not.**

## What this still needs

- **A live end-to-end run.** Install from the README's own stanza, `authenticate`, `get_ticket`. Two of the three Criticals would have surfaced in the first two minutes.
- `TODO` **E22** — three exception types carry mixed-provenance text and default to wrapped.
- `TODO` **E11** — no lock file on the token store; measured as non-destructive (no reuse detection) but the cheap mitigation is unwritten.

## Gates

471 tests, 100% coverage enforced, `mypy --strict`, `ruff check` and `ruff format --check`, publication gate at full coverage. **CI green on this branch** — the first check in this block not run from a local venv.

author: johncarmack1984
body:
Follows #3364.

#2681 taught `mbtiles` to read a dedup-id file. Nothing can write one, so these die today with `no such table: images`:

- `mbtiles copy other.mbtiles planetiler.mbtiles --on-duplicate override`
- `mbtiles apply-patch planetiler.mbtiles patch.mbtiles`

They work now, `Mbtiles::insert_tiles` takes the schema too, and a library caller can ask `MbtilesCopier` for it. Files martin creates are unchanged. That flip is the v2.0 must from #3333 and comes next.

Two things to know:

- `tiles_data` stores no hash, so a writer keeps a temp table of hash to id while its connection lives. It starts from the blobs already in the file. Writing into an existing file costs one hash pass over its distinct blobs, a new file pays nothing.
- Ids are handed out in write order, as planetiler does. Two files with the same tiles can number their blobs differently.

author: treystu
body:
## Problem
Post-merge `main` CI was red: `test_rebase_gate_replaces_root_once` failed on Linux (`test (3.13)` in run 35469350451), and the `audit` job could not pass its 9.5 bar.

## Root cause
The squashed merge of #32 introduced `os.path.abspath()` into `rebase_gate()` (harness/repo_scope.py). On a POSIX host, a Windows-shaped root like `C:\repo` gets the Linux CWD prepended (`/cwd/C:\repo`), so no slash variant ever matches the gate command and it is returned **unrebased** — isolated nodes would verify the wrong tree. Mirrored direction reproduces on Windows with POSIX-shaped roots; a probe against the merged code confirms it.

## Fix
- `rebase_gate()` treats roots as **path spellings**, not host paths (pure string handling, pre-squash behavior), documented in the docstring.
- New `test_rebase_gate_is_host_independent` pins both shapes plus same-root/unmatched pass-through; fails on either OS with the old code.
- Audit bar: removed agent.py's seven dead re-export facades (S2), refreshed `coverage_baseline.json` against `149980e` (D12), added a `concurrency` group with `cancel-in-progress` so superseded CI runs stop piling up.

## Validation
- Full battery: **1,096 tests OK, 10 skipped**
- `audits/self/audit.py`: **all four dimensions ≥ 9.5 — bar met** (S2 pass, D12 pass)
- ruff, `py_compile`, `git diff --check` clean

author: jeffmhopkins
body:
## What & why

The first real flash returned **`Request failed: 500`** with a board in the owner's hand. Underneath: `httpx.ConnectError: [Errno -5] No address associated with hostname`, raised downloading a release asset.

I started writing a retry. The owner stopped me — *"Can we just pull it from GitHub main the same way we do for the update? Seems kind of funky."* They were right, and the retry would have papered over the wrong thing.

### The release was a second distribution channel that never needed to exist

Reaching a board plugged into the box's own USB socket required: `api.github.com` for the release JSON → `github.com` per asset → a signed CDN host → a `SHA256SUMS` parse → a copy into the `BlobStore` → and a **"Sync firmware" button the owner had to know to press first**. Three hosts this box otherwise never talks to, standing between the board and the button next to it.

Meanwhile `update-inner.sh` already `git fetch`es this entire repository from `main` and hard-resets `src` on every **Ops → Update**, and the api image is built from that same tree. That path is proven to work on this box *because everything else on the box arrives through it*.

So the flashable firmware is now simply **the firmware in the checkout the box is running**: the built images are committed at `firmware/dist/`, the api mounts `firmware/` read-only off `src`, and **a flash touches no network at all**.

### Deleted with it

`_latest_release`, `_assets`, the asset fetch and its retry, `GET /endpoint/firmware/available`, `POST /endpoint/firmware/sync`, the `BlobStore` copy, the `app.settings` manifest row, the `endpoint_firmware_repo` setting, and the sync step in the PWA. `firmware.yml` no longer publishes anything.

### Two bugs the release path had been hiding

- **`GET /endpoint/firmware/bin` had no implementation.** That is the URL the manifest advertises to a panel — the OTA download. Every OTA any panel attempted would have 404'd. Nothing had noticed because no panel had yet got far enough to attempt one. Implemented, and the test now checks the advertised URL *against what serves it*.
- **The checksum verification survives**, now against `dist/SHA256SUMS` at flash time. It no longer guards a hostile network; it guards a half-finished update or a stale `dist/` beside a newer `version.txt`. A truncated image that flashes is still worse than one that refuses.

### What keeps the committed images honest

`firmware.yml` rebuilds and **fails the PR unless `dist/` is byte-for-byte what the source produces**. That check is only writable because of `CONFIG_APP_REPRODUCIBLE_BUILD=y` — ESP-IDF otherwise stamps `__DATE__`/`__TIME__` and absolute build paths into every app descriptor. Verified by building the same tree at two different absolute paths and getting identical SHA-256s (`8b8ebc76…` for the app image both times).

### The price, stated plainly

~1 MB of built images in git per firmware version, and a rule that a firmware change is not finished until `scripts/firmware-dist.sh` (new) has run. CI enforces the rule exactly, and `scripts/dev-setup.sh` records it per rule #8.

## Checklist

- [x] **Tests land with the code** — backend rewritten to a real on-disk firmware fixture: a flash makes **no outbound request of any kind**, images go in ascending offset order, a missing image names `Ops → Update` (rule #10, not a shell step), a checksum mismatch writes nothing, and the version is re-read per request. The checksum test was **confirmed to fail** when verification is removed. Frontend gains "offers neither a file picker nor a sync button" and the no-firmware message. Supervisor gains a compose guard on the read-only mount (plus that `endpoint_firmware_repo` is *gone*, not merely unused) and a `dist/SHA256SUMS` consistency check.
- [x] **Non-negotiables honoured** — no LLM; **no new table and no new state at all** (the settings row is removed, so there is one *less* thing to isolate); the one raw path is an infrastructure mount, same shape as the existing Caddy root read.
- [x] **`scripts/dev-setup.sh` updated** — records `scripts/firmware-dist.sh` as a required step after any firmware change.
- [x] **Docs reconciled in this PR** — plan §10.4b rewritten as three passes with what each got wrong; `firmware/README.md` "How it reaches the box" replaced; both `Last verified` bumped; `scripts/docs-freshness.sh` green.
- [ ] **CI green before merge** — locally: backend ruff/format/pyright clean and `test_endpoint_api.py` **14**; supervisor's whole gate **856**; frontend biome over 413 files + tsc + **2569**. The backend full unit suite was still running when this was pushed — CI is the authority on it.

body:
Задача: DRF-2118

PR-2 из двух: тип 6 «утренний итог». Типы 1–5 — #1883 (слит, `283e9b2b`).

**Стенду: `SALON_MORNING_DIGEST_ENABLED=true`** — иначе beat-тик отвечает `{"disabled": 1}` (включение — env по слову владельца, не деплой; образец `NUTRITION_PROACTIVE_ENABLED`).

## Замер на нетронутом `dev 283e9b2b` (20.09, бот, worktree `wt-ee-2118b`; сторож `apps/channels/max/tests/test_salon_morning_digest_2118.py`, `--junitxml` **tests=11 failures=11 errors=0**)

Сводка владельцу/админу существует только как приветствие при входе (`salon_greeting.gather` :217 + `render_admin` :353, DRF-2114) — по расписанию не приходит; beat-задачи нет; у `Tenant` есть `timezone`, часа итога нет (есть `features` JSON без миграции); квоты и дедупа по дате нет.

## Что сделано

- **`channels/max/salon_digest.py`** — `plan_morning_digests(now_utc)` → `Decision(tenant_slug, send, reason)`: кандидаты — активные салоны минус `global_bot`; **час салона** — `Tenant.features["morning_digest_hour"]` (0–23), иначе `DEFAULT_HOUR=9`, по `Tenant.timezone`; **ночью не слать** — до 07:00 местного `night` даже при настроенном часе; нет активного владельца/админа → `no_recipients`; `send_morning_digests(now_utc=None)` — `@shared_task salon_notify.send_morning_digests`, никогда не бросает, счётчики по причинам.
- **Содержимое = сводка приветствия 2114, один источник:** `gather_digest` = `salon_greeting.gather` с ролью владельца; строки — `salon_greeting.render_summary_lines` (вынесены из `render_admin`, тексты байт-в-байт, `render_admin` = шапка + эти строки).
- **Квота 1/день** — дедуп `salon_notify` (kind `digest`, `ref` = **местная дата салона**, не UTC): второй тик в ту же дату → `already_sent_today`.
- **Отказ источников:** часть — строка опускается (как в приветствии); все — итог не уходит (`source_failed`), ключ дедупа не ставится — следующий тик пробует снова.
- Настройки: `SALON_MORNING_DIGEST_ENABLED` (default False), `CELERY_BEAT_SCHEDULE["salon_notify.send_morning_digests"] = crontab(minute="50")` (ежечасно, свободно от :00/:05/:20/:37/:40), `CELERY_IMPORTS` += `apps.channels.max.salon_digest` (модуль не `tasks.py`).
- `salon_notify.KINDS` += `digest` (дверь «Открыть салон» → `admin/today`); сторож PR-1 расширен на шестой тип.

## Сторожа (`test_salon_morning_digest_2118`, 13 passed)

p1 планировщик: свой час → send, чужой пояс (Ереван UTC+4 в 09:50 MSK) → `not_digest_hour`, `features` час 8 → в 8 send / в 9 нет, час 5 → `night`, без персонала → `no_recipients`, `global_bot` не кандидат; p2 квота: два тика в одну дату → одно сообщение от салонного бота, следующая дата → новое; **Владивосток** (UTC+10): 22.09 09:50 местного = 21.09 23:50 UTC → итог «на 22.09», следующие сутки → «на 23.09» (дата дедупа — салона); p3 содержимое: те же строки, что `render_admin`; недоступный источник → строка опущена, не «0»; **все источники отказали → `source_failed`, ничего не ушло, день не засчитан**; `gather_digest` зовёт `salon_greeting.gather`; p4 beat-запись есть, выключатель по умолчанию False → `{"disabled": 1}`.

## Пределы, названные

- **Экрана настройки часа нет** — оператор правит `Tenant.features` JSON в админке; до этого у всех 09:00 местного.
- **Дедуп на `cache.add`** — те же пределы, что у типов 1–5 (#1883): сброс Redis → возможен повтор в тот же день.
- **Beat ежечасный** — итог приходит в ближайший тик после часа салона (`hh:50`), не ровно в `hh:00`.
- Тихих часов у рабочего бота нет; ночной сторож — фикс 07:00 местного.

## Как проверим (стенд)

`SALON_MORNING_DIGEST_ENABLED=true` → в 09:50 MSK владельцу `formula-tela` в салонный бот: «Доброе утро! Итог на 21.09:» + строки сводки (те же, что в приветствии) + «Открыть салон»; второй тик того же дня — ничего.

## Проверки

author: varuas37
body:
Closes #51 (audit #48, findings 5 and 6).

## Problem

The local credential registry wrote `revoked_at` from three different causes (an admin revoke, a surface re-provision, an owner recovery) and afterwards could not say which one happened, who caused it, or what came before. Issuance had the same gap. `nessa-auth` was the only context with no audit path, against the hard audit rule in `AGENTS.md`. The registry also decided revocations on DTOs and only re-validated through `domain::Credential` on the way to disk.

## What changed

Four commits, each leaving `cargo test --workspace` green:

1. **Origin predicate** moves from the server HTTP entrypoint to `core/trusted_origin.rs`. The browser-session journal no longer depends on a transport. No behaviour change.
2. **Domain transitions.** `Credential` now produces a `CredentialTransition` (target, before, after, cause, initiator, time) for issuance, explicit revocation, and automatic supersession. Explicit revoke still rejects a time before issuance; supersession clamps forward and names the replacing credential. Both rules live in the domain with tests instead of a comment.
3. **Registry journal.** The registry file gains an append-only `transitions` list (schema 2), written in the same atomic commit as the state it describes. Every mutation goes through `Credential`; the old `supersede()` helper is gone. `validate_registry` checks the list with one rule on every write and every reopen, so a hand-edited file fails the same way a bad live write would. A failed write is a failed commit, so there is no "committed but unaudited" state to reconcile. Schema 1 files are upgraded in memory on open with honest `predates_journal` records and written back by the next mutation. Issue, bootstrap, and revoke results carry their transitions; a `CredentialTransitionReader` port lists them per organization.
4. **Docs.** Auth crate README, ADR 0010, and the design write-up with the decisions at `docs/design/auth/credential-transition-audit.md`.

## Decisions recorded

- Evidence lives in the registry file, not a second journal, so state and evidence share one commit, one lock, one validator.
- Expiry is not a transition. Nothing happens at expiry; the instant is already in the issuance record.
- The browser-session single-validator design is untouched; only the origin function moved.
- The gateway wire result still reports the revision. Exposing transitions over the socket is a protocol change for its own issue.
- The rotation filter in `issue_internal` is unchanged (#56); the new `superseded` records make its scope visible.

## Tests

Registry tests cover every lifecycle path's cause, initiator, before/after, and correlation; once-only revocation keeping its first cause; idempotent issue replay returning the original records; a failed commit leaving no evidence and the retry recording it once; nine tampered-file cases rejected on reopen; and schema 1 upgrade. Domain tests cover the transition rule and each `Credential` method.

author: 27bslash6
body:
<!-- kody-pr-summary:start -->
## Summary

This PR fixes a bug (LAB-4127) in how the proxy injects the OAuth system prompt into requests for OAuth-authenticated accounts (`sk-ant-oat*` tokens).

## Problem

OAuth tokens require the Claude Code identity prompt (`"You are Claude Code, Anthropic's official CLI for Claude."`) to be present in the request's `system` array to access sonnet/opus models. Previously, the proxy always **prepended** this prompt at index 0 of the `system` array.

However, Claude Code also sends an **attribution block** (a billing header containing client version and conversation fingerprint) as `system[0]`. The upstream API only strips this attribution block when it arrives unchanged at index 0. By prepending the OAuth prompt, the proxy displaced the attribution block from index 0, which:

- Prevented the upstream from stripping the attribution block, so it leaked into the model input
- Broke the prompt-cache key

This was triggered on every OAuth request whose identity persona didn't already match the expected sentinel (e.g., the Claude Agent SDK personas introduced in Claude Code 2.1.x).

## Changes

- **Position-aware injection**: The OAuth prompt is now inserted at index 0 by default, but at index 1 when `system[0]` is a Claude Code attribution block (detected by the `x-anthropic-billing-header:` prefix). This preserves the attribution block's leading position so the upstream's positional strip still fires.
- **Broader detection**: `has_oauth_system_prompt` now scans the entire `system` array rather than only the first block, since the identity prompt can now appear after the attribution block.
- The upstream API accepts the OAuth prompt at any position in the `system` array, so it no longer needs to be first.

## Tests

Added regression tests covering:
- Injection after a leading attribution block across all three Claude Code 2.1.x personas, verifying the attribution block stays at `system[0]` and client `cache_control` moves with its original block.
- The case where the attribution block is not at index 0 (sentinel goes to index 0, no reordering).
- A full proxy roundtrip on an OAuth account confirming the forwarded body preserves the attribution block at `system[0]` and the sentinel at `system[1]`.
<!-- kody-pr-summary:end -->

body:
## Scope

Stacked Bank Reconciliation / Evidence-Audit RED on #66 exact `9a3eb05a1d5695bb9263b80c629718945e8d6f76`. This child preserves #59–#66 and does not rewrite their history.

Current exact head: `59e2928de415edeb542f5ceb2fbc495f55dd0759`.
Base: `test/accounting-structured-tax-evidence@9a3eb05a1d5695bb9263b80c629718945e8d6f76`.
Ordinary ancestry: 2 ahead / 0 behind.
Net delta: one new focused RED file, `tests/test_postgres_bank_statement_structured_referred_document_remitted_amount_evidence_red.py`, +240/-0. No production source, schema/migration, workflow, ADR, posting/reversal, Period Close, Accounting Policy, shared product docs, or Billing authority changed.

## Valid accounting finding

ISO 20022 structured remittance defines `RfrdDocAmt/RmtdAmt` as the amount of money remitted for the referred document, and PMPG guidance treats `DuePyblAmt` and `RmtdAmt` as distinct structured reconciliation evidence. Protected production still has no source-faithful structured-remittance projection and reduces buyer remittance evidence to the first `RmtInf/Ustrd` scalar. A bank-reported remitted amount can therefore disappear without changing authoritative transaction amount truth.

The RED keeps the referred invoice and `DuePyblAmt=26000 KRW` stable and changes only `RmtdAmt` from `22922 KRW` to `22923 KRW`. Required behavior is:

- the remitted-amount change is material to canonical `source_detail_hash -> source_entry_hash -> normalized_payload_hash`;
- every compared digest is first validated as canonical `sha256:<64 lowercase hex>`;
- statement-owner account identity and untouched sibling entry remain stable;
- entry/detail transaction amount truth remains exactly `25000.00 KRW` and is not derived from referred-document amounts;
- replay under the same statement identity requires the existing explicit-correction boundary;
- buyer reconciliation read retains invoice, due-payable amount, and remitted amount association in source order.

`RmtdAmt` remains bank-reported Bank Reconciliation / Evidence-Audit provenance. It does not acquire journal/posting/reversal, matching approval/completion, Period Close/reopen, Accounting Policy/financial-control, tax-policy determination, or Billing authority.

## Standards trace

- ISO 20022. (2026, March 19). *ISO 20022 Message Definitions — Bank-to-Customer Cash Management*. Current catalogue lists `camt.053.001.14 / BankToCustomerStatementV14`. https://www.iso20022.org/iso-20022-message-definitions?search=camt
- Payments Market Practice Group. (2024, May). *Structured Remittance Information*. SWIFT. The structured referred-document example distinguishes `DuePyblAmt` from `RmtdAmt` (remitted amount / amount paid). https://www.swift.com/sites/default/files/files/structured-remittance-information_final-updated.pdf

These references establish message/field semantics only. They do not prescribe AIS posting, close, maker-checker, evidence-hash, persistence, or correction implementation details.

## Fixture repair and evidence boundary

The initial child `f370ff289ebf04f1c713382bfdfee0b4a3380063` used non-zero fractional KRW amounts for the referred-document values. Before accepting review evidence, ordinary descendant `59e2928de415edeb542f5ceb2fbc495f55dd0759` made the fixture whole-won (`26000`, `22922`, `22923`) while preserving the one-field mutation and every oracle. This is a test-fixture realism repair, not an accounting-policy change.

Static Python syntax validation was repeated before publication. The exact is intentionally RED-only: current production is expected not to satisfy structured remitted-amount projection yet. Do not call this PostgreSQL GREEN, 100% production coverage, security GREEN, qualifying approval, or release evidence until the canonical production owner implements the source-faithful path and exact hosted evidence proves it.

#29 remains the production owner for parser/admission, normalization, tenant persistence/readback/recovery, evidence identity, and correction/replay. #37 remains the single writer for `docs/product-technical-gap-baseline.md`, shared `CHANGELOG.md`, and `docs/doctoring/STANDARD_TRACEABILITY.md` after protected integration.

Keep Draft. No self-approval, bypass, force-push, destructive rebase, predecessor-evidence transfer, source-neutral wake, premature shared-doc update, tag, or release.

author: aviclaw01
body:
Partly closes #28 — four of five soft-404s fixed; `/partners/[slug]` remains open and is documented in the file.

## What I found

#28 was filed about `/partners/<unknown>`. Probing the neighbours, **four more routes have the same bug**, and they matter more:

```
/brands/not-a-brand              200  →  404
/compare/not-a-vs-pair           200  →  404
/sizing/not-a-sizing-page        200  →  404
/budget/not-a-budget-page        200  →  404
```

`/brands` is the significant one — 34 real brand pages and the site's main organic surface. Every invented slug under these four prefixes was a live, indexable 200 carrying "We could not find that page." That is an unbounded duplicate-content surface on a site whose entire strategy is SEO.

## Cause — isolated, not guessed

My first two attempts were wrong, so I stopped patching and bisected it with throwaway routes:

| Probe | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Bare route calling `notFound()` | **404** |
| …with `force-dynamic` | **404** |
| …with `generateMetadata` returning normally, `notFound()` in the component | **404** |
| …with `notFound()` raised *inside* `generateMetadata` | **404** |

So `notFound()` is fine and `generateMetadata` is innocent — both theories I had been working from.

What the four broken routes share is **`generateStaticParams` with no `dynamicParams`**. It defaults to `true`, so Next renders an unknown param on demand, `notFound()` swaps in the not-found body, and the response still goes out as **200**.

Each of these four is generated from a fixed, code-defined set (`BRANDS`, `comparisonPairs()`, the sizing and budget tables). `export const dynamicParams = false` is not a workaround here — it states the truth about the route.

## Verified both directions

Unknown slugs now 404. Every real page still 200:

```
/brands/deye                                     200
/compare/deye-vs-felicity                        200
/sizing/what-size-inverter-for-1-5hp-ac          200
/budget/what-can-1m-of-solar-get-you-in-nigeria  200
/brands, /partners                               200
```

## `/partners/[slug]` is NOT fixed

Being explicit rather than letting the PR title imply otherwise. It is data-driven with no `generateStaticParams`, so `dynamicParams` does not apply. I tried `notFound()` inside `generateMetadata`, dropping `force-dynamic`, and `revalidate = 0` — **none changed the status**. Root cause not found. Documented in the file and left open on #28.

Low urgency: `partners` has **zero rows**, so no real profile URL exists to crawl yet. Worth solving before the first partner is approved, not before this merges.

## It does carry a real fix though

The lookup now goes through `dbGetChecked` inside a React `cache()`:

- **One query per request instead of two.** `generateMetadata` and the page each hit the database independently before.
- **A read failure no longer 404s.** `getPublicPartnerBySlug` goes through `dbGet`, which returns `[]` for a genuine miss *and* for a network failure — so a Supabase blip would have un-published a partner we vouched for and told crawlers the page was gone. Those outcomes are now distinct, and an outage renders "we could not load this profile just now" instead. That is #26's failure mode, fixed at this call site.

## Scope

Five files, all page components. Nothing owned by the concurrent agent.

Independent of #37, #41 and #42 — no overlapping files.

_Requested by **Colin** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WQFo24XvJJ8zQYn3pAmZSG?thread=cmsg_01WQFo24XvJJ8zQYn3pAmZSGXjkE7SMN2QjXH4He8vvKgx)_

## Change

Before: every routine Dependabot bump of `actions/attest-build-provenance` broke CI. `image/tests/test_release_provenance.py` held that action's exact commit SHA as a string literal, so the moment the pin in `release.yml` moved, `test_release_attests_and_retains_exact_subjects` failed in all three jobs. #117 is the current example.

After: a bump of that action passes CI on its own, while a pin that stops being a pin still fails. The test now asserts the shape the reference must keep rather than one particular SHA.

Concretely: `release.yml` must contain exactly one reference to the action, pinned to a 40-character commit SHA and carrying a trailing `# vX.Y.Z` comment, and every reference to the action in the file must be that pin. A floating `@v4` tag, a SHA with no version comment, a second unpinned reference, or the attestation step being dropped all still fail. Nothing else in the test changes; the digest, permissions, subject-path and bundle-path assertions are untouched.

## Verification

- Source revision and execution environment: 658ef828dc83eae74a8051bde8f44eb3825a5aae, Python 3.11.15 on Ubuntu 24.04.4.
- Focused tests and preflight: `python3 -m unittest discover -s image/tests -p 'test_*.py'` (150 tests, OK) and `python3 -m unittest discover -s services/clawosd/tests -p 'test_*.py'` (32 tests, OK), matching what `ci.yml` runs. I also ran `test_release_attests_and_retains_exact_subjects` against four locally mutated copies of `release.yml`: #117's bumped SHA passes; a floating `@v4` tag, a SHA stripped of its version comment, and the step deleted each fail.
- Live/visual or fresh-install evidence, where applicable: not applicable, this is a test-only change with no runtime or image effect.
- Deployment receipt/checkpoint, if used: none.

## Risk and limits

The assertion is a regular expression over `release.yml` text, so it proves the reference is SHA-pinned and commented; it cannot prove the SHA corresponds to the commented version, or that the commented version is one anyone reviewed. Reviewing what a bump actually points at remains a human step on the Dependabot PR. Recovery is to revert this one commit, which restores the literal-SHA assertion.

Note for landing: merging this does not by itself turn #117 green. That PR's checks ran against the old test, so it needs a Dependabot rebase comment once this is on `main`.

- [x] No credentials, VM state or personal transcripts included.
- [x] Unrelated changes preserved; no foreign-distribution runtime dependencies.
- [x] Claims distinguish unit, runtime and fresh-install proof. Everything above is unit-level evidence only; no runtime or fresh-install proof is claimed.

body:
Closes #837.

One model is named ONCE, in the catalog. Before this, 6 places named the same model and 4 names had already drifted.

## What each head reads now

| Site | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `CloudTranscriptionModel.cs` | 35 `DisplayName = "..."` literals | `SharedModelsCatalog.DisplayName(provider, kind, id)` |
| `CloudTranscriptionModels.swift` | 33 literals | `SharedModelsCatalog.entry(provider:kind:id:)?.displayName` |
| `STTCapabilities.swift` | 12 more names, read by NOTHING | field deleted |
| Linux Provider row | 11 hard-coded tier ids + 11 locale keys | `cloud_stt_cloud_tier_vendor_groups` |
| macOS + Windows Streaming | `modes.cloudAccuracy.<tier>.label` | the catalog tier name |
| 80 locale files | 441 resx blocks + 240 `.strings` lines | deleted |

## The Linux Provider row is a company now

A row was a TIER, so Google appeared twice and `ElevenLabs Scribe v2` repeated the model name below it. A row is a COMPANY now, sorted, and the Model row decides the tier — picking a Gemini family model moves the mode off `geminiTranscribe` and onto `gemini`, which is a different route and different credits.

Folding `gemini` + `geminiTranscribe` into one *Google* row is deliberate and was agreed. 12 eligible tiers → 11 company rows, which is exactly the tier set the old hard-coded array held.

![provider row before and after](https://public-media.21dreams.org/2026-09/9a96d91868ac5fb742e9ead781b8aaa5/hw-provider-before-after.png)

## Two blank-row defects the screenshots found

Both were found by driving the built app, not by reading code.

1. The Model row drew EMPTY whenever the mode's stored model was not one the tier offers — which is every HyperWhisper Cloud mode that never chose a model. The getter falls back to the tier default. Save still writes null, and the send path still resolves the default from the same catalog.
2. Changing company blanked the row again. A `ComboBox` drops a selection its new `ItemsSource` does not hold and writes that null back through the binding; the notification the view model raises then arrives while the binding is still writing, so the binding ignores it. The dialog re-applies the selection after the list change settles.

![closed rows before and after](https://public-media.21dreams.org/2026-09/73a20896d5a64a3b9a2f3c70de011a3a/hw-rows-before-after.png)

## The macOS names were wrong, not just duplicated

- `"modes.cloudAccuracy.grokStt.label" = "High (Grok SST)"` — a typo, and a stale High/Medium prefix scheme — against the catalog's `Grok STT`.
- `STTCapabilities.swift` said `Nova-3 General`; the catalog says `Nova 3 General`.
- `translation-status.json` already classified all 11 tier-label keys as "identical by design", which is independent evidence they were never translated.

## The gate

`tools/check-model-name-literals.sh` runs as a 4th `static-gates` job. It states what it does NOT hold, so the carve-outs are readable rather than remembered:

- a TIER or company name (`Gemini 3.5 Transcribe` in 10 provider enums) — the same 5 steps again, filed separately;
- a POST-PROCESSING model name — a `kind: "text"` row carries no `displayName` at all, so those 3 registries have nothing to read yet;
- a LOCAL model name — no shared catalog lists one, so onboarding is its only owner.

Proved it catches a regression: re-adding `"Nova 3 Medical"` to `StreamingView.swift` fails it at exit 1, naming the file and the line.

## Verification

<details><summary>All green on this box</summary>

```
cargo test --workspace        566 passed, 0 failed
cargo clippy --all-targets    -D warnings, clean
HyperWhisper.Application.Tests            passed  (new RunCloudVendorPickerTestsAsync)
HyperWhisper.Localization.Tests           10/10   (base key pin 864 -> 853)
HyperWhisper.CatalogConformance.Tests     7/7
HyperWhisper.AppTypeConformance.Tests     4/4
HyperWhisper.LanguageConformance.Tests    9/9
app/linux/HyperWhisper.Linux              0 warnings, 0 errors
app/windows/HyperWhisper.SmokeTests       0 errors
tools/check-model-name-literals.sh        exit 0
```

The new suite really runs — flipping its tier count to 13 aborts the harness at exit 134 on that assertion.

</details>

Windows and macOS build and test on their own CI runners; this box compiles the Windows head but cannot run WPF.

### CI on this branch

All 8 checks are green on `934036c7`: macOS CI, Windows CI, Linux CI, nextjs-ci, static-gates, Shared Core Tests, Binding Drift, Drizzle journal.

Two red checks on the first push were real, and both are fixed here:

- **macOS CI** — the Meta BYOK row builds its `CloudTranscriptionModel` at run time, so the static sweep missed it and it still passed `displayName:`.
- **nextjs-ci** — `/latency` and `/choosing-a-model` each keep a mirror of `cloud-stt-catalog.json`, and a test reads the real catalog and fails on drift. `Muse Voice Transcribe 1.0` -> `1` had to land in both.

macOS CI then aborted twice inside `BackupLicenseStorageTests` with no message, in 0.000 seconds — the known test-host crash, not this diff. The `if: failure()` crash dump printed nothing, because `find -name 'hyperwhisper*.ips'` is case-sensitive and the binary is `HyperWhisper`. That step is fixed in this PR.

Fixes the underlying reason legitimate hiring opportunities can exist while /jobs remains empty.

## Duplicate prevention
- Adds a database unique guard so one client cannot have multiple open roles with the same normalized title.
- Client form gracefully reuses the existing role if two submissions race.
- Expands guest-form duplicate detection from 5 to 30 minutes.
- Consolidates the existing Amara Island duplicate role set into one canonical open role while keeping redundant job records as closed history and preserving shortlist candidates.

## Publication blockers
- Adds a shared publication-blocker helper.
- Recruiter role list shows: Needs client account / Needs role details / Needs terms / Waiting client approval / Published.
- Role Control Center shows the blocker explanation and the correct next action.
- Admin job list shows the same publication state.

## Guest client linking
- Adds a recruiter "Send client account link" action.
- Uses the existing lead-bound claim flow, which only attaches the role when the client signs up/logs in with the matching email.
- Claim email now links directly to the secure client-account claim path.

### [`v6.0.0`](https://redirect.github.com/cplieger/auth/releases/tag/v6.0.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/cplieger/auth/compare/v5.0.13...v6.0.0)

##### Breaking changes

##### Verify ceremony origins by policy, not an enumerated list

- The module path is now `github.com/cplieger/auth/v6`; update every import and the `go.mod` require.
- `webauthn.BeginRegistration`, `webauthn.BeginLogin` and `webauthn.BeginConditionalLogin` take the browser's origin as a new last argument: build it with `webauthn.ParseOrigin(r.Header.Get("Origin"))` and handle the returned `*webauthn.OriginError` (its `Reason` names why) before calling them.
- A ceremony now verifies against the origin it was begun at, so no expected-origin list has to be enumerated in advance; a `Ceremony` not produced by a `Begin*` call fails at Finish with `webauthn.ErrCeremonyUnbound`.
- `webauthn.RPConfig.Origins` is now optional and only narrows: leave it nil to accept every `https://` origin at or under the relying-party ID (and `http://localhost`), or list origins to accept exactly those on scheme, host and port. A list of `https://` origins at or under the relying-party ID behaves exactly as before.

- `webauthn.New` now refuses a relying-party ID that is not spelled in lowercase, with an error matching `webauthn.ErrIllegalRPID`; lowercase the configured value. `webauthn.ValidateRPID` is exported for checking a value before construction.
