author: joela510
body:
Two live defects on the workflow dashboard, same shape: **a component reads a field that nothing produces.** Both turned out to be the twin-arm shape as well — a fix applied to one panel and not its sibling. ## Where the brief was wrong **1. The prescribed fix direction was backwards.** The brief said `formatDate` "falls through to the host browser's timezone" and directed me to route the season zone in from `seasonClock.js`. Doing that would have *introduced* a bug. `formatDate` goes through `anchorToSeasonClock` first, and the value being formatted is the wrong kind of thing to zone. `generatedAt` is `scheduler_runs.completed_at || created_at` (`practiceSummaryMapper:21`, `gameSummaryMapper:21`), or `new Date().toISOString()` (`GameSchedulingPage:729`) — **a real instant, not a season wall time.** #402 already settled this on `PracticeReadinessPanel`: *"a real instant carrying a zone, and the viewer's own clock is the right one to read it on… There is no `timezone` prop, and its absence is the contract."* So the remedy is to **delete** the prop, not supply it. **2. `TeamListView` does read `timezone`** — `TeamListView.jsx:30`. (The brief's grep named `components/TeamListView.jsx`; the file is at `components/teaming/`, and `2>/dev/null` swallowed the error.) **3. The defect was not purely latent.** `GameSchedulingPage:1197` holds a **real** `currentSeasonSetting.timezone` and passed it to `GameReadinessPanel`, rendering the run timestamp on the *season's* clock instead of the operator's. **A false docblock.** `TeamOverviewPanel` claimed `TeamListView` "DOES honour a `timezone`… the two render different timestamps, not the same one two ways." They render the same one: `DashboardWorkflow:185-201` renders them as the fallback and child of a *single* `FeatureGuard` with identical `teamData.generatedAt`. Corrected. ## Defect A — the dead `timezone` thread Removed from all six sites, including the one real producer at `GameSchedulingPage`. `GameSchedulingPage` keeps its zone everywhere else — it places naive slot wall times on the season clock, which is what a zone is for. ## Defect A3 — the swallowed error All three child hooks hold an `error`; `useDashboardData` returned none, so `WorkflowPage`'s error banner could never open and an RLS refusal reached the operator as an empty dashboard. Now surfaced **as a string** (the banner renders into a ``; a raw `Error` child crashes React). ## Defect B — four KPI cards no producer can fill `balancedScore`, `manualActionRequiredCount`, `venueSaturation`, `conflictFreeTeams` appear **only** inside `PracticeReadinessPanel`. All four rendered `0%`, `0`, `Unknown`, `0%` permanently. **LIVE-8's fix was a one-arm fix on this same component** — it took the header line and left four identical defects below it. | Card | Outcome | |---|---| | Manual Actions | **Wired** to `summary.unassignedTeams` (`ROSTERED_TEAM`; `manualFollowUpRate`'s own numerator) | | Field Distribution | **Deleted** — no metric measures field evenness | | Venue Saturation | **Deleted** — `slotUtilization` is per-slot occupancy, not a saturation band | | Conflict Free | **Deleted** — `coachConflicts` counts coach pairs, not conflict-free teams | Nothing synthesised. `GameReadinessPanel` and `TeamListView` were checked for the same disease, enumerating fields from component *and* producer independently: all have producers. --- # Review rounds ## `/code-review` (pre-open) — 4 findings, all fixed in `fe3a0f7` 1. **MEDIUM** — the error banner was a one-way latch, and this PR made it reachable (`useTeamSummary` re-polls every 2s; one failed poll then a success left a red banner over a loaded dashboard). Sources separated by lifetime. 2. **MEDIUM** — **my own tests were host-timezone coupled.** A hard-coded `SEASON_TZ` meant three assertions passed *vacuously* on a Pacific-time machine; CI was green only because runners are UTC. The zone is now chosen against the host at load time. Verified green under six zones, and still red under each for the realistic regression. 3. **LOW** — `TeamAnalysisPage`'s `error: _error` became a live value being discarded; no longer destructured, reason stated. 4. **LOW** — the `toSeasonInstant` caller list went stale; updated. ## Supervisor round 1 — 4 findings, all fixed in `3358134`, none rejected **The substantive one: a total and a breakdown that could silently disagree.** `summary.unassignedTeams` is roster-derived; `unassignedByReason[].count` increments *before* the roster lookup (`practiceMetrics.js:331`), so it counts list entries. Three divergences reproduce from the real engine: | Case | card | reasons sum | `dataQualityWarnings` | |---|---|---|---| | A — `unassigned` entry names unknown team | 1 | **2** | warns | | B — team in **neither** list | **2** | 1 | **empty** | | C — `assignments` entry names unknown team | **1** | 0 | warns | **Divergence B emits no warning**, so rendering `dataQualityWarnings` alone would not have reconciled it — and B is what any writer that persists no `unassigned` list produces for every team. Also found: the empty state said **"All teams assigned automatically."** whenever the reasons list was empty — *including over a card reading 7*. A false sentence, not just two numbers disagreeing. Fixed so the panel cannot disagree in silence: the card keeps the engine's quantity, a reconciliation line appears when the two part company, the empty state no longer over-claims, and `dataQualityWarnings` is rendered (nothing in the app rendered it anywhere). Plus: dismissal scoped to the occurrence rather than the message; the one-card grid; and the skeleton's KPI promise now **verified** by a test asserting the engine always emits a numeric `summary.unassignedTeams`. ## Supervisor round 2 — 1 finding, fixed in `a73aef7` + `3753ed3` The reconciliation line ended *"see the data-quality notes"* unconditionally, while the notes render only when warnings exist — and divergence B, the case the reconciliation exists for, has none. A pointer to nothing in the branch that matters most. The explanation now stands alone and the pointer is appended only when there are notes. The same round raised the `

` using `insight-card__empty` on a non-empty message. I swapped to `insight-card__alert-text`, then **reverted it**: that class is `display: inline-flex` with a `gap` and no `flex-wrap`, built for an icon plus a short label — every JSX fragment of this sentence would become its own non-wrapping flex item — and it has no other user in the repository. The swap traded a naming mismatch for a layout defect. The mismatch stands knowingly, recorded at the call site. --- ## Verification (all executed and observed) | Gate | Result | |---|---| | `npm run typecheck` | 0 errors | | `npm run lint` | 0 errors, 1 warning = baseline | | `npm run test` | **3353** passed / 34 skipped / 6 todo — `main` baseline **3318**, so **+35**, exactly this PR's new file | | same under `TZ=America/Los_Angeles` | 3353 — identical | | `npm run frontend:build` | clean | | `check:advisors` / `check:bundle` | PASS / PASS (222.96 KB gz of 244.14) | | season-2026 fixture suite (32 files) | 1817 passed | No migration needed; none written. ## Seventeen breaks, each constructed, run red, reverted Highlights: adding `venueSaturation` back to `practiceMetrics.js` reddens the "none of the four" test — proving the subject set really is the engine, not a fixture. Dropping the team arm from error aggregation reddens *only* the team-arm test. Making the notes pointer unconditional reddens divergence B; removing it entirely reddens divergence A — symmetric, so neither direction drifts unnoticed. ## Adjacent findings, filed separately, not fixed here - `WorkflowPage:64`/`:206` read the `loading` **object** as a boolean — `LoadingScreen` is unreachable and `IngestionOverlay` mounts unconditionally (harmless only because it self-gates). - `DashboardWorkflow:270` hardcodes `dashboardLoading={{ practice: false }}`. - P

author: ericgriffin
body:
Closes #2184

## The dead code

The dive detail page carried a block of playback UI nothing could reach.

The "Playback" button that revealed it was removed in c4e70ae1814
(2026-02-26), *"until the functionality can be more thought-out"*. That commit
took only the 17-line button; the block it revealed stayed behind
`if (playbackState.isActive)`. Nothing on the page can set that flag. The one
widget that could is `PlaybackControls`, whose activation branch sits inside
the very gate it would have to open. The fullscreen profile page became the
sole producer of `isActive`, and it clears the flag again on dispose, so the
detail page is guaranteed to read false.

## It was not inert

The page called `ref.watch(playbackProvider(dive.id))` unconditionally at the
top of `build`, only to evaluate that gate, and it stays mounted under the
fullscreen route (`MaterialPageRoute`, default `maintainState`).

Measured, not assumed: the detail page is still mounted while fullscreen is up,
and `playbackProvider` notifies **31 times per wall-second** at the default 30x
replay. So playing a dive fullscreen rebuilt the entire detail page about 31
times a second behind it, to render something that could never appear.

## Removed

- The gated block, plus the `playbackProvider` and profile-analysis watches
  that only fed it. The analysis watch's own `activeDiveSourceProvider` read is
  still made a few lines below, so no subscription is lost.
- `playback_controls.dart` (240 lines) and `playback_stats_panel.dart` (345),
  reachable only through the gate.
- `tissue_saturation_panel.dart` (233) and `tissue_saturation_chart.dart`
  (332). `TissueSaturationPanel` never had a caller, not even in the commit
  that introduced it, and the chart was used only by that panel. Only
  `CompactTissueSaturation`, in the same file, was reachable, through the gate.
- 22 ARB keys across all 11 locales, found by baseline-diffing a repo-wide
  reference scan rather than trusting "unreferenced" (about 790 keys are
  already unreferenced for unrelated reasons). 19 were orphaned by this change;
  `diveLog_detail_button_playback` has been orphaned since c4e70ae1814, and
  `diveLog_playbackStats_pressure` and `diveLog_playback_speed_label` were dead
  strings inside the dead files.

The range-analysis button loses its `if (!playbackState.isActive)` wrapper,
which was always true. That is the only behaviour change visible to a user, and
it is a no-op.

## Not touched

Playback itself. The fullscreen profile keeps its own transport
(`profile_transport_controls`), which is the only surface that offers playback,
and `PlaybackNotifier` stays as its engine.

The live tissue surfaces: `tissue_heat_map`, `tissue_area_chart`,
`compact_tissue_loading_card`, the surface-interval `tissue_recovery_chart` and
the `dive_3d` tissue widgets. `diveLog_playbackStats_deco` and
`diveLog_tissue_title` stay, since the profile chart and heat map still use
them.

Historical plan docs that mention the deleted files are records and were left
alone. The one exception is the 3D flythrough spec, which named
`playback_stats_panel` as a component to reuse; that line now points at this
removal, since the file is recoverable from history and the HUD may want
different content against a 3D scene anyway.

## Tests

No tests covered any of the removed code. Full suite green: 30471 passed, 21
skipped. `flutter analyze` clean, `dart format` clean, l10n regenerated with
`flutter gen-l10n`.

author: ksquared-16
body:
## Resolve independent metric keys concurrently

`resolveMetrics` walked its keys in a `for await` loop, so a multi-key request paid their **sum**.

### The decomposition that motivated it

Measured on the canonical Work Unit header request — deployed, warm, 6 reps, one session. An unknown-key request returns 400 *after* `requireAnalyticsReadAccess()` but *before* the `org_settings` read and `resolveMetrics`, which isolates the authorization floor cleanly:

| probe | wall | metric work (− 266ms floor) |
|---|---|---|
| authorization floor only | **266ms** | — |
| `enrollment.lead_count` | 1,104ms | **838ms** |
| `enrollment.active_leads` | 1,096ms | **830ms** |
| `ops.needs_attention_count` | 496ms | 230ms (7 candidates) |
| `ops.work_overdue_count` | 466ms | 200ms |
| all three combined | 1,307ms | 1,041ms |
| all three, alias substituted | 1,288ms | — |

Three results worth recording:

- The floor is **266ms**, not the ~600ms previously estimated.
- The deprecated alias is **empirically cost-identical** (1,096 vs 1,104ms) — settling Part 4. Substituting it buys nothing.
- Individually the keys cost 1,268ms of metric work; combined, 1,041ms — so some setup already amortises. The parallel floor is the slowest key, **~838ms**. The serial edge is worth roughly **200ms**.

### What this change does and does not do

Nothing shared is written. Each resolver derives its own scope from the same immutable `ctx`, reads, and returns; there is no ordering dependency and no mutation either key could observe. Result order still follows the requested keys, because some call sites index by position.

**Failure semantics are deliberately unchanged.** The loop propagated a thrown key and failed the request; `Promise.all` preserves exactly that. `allSettled` would be a different contract — arguably a better one — and changing it silently inside a scheduling commit would hide a semantic change in a performance change.

This does **not** by itself make the document's KPI seed bind: the lead path alone (~838ms) still exceeds the composition it races.

### The lead path, classified but not repaired

`enrollment.lead_count` → `resolveParticipantMetric` → `enrollmentProjection.load(...)`, which for a work-unit scope performs 5–6 **sequential** round trips (work_unit → department work_units → department-wide opportunities → OCM → process_instances → stitch) and materialises the whole participant projection, then counts in JS. The header needs one number.

Classification: **`C — OVERFETCH_FOR_COUNT`**, compounded by **`D`**. Not repaired here: reproducing `isActiveLeadParticipant` as a scoped count cannot be proven semantically equivalent within this slice, and Part 6 forbids reuse without that proof.

### Certification

5/5 gates; 2 planted defects caught (serial loop restored; failure contract silently switched to `allSettled`). Regression red set identical to base (same 12 files, 20 pre-existing failures): zero new failures, +32 passing. `typecheck`, `typecheck:tests` and a real production build all pass.

author: azmartone67
body:
## Why attribution reads 0.0

`paid_signal_attribution_30d.attribution_rate_pct = 0.0`. The bridge lanes aren't broken — **nothing reaches them.** Two independent defects, both in `utils/paywall_response.py`.

### 1. The pair code was minted `if user_id:`

The pair code is the only thing that puts `client_reference_id` on a checkout. Anonymous callers are the **majority** of paywall volume — the anon-escalation note ten lines above says exactly that — so their Stripe links carried `utm_*` and nothing else. The sale reached the webhook with no session, no `caller_id` and no signal id, so all three lanes failed **by construction, at any volume**.

Measured live 2026-09-19, anonymous, `/api/v1/pipeline`:

```
recommended_upgrade_url -> buy.stripe.com/...?utm_source=mcp_paywall&utm_tool=pipeline
```

No `client_reference_id`. UTM params reach Stripe's dashboard and never touch our tables.

It now mints against `user_id or _anon_caller_id`, where `_anon_caller_id` is the **same identity `mcp_signal_canonical` stamps on every `mcp_upgrade_signals` row** — so the code is joinable by the `caller_bridge` lane that already exists. No new concept, no new table.

**Safe with no key behind the hash:** `redeem_pair_code`'s two UPDATEs (`api_keys`, `mcp_dev_keys`) match zero rows and it already tolerates that (`rows_flipped = 0`, both wrapped). An anonymous buyer has no key to flip — the point is to *record which signal sold*.

### 2. `recommended_upgrade_url` was the last raw Stripe link

FF+16 re-routed `one_click_upgrade_url` (developer) through `/checkout/start` and missed this one. But this is the field we literally name **recommended**, it's the cheapest unblock, and `_build_human_message` leads with it — so the CTA an agent is most likely to surface was the one taking the sale out of DC Hub entirely, past the email capture and past any click we could log.

Same override and the same `_direct_stripe` convention the developer CTA already uses, `tier='starter'` so the **product does not change**.

`mcp_gatekeeper.py` is untouched — it already mints (from `api_key`) and already routes `buy_now_url` through `/checkout/start`. This brings the second builder, the one `api_tier_gating` uses for every gated REST tool and where most signals are raised, up to the same standard.

## Verification

Mutation-tested, restored in `finally`:

```
CAUGHT  revert fix 2 — mint only for user_id            (2 failed)
CAUGHT  revert fix 1 — drop the starter re-route        (2 failed)
CAUGHT  silently upsell starter -> developer            (1 failed)
CAUGHT  drop the raw link instead of moving it aside    (1 failed)
restored: 5 passed
```

The third and fourth matter as much as the first two: a re-route that quietly changes which product is recommended, or that deletes the raw link instead of moving it aside, would both "fix" attribution while breaking something else.

75 passed across `test_anon_attribution_lane`, `test_conversion_funnel_stalls`, `test_conversion_loop_flow_not_stock`, `test_conversion_visibility`, `test_honest_demand_and_attribution`, `test_auto_trial_conversion` and the new file. `regression_lint --mode delta --base origin/main` → `✓ no NEW violations`.

**Not yet verified in production.** After deploy, an anonymous gated call should return a `recommended_upgrade_url` on `dchub.cloud` and every Stripe URL in the payload should carry `client_reference_id=DCM-…`. The metric itself only moves on the next real sale.

## Scope

This makes the signal → paid path *measurable*. It does not by itself raise conversion — but it is the prerequisite for pricing the `$10 one-time = 1,000 calls` tier against real data instead of guessing.

author: akshay7273
body:
Implements V20-PR02: the local outbox — a durable offline queue for targeted sends, built on the V20-PR01 job/recipient-attempt model.

## What's new

**Engine (`packages/engine/outbox/`)**
- `Enqueue`: expands/digests sources with production transfer semantics, fingerprints them, binds one queued attempt per recipient, and records source paths in a `0600` sidecar (`<jobID>.sources`) kept outside the Job schema.
- `DispatchOnce`: lease acquisition with stale/crash adoption, expiry, source re-expansion + SHA-256 re-verification before every dispatch (changed/missing/corrupt sources fail the job closed — never silently resent), bounded parallel dispatch across jobs.
- Outcome policy: `ok` counts as delivered only with a valid 64-hex content digest (ok-without-digest fails closed); offline/transient failures re-queue as interrupted with exponential backoff while attempt budget remains; explicit refusals are terminal.
- Lease heartbeat during sends so a long transfer isn't mistaken for a crash (no duplicate sends); in-flight results are dropped if the job was cancelled or the lease moved on — cancel can't resurrect a job.
- `Cancel` (terminal, never dispatches again) and `RetryFailed` (explicit operator re-queue of failed targets with a fresh budget).
- `jobs.QueueJob`: draft → queued transition used at enqueue time.

**CLI (`sendbeam outbox`)**
- `enqueue` / `list` / `show` / `dispatch` / `cancel` / `retry`, with `--json` output and `--config-dir` isolation.
- Dispatch wires the production sender: trust credentials resolve at dispatch time from the trust store, and the resolved device ID must equal the attempt's device ID (job labels are never trusted for peer binding).
- `send --to` target resolution/building extracted into shared helpers (`targeted.go`) so both paths bind peers identically — no behavior change to `send`.

## Verification
- 20 engine tests (`-race` clean): backoff, restart adoption, expiry, cancel-during-send race, corrupt/missing sources, digest honesty, mixed per-target outcomes, attempt exhaustion, parallel dispatch.
- 7 CLI tests: enqueue/list/show/cancel flows, unknown device, arg validation, empty dispatch.
- Full CLI suite green; `go vet` clean; `gofmt` clean.

## Security notes

author: trentas
body:
Aplica **todos** os grupos pendentes do Dependabot num branch só, em vez de uma cascata de rebases — eles tocam o mesmo lockfile, então em sequência cada merge invalidaria os outros.

## Dependências

| Grupo | Conteúdo |
|---|---|
| next-react | react/react-dom 19.2.4 → **19.3.0**, `@next/mdx` e `eslint-config-next` 16.3.5, `@types` correspondentes |
| radix-ui | 16 pacotes |
| dev-tooling | typescript-eslint 8.58 → 8.70, tailwind, postcss, prettier |
| npm-minor-patch | zod 4.6.5, resend 6.28, lucide-react 1.46, react-hook-form 7.88 + 4 |
| supabase | `@supabase/ssr` 0.10 → **0.12.7** |
| types | `@types/mdx` |
| pip | PyJWT 2.8.0 → **2.14.0** |

Mantidos de propósito: `next-auth` no **v4**, `stripe` no **v21**.

### Lockfile regenerado, não remendado

A resolução incremental travou: o `eslint-config-next@16.2.1` pinado arrastava `typescript-eslint@8.58`, que dava peer-conflict com o parser 8.70 que ele mesmo estava sendo mandado aceitar. Ovo-e-galinha. Regenerei do zero — daí o diff grande do lockfile. Continua em **0 vulnerabilities**.

### Sobre o `@supabase/ssr`

Era o que mais me preocupava: em `0.x`, minor é breaking por convenção, e `^0.10.0` nem cobre `0.12.7`. Na prática o pacote é usado em **um único lugar** (`lib/supabase.ts`), com `createServerClient` e `CookieOptions` — ambos ainda exportados, confirmado pelo typecheck.

## Lint novo do React Compiler

O `eslint-config-next` 16.3.5 traz `eslint-plugin-react-hooks` v6, que promove duas regras do React Compiler a **erro** e expôs 9 violações pré-existentes. Corrigidas, não rebaixadas:

- **`verify-email`, `accept-invite`** — os effects de fetch-on-mount agora guardam os updates de estado numa closure async com flag de cancelamento. Rodam quando a request resolve, não sincronamente na montagem, e deixam de escrever em formulário desmontado.
- **`reset-password`** — o token vinha da URL mas era copiado pra state por um effect. Agora lê direto do `searchParams`; o effect sumiu.
- **`signup`, `verify-email`** — estado inicial derivado da URL no primeiro render, em vez de corrigido por effect depois.
- **`accept-invite`** — o branch de token ausente setava estado que **nada podia renderizar**, porque já existe um render guard `if (!token)` que retorna um card próprio. Removido como código morto.
- **`Enable2FADialog`** — o reset de step foi pro `onOpenChange`, onde pertence como evento, em vez de effect reagindo a `open` depois do fato.
- **`profile`, `Enable2FADialog`** — helpers memoizados e declarados antes dos effects que os chamam.
- **`carousel.tsx`** — `eslint-disable` pontual e comentado. É shadcn/ui vendorado sincronizando estado externo do Embla; reescrever em torno de `useSyncExternalStore` divergiria do upstream sem ganho de comportamento.

## Verificação

| Etapa | Resultado |
|---|---|
| `eslint .` | **0 errors** (59 warnings, permitidos) |
| `tsc --noEmit` | limpo |
| `vitest run --coverage` | **183/183** |
| coverage | 76.3% stmts · 72.8% branches · 81.2% funcs · 76.4% lines (gate 70%) |
| `next build` | sucesso, 35 páginas estáticas |
| `npm audit` | 0 vulnerabilities |

## Ressalva

As mudanças de fluxo de auth estão cobertas **só por teste unitário** — os caminhos de renderização não têm e2e. As alterações são conservadoras (derivar estado em vez de corrigir via effect, remover código morto), mas vale um smoke manual em signup, verify-email, reset-password, accept-invite e ativação de 2FA antes de usar como base de projeto novo.

## Fecha

Supersedes #28, #29, #30, #31, #35, #36, #37, #38, #40, #41, #42.

author: hexblot
body:
Two findings from Gitar's dashboard, both confirmed against current code and both
in already-released behaviour. A third finding from the same list (an OSV document
whose affected entries are all unreadable dropping silently) was checked and is
already closed by `e884953`; its four reproductions all produce an unattributed
coverage gap today.

Independent of #21 and branched from `main`.

## A run that lost a worker counted the work it redid twice

`Planner::planGroupsInParallel()` re-plans the packages a dead worker never
reached, in the parent process. `solve()` counts each run as it happens, and
`$keep()` — which exists to bring a *child's* count home, since the child's tally
dies with it — then added the package's total again.

Measured on the three-package scenario the new test uses:

```
healthy:  solver_runs=10, per-package=[acme/a:3, acme/b:3, acme/c:3]
degraded: solver_runs=19, per-package=[acme/a:3, acme/b:3, acme/c:3]
```

Reporting only: budgets are counted per finding (`findingSolves`) and were never
fed from this counter, so no search was ever cut short. What it corrupted is the
reproducibility metadata, whose purpose is to let someone run the same thing again.

`$keep()` now takes whether to count, and the fallback says no. The test compares
a degraded run with a healthy one — the killed worker dies before completing a
single solve, so the work is identical and only the counting can differ.

## The action ignored `labels` and `draft` on a pull request it had already opened

`action/run.sh` honoured both inputs on the `gh pr create` path only, so a label
added to the workflow later never reached the open pull request.

- **labels**: re-applied on every run (`--add-label`, idempotent).
- **draft**: deliberately *not* re-applied. Once a pull request exists, ready-for-review
  is a decision a person made about it; a nightly run that flipped it back would be
  arguing with them. Now documented as such in `action.yml` and `docs/ci-integration.md`.

The harness had the same blind spot as the code: its `gh` stub reported no open
pull request, so both runs took the create path and the update path — the one a
scheduled job takes every day but the first — shipped untested. Its second run now
meets the pull request the first one opened.

## Verification

- Both regression tests validated by reintroducing their faults.
- `composer check` on this branch: 407 tests / 3371 assertions, PHPStan clean, Deptrac 0 violations / 0 uncovered, action harness
  all checks passed.
- `mkdocs build --strict` clean.

author: arena-ai-coding-agent[bot]
body:
## The bug

Found while spot-checking the live site after merging #21: every Season 2
participant page rendered **"Round trips (largest 40): No closed round
trips"** directly below post-mortem prose that counted those same trips
(e.g. `@NBA_Slate_Attention`: "79 closed round trips" … "No closed round
trips"). This had been true of every published page since the first
Season 2 release.

Root cause in `sim/ledger.py`: `build_round_trips` keyed open lots by
**symbol alone** and never wrote a `participant` field into any trip row,
so the site builder's `trips_for(username)` matched nothing for anyone.
The same symbol-only keying meant that in the all-participant ledger two
participants trading the same symbol could blend into or close each
other's lots, so the trip list was not the union of the per-participant
ledgers.

## The fix

- Lots are keyed by `(participant, symbol)`; every trip row (closed and
  open) carries the participant whose lot it closed.
- Season 2 memory re-derived: **per-participant trip counts now equal the
  leaderboard's `closed_trades` for all 19 participants**; total net P&L
  unchanged to the cent ($35,302.81 — it is fill-invariant; only
  attribution moved); the ledger digest hashes the fill tape, which did
  not change. Stress labels' round-trip counts moved by 1–3 (the
  phantom closes); primary's did not.
- The independent audit's own re-derivation had the **same symbol-only
  keying** — which is exactly why it agreed with the contaminated
  published list. Fixed identically, plus three new permanent checks:
  every published closed trip names a participant present in the fill
  tape; each participant's published trip count equals their leaderboard
  `closed_trades`; the audit's re-derived per-participant counts equal
  the published ones.
- Regression test: two participants, one symbol — the case that produced
  phantom attribution.
- IR-78 records the finding; README register counts updated (78).

## Verification

- **634 tests green** (one new regression test).
- Season 1 audit: 1,260 checks, 0 failures.
- Season 2 audit: 0 failures, now including the participant-attribution
  checks above.
- Participant pages render their round-trip tables (e.g. the NBA
  persona's worst trade, FLUT −$5,436, now appears in the table where
  the prose already described it).

author: fattchris
body:
## Summary

Five fixes to the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash EXL3 serving path. The first three are in the disk-Engram graph path; the fourth is a loader bug that was silently running the DSpark draft at **25% of its expert weights**.

Net effect on 4x DGX Spark (TP4/EP4, bs1, k=2 spec decode), measured with `llm-inference-bench` sustained 30 s cells at c=1: **eager 21.2 -> ~26 tok/s repeat**, and **+9% to +20%** on the multi-domain matrix after fix #4, best cell **30.21 tok/s**. Correct output at every state (`The capital of France is` -> `Paris`, temp 0).

---

## 1. Engram registry-key collision (correctness under replay)

`Engram.prepare_embeddings` registers itself in `_ENGRAM_OPAQUE_LAYERS` under

```python
name = getattr(self, "layer_name", None) or getattr(self, "prefix", "engram")
```

but `Engram.__init__` **never stores `prefix` or `layer_name`** - it takes `prefix` as an argument, uses it once, and discards it. Both `getattr`s fall to their default, so **every** Engram layer registers under the literal key `"engram"`.

The config has two Engram layers with **different tables** (`engram_layer_ids: [1, 14]`, `engram_num_embeddings: [384006168, 384016682]`). Eager and capture are set-then-call, so they are self-consistent. **Replay is not**: the breakable runner records `fn(weak_ids, "engram", weak_rows)` and resolves the key **at call time**, so every replayed step fills layer 1's staged rows from **layer 14's** table using layer 1's hash ids.

Symptom: correct under eager, wrong under graphs. Under speculative decoding the target distribution is off, so every draft token is rejected and **acceptance collapses to exactly 1.00**.

Fix: key on the `layer_hash_index` that `__init__` *does* store.

## 2. Host-dependent lookup inside capture (blocks FULL_DECODE_ONLY)

`FULL_DECODE_ONLY` bypasses the breakable wrapper entirely - `@eager_break_during_capture` is a no-op when `cudagraph_runtime_mode == FULL` - so the split-op trick that keeps the disk fetch eager under PIECEWISE does not apply, and the host-side D2H lands inside a plain `torch.cuda.graph` capture:

```
RuntimeError: Cannot copy between CPU and CUDA tensors during CUDA graph capture
```

Fix: stage the hash + lookup **eagerly, once per real step**, in `DeepseekV41ModelState.prepare_inputs` (which already runs outside capture and already owns the engram lookback window), and skip it in the forward behind a **static** flag - a per-step flag is evaluated at capture time and would be `False` there. `Engram.staged_rows` is `__init__`-allocated and written in place, so it is address-stable for the captured graph.

Verified parity (eager, `VLLM_ENGRAM_HOIST_CHECK=1`):

```
_ENGHOIST CHECK n=2 equal=True ref=(2, 2, 24) fwd=(2, 2, 24)
```

## 3. Serial NVMe page faults in the row fetch (cold I/O)

`fetch_unique_local_rows` gathers rows one at a time. Measured in-serve: `work_ms` = 5.8 + 5.0 ms/step across the two layers **while the GPU is drained** - ~36 serial page touches per step at ~160 us, one NVMe 4K random read at a time (QD1).

Fix: `posix_fadvise(POSIX_FADV_WILLNEED)` over each row's byte range before the memmap gather, so the kernel submits all reads at once (QD ~36) and the gather waits for the slowest instead of the sum. Hint only - the same bytes come through the same gather, so parity is unchanged by construction. `work_ms` **5.76 -> 0.586** (layer 1), **4.98 -> 0.201** (layer 14), `majflt=0`.

**ABBA cold A/B** (8 never-seen essays, live flag flip on all four nodes):

| arm | ms/step | majflt/step (max node) |
|---|---|---|
| cold **ON** (WILLNEED) | **69.9** | 0.3-0.7 |
| cold **OFF** | **89.1** | 62.6-67.5 |
| warm ON vs OFF (control) | 67.8 vs 67.5 | 0.1 |

**+27.4% on novel text**, faults present only on the OFF rows. Warm/repeat rows are untouched.

## 4. Draft expert weights dropped by the loader's EP pre-filter

The DSpark draft was running with **only 25% of its expert weights loaded**, silently. The loader drops expert weights it considers non-local *before reading them* (`should_skip_weight(name, local_expert_ids)`), and the window comes from `model_config.get_num_experts()` = `n_routed_experts` = **384**. The draft has **128** (`dspark_n_routed_experts`). With EP=4:

| EP rank | filter keeps | draft map owns | owned weights that arrive |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | E in [0, 96) | [0, 32) | **32/32** |
| 1 | E in [96, 192) | [32, 64) | **0/32** |
| 2 | E in [192, 288) | [64, 96) | **0/32** |
| 3 | E in [288, 384) | [96, 128) | **0/32** |

The drop happens **before** `get_tensor`, so the names never reach the draft's load loop: no error, no warning, just missing weights. Post-load probe:

```
LIVECHK TP0_EP0  w13_weight absmax=255.0 nz_rows=32   <- loaded
LIVECHK TP1_EP1  w13_weight absmax=0.0   nz_rows=0    <- empty
LIVECHK TP2_EP2  w13_weight absmax=0.0   nz_rows=0
LIVECHK TP3_EP3  w13_weight absmax=0.0   nz_rows=0
```

Symptom: acceptance is **flat and low across every domain**, and specifically **code is no faster than prose** - the opposite of what a live expert FFN gives, because the drafter degrades to attention + shared experts + the Markov bigram head.

| domain | ctx | before tok/s | after | before acc | after acc |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| code | 0 | 24.12 | **27.02** | 1.72 | **1.89** |
| code | 2k | - | **27.01** | - | **1.92** |
| prose | 0 | 25.07 | **27.44** | 1.76 | **1.97** |
| prose | 2k | - | **30.21** | - | **2.21** |
| structured | 0 | 25.02 | **27.73** | 1.81 | **1.99** |
| structured | 2k | - | **29.70** | - | **2.14** |

Fix: `_EPFILTER` bypasses the pre-read skip for `mtp.*` names (the draft's own expert map still drops non-local ids inside `RoutedExperts.weight_loader`, which is the designed behaviour), plus an `_EPGATE` accounting check that **fails closed** if any owned slot is empty. After the fix all four ranks report 32/32.

**Upstream fix** (the proper one): size the draft load's EP filter from `dspark_n_routed_experts`.

---

## Runtime identity for the numbers above

| | |
|---|---|
| hardware | 4x NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, SM121), TP4 / EP4 |
| kernel | `vllm_exl3_c`, ABI 4, built with `-DP2B_CB=2` from the vllm-exl3 PRs below |
| vllm-exl3 | **#31** (multi-K), **#32** (codebook `P2B_CB`), **#33** (padded). The wheel must be built from **#33**; these kernels are not on `main` yet. |
| model | DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash EXL3 pack |
| engine | `cudagraph_mode: FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, `cudagraph_capture_sizes [3,6,9,12]`, `max-model-len 4096`, prefix caching on |
| spec decode | `method: dspark`, `num_speculative_tokens: 2`, `draft_sample_method: probabilistic`, `rejection_sample_method: block`, `quantization: mxfp4` |
| engram | `VLLM_ENGRAM_DISK_BACKED=1` |
| benchmark | `llm-inference-bench`, sustained 30 s cells, c=1, `max_tokens 512` |

**Restart required.** Every script here patches files that Python binds at import
time. Applying one to an already-running server prints `installed` while the live
process keeps the old code — no error, and the fix appears to do nothing. Apply
before the server starts, or restart it after.

## 5. Large context blocked by flashinfer's persistent topk on SM12x

Booting with a large `max-model-len` fails at **engine init**:

```
RuntimeError: launch_persistent_topk, topk.cu:138, persistent_topk would oversubscribe
and the FilteredTopK fallback requires >=128KB smem per block (have 101376).
total_ctas=90 > num_sms*occupancy=48 (TopK=512, vec_size=4, ctas_per_group=90, smem=48688).
```

flashinfer's `persistent_topk` derives `ctas_per_group` from the **logits stride**, which grows with
context: fixed smem 2,080 B, max chunk `(49,152-2,080)/4 = 11,768` elements,
`CTAs = ceil(1,048,576/11,768) = 90`. On **SM12x the device allows only 99 KiB smem/block**
(`sharedMemPerBlockOptin` = 101,376), so the `FilteredTopK` fallback (>=128 KiB/block) is
unreachable and 90 CTAs do not fit in 48. **Not a memory problem** — the KV pool had 1.9x headroom.

En el admin de producto (`/admin/productos/[id]`) las imágenes solo se podían agregar al final y no había forma de elegir cuál se ve primero en la tienda: ahora las miniaturas se arrastran para definir el orden (`Reorder` de framer-motion, que ya estaba instalado — cero dependencias nuevas) y la primera lleva un badge **Principal**. No hizo falta tocar el modelo de datos ni la API, porque el orden del array `images` ya *es* el orden y todo el front público lee `images[0]` como imagen principal.

Además, subir una imagen no daba ningún feedback más allá del botón pasando a `"..."`: ahora la miniatura aparece al instante con un preview local, cada archivo muestra su progreso real (`uploadBytesResumable`, expuesto como el nuevo helper `uploadFileWithProgress`) y los fallos se ven con un toast, un tile en rojo y un botón para reintentar sin volver a elegir el archivo. Las subidas van en paralelo pero se agregan en el orden en que se eligieron y en una sola llamada, y el array se lee desde una ref para no pisar un reordenamiento hecho mientras algo estaba subiendo.

Verificado con `npx tsc --noEmit` y `pnpm lint` (sin hallazgos en los archivos tocados) y probado a mano por el usuario en local; queda pendiente como deuda preexistente que borrar una imagen no elimina el archivo de Firebase Storage.

author: 0xamlab
body:
## Incident

Sync PR #86 (`sync: mirror from thyn-ai/algenta@dbaf88b`) merged through the merge queue at 2026-09-20 00:29:20Z as 3745dd9 even though its `ts-sdk` CI job had **failed**:

- `ts-sdk` failed on the PR head `fb361900` (check-run started 00:25:14Z).
- `codna review` succeeded at 00:28:29Z; the sync App enqueued the PR at 00:28:30Z; the queue merged it at 00:29:20Z.
- The post-merge `push` run on main, [35478899528](https://github.com/thyn-ai/algenta-sdk/actions/runs/35478899528), failed on `ts-sdk` again (python-sdk and examples-shared green, contract-drift-check skipped).

Root cause: ruleset 20910740 ("branch") requires only `codna review`. The CI and CodeQL jobs were informational, so nothing stopped a red `ts-sdk` from merging.

## Why the trigger has to land before the ruleset change

The fix is to make `python-sdk`, `ts-sdk`, `examples-shared`, `contract-drift-check`, `CodeQL (python)`, `CodeQL (javascript-typescript)` and `CodeQL (actions)` required. But the queue only merges an entry once every required check has reported on the **merge group's own commit**, and neither `ci.yml` nor `codeql.yml` had a `merge_group` trigger — this repository has never run a single `merge_group` workflow (`actions/runs?event=merge_group` returns 0). Requiring them first would have parked every queue entry until `check_response_timeout_minutes` (60) evicted it.

## What changes

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: add `merge_group:` to `on:`. `python-sdk`, `ts-sdk` and `examples-shared` have no event-specific conditions; both Codecov uploads use OIDC with `fail_ci_if_error: false`, so they behave the same on a merge group. `contract-drift-check` stays `pull_request`-only — a merge group carries no `pull_request` payload, so there is no PR author to gate on — and is skipped on `merge_group`, which GitHub counts as a passing required check; the gate already had to pass on the PR before the queue accepted it.
- `.github/workflows/codeql.yml`: add `merge_group: { branches: [main] }`, matching the file's `pull_request` filter. The concurrency group keys on `github.ref`, which is unique per merge-group entry (`refs/heads/gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-N-...`).
- `actionlint` is clean on both files.

## Why `security.yml` is not touched

`.github/workflows/security.yml` is rendered by `thyn-ai/security-toolchain`'s `propagate.py`; a hand edit here would be overwritten on the next propagate. Its `merge_group` trigger is being added in the toolchain template separately, and `full / security gate` is not part of the required-checks set this change enables.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

Once this is on main, ruleset 20910740 gets the seven contexts above added to `required_status_checks` (keeping `codna review`, `strict_required_status_checks_policy: true`, every other rule and the bypass-actor list unchanged), and the next PR through the queue proves the merge-group build runs them.

author: moul
body:
Add the one validator view `/validators` cannot be: a single validator over time.

> **Stacked on #234 → #233 → #231 → #230 → #229.** Base retargets as each merges.

## Smaller than planned, because the page was better than I thought

The plan was to replace `/validators` on the grounds that it renders the valoper registration log rather than the set. That is half true and the half that matters is wrong: the page **already** derives the set from recent block proposers, draws a liveness sparkline per row, and joins gnockpit's power, missed-block and spof columns onto them. The registration table sits below it, not instead of it.

I built the replacement first, saw it duplicate what was there, and took it back out. What is left is what was genuinely missing.

## What this adds

**A per-validator page**, `/validator/<consensus-addr>`, linked from each row of the existing set table:

- power, blocks proposed, share, txs in them, missed blocks, average block time
- the last 50 blocks it proposed, each linking to the block
- a daily share series

**`in_set`**, which separates two cases that otherwise look identical. An address with proposal history that gnockpit no longer lists has **left the set**, and the page says so rather than rendering an active-looking validator. A live member this instance has never seen propose is served too, with zero blocks. An address that is neither is a 404, because an empty page reads as an idle validator.

## The address-space trap, stated

Two disjoint keys travel under the word "validator", and conflating them is a bug this repo has already had (`loadValMonikers` never matched a proposer):

| key | who has it | where it appears |
|---|---|---|
| **consensus** | the node signing blocks | `blocks.proposer_id`, gnockpit |
| **operator** | the account registering the validator | `valoper_registrations` |

Nothing on chain maps one to the other. Everything here is keyed on the consensus address, and the registration table stays its own view. Verified against mainnet on 2026-09-20: all four gnockpit addresses matched the interned proposer addresses exactly, so *that* join does work and is the one used.

## No voting-power timeline, and why

There is no historical validator set stored anywhere, and gnockpit reports only the current one, so a real power timeline is not derivable at any price. `shares` is the observable half of one: each day's blocks split between proposers, so a validator joining or leaving shows up as its share appearing or going to zero. A share rather than a count, because variable block time makes per-day counts incomparable. The page says this in as many words rather than presenting it as the thing it is standing in for.

Also no staking columns. gno has no delegation and its set is governance-assigned, so APR, bonded ratio, commission and a delegator list would be four confident zeros.

## Verification

- `gofmt -l .` clean, `go vet ./...` clean, `go test ./...` **green across every package**.
- New Go coverage: the detail response, newest-first block ordering, a 404 for an address that is neither in the set nor has proposed, the live-and-local merge, a live member with no blocks, and the share series summing to one within a day.
- New Playwright spec: the page, the left-the-set wording, and the link from the set table. Full e2e suite: **118 passed, 16 skipped, 0 failed**, including the two existing specs (`validators`, `identicon`) that my first, larger version had broken.

The gnockpit-dependent tests stub it. They were reaching the real `gnockpit.gno.land` and passing for the wrong reason, which would have made the suite depend on a third party being up and on whatever mainnet's set happened to be.

author: mattias800
body:
Eligible complete compute results can now publish directly into an existing renderer target instead of first becoming a CPU renderer snapshot. The path preserves ordinary guest-memory writeback and alias invalidation. It supports RGBA8 and packed R11G11B10, including GPU seeding for a later R11 partial writer.

Refs #3407. This is a bounded publication/copy reduction, not a completed performance roadmap.

The destination-only lease may pin an invalid renderer image but cannot source-read it. Admission
requires exact full-2D extent, format, mip and layer identity. Authority is revoked before writing
and notification occurs only after successful work, guest writebacks, and alias/metadata checks;
the CPU fallback remains available. Packed R11 uses canonical buffer transfers rather than an
incompatible image-copy format.

## GTA observation

On the GTA Performance Story route, one matched baseline/candidate pair measured the same observed program (`0x9615306ad38ca72a`). Baseline/candidate means were 9.568/6.675 ms dispatch elapsed and 5.800/2.978 ms writeback (n=36/44): observed reductions of 30.2% and 48.7%. GPU-device time rose 2.368 -> 2.722 ms, consistent with the added GPU copy. These are elapsed per-record observations, including waits; F8 does not prove equivalent dispatch dimensions or fixed work, and fresh rendered-frame count is unavailable under GPU presentation. This PR therefore makes no FPS, throughput, or fixed-work speedup claim. The candidate executable is SHA-256 `60b64729f3ba7ad5121fde9c7a2987cd3af48874d67af41958e43a9d924716d7`, built from the same final source; its F8 revision header still says `62a9b2bf3`, so it is not evidence that F8 itself reported `ac57`.

Both captures have zero dropped renderer/compute records. Their frozen route and capture-driver SHA, and normalized effective environment, command line and driver identity, match. Samples with no peers cover the actual F8 intervals (113.732--118.826 s baseline, 113.659--118.779 s candidate; maximum gaps 1.025/1.026 s). The raw wrapper verdicts remain invalid as whole-run artifacts: each has one post-timeout sample naming the measured child PID after `/proc/<pid>/exe` became unavailable, consistent with teardown. That exception is limited to the independently audited F8 intervals above; it does not validate perf stacks, later run time, or the four earlier runs. Those older baseline/candidate/candidate/baseline captures corroborate the direction only and did not continuously watch peers through F8.

Focused private-harness shape:

```sh
python3 "$EVIDENCE/profile_pair_ddb4.py" gta "$LABEL" --root "$WORKTREE" --binary "$BINARY" \
  --duration 140 --attach-at 130 --window 5 --f8-after-ms 112000 \
  --env PROSPER_PAD_SCRIPT_LOG=1 --env PROSPER_CAPTURE_SCREENSHOT_AT_FRAME=2070 --attempts 1
```

The frozen `profile_pair_ddb4.py` driver has the same bytes as the `profile.py` executed for the baseline; later harness fixes are outside this pair. The harness freezes the binary and route, records build IDs, filtered effective environment, driver identity, command line and peer samples. Native scene captures are outside F8 and show the same bank office scene with minor motion differences.

## Validation

- Nine focused GPU tests pass normally and through the strict synchronization scanner. Its deliberate write-after-write control fires. The only known VUIDs remain #1710 07987/08602 and #1715 00715; no unaccounted message was reported.
- `game_compute_rtt_destination_mirror` covers invalid-source refusal, exact destination identity/lifetime, failure revocation, real renderer sampling against a CPU oracle, repeat publication, and packed-R11 partial-write preservation with GPU source-seed activation. The repeated-input fixture did not traverse the cached unchanged-writeback shortcut; that branch is not claimed as covered.
- Disabling destination mirroring makes that fixture fail. Disabling packed-R11 GPU seeding fails the seed-activation assertion even though its small fixture can retain pixel equality via CPU fallback.
- The optional copy probe partitions callers by immutable selected OS TID with cached per-thread IDs. Its controls keep the default report unchanged, separate two threads at one call site, reject malformed or duplicate targets, and expose bounded-table loss; its counts and cycles are attribution, not latency or FPS.
- Blue Prince passes the reviewed fresh-save native-scale Mount Holly hall guard. This is correctness-only evidence, not timing evidence.

```sh
ctest --test-dir "$BUILD" --output-on-failure --no-tests=error -R '^(game_compute_exec|game_compute_exec_no_adaptive_storage_result|game_compute_exec_scratch_poison|game_compute_rtt_destination_mirror|texture_preparation|texture_preparation_control|render_diagnostic_paths|interp_render|rect_synthesis_render)$'
python3 prosper/tools/vkval/vk_validation_scan.py --build-dir "$BUILD" --sync --ctest-arg=-R --ctest-arg='^(game_compute_exec|game_compute_exec_no_adaptive_storage_result|game_compute_exec_scratch_poison|game_compute_rtt_destination_mirror|texture_preparation|texture_preparation_control|render_diagnostic_paths|interp_render|rect_synthesis_render)$'
```

## Sonic comparison

Fresh-save live-renderer runs on frozen main `3cad5468d` and the candidate both reach Cyber Space stage `w6d01`, verified by stage UI and all 100 terrain-sector loads. Native 3840x2160 captures at the same 300-second trigger show legible HUD, cyan horizon and severely incomplete geometry in both arms (stage timers 00:58.85 baseline and 00:56.38 candidate). This establishes that the gross missing-world defect is also present on the baseline; it does not establish correct Sonic rendering or pixel equivalence. No new defect class was observed in this pair. These runs provide visual regression evidence only: they did not collect the optimization-path counters or establish Sonic performance.

Retained evidence: `prosper-evidence/issue-3407-roadmap-20260920/`, including `EVIDENCE.md`, frozen binaries/routes, raw F8 files, peer samples, and native game captures. The umbrella issue remains open.

body:
## 何が食い違っていたか

docs は「`container-compose` を直接叩かず `pnpm run stack:up` で起動してください」と言う一方で、生の `container-compose up -d -b` / `down` を案内している箇所が 4 か所残っていた。stack.sh を通らないと、次の 3 つが渡らない。

- 署名の `--profile signing` と `--env-file signing.env` の対（`.env` の 1 行から導く）
- submodule の版（build 引数。渡らないで建った image は、BrowserHive v9.4.0 から**起動を拒む**）
- 起動の前の点検（道具・DNS ドメイン・submodule）

## 直した 4 か所

| 場所 | 前 | 後 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `docker-compose.yml` 冒頭の使い方 | `container-compose up -d -b` / `down` | `pnpm run stack:up` / `stack:down` ＋ なぜ stack.sh からなのか（3 点）と、例外は `prod-smoke.sh` だけという注記 |
| `docker-compose.yml` capture-fixtures | `container-compose --profile capture-fixtures up -d -b` | `pnpm run stack:up --profile capture-fixtures` |
| `docker-compose.yml` search | `container-compose --profile search up -d -b` | `pnpm run stack:up --profile search` |
| 開発環境のページ ja/en の対応表 | `docker compose up -d --build` → `container-compose up -d -b`（`down` も） | `pnpm run stack:up` / `stack:down`。列の見出しを「このスタックでは」に変え、表の後に理由を 1 段落 |

あわせて、browserhive の build 引数のコメントに「そうして建った image は起動を拒む」を足した（以前は「既定に落ちる」までで止まっていた）。

## 確かめたこと

- `pnpm run check` 全段緑（site の build と doc-ref を含む）
- `git grep` で、案内としての生の compose は 0 件。残るのは `scripts/stack.sh`（実体）と `scripts/prod-smoke.sh`（版の計算だけを共有するもう 1 つの入口）、それに「container-compose には healthcheck が無い」のような説明だけ

author: rodacato
body:
## What

Fix the documented manual database backup, which silently replaced the previous backup with an
empty file, and explain the three parts of the command that keep it from happening again.

## Why

The snippet was:

```bash
sudo -iu shellmer sqlite3 ~/.shellm/shellm.db ".backup '/home/shellmer/shellm-backup.db'"
sudo mv /home/shellmer/shellm-backup.db /var/backups/shellm.db
```

Two defects compose into data loss:

1. **The tilde is expanded by the calling shell, before `sudo` exists.** It resolves to the
   operator's own home, not `shellmer`'s, so the backup cannot open its source and exits 1.
2. **A failed `.backup` still leaves an empty file at the destination**, and the `mv` is on a
   line of its own, so it runs anyway — moving zero bytes over the backup that was already
   there.

What an operator sees is an error, then a successful `mv`. The good copy is gone. This is the
command someone runs at the moment they are about to need it.

The second half was introduced in ad666f7; the tilde predates it and survived that change
because the note added there covers the *other* tilde, the literal one inside the `.backup`
argument.

## How

```bash
sudo -iu shellmer sqlite3 /home/shellmer/.shellm/shellm.db ".backup '/home/shellmer/shellm-backup.db'" &&
  sudo test -s /home/shellmer/shellm-backup.db &&
  sudo -iu shellmer sqlite3 /home/shellmer/shellm-backup.db 'PRAGMA integrity_check' | grep -qx ok &&
  sudo mv /home/shellmer/shellm-backup.db /var/backups/shellm.db
```

- Absolute source path, so the command reads `shellmer`'s database.
- `&&` throughout, so a failed snapshot never reaches the destination.
- **Both** checks, because neither subsumes the other: an empty file is a valid empty SQLite
  database and `integrity_check` answers `ok` for zero bytes, so only `test -s` catches the
  failure above — while `integrity_check` catches a copy of plausible size that cannot be read.
- `sudo test -s` rather than `test -s`, because the operator's own shell may not be able to stat
  inside `shellmer`'s home, and a permission error there would block a perfectly good backup.

The WAL paragraph now carries real numbers instead of "hundreds of kilobytes": on a live install
the `.db` was 86 KB with an mtime six months old while the `-wal` beside it held 3.3 MB. The
point that was missing is that the stale copy looks entirely healthy.

### Verified

- A tilde in `sudo -iu <user> cmd ~/path` expands to the **caller's** home before `sudo` runs —
  reproduced, it yields `/home/<caller>/.shellm/shellm.db`.
- `PRAGMA integrity_check` on a 0-byte file returns `ok`, so the size check is load-bearing and
  not belt-and-braces.
- Old snippet, simulated against a stand-in that fails and leaves 0 bytes: the previous backup
  ends up 0 bytes. New chain, same stand-in: exit 1, previous backup intact. Success path still
  moves the snapshot.
- Swept the rest of the docs: no other snippet passes a tilde through `sudo`, and no other
  follows a fallible command with a destructive one.

## Breaking changes

None — documentation only.

## Checklist

- [x] `npm test` passes locally — unchanged, no code in this diff
- [x] Follows [conventional commit](../CONTRIBUTING.md#commit-messages) format (`feat:`, `fix:`, etc.)
- [x] `CHANGELOG.md` updated if this is a user-facing change
- [x] `docs/openapi.yaml` updated if an endpoint was added or changed — n/a
- [x] `VERSIONS.md` updated if a CLI dependency version changed — n/a
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or credentials in the diff

author: marabi766
body:
Closes #205. The **first commercial admin surface** in the frontend. `apps/web` had no `/admin/commercial` route group, `admin-api.ts` had no commercial namespace, and a grep for "commercial" across the web app returned nothing — so #173's nine merged, tested routes were unreachable from any screen. The nine admin nav entries did not include one. Screen 40, which screen 50's spec says to be consistent with, does not exist in code either. The patterns here are **established rather than followed**, which is why #173's surface is split: this is the read half; the shape-aware editor with its publish and retire dialogs is its own story. ## Three facts kept apart | Fact | What it means | |---|---| | `zero` published | somebody decided to charge nothing | | nothing published | nobody has decided | | the read failed | we do not know | All three collapse into one screen under a reused empty state, and the difference matters: `#43c` depends on the first two being distinguishable, and rendering the third as the second tells an administrator the platform charges nothing when the server never answered. Three sentences, asserted distinct by test, and only the failure offers retry. ## The three components are a constant, not a server list `COMMISSION_COMPONENTS` is closed and **ordered** — ADR-052 §3 allocates a held ceiling across components in exactly that sequence. Deriving the cards from whatever the list route returned would make an unpublished component *vanish* rather than report itself. The page re-declares that vocabulary (and the four shapes, and the two bases) as literal unions rather than pulling a server package into the browser bundle. A test asserts the two still agree **against the real contract**, so the duplication cannot drift silently. ## Rendering reads the shape first `zero` shows no fields, `fixed` shows no base, `percentage` shows no amount. Reading `ruleKind` rather than printing whichever fields happen to be non-null is what stops a future response with a stray field from being rendered as though it belonged. No rate, amount or base is ever proposed by the UI — the test asserts an unpublished surface contains **no digit in either numeral system**, and none of the words that would imply an incident. ## Two structural decisions - **Presentation split into `commission-policy-view.tsx`**, the way `funds-by-state.tsx` is split from `finance-workspace.tsx`: the page owns fetching and which read failed, the component owns what each state looks like. That split is what let the rendering be checked in a browser against fixed data — no session, API or database. - **The nav entry is capability-gated** on `bc_manage_commercial_plans`, so an operator without it is never offered a route they cannot open. ## What the browser caught that jsdom could not The timeline's `` inherited the table's `min-width: 520px` and was clipped by its own horizontal scroll container at 390px — a sentence the reader could only finish by scrolling sideways. It is now a `

` outside the container, associated by `aria-describedby`, with the heading as `aria-labelledby`. (Screen 50 §8 asks for a real `` with ``; it does not require a caption.) | | | |---|---| | New tests | 8 | | Web suite | **20/20 suites, 318/318 tests** | | Typecheck / lint | clean | 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: tomasruizr
body:
Plugin **0.99.0 → 0.99.1**, marketplace metadata 0.48.0 → 0.48.1.

Three fleets were driven end to end on shipped 0.99.0 — the first real executions of the wave yield. Each defect below was found by running them, not by review, and none is visible to any gate in this repo: `/verify-build` could not certify the orchestrator half of the yield because it is pinned by presence-greps rather than behaviour, and this is exactly the blind spot it named.

## The four fixes

1. **`scripts/fleet-loop.py` — a `--run` path that does not exist is no longer reported as contract drift.** GH-429 removed the unconditional refusal on a missing `run.yaml` (a fresh run legitimately has none before its first tick writes one) and nothing replaced it as an operator-error detector, so a typo or the wrong working directory ticked a whole orchestrator and then reported `still records no pluginVersion`. Observed against a lane worktree with no `.work/multi` at all. One `os.path.isdir`, in the post-tick branch — checking up front is the refusal that broke every fresh run, which is why the fresh-run case is untouched.
2. **The driver's docstring now carries `CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS=0` on the `--tick` invocation.** A tick runs until every unit of its wave is terminal — hours — while print mode terminates background tasks after 600 s, so without it the orchestrator is killed before step 8, never prints `FLEET-STEP:v1`, and the driver correctly reads the absence as `infra`. A truncated tick is indistinguishable from a failed one. Confirmed working on the `multi-XL-56…` fleet, where two units reached `passed` inside one long tick.
3. **Tick-boundary precondition 5: the verdict is blocking.** It said print it last; it did not forbid deferring it to a notification, and in print mode a turn that ends *is* the tick ending, so nothing arrives. Observed on the RAI fleet: the tick merged its unit, wrote its bookkeeping, marked it terminal — then said it would be notified when the background gate finished, and stopped. The env var of (2) does not help; the model chose to stop rather than being cut off.
4. **Tick-boundary precondition 1 extends to the orchestrator's own commits.** It covered lane branches; the integration merge is the orchestrator's own work and fell outside it, so a tick could end with `int/` merged locally and unpushed. Observed on RAI: 12 unpushed commits, `origin/int` a whole wave behind. Subject to the existing rule that a red gate is never pushed as a fetchable base.

**ADR-012's ceilings are unmoved.** The companion absorbed (3) and (4) and came back to **796 words against its 800 ceiling** by compressing elsewhere in the same file; `commands/start-multi.md` is untouched at **3,383/3,400**. (2) lives in the driver's docstring, where the `--tick` command is documented and where there is no ceiling. D39's objection to raising a ceiling therefore does not arise.

## Gates run

`sh .claude/gate.sh` — **SCOPED**, the default — **GATE: PASS**, no FAIL and no INCONCLUSIVE. CI is disabled repo-wide, so this is the only evidence that exists. Named blind spot: a scoped run certifies this diff and its importers, not the repo; the census and ratchet guards that glob the tree ran or SKIPped per their declared surface, and no whole-repo `--full` was run (and none is claimed).

`scripts/test-fleet-loop.sh` gains a missing-run-dir scenario pinning fix (1): it asserts the refusal names the run directory and points at `--run`, and asserts it does **not** say `still records no pluginVersion`. Verified **red alone** — 3 failures with the driver reverted — and green with the fix; 54 pass. `scripts/test-flow-seams.sh` is 546/546: two of its literals over the companion were broken by the first compression pass and restored, which is the pin doing its job.

## Found by the same runs, NOT fixed here — each needs its own decision

- **`run-metrics`' `agents.yaml` reader accepts only top-level `lanes:` / `provisioners:` / `serial:` with inline flow-mapping rows.** `agents:` is ignored entirely, so a run keyed that way reports `Run cost: not measured`. Measured 2026-09-19 against 0.99.0's reader: `multi-XL-56…`, `multi-ESAS-93-94`, `multi-ESAS-225-228` and the teselly3 runs are invisible to it; `multi-RAI-34…` and `multi-ESAS-211…` are read. A one-line rename per run, deliberately not done without the owner's word.
- **`grep` over `scripts/run-metrics.mjs` is a silent false negative.** The file holds a deliberate NUL byte (`${role}\x00${cls}`), so grep calls it binary and prints nothing at exit 0. Use `grep -a`. This already cost one `/plan` a wrong premise ("there is no `--fleet` code"; there are 43 `fleet` matches and a real `readAgentsYaml`).
- **The plugin's `bin/` is on `PATH` only inside Claude Code's own Bash environment.** A plain shell must invoke the driver by absolute path, `~/.claude/plugins/cache/bett3r-ai-workflow/bett3r-ai-workflow/<version>/bin/fleet-loop` — a path that contains the version and so breaks on every release, this one included.
- **`claude -p` auto-denies every tool call that is not pre-allowlisted, silently.** It is a permissions failure, not a credentials one: a correct `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot make a denied `Bash(git:*)` succeed. The esas sandbox container has zero `permissions.allow` rules, which is why its orchestrator lost `git`, `ps` and `find` and refused to dispatch — and an orchestrator that refuses for lack of `ps` is behaving correctly: that run's own `duplicateLaneIncident` came from re-dispatching a live lane on transcript-mtime evidence.
- **The three eval scenarios guarding the new `reference/` companions remain `_calibration: UNVALIDATED`.** `check-eval-coverage.py` proves a guarding scenario exists and runs no session; whether the pointer is opened is `run-behavioral-eval.py`, which is manual and costs money. 1,760 words of normative rules — now slightly more — still sit behind pointers with nothing proving a reader follows them. This patch does not change that, and fix (3) adds to what is unproven.

`.work/learnings.md` still holds an undrained GH-429 buffer (the `design-map` / `work-docs-path` disagreement over GitHub-issue work items); it is preserved, not processed here.

author: csuzngjh
body:
## Owner Review Card（agent 填）

### 1. Problem

旧开发安装链（`scripts/install.mjs` → `packages/openclaw-plugin/scripts/sync-plugin.mjs`）会把开发构建写进**正式安装面**。2026-09-20 只读复核（8/8 结论成立，`docs/audit/install-mjs-dev-prod-isolation-review-20260920.md`）实证两条写穿路径：EPERM 后"原位覆盖"留下混合树；`sync-plugin.mjs:879-901` 对插件内 junction 先 `realpathSync` 解析、再删除并覆盖**真实目标**（本机 3 个链接全部指向 `~/.pd/runtime/{core,host-runtime}`）。同族风险已造成实际损害：本机 2.1.0 于 09-19/20 被 npm 安装器三连盖回 1.74.1（gen21/22/23）。

---

### 2. Before

两个脚本可被任何参数组合（含 --force/--dev）直接执行：先删后装、删除失败原位覆盖、junction 解析后写穿 `~/.pd/runtime`、写正式 `openclaw.json`/`installs.json`、杀 18789 端口进程并 schtasks 启动正式 "OpenClaw Gateway" 计划任务、对正式 workspace 跑规则脚本。旧测试仅对源码文本做静态断言，不执行脚本。

---

### 3. After

两个脚本的 `main()` 第一语句（任何 IO/子进程之前）无条件拒绝执行：输出弃用原因 + 三个正确入口（安装/修复=npx create-principles-disciple；更新=Console 更新页；开发验证=worktree 源码运行）→ exit 1；`--help` 显示同一说明后 exit 0。**无参数可绕过**；旧函数体原样保留但不可达（可 git revert 回滚）。测试重写为真实边界契约：重定向 HOME 下 spawn 两脚本 × 全部已知参数组合，断言退出码、弃用文案、哨兵零写入。

---

### 4. Existing mechanism reused

弃用守卫沿用仓库"死 flag 墓碑"式的可解释退役模式（PRI-751 先例）；开发验证替代路径复用现行 worktree 纪律（git-1/10/11/13）；错误落册复用 structured records 权威（PRI-799 Phase C，`npm run error:record`）。

---

### 5. Complexity Delta

* New durable source of truth: NO
* New persisted schema/state: NO
* New subsystem/service/background process: NO
* New public abstraction/interface: NO
* New runtime feature flag: NO
* New cross-package dependency: NO
* New host/platform-specific behavior: NO
* New external/network capability: NO

纯行为移除 + 测试 + 文档；打包副本无需改动（`bundle-plugin.mjs:84-88` 已剔除 scripts 目录）。

---

### 6. Verification

* 新契约测试 `tests/sync-plugin-installation-truth.test.js`：21/21 PASS（19 组拒绝用例含零写入哨兵[顶层文件名+内容] + 2 组 --help），已接入 CI `test-scripts` 作业与 `verify:merge`（`test:guard-contracts`）。
* `npm run check:error-handbook` OK（97 active patterns，ERR-137 已映射 EP-12）。
* `npm run verify:merge`：见 Merge gate 一节。
* Linear PRI-868 已 In Progress，PR 建立后 handoff → In Review。

---

### 7. Risk

* 完全无逃生门是有意设计（专家方案要求 --force 也不可绕过）；紧急恢复 = `git revert` 本 PR 的守卫提交。
* 打包内嵌 `plugin/package.json` 仍含同名 npm script 文本，但 scripts 目录不随包发布，执行会自然失败——无害残留。
* npm 安装器当更新的回退通道本 PR 不解决（PRI-869 跟进：npx 不再捆绑 1.74.1）。

---

### 8. Rollback / recovery

`git revert` 守卫提交即恢复原行为（向后兼容回退，无 schema/flag 涉及）。

---

### 9. Follow-ups

* PRI-869：npm 安装器版本线对齐核验（治本回退通道）。
* PRI-870：本机恢复 2.1.0 运营单（等 PRI-868/869 完成 + Owner 授权窗口）。
* PRI-871/872/873：开发验证三层流程与同机隔离设施（审计文档 §5-8）。

---

---

## 产品意图（agent 填，Owner 确认）

* 对应 Linear issue: PRI-868
* 解决的产品问题（一句话）: 旧开发安装链会写穿正式安装面导致产品损坏与版本回退，本 PR 使其在任何副作用之前零副作用拒绝。
* 工单状态对账（AGENTS.md §21 rules 9–11）: PRI-868 由本 PR 实质解决——PR 创建后执行 `handoff` 置 In Review 并附证据评论；已搜索 Linear（install.mjs/sync-plugin/隔离/版本权威关键词），无其他在办工单覆盖本范围（PRI-849 已 Done 不含停用范围）。

### 是否触及产品边界

* [x] 否

说明：纯工程防护 + 文档，不改产品行为面（正式安装/更新链不受影响）。

---

### MVP Questions

#### `mvp-q-1-what-if-skip`

不做则旧脚本继续可执行：本机已被实证三次回退（2.1.0→1.74.1），且 junction 写穿可在一次 EPERM 后损坏正式 runtime。当前值得处理（P1）。

---

#### `mvp-q-2-how-observed`

运行任一脚本（任意参数）立即输出弃用说明并 exit 1（未知参数同样 exit 1，仅显式 --help exit 0）；契约测试（21 用例）已接入 CI `test-scripts` 作业与 `verify:merge` 保护该行为；`--help` 显示正确入口。

---

#### `mvp-q-3-how-disabled`

* [x] backward-compatible revert

说明：`git revert` 守卫提交即可恢复原行为；无 flag 涉及。

---

> 新 feature flag 不是默认答案。只有独立 runtime disable 能提供真实风险控制时才新增。

#### `mvp-q-4-emotional-value`

* [x] N/A — internal engineering change

---

---

## 变更概览（agent 填）

### 变更类型

* [x] 🔒 Security / safety
* [x] 🧪 测试
* [x] 📝 文档

author: remcostoeten
body:
Closes #392

Backend-ranked full-text search and saved searches on mobile, entirely inside the owned path `mobile/src/features/search`.

## What changed

**Search.** `search-runner.ts` plans a query and answers it. The plan resolves `#tag`, `$person`, `tag:` and `person:` operators against the hydrated store into a candidate set and strips them from the free text; storage gets the text plus the candidate ids through `bridge.searchWorkspace` and does the ranking. Nothing re-scores on the client — a filter-only query never reaches the backend at all (there is nothing to rank), and an unresolved or ambiguous name blocks the query with its problem instead of answering a different one. A response for a query the field has moved past resolves to `null` and is dropped.

**Surface.** `search-screen.tsx` is the field, the saved-query chips, the index line, the problems and the ranked list. Opening a hit calls `activateNote` in the press handler, so the note is active in the same frame; snippets keep the `<mark>` runs storage produced. Every control is ≥44 pt with a role and a label (R-Q2).

**Saved searches.** `saved-searches.ts` reads and writes `settings.savedSearches` — the same key and the same bounds (1–512 characters, 100 entries) the desktop sidebar uses — through `update_settings`, so a workspace saved on one interface reads back on the other. A corrupt preference costs the chips, not the frame.

**Index status.** `index-status.ts` reconciles the rebuildable projection after the first paint, publishing `rebuilding` while it happens and `unavailable` with the runtime's own message when the command surface refuses it. Nothing on the navigation path waits for it (R-P1).

**Copied modules.** `query-parser.ts`, `filter-resolution.ts`, `search-plan.ts` and `snippet.ts` are copies of `app/src/features/search/*`. That grammar was never extracted to `shared/renderer-core` and `app/` is outside this issue's owned paths, so mobile carries a copy guarded by `__tests__/desktop-parity.test.cts`: it compares each file against the desktop original (doc comments and import paths normalised) and runs both parsers over a 20-query corpus. See the [issue comment](https://github.com/remcostoeten/skriuw/issues/392#issuecomment-5746467347) for the extraction that removes them.

## Checks

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `./scripts/check-mobile.sh` | passed (lockfile, `tsc --noEmit`, `tsc --noEmit --project __tests__`, unit tests) |
| `bunx tsc --noEmit --project src/features/search/__tests__` | passed |
| `bunx tsx --test 'src/features/search/__tests__/*.test.cts'` | 37 passed, 0 failed |
| `bunx expo export:embed --platform android` | bundled, 1,719 modules |
| `./gradlew app:assembleRelease` (x86_64) | built, 47 MB APK |
| `e2e/run-android.sh` install and probe | **blocked**, see below |

Re-run the suite with `bun --cwd=mobile x tsx --test 'src/features/search/__tests__/*.test.cts'`.

**Query-to-results over the 1,000-note fixture, on the host against the in-memory adapter:** p50 0.0 ms, p95 1.0 ms, max 3.0 ms over 30 samples (6 queries × 5 rounds). `__tests__/query-latency.test.cts` prints this on every run and fails over a 500 ms ceiling, so a quadratic regression in the plan trips the gate.

## Unverified

- **iOS unverified.** Not built, not simulated; Linux cannot do either.
- **The emulator run did not complete.** `e2e/run-android.sh` got through `expo prebuild`, the Metro bundle and the release APK, then `adb install` failed with `Requested internal only, but not enough space` — the local AVD's `/data` is 96% full, and the host disk has 1.6 GB free of 911 GB, so the emulator will not boot with a larger partition either. Freeing host space (`~/.android/avd/ExpoAVD.avd.bak` alone is 10 GB) or recreating the AVD with `disk-size: 6000M` the way `mobile-ci.yml` does should be all it needs. **No device number for query-to-results is recorded.**
- **The recorded P95 is a floor, not the product number.** `mobile/src/bridge/native-adapter.ts` still refuses `searchWorkspace`, `searchIndexStatus` and `rebuildSearchIndex` because `crates/skriuw-mobile` does not expose them, so this feature runs on `createMemoryBridge` as the spec's work breakdown intends. The measurement covers the plan, the command round trip and the filter intersection — not SQLite FTS ranking. It has to be re-taken once the facade carries search.
- **Nothing mounts `SearchScreen` yet.** The shell has no search route or destination and `mobile/app`/`mobile/src/shell` are Mobile 07's paths. Described in the issue comment with the exact changes needed.
- **The gate does not run this suite.** `mobile/package.json`'s `test` and `typecheck` scripts cover `__tests__/*.test.ts` only, so the `.cts` suites from Mobile 07, Mobile 08 and this PR run nowhere in CI. Also in the issue comment, with the two script lines that fix it.
- **The React surface has no render test.** There is no RN test renderer in the workspace; `search-screen.tsx`, `search-result-row.tsx` and `saved-search-bar.tsx` are covered by typecheck and by the Metro bundle only. Their model — the runner, the plan, saved searches, the index — is covered by the 37 unit tests.
- The pre-commit hook (`cd v1 && bun lint-staged`) was bypassed: `v1/` is outside the bun workspace and has no `node_modules` in this worktree, so it fails on `Script not found "lint-staged"` regardless of the change.

## Summary by Sourcery

Add the mobile search experience with backend-ranked results, workspace filters, saved searches, and rebuildable index status.

New Features:
- Add mobile full-text search with tag and person filters, backend ranking, snippets, saved queries, and index status feedback.

Enhancements:
- Keep mobile search behavior aligned with the desktop parser, filter resolution, search planning, and snippet formatting.
- Provide responsive search behavior that ignores stale results, activates selected notes immediately, and avoids blocking navigation on index maintenance.
- Add accessible search controls and result presentation for the mobile surface.

Tests:
- Add parity, search planning, runner, saved-search, index reconciliation, and 1,000-note latency coverage, including an Android probe.

Chores:
- Carry the search feature within the mobile-owned path until the shared extraction is available.

body:
## Two numbers that were not what they said

`run-helper-suites.py` exists because `run-repo-guards.py`'s globs do not match `*_test.py`, so twelve suites could break with CI green (#896). It drives them.

**It refused only when the total was zero.** One suite losing every case — a class renamed, an import guard that stops being satisfied — lowers a number nobody reads and passes. That is the shape of a guard that checks nothing, sitting inside the drive written to close exactly that gap.

**And the total was not the number of cases.** `logic_bounce_test.py` imports three `TestCase` classes from its neighbours to re-export them, and `unittest` discovery loads a class wherever it finds it. 32 cases were being run — and counted — twice: `167 case(s) pass` over **135** distinct ones.

## What changed

- Cases are grouped by the module that **defines** them, so an aggregator re-exporting a class cannot hide a loss somewhere else.
- `Scripts/helper-suite-cases.json` carries a **floor per suite**. Below it, undeclared, or declared-and-not-found each refuse. Growing is free; lowering one belongs in the diff with the reason.
- An empty or unreadable floor file is **refused**, not passed — otherwise the rule evaporates the moment its input does.
- The suite that runs is the deduplicated one: **135 cases in 30s** instead of 167.

## Evidence

```
135 distinct case(s) pass across 11 *_test.py suite(s) the runner does not discover,
each at or above its committed floor
```

Seven new cases in `Scripts/test_helper_suite_floors.py`, driven against fixture directories so they run anywhere — the real suites compile Swift and import AppKit, which is why the runner does not discover them:

- a tree at its floors passes (**the control**)
- a suite that lost a case → exit 1
- one suite of two vanishing entirely → exit 1 (`discovery found NONE of it`)
- an undeclared suite → exit 1
- an empty floor file → exit 1
- a re-exported class counted **once**, under the module that defines it (`Ran 2 tests`, not 4)
- every real `*_test.py` that defines cases is declared

`python3 Scripts/run-repo-guards.py` → `all 72 passed`.

## Ruled out

Renaming the twelve to `test_*.py` so the runner discovers them — #896's end state. It makes the guards job platform-dependent: `logic_key_event_test.py` compiles Swift that imports AppKit and the guards job runs on ubuntu. That rename needs the job split first.

## Where the floors live

Beside the drive, not in `docs/canon/` with this repository's other ratchets. That prefix is Logic-facing, so a change touching anything under it must cite a row of Apple's data in its pull request body. This file counts test cases and rests on no such row — putting it there would make every future edit manufacture a citation, which is exactly what the citation rule exists to stop.

This pull request body states no fact about Logic: every number in it counts test cases in this repository's own helper suites.
