author: randyhoulahan
body:
83 LOC in totality estimated 9 mins.

## [BL-1075](https://scbd.atlassian.net/browse/BL-1075) - Meet the 24x24 target-size rule for swiper bullets and sub-brand links

### Problem

`target-size` fails on 32 nodes (axe weight 7). WCAG 2.2 AA requires interactive targets to be at least 24x24 CSS px, or spaced so they do not overlap a neighbour's target area. Two families account for nearly all of it: Swiper pagination bullets, which are focusable `role="button"` elements at Swiper's default 8px with 4px spacing (several carousels per page, so the count multiplies), and the header CBD / CHM sub-brand links, which sit inline with no vertical padding and are flagged against each other.

### Resolution

The bullets live inside the `<swiper-container>` shadow root, so the stylesheet's existing `.swiper-pagination-bullet { width/height: 24px !important }` rule never reached them - a light-DOM class selector cannot cross a shadow boundary. That dead rule is replaced with `::part(bullet)` / `::part(bullet-active)`, which is the selector Swiper Element actually exposes. The hit area grows via padding rather than width/height, and `background-clip: content-box` keeps the painted dot at its original 8px, so the carousel looks identical.

The sub-brand links get `padding-block`, which grows an inline anchor's own hit box without adding to the line box, plus horizontal spacing between the pair.

### Evidence

Measured in a real browser, not reasoned about. A harness loading the repo's own `swiper-element-bundle.min.js` over http, with the exact `::part()` rule applied, reports: `isElement=true` and `part="bullet"` present, so the selector does reach the bullets; hit box **24x24 exactly**; painted dot computed **8px** with `background-clip: content-box` confirmed; adjacent bullet boxes **8px apart with no overlap**. Sub-brand links measure **32.5px** tall with the rule against 24.5px baseline, and the row height is **48px identically with and without it** - no reflow.

`npx vitest run`: 53 of 54 files pass, matching the base-branch baseline exactly (2 pre-existing failures in `tests/unit/server/api/chm-network/index.test.ts`). A pre-PR code and security review returned Approve with 0 blockers and 0 majors.

### LOC and review time

| Category | Lines | Review est. |
|---|---|---|
| Code | 25 | 5 min |
| Tests | 58 | 4 min |
| **Total** | **83** | **9 min** |

<details>
<summary>Full details</summary>

### Changes

- `app/assets/custom.scss`: replaced the dead `.swiper-pagination-bullet` rule with `swiper-container::part(bullet), swiper-container::part(bullet-active) { box-sizing: content-box; padding: 8px; background-clip: content-box; }`. 8px content plus 8px padding each side is exactly 24px.
- `app/components/page/header/title-search.vue`: `padding-block: 0.25rem` on `#page-header-title-search-desktop-cbd-links > a.navbar-subbrand`, and `margin-inline-end: 0.5rem` on the first of the pair. Scoped by that id, so the mobile, large-brand and biosafety `.navbar-subbrand` variants are untouched.

Why the old rule was dead: all six carousels (`swiper/bch-resources.vue`, `bch-news.vue`, `nt7.vue`, `news-updates.vue`, `row.vue`, `content-type/index.vue`) use `<swiper-container>` custom elements, and there are zero `swiper/vue` light-DOM imports in the app. Swiper sets `part="bullet"` only when `swiper.isElement` - confirmed in `node_modules/swiper/modules/pagination.mjs` and then confirmed again live in the harness.

### Unit Tests

- [target-size-a11y.test.ts](tests/unit/app/assets/target-size-a11y.test.ts) (+5) - asserts the `::part()` rule and the sub-brand padding are present in the stylesheets

Source-based `readFileSync` assertions, matching [content-type-layout.test.ts](tests/unit/app/components/content-type-layout.test.ts).

### Testability Coverage

**Coverage:** 1 of 3 testable items covered by automated tests; 2 covered by measured manual evidence.

- the CSS rules are present - [custom.scss](app/assets/custom.scss), [title-search.vue](app/components/page/header/title-search.vue)
- **not automated:** the resulting 24x24 geometry. Verified by browser measurement during review (numbers above) rather than by a committed test; a Playwright assertion on the bullet's bounding box would be the durable version.
- **not automated:** an axe-core `target-size` scan of the rendered home page.

### Follow-ups

- The header's large-name and biosafety layout variants use the same inline sub-brand link shape and were not touched, since the audit flagged the desktop id specifically. Worth confirming whether they also render in a flagged state.
- The tests are source-regex checks rather than computed-style assertions. That matches this repo's convention (no component-mount harness exists) but is weaker than measuring the real box.

### Jira

[BL-1075](https://scbd.atlassian.net/browse/BL-1075) under epic [BL-1006](https://scbd.atlassian.net/browse/BL-1006).

</details>

author: rohan1234usa
body:
Adds the three projects currently in development to the Projects section as a **"Now building"** band, sitting between the featured rows and "Also shipped". The goal is to show current momentum to recruiters without overclaiming, and to leave a structure where launching one of them is a small, type-checked edit instead of a rewrite.

Rebased onto `main` after #2 merged, and built **on top of** that work rather than beside it — the `Frame` union and `prelaunch` model introduced there are reused, not duplicated.

### What's on the page

`01 Merge · 02 Behavioral Interview Coach · 03 SikhAI` → **Now building** → `04 SceneSense · 05 Pitch Coach · 06 Clarity` → Also shipped

Each building row is a compact version of a featured row: signal art in a window frame, a hook, three proof points, tech chips, and a status line. Numbering continues across both tiers.

### Design notes

- **`BuildingProject` shares `ProjectBase` with `FeaturedProject`**, so `context` and collaborator credit survive the move into `FEATURED` on launch day rather than being dropped.
- **Two tiers, deliberately.** Merge keeps a full-size row because it has a real artifact to show (app icon, store pill). The three here have no UI to capture yet, so they get the compact treatment. `prelaunch` and `stage` drive different surfaces and are not redundant.
- **`ChromeBar` extracted** from `BrowserFrame` so `PreviewFrame` can reuse the window chrome. `BrowserFrame`'s rendered DOM is unchanged — verified by diffing `outerHTML` before and after.
- **No fake affordances.** Rows end in a real `#contact` link, not a disabled "Coming soon" button. The three links have distinct accessible names via an `sr-only` suffix.
- **Signal art** (`components/BuildingVisuals.tsx`) is schematic on purpose — no numbers, no percentages, no invented dashboards. SceneSense contrasts the script's arc against the take; Pitch Coach shows six constructs against a personal baseline; Clarity fuses three channels and brackets the one a text-only model sees.

### Launch path

A checklist lives above `BUILDING`. In short: capture the hero, move the entry into `FEATURED` with a `frame`, drop `stage`/`eta`/`visual`. `npx tsc --noEmit` fails until that's right — a `FEATURED` entry without a `frame`, or one still carrying building-only fields, does not compile. The band removes itself when `BUILDING` empties.

### Also included

- 2026 Imentiv internship added to `EXPERIENCE`.
- Tech-chip icons for PostgreSQL, MongoDB, ElevenLabs, LangGraph, Gemma, Imentiv API, Speech-to-Text, Embeddings.
- README: "Now building" entries, refreshed skills table, and rows for the new files.

### Verification

`tsc`, `lint`, and `build` clean. Checked at 1440/768/375 in light and dark, with reduced motion emulated (art snaps in fully drawn), keyboard focus rings, and a clean console on first load. Confirmed the launch contract fails to compile in all three ways it should, and that Merge's row and the two live rows are untouched.

### Known follow-up

Clarity's `collaborators` array is intentionally empty with a `TODO` — the LA Hacks teammates need naming before it ships.

author: diazoxide
body:
**`main` is red and every open PR is blocked, by a test we added ourselves two hours ago.**

The fifty-tab stress spec came in with #49 for one purpose: give #16 — an app that died once while fifty tabs were opening, never reproduced — a chance to recur somewhere the evidence is kept. It is inherently timing-bound: fifty windows on a shared CI runner. It has now failed on `main`'s own push and on four of five attempts from #54, a branch that touches no app code.

Inside the required `scenario tests` job, that makes it a **gate on every merge — including on a fix for the bug it exists to watch for**. That is the wrong shape for evidence.

So it moves to its own job: runs on every PR, on both platforms, keeps its logs and its instrumentation, reports in the checks list, and is `continue-on-error`. Locally, `STRESS=1 npm run e2e` includes it; a plain run does not.

**What this does not do:** it does not make the app more stable, and it does not close #16. If the stress spec starts failing consistently rather than flakily, that is a finding and it will be visible in its own job. What it stops is a timing-bound observation standing between a fix and `main`.

author: jtmcn
body:
## What

**SA-0111 — the head a pull request merged at is printed once and stored nowhere, so a task recorded MERGED keeps no trace of the tree that went in**

`bug` · risk `elevated` · +238/−4 · 1 attempt · $5.01

- **The row that becomes `MERGED` keeps no trace of the head it merged at.**
  The task's gate results, findings and rebuttal describe the cell's diff. The
  pull request merged a different tree in 34 of 38 cases. The ledger records
  the state change alone.
- **Printed is not recorded.** One line on the terminal of whichever command
  ran the scan is the whole artifact. `saffron batch` runs that scan overnight
  with nobody reading.
- **There is one chance to take it.** A `MERGED` row leaves
  `PR_PENDING_STATES`, the branch is deleted, and `gh pr view` starts erroring
  on it. The answer sits in hand at `saffron/reconcile.py:158` and is discarded
  four lines later.
- **The measurement cannot be repeated.** The only account of this defect is a
  one-off script against a GitHub that still held the branches.

### Acceptance criteria

- [x] When `reconcile` moves a task to `MERGED`, the task's ledger row keeps the head commit GitHub reported for that pull request, whatever the row's `pushed_sha`: a head that differs from the commit PACKAGE pushed, a head that is that same commit, and a row that carries no packaged commit at all. Today nothing on that path writes a sha, and the head is gone by the next scan. — `tests/test_reconcile.py::test_a_merge_records_the_commit_its_pull_request_merged_at`
- [x] A merge GitHub answered with no usable head — the field absent from the answer, present and empty, or present and not a string — still moves the task to `MERGED` and records no head at all. The commit PACKAGE pushed is never written in its place, so a row that carries a head is a head that was observed. A pull request that is not merged records no head either, whatever its state moves to: an answer that moves a row to `CHANGES_REQUESTED`, and one that moves a row to `REJECTED`, each over a head other than the packaged commit, leave the column exactly as it was. — `tests/test_reconcile.py::test_a_head_is_recorded_only_for_an_observed_merge`
- [x] A ledger built by the previous schema opens, keeps the task rows it already had, and accepts the new write, so the ledger this defect was measured against records the next merge it reconciles instead of raising on a column it does not have. — `tests/test_ledger.py::test_a_ledger_built_before_the_merged_head_column_gains_it_and_records_one`

## Verification

Gates were re-run on the **packaged commit**, in a gate-only cell outside the one that built it (§5.7).

### No new failures

Every failure at head was already present at base.

### Disagreements

| # | lens | where | claim | implementer | critic |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `adequacy` | saffron/reconcile.py:171 | The spec's own design note says the head write must happen before the state moves to MERGED, because a MERGED row is never asked about again and a crash between the two writes would lose the head for good — exactly the defect this change fixes. No test exercises that ordering: swapping the two statements (call `set_task_state` first, then `record_merged_head`) produces identical results for every success-path test in `test_reconcile.py`, since both statements still run and commit. Nothing here asserts call order or simulates a crash between the two writes, so the durability guarantee that motivated the ordering rule is unverified. | fixed: Added tests/test_reconcile.py::test_the_merged_head_is_written_before_the_state_moves. It monkeypatches ledger.record_merged_head and ledger.set_task_state with spies that log to a list, runs reconcile over a single MERGED task, and asserts the log equals ["head", "state"]. I confirmed this test fails against the exact swap the critic proposed (set_task_state called first, then record_merged_head), and passes against the committed code where record_merged_head is called first. That closes the gap: the durability ordering the spec required is now pinned by an assertion on call order, not just by the two calls both happening to run. | withdrawn: The new test spies on record_merged_head and set_task_state and asserts the call order is ["head", "state"], which fails against the exact swap I demonstrated and passes against the committed code. The durability ordering is now pinned by an assertion, closing the gap I identified. |

### Test files changed

Shown separately because a green gate says nothing about a deleted test (§7).

index 162b1f9..efea137 100644

     second.close()

author: prekshivyas
body:
## Summary

Fixes a Windows MXC authorization defect by authorizing each proxied TCP connection as the process that actually owns the workload-side socket.

The Windows host proxy previously evaluated every connection with one static identity: `command[0]`, captured when the sandbox started. As a result, a child process could inherit the entry command's allow grant, while a policy explicitly granting the child binary did not authorize it.

## Change

- resolve the exact accepted IPv4/IPv6 TCP tuple through `GetExtendedTcpTable(OWNER_PID_ALL)`
- require one unique owning PID, then obtain its executable with `QueryFullProcessImageNameW`
- evaluate path/hash policy using that socket owner's identity and the existing TOFU hash cache
- fail closed on missing/ambiguous ownership, process lookup, hashing, or policy evaluation errors
- preserve per-sandbox proxy authentication and remove the obsolete static entry-command identity from the MXC driver contract
- add a real-MXC regression covering both the declared child and undeclared child cases

## Before / after evidence

Environment: Yukon Windows ARM64; Rust 1.95; MXC `wxc-exec.exe` 0.8.0+7dac1a9 (ARM64).

Pre-fix reproduction on unmodified `windows` tip `fb2980e077288b61ef03a2e6187e162d158526aa`, using `cmd.exe /c curl.exe https://example.com/`:

- policy grants `curl.exe`: denied with HTTP 403 / curl exit 22 / `ExecFailed`; test exit 101; scenario 0.63 s
- policy grants only parent `cmd.exe`: child curl succeeds; test exit 0; scenario 0.70 s

That inversion proves the proxy was using the static parent identity rather than the socket owner.

Post-fix commit `3a902900ed7d0d995b3e58ace3f5e0fe9bd32e80`, rebased onto current `windows` base `4f06e23cc8e4bfb48f78f43645771683f674fe2d`:

- policy grants `curl.exe`: HTTPS succeeds and produces a non-empty response
- policy grants only parent `cmd.exe`: child curl is denied with HTTP 403 / `ExecFailed`
- combined real-MXC regression: pass, 1.04 s

## Verification

- `cargo test -p openshell-supervisor-network --lib --target aarch64-pc-windows-msvc windows_process::tests -- --nocapture` — 2 passed
- `cargo test -p openshell-supervisor-network --lib --target aarch64-pc-windows-msvc per_sandbox_credentials_reject_missing_wrong_cross_and_duplicate_auth -- --nocapture` — 1 passed
- `cargo test -p openshell-driver-mxc --test wxc_exec_real --target aarch64-pc-windows-msvc pc_proxy_scopes_network_policy_to_socket_owner -- --ignored --test-threads=1 --nocapture` — 1 passed, 1.04 s
- full supervisor-network suite — 1,232 passed, 2 ignored
- focused MXC surface — 93 unit, 3 OpenClaw, 10 example, and 44 matrix tests passed
- `mise run --jobs 1 pre-commit` on the rebased tree — exit 0, 219.975 s
- post-CI portability fix: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and focused Windows ARM64 Clippy — pass
- `git diff --check` — pass

The full Windows gate used the installed x64 Biome binary because Biome's native ARM64 executable crashes on this host, plus the official Z3 4.16.0 ARM64 release because the unauthenticated prebuilt download endpoint returned HTTP 403.

## Security impact

This removes an authorization-broadening path: an allowed Windows entry process no longer lends its binary-scoped network permissions to arbitrary descendants. Identity failures deny the request; they do not fall back to entry-command or endpoint-only authorization.

## Scope and residual risk

This is intentionally limited to Windows proxy process-identity binding. It does not normalize Windows path spelling or case; that separate behavior remains tracked separately. The latest base already contains the independent governed-proxy lifecycle fix.

Validation was performed on native Windows ARM64 with real ARM64 MXC. x64 compilation/CI remains expected coverage. A process that exits before its image can be queried is denied, which is the intended fail-closed behavior.

author: awtprod
body:
Stacked on #88 (base branch `efficiency/judge-tier-judgment`). Merge #88 first, then retarget this PR to `main`.

## Problem

A big chunk of what a Claude session spends context on is tool output the task never needed: a 400-line file read to change one function, a Grep dump where three matches mattered. Once in context it costs tokens on every subsequent turn and pushes the session toward compaction. This is the winnow idea from Andrew's request: judge each block of a large tool result for relevance, hide the confident-no blocks, and tell the agent how to get them back.

## Solution

- A pure sieve module splits large `Read` and `Grep` results into 25-line blocks, asks the `Judge` service (from #88) one yes/no question per block plus one "is this an error or empty result" question, and applies thresholds owned by code: hide only when the probability of being needed is below `dropBelow`, keep anything uncertain, hide nothing when the output looks like an error, and skip the rewrite entirely when less than `minPruneRatio` of the text would go. Hidden runs become a short deterministic stub with an exact re-run hint (`Re-run Read with offset=26 limit=100 if you need them`).
- The Claude adapter registers a `PostToolUse` hook only when the sieve mode is not `off`. The hook derives the current task from the last user request and the assistant's stated intent, passes subagent calls through unjudged, bounds its own time, and can never throw into the SDK. Any judge failure or unknown output shape leaves the result untouched.
- `shadow` mode judges and logs to the judge decision log without rewriting, so the hide rate and regret can be measured before anyone turns on `active`.
- `Bash` is never sieved: re-running has side effects and there is no recall cache.

Default is `off`, so query options stay byte-for-byte identical to today. A test asserts no `hooks` key is passed when the sieve is off.

## Verification

- Live probe on the deployed provider CLI 2.1.258 and on 2.1.278: the SDK's `updatedToolOutput` replacement reaches the model only when the replacement keeps the tool's output shape; the rebuild here preserves it, and a real end-to-end run with the real module and a fake judge showed the model receiving the stub and the re-run hint verbatim. In an unconstrained run the agent followed the hint and re-read the hidden range, which is the intended safety property.
- `apps/server` typecheck: 0 errors, exit 0. `vp check`: 0 errors, formatting clean.
- `src/efficiency`, `src/provider/Drivers`, provider registry tests: 90 pass. `ClaudeAdapter.test.ts` including four sieve-wiring tests and `server.test.ts` (151) pass.
- Not verified live: the sieve against a real judge model end to end, since no judge transport is configured on the host yet. The design intent is to run `shadow` mode first and read the decision log.

_Implemented by a claude-opus-4-8 subagent, coordinated by claude-fable-5-1, via Claude Code (Command Center)._

author: tripandcode
body:
**Origin:** Interactive session

`ReportResponse.rows` was `unknown[]`, so both report consumers reached the real
row shape through a blind `as unknown as` cast — nothing checked the asserted
shape against what `api/routers/reports.py` actually returns, and a backend row
change would surface as a runtime `undefined` rather than a type error. This
models the response as a discriminated union on `report_type`, with each
variant's row element type derived from the Python that builds it, so the
`report_type` tests the components already perform do the narrowing the casts
were standing in for. `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` raises 236 errors across 50
`src` files, so per the plan's stop rule it is enabled only for the scoped
build-config project and the inventory is recorded below.

## What changed
- `src/api/types.ts`: new `ReportType` literal union (mirrors `_REPORT_TYPES`),
  per-report row types (`RankingRow`, `OnTimeRow`, `Worst5MinRow`,
  `CompareRankingRow`, `DowRankingRow`, `CouncilSummaryRow`,
  `DelayCertificateRow`, `TrendPayload` + `TrendHourlyCell`/`TrendDowBand`), and
  `ReportResponse` rebuilt as a discriminated union over them.
- `DecimalCell = number | string` documents a real wire quirk: the backend
  computes these columns as `Decimal` (to match Postgres `ROUND`'s half-up
  rounding) and `rows` is an untyped `list`, so a bare `Decimal` serialises as a
  JSON **string** while the `int` columns beside it stay numbers. Verified
  directly: `{"rows":[["R1","平日","2.00","2.50",null,30]]}`.
- `AnalysisTab.tsx`: the three casts at the `trend` / `dwell_run` / table branches
  are gone — `detail.data.rows` narrows from the `report_type` checks already
  there. `TrendBlock` takes `TrendPayload[]`, so `payload.dow_band.grid` is
  checked rather than asserted.
- `ReportsHomeTab.tsx`: `trend.data.rows[0]` and `ranking.data.rows` narrow on
  `report_type` instead of `as { days?: TrendDay[] }` / `filter(Array.isArray) as
  unknown[][]`; `rankingToCsvRows` takes `RankingRow[]`.
- `src/api/reportPayloads.test.ts`: `expectTypeOf` narrowing assertions for
  trend, ranking (incl. positional cell types), dwell_run, council_summary and
  delay_certificate, plus a `@ts-expect-error` proving `route_forecast` is not a
  member. Enforced by `tsc`, not just at runtime.
- `tsconfig.node.json`: `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` enabled for that project only.

## Findings addressed
- F-33 — blind `as unknown as` report-payload casts:
  `frontend/src/tabs/AnalysisTab.tsx`, `frontend/src/tabs/ReportsHomeTab.tsx`,
  `frontend/src/api/types.ts`.
- F-34 — `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`: `frontend/tsconfig.json` deliberately
  **not** changed (236 errors / 50 files — see below); enabled scoped in
  `frontend/tsconfig.node.json`.

### `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` inventory for `src` (deferred, not half-fixed)
236 errors / 50 files. Almost none are report payloads; the bulk is unguarded
array indexing in drawing/layout code. Heaviest: `pages/landing/vehicleIcons.ts`
(31), `components/ServiceSplit.tsx` (24), `tabs/map/currentRouteStatus.test.ts`
(15), `components/ConcentrationBar.tsx` (15), `pages/landing/cityMapScene.ts`
(14), `styles/mapStyle.test.ts` (12), `components/InlineSparkline.tsx` (9),
`components/charts/DailyChart.tsx` (9). 21 of the 50 files are tests. By code:
102 × TS2532, 61 × TS18048, 34 × TS2345, 27 × TS2322, 7 other. The new
`reportPayloads.test.ts` is already clean under the flag.

## Verification (static only — no DB, no live data)
- `npm run typecheck` → clean (pre-change baseline also clean; the new test file
  fails to compile against the old `report_type: string` — 16 errors — which is
  the RED step)
- `npm run lint` → 0 errors, 4 pre-existing warnings (all `no-explicit-any` in
  files this PR does not touch)
- `npm run test` → 107 files / 620 tests passed
- `npm run lint:i18n` → pass · `npm run lint:i18n-strings` → pass
- `npm run deadcode` (knip) → clean
- `npm run test:check-entry-chunk` → pass
- `npm run build:bundle && npm run check:entry-chunk` → built; entry static
  closure 504.7 KiB, MapLibre stays out of every entry
- Mutation check: widening `RankingRow`'s `samples` to `number | null` makes
  `reportPayloads.test.ts` fail to compile, so the assertions do bite.
- Not run: `tests/api/test_reports.py` and every other DB-backed suite (no test
  Postgres/ClickHouse in this batch). No Python changed — the backend was read
  as the contract, not edited.

## Review status
Reviewed via `/review-pr`. Merged with `main` first; no conflicts. **One fix applied.**

### The union was checked against the backend, not accepted on its word

Replacing `as unknown as` with a declared shape is only an improvement if the shape is right — a
wrong type is worse than `unknown`, because every consumer now trusts it. So all eleven members
were traced to what `api/routers/reports.py` actually puts in `rows`:

- `_REPORT_TYPES` holds exactly these eleven, and `route_forecast` is correctly absent.
- **`OnTimeRow`'s sixth element is real.** `compute_on_time` returns a 5-tuple; the router appends
  `low_confidence` via `annotate_on_time_pct_confidence` before serialising, so the type matches
  the response rather than the builder.
- **`CouncilSummaryRow` looked wrong and isn't.** `compute_council_summary` returns an 8-key dict,
  but the router flattens it to precisely the declared 6-tuple; `is_stale` and `clamp_pct` feed
  footnotes and never reach `rows`.
- `CompareRankingRow` carrying no `service_type` matches the SQL, which overrides `service="all"`
  and selects five columns.
- `DowRankingRow`'s `dow_label`, `Worst5MinRow`, `RankingRow` (including `ranking_best`, which is
  `compute_ranking` with the opposite sort) and `DelayCertificateRow`'s 7-tuple all match.
- `trend` and `dwell_run` really are `rows=[<one object>]`, which is the asymmetry the
  `TrendPayload` comment calls out.

Every declared shape is accurate. That is the substance of this PR and it holds.

### A test that could not fail

`rejects a report_type the endpoint does not serve` did not test that:

```ts
// @ts-expect-error
expectTypeOf(res.report_type).toEqualTypeOf<"route_forecast">();
```

`res.report_type` is the whole union whether or not `route_forecast` is a member, so the
comparison fails either way and the directive stays satisfied. Demonstrated by adding
`"route_forecast"` to `ReportType`: `tsc -b` stayed **green**.

Rewritten as an assignment. Adding the member makes it legal, and TypeScript then flags the
directive itself:

```
src/api/reportPayloads.test.ts(59,5): error TS2578: Unused '@ts-expect-error' directive.
```

Same mutation now fails the build.

### Confirmed sound
`tsconfig.json`'s `include: ["src"]` covers `src/**/*.test.ts`, so `tsc -b` genuinely enforces the
`expectTypeOf` assertions rather than skipping the file — worth checking, because if it didn't,
every type assertion here would be decoration. The `DecimalCell = number | string` modelling is
right: `rows` is an untyped Python `list`, so a bare `Decimal` serialises as a JSON string beside
`int` columns that stay numbers. Scoping `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` to `tsconfig.node.json` rather
than `src` is the right call — it holds the line on new build-config code without opening a
hundreds-of-sites migration.

Verification: `npm run typecheck`, 620 frontend tests, `lint` (0 errors), `lint:i18n`,
`lint:i18n-strings`, `deadcode`.

body:
## What and why

A whole-product sweep of Rawhide found Highs that quietly poison the prompt or wipe lived-in state. This PR closes the ones that were in scope: Settings writing into the open chat, keyword lore rewriting the system head, group AFK naming the leftover 1:1 card, quiet Needs zeros inventing a swing, and the phone composer having no photo attach.

User-visible:

- **Porch Life is defaults, not the open chat.** Turning Needs / Realism / Passage of Time / Objectives / Afterglow off in Settings no longer writes that into the conversation you have open. Lived-in meters stay. Use the sidebar for that one story.
- **Keyword lore sits after the transcript.** Triggered world facts no longer live in the system prefix, so flipping a keyword does not force local backends (Kobold / oMLX / LM Studio) to re-read the whole chat.
- **Group away-time is about who actually speaks.** Dynamic Responses in a group uses that member’s name, ambitions, and hygiene — not the leftover 1:1 card.
- **A quiet beat can leave Needs still.** Tools still retry as text once; all-zero after that is kept. The Director no longer “repairs” a sit-together into a hunger or bathroom swing.
- **Attach a photo from the phone.** Composer has an Attach photo control. `POST /api/chat/send` takes additive `imageBase64`. Empty text with a picture is allowed. Desktop already had photo drop.
- **Open Thought follows the newest tokens.** Scroll that pane up and it stays put. Same on the phone.
- **Error banners are not story.** Generation / backend banners still show, but they are not saved and the next reply does not treat them as something that happened in the scene.
- **What’s New vacuum.** `docs/Rawhide.md` now lists only what landed after `rawhide.20260918.c11669b`.

Also in this commit (not a separate PR, same sweep): v52 `chat_worlds.is_primary` re-run no longer puts weather back on a lore-only place; hygiene-catastrophe ack survives reload; fork gifts restore oldest→newest; RAG awaits history hydrate and stamps story-day against the persist window; Journal/Growth rewrite receipts; changing the search key or evals GGUF path on the phone asks for the password.

author: minipuft
body:
## Summary

After this merges, a workspace's config can be `config.jsonc` — comments and trailing commas allowed, every setting shown as a commented-out example generated from the schema — and nothing that reads or writes the config loses those comments.

- The server, `cpm`, the Python hooks and skills export read `config.jsonc` first, then `config.json` (still strict, still translated from 4.x), then the packaged default.
- **Breaking:** a workspace holding both names refuses startup, and `cpm config` refuses the same way, naming both paths.
- `cpm init` and the server's `--init` write a `config.jsonc` with `$schema` and `"version": 5` live and all 66 settings commented out with description, default and permitted values.
- `cpm config set` and a persisted `system_control` toggle change one value in place; `cpm config reset --force` backs up and never renames.
- Hooks now read the workspace's config, not only the packaged file, so `hooks.expandedOutput` set by an operator takes effect.

## Demonstration

**Before**

```
$ cat config.json            # a comment is a parse error; every write re-serializes the document
$ cpm config set gates.enabled false   # rewrites the whole file
system_control config validate  →  ✅ config.json matches its schema.
```

**After** (built server, streamable-http, hermetic roots; `config.jsonc` = generated template + a live block carrying three comments)

```
config get chainSessions.timeoutMinutes → 🔎 chainSessions.timeoutMinutes = 777 · source: file
config validate                         → ✅ config.jsonc matches its schema.
gates disable persist:true              → 📁 Persisted gates.enabled=false to config.jsonc.
diff before after                       → 23a24,26  > "gates": { > "enabled": false > },
comment lines before/after              → 330/330
cpm config set … 778 ; 2.5 s later get  → 🔎 chainSessions.timeoutMinutes = 778   (trailing comment intact)

# workspace holding both names
Refusing to start: … that path holds both config.jsonc (/tmp/ws/config.jsonc) and config.json (/tmp/ws/config.json).
Expected a single config file at that path, or keep config.jsonc, the current name, and remove config.json (also still read).   exit 1
```

## How it was verified

| Claim | Probe | Baseline → measured | Mutation that fails it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A commented `config.jsonc` loads; a commented `config.json` does not | `paths.runtime.test.ts`, `config-file-translation.test.ts`, live drive | strict `JSON.parse` at 5 sites → 1 owner module; drive: jsonc healthy, same text as `.json` exits 1 "not valid JSON" | restore `JSON.parse` at either site → exactly the 2 jsonc tests there fail |
| `.jsonc` and `.json` with the same values serve the same configuration | live drive, `config list` on twin workspaces | — → byte-identical, 115 lines | n/a: comparison of two live outputs |
| Both names refuse startup, naming both paths | `paths.runtime.test.ts`, live drive | silently one file → exit 1, both absolute paths in stderr | not mutated; control: the same workspace with one name starts healthy (drive) |
| A 4.x file still translates, under either name | `config-file-translation.test.ts`, live drive | — → `advanced.sessions.timeoutMinutes` answers as `chainSessions.timeoutMinutes = 555` (`.json`) / `444` (commented `.jsonc`); notice names the file | fixture values differ from every default, so a fallback-to-defaults mutant fails |
| Every setting's example is valid when uncommented | `config-template.test.ts` (one case per key + uncomment-everything) | 0 → 70 cases over 66 keys | template `port: 99` → 2 of 70 fail |
| The template cannot drift from the schema | `validate-config-schema.ts` + self-test | 12 → 14 self-test cases | one character edited in the generated file → exit 1 naming it |
| Writes change only the target value | `config-file-write.test.ts`, `safe-config-writer.test.ts` on hand-authored fixtures | whole-document rewrite → fixture differs only in the value's characters | swap in `JSON.stringify` write → 5 named tests fail; in-test control shows the old behaviour does differ |
| `cpm` works on the file end to end | `cli/tests/integration/config-jsonc.test.ts` on a built `cpm.js` | 81 → 88 CLI tests | old whole-document `reset` → "keeps comments" test fails |
| Hooks read the workspace file; `//` inside a string survives | `test_config_loader_lookup.py` (13) | packaged file only → `MCP_WORKSPACE` → `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA` → packaged | string-unaware stripper → the 2 string-awareness tests fail |
| Skills export honours `gates.harnessCovers` from a commented file | `export-command.test.ts` | silently `[]` → honoured; same text as `.json` → `[]` | restore `JSON.parse` → named test fails |
| No other reader parses config text strictly | `config-text-parse-guard.test.ts` (holds a config path AND calls `JSON.parse`) | unguarded → 5 files pinned with reasons | delete one pinned entry → guard fails naming the file; in-memory sample is reported |
| Both bundles start with the new dependency inlined | `node dist/index.js --help`, `verify:mcp`, CLI suite, post-build check | `Cannot find module './impl/format'` → exit 0, 18/18, 88/88 | remove the ESM alias → build fails naming `./impl/format`, `./impl/edit`, `./impl/scanner`, `./impl/parser` |
| `--init` writes the config the README names | `init-workspace.e2e.test.ts` | no config written → `config.jsonc` equals the template; an existing `config.json` untouched | remove the `initConfig` call → template-equality test fails |
| Replies name the loaded file | `config-action-handler.test.ts`, `system-control-router-persist.test.ts`, `file-observer.test.ts`, `artifact-kinds.test.ts` | literal `config.json` → basename, asserted for both names | hard-code the literal in the validate reply → 2 named handler cases fail |
| Workspace-id read for `cpm` history follows the same resolution | `version-history.test.ts` | `config.json` only → either name, by format | control case shows rows land elsewhere without it |
| Format owner rejects everything beyond comments and trailing commas | `config-file-format.test.ts` (26) | — → unquoted keys, single quotes, empty text, truncation rejected with line:column | drop the parse-error check → 5 named tests fail |

## Notes for Reviewers

- `cli/esbuild.config.mjs` + `server/esbuild.config.mjs` — distrust because every other gate was green while neither bundle could start: `jsonc-parser`'s default entry is a UMD build esbuild cannot trace. The fix is a per-package alias to its ESM entry plus a post-build check for untraceable relative `require`s; the unminified dev budget rose 640,000 → 680,000 B (measured 673,115), the shipped budget is untouched (339,971 of 512,000 B).
- `server/src/cli-shared/config-operations.ts` — distrust because four write paths now share one in-place editor and one both-files detector; the detector fires only for the two config basenames, so an operator-named `--config` path is never refused for its neighbours.
- `hooks/lib/config_loader.py` — distrust because hooks previously read only the packaged file, and now read the operator's: a behaviour change for anyone whose workspace config sets `hooks.*` or Ralph isolation settings that were silently ignored before.

## Still open

- A fetchable schema URL so editors validate a config anywhere, and a docs page that owns the config file — the next PR in this series.
- `cpm init -w <path>` ignores `-w` (it takes the path positionally); pre-existing, not changed here.
- `server --init` on an existing workspace exits 1 before looking at the config, the same gating as `cpm init`.

## README Charter Compliance

1. Charter sections touched: the "Custom resources" line below the install details — one word, `config.json` → `config.jsonc`.
2. Did `npm run validate:readme` pass locally? Yes (391 lines).
3. First 30 lines still contain the pitch table? Yes, untouched.
4. Any new `<details>` blocks above the fold? No.
5. Any new cross-link? No.

author: wenzlik
body:
## The report

2026-09-19, MKV h264 stream-copy → fMP4 over a Wellspring proxy, 18 s to a ready player:

```
probe 10583ms (open 10560 + info 7 + describe 14)
startup … plan 7344ms (builtFromSource, 591 seg) → segment 7401ms
```

## What those numbers are

Neither is work — both are **round trips through the host's proxy**. A Matroska startup makes four requests:

| # | request | phase |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `bytes=0-` (header) | probe `open` |
| 2–3 | two reads at the tail (Cues) | the segment plan's index-load nudge |
| 4 | `bytes=<first cluster>-` | the plan's rewind to the head |

Aether hands PrismCore a **localhost range proxy** (`WellspringRangeProxy` and its SMB/WebDAV twins), and that proxy fetches every forwarded window *whole* — `URLSession.data(for:)`, 8 MB bites — before it writes a single byte downstream. FFmpeg's HTTP asks for `bytes=N-`, so requests 1 and 4 each wait for a full 8 MB however few bytes the demuxer wanted: at ~800 KB/s that is 10.5 s each, which is exactly `open 10560ms` and the bulk of `plan 7344ms`.

Reproduced with `Scripts/proxy-model-server.py` (added here), 60 min Matroska: `probe 10581ms (open 10546 …) … plan 10780ms (builtFromSource, 601 seg)`.

## What this PR changes

- **A plan built from the container's own seek index is kept in the keyframe cache**, not only a harvest from a session that could not be planned. The keyframes are already in memory when the plan is made — the demuxer's index, loaded by the nudge seek — so storing them costs a JSON write and no I/O against the source. Next play: no requests 2–3.
- **`HTTPRangeInput` retains recently fetched blocks (4 MB) instead of exactly one**, so request 4 is served from memory. Bounded by bytes, not block count: the two tail reads are tens of kilobytes each, and counting them as equals to the 1 MB head is what evicted the head.

## Measurement

`Scripts/proxy-model-server.py` (8 MB bites, ~800 KB/s origin) + `StartupCheckpointBenchmark` — probe + `start()`, the way a host runs it:

| | first play | second play | requests |
|---|---|---|---|
| before, FFmpeg's HTTP | 21.5 s | 21.5 s | 4 |
| after, FFmpeg's HTTP | 21.5 s | 21.5 s | 4 → 3 |
| before, coordinated HTTP | 3.3 s | 3.0 s | 4 |
| after, coordinated HTTP | **1.7 s** | **1.5 s** | 3 → 2 |

FFmpeg's own HTTP has no block cache to retain anything in and re-opens on every backward seek, so it keeps its shape; the coordinated reader is where round trips can be removed at all.

## What is deliberately left alone

- **The proxy's buffering, which is the biggest single win** — streaming the forwarded body instead of buffering 8 MB takes the same startup from 21.5 s to **0.6 s** in the model. It lives in `AetherCore/Sources/AetherCore/MediaSources/Wellspring/WellspringRangeProxy.swift` (and the SMB/WebDAV twins), not here.
- **`developer.prismCoreCoordinatedHTTP` (default OFF)** — flipping it on is worth 21.5 s → 3.3 s on the model before any of this lands. A host default, Aether's call.
- The probe's own reads, the CC scout, the readiness gate: none of them showed up in the round-trip count.

## Tests

- `CoordinatedHTTPTests.aBlockSurvivesAnExcursionToTheTail` — head → tail → head costs two requests, not three. Fails without the change (3 ≠ 2).
- `KeyframeIndexCacheTests.containerIndexIsKeptForTheNextPlay` — first play reports `builtFromSource` and stores a complete map; second reports `keyframeIndexCache`.
- Full suite: 547 tests, 86 suites, green. (`DemandDrivenTests.waitsForCuesRatherThanAnsweringEmpty` failed once in four runs on a 300 ms sleep race — local directories only, no HTTP and no keyframe cache, so nothing this diff touches. I did not bisect it to `main`.)

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

body: ## Summary Two defects, both fixed, each in its own commit: 1. **TV profitability panels served a frozen cache (last data 2026-08-25).** The six platform panels request `profitability?days=30&desktop_cost=1.2&mobile_cost=0.3`. The cache key includes cost params; that legacy key is only written by the old per-user-assumption writer, which is gone. The precompute cron refreshes the default key (`days=30`, cost from billing — `costSource: real`), and the GET route serves any cached doc at any age, so the panels showed a month-old snapshot while a fresh one sat in the next doc over. The classic dashboard page fixed this same class for itself; the Grafana board and the builder's `PROFIT_PATH` kept the legacy params. Fix: query PostHog for mobile actives — the same source already proven for desktop — with the Mixpanel segmentation kept as fallback. Live-verified: PostHog returns 2.2k–2.9k mobile uniques/day; Mixpanel returns 0. ## Failure-Class Failure-Class: new ## Verification - Firestore payload cache: legacy key doc `freshAt 2026-08-25T20:31Z` (last users day 2026-08-25 — matches the board symptom exactly); default key doc minutes old, `costSource: real`, all 7 sources ok. - PostHog HogQL live query (project 302298): 6 rows, mobile uniques 718–2869/day; Mixpanel returns 0 for the same window. - `python3 web/admin/grafana/test_build_dashboards.py` — 27 OK (incl. rebuild idempotency, which caught that the builder's `PROFIT_PATH` also carried the legacy params). - Admin suite 36 files / 259 tests, `tsc --noEmit`, eslint, prettier 2.8.8 — all clean.

author: onlyabrak
body:
Part of #24. **Stacked on #25** (it needs `Applied::parity`, which arrives with the `9764b86` pin) — merge #25 first, and #25 itself needs craft-ec/freenet-contracts#35.

A new crate `engine`, not a module: the claim is that it has no I/O, no clock and no randomness, and the way to *keep* that true is for it to be unable to reach any. It does not depend on the SDK — a core that can call the SDK is a core that will.

### Shape

`step(Event) -> Vec<Effect>`. Effects carry **dependencies and no batch size**: how many operations fit in a delegate round is a platform fact that has already changed once (F15, F21) and is the shell's business.

| state | promise |
|---|---|
| `Accepted` | in memory. Survives a tab close, not a node restart. |
| `Durable` | blocks **read back** from our own node. Survives a restart. |
| `Published` | head read back. |
| `ParityComplete` | the redundancy the nodes promise exists. |

`UpdateHead` is not emitted until every block of its commit is confirmed — a head naming a root whose blocks are not all there is a tree readers cannot walk. Every pack carries a commit manifest under its own magic (`prev head`, new `(seq, root)`, owed groups), so the network is the journal.

Owed parity is a **map**, newest wins. Coalescing defers a group that is still moving; the age bound stops "wait until it settles" meaning "wait for ever" for the hottest key in the store — the one most worth protecting.

### The differential found two real bugs

That is what it is for, and both would have been very hard to see any other way.

**1. Last-write-wins was first-write-wins.** A batch's duplicate keys were deduplicated with sort-then-dedup, which keeps the *first* op per key. The SDK's rule is last-write-wins — what a caller who wrote `put` then `delete` expects — so the same ops in the same order produced a different tree. Caught at seed 4 as a published root that is not the root a rebuild produces.

**2. Coalescing silently did nothing.** The supersede check scanned every block the store holds. Superseded nodes are never deleted, so it found every parity id ever listed and concluded nothing had ever been superseded. Caught by its own control: coalescing and the every-commit mode both emitted 15 blocks. Now scoped to nodes reachable from the current root, coalescing saves exactly the 6 blocks of the two superseded re-codings.

```
  coalesced 9 parity blocks, every-commit control 15 (6 saved)
```

### A test that could not fail, and now can

The fixture for "the head waits for its packs" produced **one** put, so the "confirm all but the last" loop ran zero times — the test could not tell a head that waits from one that does not, and a mutant emitting the head on the first confirmation **survived it**. The fixture now produces several puts and *asserts that it did*, and that mutant dies.

### Mutation table

| mutant | result |
|---|---|
| head emitted without waiting for confirmations | **killed** — `the head moved while a pack was still unconfirmed` (after the fixture fix above; survived before it) |
| `UpdateHead` declares no dependencies | **killed** — `UpdateHead does not name every block it depends on` |
| batch keeps the first op per key | **killed** — `seed 4: the published root is not the root a rebuild produces` |
| supersede check over every block ever written | **killed** — `coalescing bought nothing…` |
| backlog bound removed | **killed** — `an over-budget write was accepted` |

### Acceptance

1. ✅ one write → effects in dependency order; states once each, in order
2. ✅ four writes across two clients folded into one commit, all reach `published`
3. ✅ **the differential** — 24 seeds, confirmations shuffled, duplicated, for unknown ids, with `PutFailed` at seed-chosen positions; the published root equals a from-scratch `TreeBuilder` root every time; states are monotone. Seeds printed.
4. ✅ coalescing, with an executing control
5. ✅ `UpdateHead` never before its packs, with the mutant
6. ✅ age bound under continuous rewriting of one group
7. ✅ an opaque value passes through untouched — both the packed and the own-PUT path
8. ✅ no panic: 2400 events across 40 seeds, count asserted so an empty run cannot read as a pass

Plus: a full backlog refuses a write **without applying it** — a write both applied and refused is the worst of both.

### One gate finding

`cargo test` at a root package does not run workspace members, so the command in the README silently skipped this entire crate. Changed to `cargo test --workspace`. Worth checking wherever else that command is written down.

### Gates

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` — **11 suites, 42 passed, 0 failed** (with `CRAFTWORKS_CONTRACTS` pointing at #35's branch, i.e. the state after the stack merges).

### Two things I decided, flagged for review

- **The engine does not depend on `craftworks-sdk`.** You asked that it consume #22's owed-parity surface as `group → members`; it consumes the same *shape* (`ParityIds` + members) but derives it from `Applied::parity` and the nodes directly, because the engine also needs the **emitted blocks** to build packs and only `apply_with`'s sink provides those. Depending on the SDK for the type alone would invert the layering. If you want them unified, the natural move is to lift the shape into `freenet-prolly` — happy to do that as a follow-up.
- **`pack.rs` is a second implementation of the pack format**, whose authority is `freenet-contracts/block/src/pack.rs`. Two spellings of one format drift, and the drift appears as a host refusing a commit. It is here because the engine cannot depend on the contracts repo. A shared crate is the eventual answer; I have written that at the top of the file rather than leaving it to be discovered.

author: worksahilca-jpg
body:
A pass over a beta tester's first hour, fixing every place FollowUp stated something about itself that its own code contradicted.

## The root cause is one column

`Business.holdAllForApproval` is set on every beta account (`grantBetaPlan`) and was read by exactly two schedulers and written to no screen. So:

- The lead page offered **"Handle it all — every reply sends automatically with no review"**, with a red confirm, for something the account cannot do.
- Settings' "here's what's active" sentence said FollowUp *nudges*, *steps in*, *switches to a reactivation message*. It drafts all three and files them.
- The plans page sold a four-step plan. On a holding account a plan drafts step 1, holds it, and **unenrols the lead** — it has never reached step 2 for any tester.

It now reaches all three surfaces via `FreeTierStatus` and `/api/automation/settings`. The tier selector still offers every tier (the choice is real — it's what takes effect when holding is lifted), but the sentences describe what will actually happen.

## My own regression from yesterday

`ChannelNotReceiving`'s coral *"nothing people DM you reaches FollowUp"* is false for Instagram, which has a poller running every three minutes precisely because the first real account never got a webhook. It takes `stillWorks` now: calm, `--slate`, "arrives every few minutes, not instantly". Facebook passes nothing and keeps the alarm, because Facebook really does receive nothing.

## "Held because …" had to be a sentence

It rendered, to every tester: *"Held because Ready to send — this account holds every automated message for you to approve."* The reasons are clauses now, shared from `src/lib/holdReasons.ts`, stated as a rule to the model in `SEND_RISK_SCHEMA`, and enforced by a test against the real strings.

## Other claims corrected against the code behind them

| Screen said | Code did |
|---|---|
| "replies within a minute" | Push is off, so capture waits ten minutes; `getGmailStatus` already reported `pushActive` and the dashboard discarded it |
| "they'll join automatically when they sign in" | Auth checks the beta allowlist **before** the team invite, so an invited teammate is refused and the invite never consumed |
| "email steps send a text instead" | The fallback is whichever channel the lead came in on; SMS needs a number the carrier flag won't let them buy |
| "check Settings → Phone" (a send error) | That panel is hidden by the same flag |
| "Good morning" | Server's clock — UTC on Vercel, at 8pm in Toronto |
| Lost Gmail token blamed on removed access or a changed password | Google expires it every seven days for every unverified app — the likeliest cause, and the only one the owner didn't do |
| Nothing before Google's consent screen | A full-page red "hasn't verified this app", continue link folded under *Advanced* — the likeliest single point of tester loss |
| "docs/meta-oauth-setup.md, section 3" | A path in our own repo, shown to a customer |

## Two plain bugs

The setup strip ran its query on every dashboard load but rendered only in the has-leads branch — so the brand-new account was the one account never shown its next setup step. And the test-lead button lived only in the zero-lead branch, so using it created a lead that removed the button.

## Not fixed, deliberately

The website-widget setup step clears only when a real widget lead arrives, so a business with no website can never finish setup. That needs a dismissal — an additive column and a route — and whether setup steps get a "skip this" is your call.

## Two product questions for you

1. Should a held workflow step **resume** after approval, rather than unenrolling the lead?
2. Should a team invite from an approved tester be enough to let their colleague in? Right now the Team feature cannot work at all.

## Verification

Typecheck, 1348 tests and a production build all clean. Two new test files; the greeting one was checked against the bug restored (3 of 4 fail without the fix). The database is unreachable from the sandbox, so none of these screens were rendered — they are copy and branch changes, the kind that typecheck clean and can still read wrong.

author: penmoid
body:
## What was wrong

Codex sessions on this host refused to open with the bwrap/AppArmor sandbox message, even though the host sandbox works.

The host was fine: `/etc/apparmor.d/bwrap-userns-restrict` is loaded in **enforce** and covers `/usr/bin/bwrap`, `codex app-server` emits no sandbox `configWarning`, and a live `codex exec --sandbox read-only` (codex-cli 0.155.1) ran a shell command and returned its output.

What was stuck was Calandria's memory of the host. `agent_sandbox_broken_codex` was recorded earlier in the day, and `sandboxRefusal()` reads it to fail every `workspace-write` and `read-only` turn before it starts. Only two things clear that flag: a completed app-server turn, and the "Check again" button on Settings → Models. The refusal blocks the first of those, so once a host is fixed the flag survives forever and nothing in the failing task points at the button.

## The change

`sandboxRefusalChecked()` (`lib/agents/codex/sandbox.ts`) re-probes the CLI before spending the refusal, and `driver.ts` calls it in place of `sandboxRefusal()`.

- The probe costs one throwaway `codex app-server` spawn, and runs only on the path that was otherwise going to end the turn without doing any work.
- A probe that cannot reach the CLI leaves the flag as it was and the turn is still refused. "We could not ask" stays not-evidence, matching `probeCodexSandbox()`'s existing rule.
- The refusal text is re-read after the probe, so it quotes what the CLI says now.

The live instance was also unblocked directly via `POST /api/agents/codex/sandbox`, which re-probed and cleared the stale row.

## Verified

- `npx vitest run tests/codexSandbox.test.ts` — 4 new cases: host fixed since the flag was set (runs, flag cleared), warning still present (refuses), probe unreachable (refuses), flag clear (no probe at all).
- `npm test` — 274 files, 3397 passed, 0 failed.
- `npm run typecheck` — clean. `npm run guards` — no violations.
- `docs/AGENTS.md` § Linux sandbox documents the re-probe and its cost.

author: thatkidplongy
body:
A captured tip's summary is the card's header — the line the Inspire list shows, and the only part read when scanning. It was stored through a 220-character cap, which the tips prompt's own "1-2 plain sentences" overran routinely.

A real capture came back 287 characters and was filed ending `through handwriting, error tracking, and…` — cut mid-clause, in the card's title.

## What was wrong

The cut happens in `_parse_distillation` (`backend/app/llm.py`), not in the UI. `MotivationPanel.tsx:264` renders the header with `numberOfLines={expanded ? undefined : 2}`, so an expanded card is already showing everything it has — the ellipsis was baked into the stored text by `_clip(summary, 220)`.

This is the same mistake the highlight caps were already fixed for, and the comment above `MAX_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT` says why:

> These are runaway guards, not display budgets … a cap tight enough to fire on an ordinary two-sentence idea silently ate the thing being recalled.

The summary cap never got that pass.

## The change

- `MAX_SUMMARY = 500` — sized so a full two-sentence summary fits whole, while a model that hands back the transcript is still cut at a word boundary and marked with `CUT`.
- The three stored lengths become named constants (`MAX_SUMMARY`, `MAX_TAKEAWAY`, `MAX_QUOTE`) so the next one is adjusted where it's explained rather than inside a call. `MAX_TAKEAWAY` and `MAX_QUOTE` keep their existing values — both already sit above what their prompt asks for.

## Tests

Two added to `backend/tests/test_insights.py`:

- an ordinary two-sentence summary (287 chars, the real case) survives whole and carries no `CUT`;
- a runaway summary is still cut to the cap, at a word boundary, and marked.

`532 passed`. The 3 `test_web.py` failures on this branch are pre-existing and unrelated — they serve the gitignored `dist/` build, which doesn't exist in a fresh clone.

## Note

Only new captures distil at the new cap. A card already filed short stays short until it's removed and captured again — `add_insight` dedupes on `(player_id, source_url, kind)`, so deleting the card first makes a re-paste distil fresh.

body:
## Why it is not needed

`MarvinJsModule` was imported in `app.module.ts` but `<app-marvin-js-editor>` appears in no template, so the editor never rendered. The only things that consumed the package were the `assets`/`styles`/`scripts` entries in `angular.json` (which copied the MarvinJS distribution into `assets/marvin-js/` and bundled `marvinjslauncher.js`, `util.js`, `webservices.js` into `scripts.js`) and the `MarvinJsEditorComponent` that called `MarvinJSUtil.getEditor` on an iframe pointing at `/demo.html`. That iframe URL was only proxied in `proxy.conf.json` for `ng serve`; in the nginx image `/demo.html` falls through to `index.html`, so the editor could not have worked in a deployed container even where it was reachable.

The fleet moved to Ketcher (served through the `/ketcher` proxy) for the structure editor. This PR removes the leftover MarvinJS/Chemaxon plumbing so the repo no longer needs a Chemaxon license, the `NPM_TOKEN` secret, or the Chemaxon Artifactory registry.

## What changes

- `.github/workflows/docker.yml`
- `.npmrc` (deleted)
- `README.md`
- `angular.json`
- `docker-compose.marvin.yaml` (deleted)
- `package-lock.json`
- `package.json`
- `proxy.conf.json`
- `src/app/app.module.ts`
- `src/app/components/chemscraper/marvinjs/index.ts` (deleted)
- `src/app/components/chemscraper/marvinjs/marvinjs-editor.component.ts` (deleted)
- `src/app/components/chemscraper/marvinjs/marvinjs.d.ts` (deleted)
- `src/app/components/chemscraper/marvinjs/marvinjs.module.ts` (deleted)

- `package.json`: `@chemaxon/marvinjs` removed.
- `package-lock.json`: its entry removed, and 2 `resolved` URLs that pointed at `hub.chemaxon.com:443/artifactory/api/npm/npm/` (the Artifactory *proxy* of npmjs, which the old `.npmrc` had made the default registry) repointed at `registry.npmjs.org`. Tarballs and `integrity` hashes are unchanged; Artifactory serves npmjs tarballs byte-for-byte, and `npm ci` verifies every hash.
- `angular.json`: the 12 MarvinJS `assets`/`styles`/`scripts` entries (6 per configuration).
- `.npmrc`: Chemaxon registry lines removed (file deleted; nothing else was in it).
- Workflows: the `hub.chemaxon.com` auth line and its `NPM_TOKEN` comment. Where that line was the only thing creating `$HOME/.npmrc`, it is replaced by `touch $HOME/.npmrc` so the Docker build secret mount still has a file.
- `docker-compose.marvin.yaml`, the MarvinJS backend entries in `proxy.conf.json`, the README's Chemaxon registry setup block.
- The MarvinJS editor component (`marvinjs/` directory: editor component, module, type declarations) and its `MarvinJsModule` registration in `app.module.ts`, since it existed only to host the package.

## Verification

`npm ci --userconfig /dev/null` (no registry credentials at all) followed by `ng build` succeeds locally on this branch (Angular 15, webpack builder): every repointed tarball downloaded from npmjs with its original integrity hash, and the production bundle builds without the MarvinJS scripts. `grep -rl chemaxon` over the repo (excluding `node_modules`, `dist`, `.git`) is empty.

## After merge

The `NPM_TOKEN` repository secret is no longer referenced by any workflow and can be deleted.

author: lia-by-librechat[bot]
body:
# Pull Request

## Summary

A terminal (`final: true`) event is kept in four places: the manager's runtime cache, the durable
`finalEvent` field of the Redis generation job hash, the Pub/Sub frame published at completion, and
late/cross-replica replay. Neither terminal producer projected the payload before any of that, so
whatever a controller handed over was stored and published at full size.

The event carries `requestMessage`, `responseMessage` and `conversation`, and those messages also
carry data assembled only to build the prompt. `sanitizeMessageForTransmit` removed `fileContext` and
`files[].text` from `requestMessage` at the controller call site, but never `image_urls`, and nothing
sanitized the event centrally. Attachment-heavy conversations therefore put base64 image input into
Redis memory and into completion-time Pub/Sub traffic.

Measured on this branch against a single-node Redis, driving the real `publishTerminalClaim` with the
message shape `request.js` actually builds (a 400 KiB extracted document, a 300 KiB base64 image, and
a legitimate answer plus a generated attachment held constant):

| boundary | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| terminal event construction | 307.0 KiB | 307.0 KiB |
| runtime terminal cache | 307.0 KiB | 6.9 KiB |
| Redis job hash `finalEvent` | 307.0 KiB | 6.9 KiB |
| transport publication | 307.0 KiB | 6.9 KiB |

`projectTerminalEvent` is one shared projection applied at every terminal boundary. It excludes
`fileContext`, `image_urls` and `files[].text` from `requestMessage`, `responseMessage` and every
`runMessages` entry, and preserves message text and structured content, attachment references and
their display metadata, generated attachment text, and the terminal/reconciliation protocol fields.
Construction is unchanged by design: the controller still builds the full object, and the boundary is
what refuses to store it.

Two scope notes, because the reported numbers do not all reproduce:

- **Of the three reported fields, only `image_urls` still leaked.** `fileContext` and
  `requestMessage.files[].text` were already removed by the caller-level sanitizer. The projection
  covers them anyway, as defense in depth for the producers that do not call it.
- **This is not delta coalescing (#16093) or background-result batching (#16102).** Neither bounded
  the terminal `finalEvent`. The reporter's 19-364 MB has **not** been reproduced at that scale; what
  is reproduced is the boundary weakness and one of the three field origins.

## How it works

Every producer projects before anything is cached, persisted or published, and the read and delivery
paths project because a frame or record may come from a replica that predates this change.

```text
publishTerminalClaim(claim, finalEvent)      # request.js, resume.js, abortJob
  projectTerminalEvent(finalEvent)  -> intendedEvent
    jobStore.finalizeTerminalPersistence     # durable Redis job hash
    runtime.finalEvent =                     # runtime cache
    eventTransport.emitDone                  # Pub/Sub publication

emitDone(streamId, rawEvent)
  projectTerminalEvent(rawEvent)             # cache + job hash + transport

queueDone(rawEvent)                          # every terminal delivery to a subscriber
  projectTerminalEvent(rawEvent)             # live Pub/Sub frame from an old replica

createCrossReplicaRuntime / deliverStoredTerminal / recovered CAS payload
  projectTerminalEvent(JSON.parse(stored))   # records written before this change
```

The projection selects rather than clones: only the containers on a path that actually holds excluded
data are rebuilt, excluded values are never copied, and the caller's objects are never mutated
because prompt processing and message persistence still own them. Projecting an already-safe event
returns the identical reference, which makes it idempotent and free on the common path.

### `files` and `attachments` are not the same thing

Both are collections of file-like entries, and only one of them carries prompt input.

```text
requestMessage.files[].text    # extracted document body, assembled for the prompt -> excluded
responseMessage.attachments[]  # resolved artifactPromises (BaseClient.js:1218)
                    .text      # model-generated output, rendered inline        -> preserved
```

`TextAttachment` renders an attachment from `file.text ?? ''`, and `useAttachmentPreviewSync` polls
`GET /api/files/:file_id/preview` only while `status === 'pending'`, with an absent status reading as
`'ready'`. Excluding generated attachment text would therefore blank the inline preview for a late or
cross-replica subscriber with no path back to it. Each collection carries its own exclusion set;
storage bookkeeping (`_id`, `__v`) is excluded from both.

### Persistence-success bookkeeping

`publishTerminalClaim` decided success partly by object identity:

```diff
-    const desiredEvent = finalEvent ?? reconcileEvent;
+    const intendedEvent = finalEvent == null ? null : projectTerminalEvent(finalEvent);
+    const desiredEvent = intendedEvent ?? reconcileEvent;
     const persistenceFailed =
-      finalEvent == null ||
+      intendedEvent == null ||
       !durable ||
-      publicationEvent !== finalEvent ||
+      publicationEvent !== intendedEvent ||
       ('reconcile' in publicationEvent && publicationEvent.reconcile === true);
```

That check distinguishes publishing the intended payload from publishing one recovered out of durable
state or a conservative reconciliation. Projection allocates a new object, so comparing against the
caller's reference would have classified every successfully persisted FINAL as a persistence failure.
The comparison now uses the projected event and the other three distinctions are untouched. A
regression test pins each, and reverting this one line turns three of them red.

### The projected type is enforced, not decorative

`FinalMessageFields` carries an index signature, so `Omit` alone removes nothing from it and the first
version of `ProjectedFinalEvent` was structurally identical to the unprojected contract. The
transient fields are now mapped to `?: never`, and overloads return the projected contract for a
`FinalEvent`, the exact type for a non-terminal event, and `ServerSentEvent` for the union every
manager call site passes. An excluded field types as `undefined` rather than `unknown`, and
constructing a projected event that carries one is a type error.

## Type of change

* [x] Bug fix
* [ ] Feature
* [ ] Refactor
* [x] Performance improvement
* [ ] Breaking change
* [ ] Documentation
* [ ] Translation
* [x] Tests / tooling / CI

## Testing

Reproduced first, then fixed. A scratch harness built an attachment-heavy FINAL, drove it through the
real `publishTerminalClaim` against a real Redis, and measured the durable hash and the published
frame at each boundary; those are the numbers in the table. It confirmed `fileContext` and
`requestMessage.files[].text` were already stripped by the caller and that `image_urls` (300 KiB) was
not. The harness was then replaced by the committed tests.

**Tested environments/configuration:**

- Redis 7.4.6 built locally, single node on 6379 and a 3-master cluster on 7001-7003
- `USE_REDIS=true USE_REDIS_STREAMS=true`, both `USE_REDIS_CLUSTER=false` and `true`
- In-memory job store and transport for the same external contract

**Automated tests:**

- `packages/api/src/stream/__tests__/terminalProjection.spec.ts`, 19 tests: exclusion, preservation of
  content and attachment metadata, generated attachment text surviving, no input mutation,
  idempotence, `null` versus absent slots, the two type-enforcement assertions, and payload scaling
  that holds the answer constant while the excluded bodies grow.
- `packages/api/src/stream/__tests__/terminalProjectionBoundary.stream_integration.spec.ts`, 10 tests:
  the actual Redis hash and published frame, in-memory parity, durable size not scaling with excluded
  bodies, a live unprojected frame p

author: antoine-le-calloch
body:
`fake_oauth2` runs in every deployment, and nginx proxies `/fakeoauth2` to it, so `/fakeoauth2/auth` answers even when `server.auth.debug_login` is false and the fake backend is unused. It redirects to any `redirect_uri` it is given.

Two changes:

- The service now reads `server.auth.debug_login` at startup and idles when it is false, so the port is not served. This check belongs in the service because the supervisor config is rendered when the Docker image is built, where the value can differ from the config mounted at run time.
- Its supervisor config becomes a template, so the program is not set up at all when `debug_login` is false, the same way `pgbouncer` and `dask` already work. `rspack` gets the same treatment with `env.debug`: it already exits on its own in production, and it no longer shows up as an exited program in `supervisorctl status`.

author: jbequ5
body:
HUB_UPDATE_REQUIRED: Adds the C-CORE-17 GPU worker image preparation evidence under SYSTEM/AGENT-EXECUTION with an explicit impact-policy owner as mapped_detail, records the C-CORE-17-GPU-IMAGE-PREPARATION change event, and advances the authority snapshot to 5298c1ac with its source-check blob links repinned.

## What this is

Under a prospective owner exception lifting **only** the recorded `new-image-build` clause of the GPU pause, the accepted accelerator builder produced Carbon's pinned NVIDIA DEVELOPMENT worker image from a clean checkout of current `main`, and the result was inspected **without initializing an accelerator**.

This is preparation evidence. Image construction and package inspection are not accelerator execution, isolation evidence, or hardware acceptance.

## Identities

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Source built | `df26e757` (main), tree `sha256:802de522…` |
| Builder | `scripts/dev/accelerator_worker_image.sh`, unmodified |
| **Accelerator image** | `sha256:728a6bf37906a2614b6fb3a29c01ee0cfafd4422daaa9b27bdf2c8ca4ef873cd` (~5.62 GB) |
| Parent | `sha256:f77312b9…` → pinned base `sha256:33ceb719…` |
| Lock / profile | `sha256:a197af53…` / `sha256:8408adc8…` |
| Build exit status | **0**, captured from the builder process rather than a log writer |

## Inspection

Lock bytes inside the image, the repository lock and `GPU_PROFILE.environment_lock_digest` are identical. Profile, base-image, source-tree and entrypoint labels agree with the parent manifest and the source. All 34 pinned distributions are installed at their locked versions, including `jax-cuda13-plugin`, `jax-cuda13-pjrt` and 15 `nvidia-*` packages; the only distribution beyond the lock is `carbon` itself. The image runs as non-root `65532:65532` with the fixed entrypoint, worker paths `dr-xr-xr-x` and metadata `-r--r--r--`, and write probes as the image user are denied. No host-grant path, paused C-CORE-15 artifact or credential-shaped file was found across 6,399 scanned files.

Package metadata was read via `importlib.metadata`. No numerical backend was imported, `jax.devices()` was not called, and no matmul, training or GPU diagnostic ran.

**Stated limits:** the filename scan covered `/opt/carbon` and `/opt/carbon-worker` only, did not read file contents or other layers, and is not an exhaustive secret or security audit. Image metadata is not a runtime control — a non-root user and bundled CUDA libraries establish neither isolation, GPU memory enforcement, device visibility, nor any ability to reconstruct a scientific workload.

## No GPU was attached

Neither builder nor the recipe contains `--gpus`, a device request, `/dev/dxg`, an NVIDIA device mapping, `--privileged` or a GPU BuildKit entitlement; build logs contain zero occurrences of `--gpus`, `/dev/dxg` or `nvidia-smi`; the daemon default runtime stayed `runc`; inspection containers ran `--network none` with `no-new-privileges`; the image's own default is `JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu`. `verify_device_release()` was deliberately not called, since it can create quarantine state.

## Unchanged

`ESTABLISHED_OBSERVATION_CONTRACTS` remains **empty** — strict admission and verified whole-device release stay unavailable on every host, and this build neither populated the registry nor certified any host. No grant, lease or journal was created. C-CORE-15 remains paused and byte-identical, verified by per-file digests, and no C-CORE-15 file entered the build context. Every other clause of the GPU pause remains in force.

## Observation for the integration owner

The accelerator overlay is left **untagged** while the C-03 parent is tagged by source digest. The manifest references it by immutable ID, which is what the controller checks, so this is not a correctness defect — but a routine `docker image prune` would discard a 5.62 GB build. Recorded as an observation; the accepted builder was not modified, since changing it would require a fresh build to re-verify.

author: leonerdcdl
body:
### Contexto e Objetivo

Implementação do sistema de votação e apuração de execuções para o jogo Blood on the Clocktower (BotC). O sistema segue as regras originais do jogo, onde um candidato só é executado se receber uma quantidade de votos equivalente a pelo menos a metade dos jogadores vivos e for o candidato com o maior número absoluto de votos. Em caso de empate na maioria, ninguém é executado.
### O que foi feito
• Criação do módulo src/botc.py com a classe SistemaEleitoralBotC.
• Implementação da Lógica de Apuração:
    • Implementação do construtor que recebe a quantidade de jogadores vivos.
    • Método registrar_votacao para contabilizar os votos de cada alvo.
    • Método apurar_vencedor garantindo as regras:
        • Verificação de quórum (votos ≥ metade dos jogadores vivos).
        • Mecanismo de resolução de empates retornando None (nenhuma execução).
• Inclusão e centralização das exportações da classe SistemaEleitoralBotC no __init__.py do pacote.
• Segurança e Validação: Lançamento de ValueError para inicializações com 0 ou menos jogadores vivos, e registros de quantidades de votos negativas.
• Cobertura de Testes (pytest): Inclusão de suíte completa no arquivo tests/test_botc.py com 7 casos de testes abordando empates, quantidade insuficiente de votos, votos majoritários vitoriosos e travas de segurança (votos/jogadores inválidos).

### Critérios de Aceite

[✓] A classe implementa corretamente a interface abstrata SistemaEleitoral.
[✓] O algoritmo respeita a condição de execução baseada em metade dos votos vivos.
[✓] O sistema barra o registro de votos negativos ou de salas vazias (0 jogadores).
[✓] Em caso de empate entre o maior número de votos que excedem a métrica, a execução é cancelada corretamente.
[✓] Os testes unitários (pytest) cobrem com assertividade os fluxos de sucesso e exceções.

### Rastreabilidade

Closes #14
