author: daniel-ospina
body:
fix(monitor): point the auth availability probe at the session-bearing origin (#4281)

#4054 moved the BFF from the marketing Pages project (`tortoise.premiselabs.co`)
to `app.premiselabs.co` (`tortoise-dashboard`) — the decided topology — and left
the availability watchdog's auth probe pointing at the marketing origin. That
route answers 404 BY DESIGN now, so the probe's own healthy expectation
(`PROBE_EXPECT_STATUS: 302`, `PROBE_REQUIRE_HEADER: code_challenge_method=s256`)
was being checked one host to the left. Verified against prod:

    tortoise.premiselabs.co/auth/start  ->  404
    app.premiselabs.co/auth/start       ->  302 + code_challenge_method=s256
    app.premiselabs.co/api/session      ->  401

Two consequences, one stale string:

1. Every scheduled run filed/commented on #4219 ("verdict: UNEXPECTED (HTTP
   404)") and failed the workflow, so main carried a permanent red
   `availability-watchdog` run and the incident list lied.
2. SIGN-IN MONITORING WAS BLIND — the regression #3628 exists to prevent. That
   issue is why the dedicated `/auth/start` step exists at all: during #3616
   `/welcome` answered 302 and `/api/session` answered 401 throughout, so a
   liveness probe of either was green while nobody could sign in. Pointed at a
   host the flow no longer touches, the step could not have caught a real
   outage on the session-bearing origin.

Changed, all four sites the same stale host lived in: the script constant
(`AUTH_PROBE_URL`, which is what puts the URL in `PROD_PROBE_URLS` and therefore
what makes the run production rather than a drill), the workflow step's
`PROBE_URL` and `PROBE_HOST_LABEL` (the incident dedupe key, so it must be the
host actually probed), the harness fixture/expectations, and the post-deploy
sign-in verification in deploy-pages (that site was later **dropped** — the probe there lives in the wrong job; see "Review follow-ups").

The harness pins the URL by literal **and** derives the label/script relationship
from it: it extracts the URL from the workflow step and
asserts that the step's host label equals that host, and that the script's
`AUTH_PROBE_URL` matches it too (otherwise only the workflow moves and the step
is silently classified a DRILL — [DRILL]-titled, no page, self-heal disarmed —
while looking correct in the diff).

⚠️ **Superseded — see "Review follow-ups" below.** The `413 passed, 0 failed`
figure described the original commit and is no longer the harness's state; the
end-to-end harness could not be re-run to completion (see below). Three drift
mutations were caught at that time, each verified —
reverting the workflow URL reds 3 assertions; leaving the script constant behind
reds the derived script-match assertion; leaving the label behind reds the
derived label-match assertion. That third case also exposed a harness defect: on
the script-constant drift the harness HANGS in the restart cases with zero
failures instead of failing — a guard that waits is worse than one that reds, so
it is filed as #4284.

**#4219 will NOT be auto-resolved** — the watchdog dedupes incidents by EXACT title and the title is built from `PROBE_HOST_LABEL`, which this change renames. #4219 was therefore closed by hand as a false incident (with the full diagnosis). Once this is on main the next scheduled run resolves future incidents through the
watchdog's own recovery path (no manual close) and the lane should go green.

Fixes #4281
Refs #4219, #3628, #4054, #3616, #4284


---

## Review follow-ups (commit `bcc5791a8`)

A fresh reviewer found three real defects in the first commit; fixing the second
one exposed a fourth. All four are fixed.

1. **P1 — a false claim in this PR body.** It said the next scheduled run would
   "resolve #4219". It would not: the watchdog dedupes by **exact title**, and the
   title is built from `PROBE_HOST_LABEL`, which this change renames — so the old
   incident is orphaned and a *second* one could be filed alongside it. The claim
   is corrected above and the consequence is now documented at the label's
   definition, where the next reader will hit it. **#4219 was closed by hand** as a
   false incident, with the full diagnosis (probe target stale; the decided origin
   answers `302 + code_challenge_method=s256` = healthy).
2. **P2 — the derived guards could go vacuous.** `assert_contains` is a `case`
   glob, so an **empty needle matches every haystack**: had the URL/host
   derivation returned empty (a quoted or folded value), both drift guards would
   have passed while checking nothing. Added `assert_not_empty` (fail closed) on
   both derivations, made the extraction quote-tolerant, and asserted the step does
   not itself set `PROD_PROBE_URLS` — a second route to a silently-DRILLed run.
3. **P2 — the docs still named the old host**, in `docs/infra-runbook.md` §7.1b.
   That is the same defect one layer down: a runbook that documents a probe which
   is *supposed* to 404. Repointed — and a VGATE pass failed on the rest of the
   section (the `PROBE_HOST_LABEL` knob table, §7.2's example incident title, and
   the host inventory that still listed `auth` as a role of the marketing origin),
   all repointed in turn.
4. **Found by fix #2, in my own guard.** The empty-check turned a silent green
   into a loud red and revealed that the derivation used GNU-only `\?`, which BSD
   `sed` on macOS reads as a literal `?` — so the value derived **empty locally**
   while CI's GNU `sed` would have been green. Switched to the portable
   `\{0,1\}` and verified the derivation for both the bare and quoted spelling
   under this box's BSD `sed`. The hardening paid for itself before it merged.

**Test status, stated plainly:** the end-to-end harness could not be re-run to
completion from this session. The execution guard refuses to run the script from
a hub-rooted session (it permits it only from inside the worktree), and a
delegated run wedged under load (`load1` > 45 — the same load that killed the
earlier child). The last complete run was `414 passed, 2 FAILED`, both failures
being the new `assert_not_empty` calls correctly reacting to defect #4; after the
fix the derivation is verified **at the expression level** for both spellings, and
the VGATE pass re-read the script and confirmed the shape. A green end-to-end
harness run is **not** claimed. CI (`ubuntu-latest`, GNU `sed`) plus a quiet-box
re-run remain the real gate.

**Separately filed:** [#4284](https://github.com/daniel-ospina/tortoise/issues/4284)
— the harness **hangs** (rather than failing) on an auth-probe drift mutant: the
drift mutations that matter most are the ones that wedge the runner instead of
reddening it, which is a worse failure mode than a plain false green.

Refs #4281, #4219, #4284, #3628, #4054

---

## Cycle 2 (fresh reviewer) — findings and disposition

A second fresh reviewer, given the two commits, returned **1 P1 + 4 P2 + 2 P3**. It
confirmed all four cycle-1 fixes are real (it re-derived the guards standalone and
mutation-tested them: label drift caught, script-constant drift caught, quoted URL
tolerated, folded URL caught, step-level `PROD_PROBE_URLS` caught). It then found
the following.

### Fixed in this cycle (`deploy-pages.yml` scope reduced; two guards added)

- **P2 — the silent-DRILL refusal was step-scoped.** GitHub env precedence is
  STEP > JOB > WORKFLOW, so a **job-level** `PROD_PROBE_URLS` reaches the script
  just as well and narrows the production set — the auth probe is then classified
  a DRILL (`[DRILL]`-titled, no page, self-heal disarmed) with the diff looking
  correct. The reviewer demonstrated the hole: with `PROD_PROBE_URLS` added to the
  job `env:`, the guard reported **0 failures**. The harness already computes the
  job-level env for the secret assertions; `PROD_PROBE_URLS` is now refused there
  too, closing the third route to a false DRILL.
- **P2 — a step-scoped guard cannot see a second step.** The old target could be
  re-added under another name ("legacy check", a copy-pa

author: yosh102
body:
`upTo()` holds a ceiling and settles what the handler fulfilled, which leaves one question the protocol cannot answer: what was the work worth? This example puts that behind `(work) => verdict` and ships two judges.

- **`ruleJudge`** — thresholds on what the handler measured. No key, no network, deterministic.
- **`jevJudge`** — [Jev](https://typesafe.ai), TypeSafe AI's System One model, asked two typed questions: was this answered (`noul`) and how much work was it (`score`, three levels). Probabilities and a confidence, no prose.

One route, a ceiling of `$0.05`, and four questions that settle `$0.01`, `$0.02`, `$0.04` and nothing.

The seller's judge decides whether the seller gets paid, so three rules are enforced in code and covered by tests: doubt charges the lowest tier; an unanswered question returns `422` and releases the hold; the buyer is told the tier, the confidence, the reason, and which model version decided.

Two more things the tests hold:

- The Jev request carries the question, the answer this server wrote, and three counts — the exact field set is asserted.
- The pricing log carries identifiers, counts, tier, amount, confidence and judge, and no request text.

Every Jev failure — no key, timeout, error, unrecognised shape — falls back to the rules and says so in the reason, so a trial key that expires changes the prices rather than stopping the server.

Also adds the guide behind it: **Price what the work was worth**, which is vendor-neutral; Jev appears as one implementation at the end.

Run it: `pnpm --filter @tollstile-examples/jev-pricing start`, then `agent` in another terminal.

author: johnnyvontruant
body:
## Summary

Implements the approved **one accountable human + Vega evidence** policy as a separately typed, development-only AEGIS review receipt.

- JT is the sole human approver.
- Vega review is content-bound engineering evidence, never a second signature.
- A successful result reaches only `ELIGIBLE_FOR_DEVELOPMENT_CANDIDATE_REVIEW`.
- Production acceptance, deployment, hardware actuation, storage writes, network reconfiguration, and automatic promotion remain denied.
- The existing two-human policy and experimental PR #160 are unchanged.

## Dependency and preservation

This PR is stacked exactly on design-only PR #162 at `92ae013410636be3000d3dd063a2a64daf722aec`.

PR #162 starts from accepted `main` at `a3b4ac54acd98230e7ad83dab807876ab7330c49`. Frozen baseline PR #78 and `feature/project-aegis` were not modified. This PR must remain separate from #78 and #162 until independently reviewed.

## Architecture

- distinct packet, receipt, result schemas and SSHSIG namespace
- exact source/policy/candidate/HoloDeck/coverage/reviewer-evidence bindings
- fail-closed freshness, replay, unknown-field, tamper, and authority-ceiling checks
- explicit deny-by-default authority consumer
- manual promotion explicitly rejects the development-result schema
- deploy and hardware entrypoints remain structurally unable to accept AEGIS receipts
- mobile Mission Control shows `Single operator · development only` and four explicit NO-authority states

## HoloDeck proof

15 deterministic scenarios:

- 1 development-eligible
- 9 HOLD
- 5 stronger-consumer DENIED
- one human with two keys still fails the two-human quorum
- 0 false eligibility, production acceptances, deployments, hardware actions, storage writes, network changes, automatic promotions, or runtime writes
- Recovery Coverage Matrix remains 8/8 trusted, 0 gaps

Evidence: `docs/evidence/aegis-single-operator-development-v1.json`

## Validation

- focused AEGIS/HANGAR/Mission Control integration: 58 passed
- full local suite: 2,779 passed; 3 AF_UNIX tests deselected because this sandbox prohibits Unix sockets
- fresh installed-wheel and isolated CLI import smoke: passed
- evidence replay exact
- HANGAR validation and generated-view parity: passed
- Ruff, JavaScript syntax, JSON, whitespace, and mobile structural contracts: passed

GitHub CI is authoritative for the three socket tests.

## Prior art

The field report compares actual TUF, in-toto, SLSA VSA, Sigstore Cosign, and GitHub protected-environment contracts. Only scoped-role, threshold, subject/policy/evidence, and environment-boundary semantics were adapted. No external code, schema, dependency, service, credential, key, or dataset was incorporated.

## Safety

No merge, deployment, BattleStation access, service/configuration/credential change, hardware/storage/network action, or boot-task change was performed. No production key or signature exists. Runtime remains `AWAITING_OPERATOR_SIGNATURE`.

## Hosted CI

- [CI #1842](https://github.com/johnnyvontruant/TruePanel/actions/runs/35489396233): passed
- complete hosted suite: 2,782 passed, including the three Unix-socket tests unavailable locally
- installed-wheel smoke: passed

The first hosted run exposed a stale installed-wheel HANGAR count (21 instead of 22). Commit `c370c2f` now verifies both the 22-entry registry and completed `TP-EXP-0022`; the complete rerun passed.

author: m-tatsuto
body:
## 概要

ローカル利用を中心に4つの変更を入れています。追加の依存ライブラリはありません。

### 1. macOSデスクトップアプリ（`issue-model-app`）
- `issue-model-app --install-mac-app` で `~/Applications/Jev Issue Router.app` を生成。`osacompile` のアプレット内にWebKitウィンドウを持たせ、ブラウザを使わず専用ウィンドウで開く。ユニバーサルバイナリなのでRosetta不要。生成後にad-hoc署名。
- 画面は `127.0.0.1` のランダムポートのみ。起動ごとのトークンとHostヘッダを検証。ウィンドウを閉じるとサーバーも終了。
- APIキーは既存のKeychain項目（`local.jev.typesafe`）へ保存。キーはargvではなくstdinで渡す。保存状態（保存日時。属性のみ読み、値は読まない）と疎通確認（固定の小さな問い合わせ1回）を表示。
- 入力内容を本人のみ読める権限のファイルへ自動保存・復元（キーと結果は保存しない）。選んだ方針の説明を表示。
- ターミナルから `issue-model-app` を実行した場合はブラウザに開く（macOS以外でも利用可）。

### 2. リポジトリの状態を判断材料に追加（`--repo PATH` / アプリのフォルダ欄）
- ローカルGit cloneの**メタデータのみ**を収集してJevへ送信: 規模、拡張子・フォルダ別ファイル数、マニフェスト、テスト・CI・マイグレーションの有無、ブランチ、未コミット件数、直近コミット件名、Issueの語に一致するパス。ファイルの中身は読まない。
- 送信内容は結果JSONの `repository` にそのまま入る。パス名・コミット件名は「信頼できないデータ」と指示文に明記。合計60,000文字、追跡ファイル50,000の上限あり。未指定時のリクエストは従来どおり。
- Slack / GitHub Actionは未対応（ドキュメントに明記）。

### 3. 保留（needs_context）の見直し
- 1回目のJev呼び出しで、目的・現状・対象・完了条件のどれが不足かも同時に判定（呼び出し回数は増えない）。結果の `missing_context` と画面に表示。
- 保留するのは**目的が読み取れないときだけ**。それ以外の不足は「暫定の選定」として推薦を出し、補足すべき情報を示す。不足項目は2回目の評価にも渡す。
- 背景: 実際の短い日本語の機能要望が保留になっていた。さらにリポジトリのメタデータを渡すと、コードの場所を特定できないことを理由に「対象が不明」と判定され、かえって保留が増えていた（同じ本文で「対象が書かれている」確率が 97% → 40%）。リポジトリは補助情報で、場所を特定できないことは保留理由にならない、と指示文に明記。

### 4. 方針 `min-cost` / `max-quality`
- `min-cost`: コスト最優先。`max-quality`: 設計品質最優先で、モデルを各社の最上位に固定し、Jevは推論設定を選ぶ（結果にその旨を表示）。
- 両方針では各候補にカタログ内の順位を付けて渡す。**カタログは各社のモデルを安い順に並べる前提**になります。
- CLI / Slack / Action / Codexスキルのすべてで利用可能。

### その他
- Jevの確率は小数2桁で返るため、僅差のとき「選択が最高確率と一致しない」と誤ってエラーになることがあった。丸め誤差（0.015）を許容。
- 判定基準の文言を変えたため `policy_version` を `2026-09-20.3` に更新。

## レビューで見てほしい点
- **保留条件の緩和**は既存の挙動の変更です。「なんかおかしいので直して」のような依頼は引き続き保留されることを実APIで確認済みですが、緩めすぎていないかの判断をお願いします。
- `max-quality` で候補を最上位モデルに限定するのは「Jevが選ぶ」原則の例外です。方針の定義として固定し、結果に明示する形にしています。
- `--repo` はパス名・ブランチ名・コミット件名を外部（TypeSafe）へ送信します。`SECURITY.md` と各ドキュメントに記載しました。

## 確認
- `python -m unittest discover -s tests`（57件）、`ruff check .`、`actionlint` はすべて成功。通常テストはモックのみで、実APIは呼びません。
- 合成の例と実タスク3件 × 3方針を実APIで手動確認（普通の機能要望は選定、無内容の依頼は保留）。
- アプリはこのMac（Apple Silicon）で、ウィンドウの起動・表示・終了時のサーバー停止・入力の保存と復元・疎通確認を確認。
- 未確認: Rosetta未導入のMacでの起動、Intel Mac、ウィンドウ内での操作の自動テスト（手動確認のみ）。

author: matthewberry
body:
## Why it is not needed

The structure input (`<app-marvinjs-input>`, used by enz-rank) renders `<app-ketcher>`; `<app-marvin-js-editor>` appears in no template. The only things that consumed the package were the `assets`/`styles`/`scripts` entries in `angular.json` (which copied the MarvinJS distribution into `assets/marvin-js/` and bundled `marvinjslauncher.js`, `util.js`, `webservices.js` into `scripts.js`) and the `MarvinJsEditorComponent` that called `MarvinJSUtil.getEditor` on an iframe pointing at `/demo.html`. That iframe URL was only proxied in `proxy.conf.json` for `ng serve`; in the nginx image `/demo.html` falls through to `index.html`, so the editor could not have worked in a deployed container even where it was reachable.

The fleet moved to Ketcher (served through the `/ketcher` proxy) for the structure editor. This PR removes the leftover MarvinJS/Chemaxon plumbing so the repo no longer needs a Chemaxon license, the `NPM_TOKEN` secret, or the Chemaxon Artifactory registry.

## What changes

- `.github/workflows/docker.yml`
- `.npmrc` (deleted)
- `README.md`
- `angular.json`
- `docker-compose.marvin.yaml` (deleted)
- `package-lock.json`
- `package.json`
- `proxy.conf.json`
- `src/app/app.module.ts`
- `src/app/components/novostoic/marvinjs/index.ts` (deleted)
- `src/app/components/novostoic/marvinjs/marvinjs-editor.component.ts` (deleted)
- `src/app/components/novostoic/marvinjs/marvinjs.d.ts` (deleted)
- `src/app/components/novostoic/marvinjs/marvinjs.module.ts` (deleted)

- `package.json`: `@chemaxon/marvinjs` removed.
- `package-lock.json`: its entry removed, and 2152 `resolved` URLs that pointed at `hub.chemaxon.com:443/artifactory/api/npm/npm/` (the Artifactory *proxy* of npmjs, which the old `.npmrc` had made the default registry) repointed at `registry.npmjs.org`. Tarballs and `integrity` hashes are unchanged; Artifactory serves npmjs tarballs byte-for-byte, and `npm ci` verifies every hash.
- `angular.json`: the 12 MarvinJS `assets`/`styles`/`scripts` entries (6 per configuration).
- `.npmrc`: Chemaxon registry lines removed (file deleted; nothing else was in it).
- Workflows: the `hub.chemaxon.com` auth line and its `NPM_TOKEN` comment. Where that line was the only thing creating `$HOME/.npmrc`, it is replaced by `touch $HOME/.npmrc` so the Docker build secret mount still has a file.
- `docker-compose.marvin.yaml`, the MarvinJS backend entries in `proxy.conf.json`, the README's Chemaxon registry setup block.
- The MarvinJS editor component (`marvinjs/` directory: editor component, module, type declarations) and its `MarvinJsModule` registration in `app.module.ts`, since it existed only to host the package.

## Verification

`npm ci --userconfig /dev/null` (no registry credentials at all) followed by `ng build` succeeds locally on this branch (Angular 15, webpack builder): every repointed tarball downloaded from npmjs with its original integrity hash, and the production bundle builds without the MarvinJS scripts. `grep -rl chemaxon` over the repo (excluding `node_modules`, `dist`, `.git`) is empty.

## After merge

The `NPM_TOKEN` repository secret is no longer referenced by any workflow and can be deleted.

body:
Closes #164.

## Summary

Resolves nine engine private symbols, all from current-binary evidence.

| Symbol | Category | Coverage | Anchor |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Draw_TextureMode_f` | func | 11 configs | exact literal per family |
| `gl_filter_min` / `gl_filter_max` | gv | 11 configs | structural walk of the `modes[]` store pair |
| `r_framecount` / `r_visframecount` | gv | 11 configs | `LLM_DECOMPILE` from `R_RecursiveWorldNode` |
| `ClientDLL_DrawTransparentTriangles` | func | 11 configs | `cl_funcs` forwarder reached from `R_DrawTEntitiesOnList` |
| `cl_funcs_pDrawTransparentTriangles` | gv | 11 configs | the member slot read inside that forwarder |
| `CL_IsDevOverviewMode` | func | 11 configs | nearest call before a `CL_SetDevOverView` call site |
| `r_entorigin` | gv | 9 configs | `LLM_DECOMPILE` from `R_DrawTEntitiesOnList` |

## Notable findings

- **The `gl_texturemode` handler is not a function in either SvEngine Windows IDB.** Both `hw.dll` files contain it as analysed code reachable only through the address pushed into `Cmd_AddCommand`, so the literal has a code xref with no owning function. New `_engine_texture_mode_common` recovers the entry from the registration and defines it in-memory (never saved), and every downstream finder repeats the definition. Recorded in `memory/lessons`.
- **The real symbol name is not stable.** hl-8684/hl-10210 renamed the callback into a cvar hook (`gl_texturemode_hook_callback`, `void (cvar_t *)` ABI); SvEngine calls it `GL_TextureMode_f`. The config symbol stays `Draw_TextureMode_f` so one identity covers every build.
- **`gl_filter_min`/`gl_filter_max` have no fixed offset relation.** Adjacent in either order, or `0x10` apart, depending on the build.
- **`r_visframecount` on svencoop-8948 has no direct absolute reference anywhere.** It is only reachable through a `.got` slot; the existing `got_indirect_targets` path resolves it, so no shared-resolver change was needed.
- **`r_entorigin` is not covered on SvEngine.** Both SvEngine builds write it in the entity dispatcher rather than the transparent-entity loader, and the dispatcher is not reachable from any existing engine artifact (the `modelorg` adjacency that holds on Linux does not hold on Windows). It is produced for the nine other configs and the gap is documented.

## Verification

- `ida_analyze_bin.py -allgamever`: 2613 nodes, 0 failed, 0 missing.
- Linux artifacts match the retained `.symtab` exactly for `Draw_TextureMode_f`, `ClientDLL_DrawTransparentTriangles`, `gl_filter_min`, `gl_filter_max`, `r_framecount`, `r_visframecount`, `r_entorigin` and `CL_IsDevOverviewMode` on hl-10210, hl-8684 and svencoop-8948.
- `tests/run_test_suite.py unit -b`: 910 OK, 2 skipped.
- `tests/run_test_suite.py repository-contract -b`: 14 OK.
- `format_repo_files.py --check`: clean.
- BLOB (hl-3248..3647) analysed through `hw.decrypt.dll`; SvEngine Windows validated against raw disassembly.

# English

## Summary

Enforce a substantive physical review report for `task-review-execution` and `task-review-consent`. Previously, review records and owner consents could be injected from in-memory JSON packets alone (e.g. `--json-input`), allowing external callers to fabricate review entries or bypass physical report verification after reviewer process crashes.

This PR introduces `assertPhysicalReviewReport` in `buildCommand` for both `task-review-execution` and `task-review-consent`:
1. The associated Markdown report at `artifacts/reports/<stem>.md` must physically exist on disk; missing files reject with `review_report_missing`.
2. The report file must be non-empty, valid UTF-8, and contain at least one Markdown heading; empty files or crash outputs (such as provider error dumps) reject with `review_report_invalid`.
3. The check runs uniformly inside `buildCommand`, guarding both runtime workers and external/CLI callers.

- In `packages/daemon/src/reviewer-artifact-publication.ts`:
  - Added `reviewReportRelativePath(reviewId, dispatchId)` to resolve the canonical report path.

body:
**Origin:** Interactive session

`toLocaleString()` called with no locale argument silently formats using the runtime's locale
instead of the app's active UI language, and four accessible names were hardcoded English strings
that never went through `t()`. This PR adds `formatNumber()`/`formatDateTime()` helpers that read
the app's resolved i18n language, migrates every bare `toLocaleString()` call site (plus two
call sites that already passed the language explicitly, for consistency), translates the four
aria-labels, unifies three different inline separator glyphs onto one shared constant, adds an
ESLint rule banning direct `toLocale*()` calls, and extends the i18n-strings linter to catch
hardcoded JSX `aria-label`/`placeholder`/`alt`/`title` literals.

## What changed
- New `frontend/src/utils/format.ts`: `formatNumber(n, opts?)` and `formatDateTime(iso, opts?)`,
  both reading `i18n.resolvedLanguage ?? i18n.language` from the app's shared i18n instance
  (`src/i18n/index.ts`). `formatDateTime` defaults to `{ dateStyle: "medium", timeStyle: "short" }`
  because `Intl.DateTimeFormat` with no options renders date-only, unlike the legacy
  `Date.prototype.toLocaleString()` it replaces (verified with a Node repro before choosing the
  default). Also exports `FILTER_SEPARATOR = " · "`.
- Migrated all 14 bare `toLocaleString()` call sites named in the brief to `formatNumber`/
  `formatDateTime`: `NetworkTab.tsx` (2), `AnalysisTab.tsx`, `ReportTable.tsx`,
  `HeadwayQualityPanel.tsx`, `WeatherDelayPanel.tsx` (4), `RouteForecastSection.tsx`,
  `DailyChart.tsx`, `RichResult.tsx`, `StopEvidenceChart.tsx` (2), `CompactDataStatus.tsx`.
- Also migrated `AccountPage.tsx` and `AdminUserDetailPage.tsx` (2 call sites) — these already
  passed `i18n.language` explicitly, so behavior is unchanged, but leaving them on raw
  `toLocaleString()` would have tripped the new ESLint ban and left a second, inconsistent pattern
  in the codebase.
- F-26: translated the four hardcoded aria-labels — `ThreadSidebar.tsx` "More options" →
  `t("ask.sidebar.more_options_aria")`, `MarkdownMermaid.tsx` "diagram" →
  `t("admin.architecture.diagram_aria")`, `LimitPill.tsx` "decrement"/"increment" →
  `t("common.decrement_aria")`/`t("common.increment_aria")`. Added all four keys to both
  `en.json` and `ja.json`.
- F-29: `FILTER_SEPARATOR` replaces the fullwidth `" ・ "` (`ThreadSidebar.tsx`, 3 sites), the
  arrow `" ▸ "` (`FilterContextBar.tsx`), and inline `" · "` literals in `ReportsHomeTab.tsx`
  (3 sites) and `MapTab.tsx` (2 sites). Updated a stale comment in `FilterContextBar.tsx` that
  had documented the two files' separators as "intentionally different."
- F-30: `nav.prototype_section_label` in `ja.json` changed from the untranslated `"PROTOTYPE"` to
  `"プロトタイプ"`.
- `eslint.config.js`: added a second `no-restricted-syntax` selector,
  `CallExpression[callee.property.name=/^toLocale(String|DateString|TimeString)$/]`, pointing at
  `src/utils/format.ts`.
- `frontend/scripts/lint-i18n-strings.py`: refactored around a `find_violations(lines)` function
  returning `Violation(line, text, rule)` records (kept `lint_file()` as a thin file-reading
  wrapper), and added a `jsx-attribute` rule: a literal (non-expression) string on
  `aria-label=`/`placeholder=`/`alt=`/`title=` containing an ASCII letter, unless the line carries
  an `i18n-ignore` marker. Deliberately regex-matches only the quoted-literal form
  (`attr="..."`), so `attr={t(...)}`/`attr={\`...\`}` expression containers and an empty
  `alt=""` (decorative-image marker) are never flagged.
- `tests/unit/test_lint_i18n_strings.py` (new): 10 tests covering both rules (kana + jsx-attribute)
  and their `i18n-ignore` suppression, plus the empty-`alt`/non-ASCII-value exemptions.
- `frontend/src/utils/format.test.ts` (new): vitest coverage for both helpers under `ja`/`en`,
  option pass-through, invalid-date handling, and the default date+time behavior.
- Updated `AccountPage.test.tsx`/`AdminUserDetailPage.test.tsx`, which previously spied on
  `Date.prototype.toLocaleString` to assert the language argument — that assertion strategy no
  longer applies once the call site uses `formatDateTime`, so both now assert the rendered text
  contains `formatDateTime(...)`'s own output for the same input.

## Findings addressed
- F-26 — `ThreadSidebar.tsx`, `MarkdownMermaid.tsx`, `LimitPill.tsx` (×2) aria-labels translated.
- F-27 — all 14 named `toLocaleString()` call sites migrated to `formatNumber`/`formatDateTime`.
- F-29 — `FILTER_SEPARATOR` replaces 3 different separator glyphs across `ThreadSidebar.tsx`,
  `FilterContextBar.tsx`, `ReportsHomeTab.tsx`, `MapTab.tsx`.
- F-30 — `nav.prototype_section_label` given a Japanese value in `ja.json`.

## Verification (static only — no DB, no live data)
- `npm run typecheck` → clean.
- `npm run lint` → 0 errors, 4 pre-existing unrelated warnings (`MarkdownMermaid.tsx` fast-refresh,
  2× `any` in admin test files) — none introduced by this change; no `toLocale*` violations found.
- `npm run test` (full suite) → `624 passed (624)` across 107 files.
- `npm run lint:i18n` → `3 passed` (ja/en key parity, user-manual parity).
- `npm run lint:i18n-strings` → clean, no output.
- `npm run deadcode` (knip) → clean, 0 issues.
- `npm run build:bundle && npm run check:entry-chunk` → build succeeded; `check-entry-chunk: OK`

- `npm run test:check-entry-chunk` → `16 passed`.
- `DATABASE_URL=... GROQ_API_KEY=test-key PYTHONPATH=$PWD pytest tests/unit -k i18n` →

- `DATABASE_URL=... GROQ_API_KEY=test-key PYTHONPATH=$PWD pytest tests/unit` (full) →

- `ruff format --check` / `ruff check` on the two touched Python files → clean.
- `mypy` (repo root) → `Success: no issues found in 138 source files`.
- Not run: `tests/api`/`tests/pipeline`/`tests/db`/`tests/query` (DB-backed, out of scope per

author: marcioaltoe
body:
## Summary

Spec 0128 asked the release planner to accept bare stable tags. Every one of its Core Features shipped — in Spec 0147, authored as that whole content rather than a slice of it. Nothing in 0128 remains to build, and it has been sitting in `docs/specs/` as active work ever since, because nothing can move it:

```
$ roundfix archive 0128-release-planning-with-bare-stable-tags
Reason:
  Task Graph manifest ".../_tasks.md": file does not exist
```

That refusal is structural. Archive proves a Spec finished by reading completed Tasks and a passing gate; a Spec whose content another Spec delivered was never decomposed and cannot acquire either. Writing a Task Graph for shipped work would be a fiction and a gate over it would prove nothing. The only record today is a `## Disposition` paragraph written by hand into the PRD — accurate, and invisible to every command.

Carved from Spec 0129 Core Feature 2.

## What ships

`roundfix supersede --spec <slug> --by <slug> --reason <text>` writes `_supersession.md`: frontmatter carrying the superseding slug, the date and the reason. The PRD is left untouched, so intent and outcome can both be read afterwards. It refuses an unknown superseding Spec, a self-supersession, and a second supersession, and writes nothing when it refuses.

`roundfix archive` gains a second accepted proof: a recorded supersession, for a Spec with no Task Graph. Every other precondition stays in force, and a Spec that *has* a Task Graph keeps its existing evidence rules untouched.

## What review found

**A governance error of mine.** The first authorization claimed all of `internal/spec` was unbounded — but I had probed `spec.go`, `errors.go` and `task.go`, the files I predicted the work would touch, and not `archive.go`, which a prior authorization had bounded and which ADR-0130 therefore keeps governed. The QA gate caught it as QA-AUTH-PATHS. The maintainer granted the path, bounded to giving `Archive` a second proof. Estimating from a directory is the same mistake as estimating from reading code: the governed unit is the file.

**A check that did not check what it claimed.** `knownSpecDirectory` stated `_prd.md` and returned true if it wasn't a directory — nothing read the status — so `--by` naming a draft or malformed Spec was accepted as a deliverer that is "neither active nor archived", the exact condition the refusal advertises. Now validated by declared status, with distinct refusals per location.

**A contradiction between two of this Spec's own decisions.** Preserving the superseded PRD byte-identically means the supersession archive path stamps no metadata, so an archived Spec still reads `status: active` — and the deliverer check demanded `archived`. Reproduced end to end. The preserved PRD isn't the defect; the check now recognises a valid supersession record as the archive proof, without rewriting anything to make itself pass.

**The glossary check never ran.** `domain.md` makes it mandatory when work introduces a term. `CONTEXT.md` now defines supersession and its archive relationship.

## What this does not yet guarantee

Both reproduced, both stated in the PRD, both carried forward rather than taken as a third correction past the ceiling:

- **Archive trusts a well-formed record.** It checks that `_supersession.md` parses, not that the Spec it names exists, so a hand-written `superseded_by: missing` archives. The guarantee holds for records the command wrote. Closing it means moving deliverer validation out of `internal/cli` into a package archive can call — a layering change, not a one-line check.
- **`--reason help` is read as a help request.** The shared `commandWantsHelp` scan runs before flag parsing and matches a bare `help` anywhere in the arguments. Every command behaves this way (`roundfix archive help` prints usage); `--reason` is simply the first flag whose plausible value collides with it, so it is fixed for the whole surface or not at all.

## Verification

- `make verify` — green
- QA gate — verdict `pass`
- `roundfix spec check --strict` — no findings
- Exercised directly: the unknown, self, draft, malformed and double-supersession refusals; the archive-by-supersession path; an archived-by-supersession Spec reused as a deliverer with its PRD byte-identical afterwards

Retiring 0128 itself is deliberately a separate change — delivering the capability and using it are different commits.

The packaged integration skill now documents the consent-policy module from #92, but its v0.10.2 pin installs a tag without that module. Release v0.10.3 aligns all eleven version declarations with the merged module and records its actual behavior and host obligations.

Module merge: `c82358700fb6f2f22b462791825aaff3b7378d6f`. Release head: `ccc1dad9b9364c2bab4f11cc0c699b3eec6b28ad`. The coordinator will tag the release PR's merge commit, not the module merge.

- Correct README prose: the quick start reports a refused consent write and performs no retry; the host owns that retry under a fresh compatible decision. All 29 fenced Lua blocks in README/SKILL remain byte-identical to main (12 + 17).
- Describe strict fallback as a choice defaulted off, requiring an explicit grant. It still permits the host to ask using its own notice; it does not suppress the consent screen. Use the merged lower-case wire vocabulary and required `signature: null` contract.
- Enumerate the full twelve-item host-requirements list and state the closed-cache clock rollback and callback-progress limits.
- Record that the first resolver release emits no `SOFT_OPT_OUT` or non-empty `operation_blocks`. [#94](https://github.com/shardpilot/shardpilot-defold/issues/94) and [#95](https://github.com/shardpilot/shardpilot-defold/issues/95) gate the future release that makes them reachable. These are contract claims, not a deployment measurement.

author: kbwen
body:
Backlog **AVO-197**. Found while building AVO-193, verified, then fixed.

## The defect

Six animations in the office were dead. SMIL resolves `begin="0s"` against the *document* timeline, so an element mounted on a status change, a behaviour change or a poke is already past its active duration and snaps straight to its end value. Nothing errors, no console warning, and the markup reads correctly — which is how this survived five features shipping.

Worst case: AVO-135's *"one-shot celebratory flash"* was **mounted for 60 frames and visible on exactly 1**.

## The fix

`begin="indefinite"` parks each animation; a mount effect starts it with `beginElement()`. One small wrapper component, six call sites.

**Deliberately not a CSS rewrite,** even though AVO-193 used CSS and CSS would be easier to unit-test. AVO-136 and AVO-158 are `additive="sum"` transforms on a root `<g>` that already carries `translate(x,y) scale(CHAR_SCALE)`. A CSS `transform` would *replace* that base transform; the CSS `translate` property composes but applies *outside* it, silently changing how far the agent bobs. Both alternatives were measured working in a controlled experiment before being rejected on these grounds — the reasoning is in the work log.

**No duration, curve or `values` list is touched.** This is a repair, not a re-tune: changing the motion at the same time would make the before/after comparison meaningless.

## Evidence

Real browser, same instrument on both sides, counting distinct animated values across each animation's own duration (a snap yields 1–2; a real animation at ~60fps yields tens):

| animation | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| AVO-135 done flash | DEAD (2) | **PLAYS (43)** |
| AVO-158 poke bob | DEAD (2) | **PLAYS (21)** |
| AVO-136 desk-slam jitter | DEAD (1) | **PLAYS (26)** |
| AVO-134 behaviour pop | DEAD (2) | **PLAYS (19)** |
| AVO-110 reason pop | DEAD (2) | **PLAYS (22)** |
| event banner fade-in | DEAD (1) | **PLAYS (24)** |

The done flash goes from **1 visible frame to 39**, with its radius ramping 16.33 → 30.00 across 42 distinct values.

Frame strips (six frames per animation, before over after) were captured and sent to the owner; **this PR is held until they have seen them**, since it changes how five shipped features feel.

## Tests

`2512 passed (133 files)`, +10 in a new `tests/oneShotSmil.test.jsx`.

The unit tests deliberately **do not** assert that the animations play — believing markup was the original mistake, and SSR cannot run SMIL. They hold the wrapper's markup contract (`begin="indefinite"` added, no extra DOM node, every timing attribute preserved) plus a **regression guard** that fails if any one-shot is ever left unwrapped again, including a self-test proving the guard can fail.

Build, single-file build, `smoke` (4 viewports, 0 errors) and `smoke:panel` all pass.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## 功能说明
修复 Codex 会话恢复与凭据保全

- 凭据上传未确认时保留恢复材料；上传已提交但响应丢失时可安全重试。

## Summary
- Persist managed session homes until credential upload is acknowledged and retry recovery from daemon startup/heartbeat.
- Avoid account history copies for fresh sessions. Retain existing thread history for resume.
- Reinitialize only inactive, untracked, fully verified ready-only empty sessions; fail closed for real history and incomplete transcripts.
- Authorize original-account resume grants from redeemed source-session audit records, bound to the same Paws account and machine; reject cross-account fork fallback.
- Acknowledge a lost credential-update response only when the exact committed credentials and version prove an idempotent retry.

author: baltacavazos
body: ## Qué ve la persona El asesor laboral ya no empieza de cero cada vez que se abre el expediente. - Al volver, saluda como quien ya conoce a **esta persona** y a **este patrón**. - Recuerda lo que se platicó: documentos, riesgos y el siguiente paso. - Si se abre el chat en otro momento o se limpia el historial del celular, el saludo y la continuidad siguen saliendo del expediente, no solo de lo que quedó guardado en ese aparato. - Habla en español cálido, caso primero, sin tecnicismos. Nunca se presenta como Helios ni como abogado. Ejemplo de continuidad: > Hola de nuevo, María. Seguimos con tu caso frente a Empresa Norte. Ya platicamos de tu contrato. El siguiente paso que dejamos: subir el recibo. ¿Seguimos por ahí? ## Cómo quedó hecho Se extendió el contexto que ya usa el asesor (`buildHeliosCopilotContext`) con una capa durable, en lugar de inventar un chat paralelo. - Nueva tabla `case_advisor_memories`, acotada a **usuario + tenant + expediente**. Un caso no puede leer la memoria de otro ni cruzar tenants. - Cada pregunta actualiza esa memoria. El resumen lo hace **OpenAI `gpt-6-astra`** (regla permanente; no hay fallback a mini). - `cases.detail` y `cases.heliosCopilotChat` devuelven la memoria. El chat la inyecta al prompt. `/auditar` usa el saludo guardado y, si no hay historial local, retoma los últimos turnos. ## Pruebas - Caso A y caso B quedan aislados: la memoria de María/Empresa Norte no aparece en el expediente de Juan/Taller Sur. - Al recargar el detalle del caso A, sigue la memoria previa (saludo, hallazgos y turnos). - El resumen de memoria pide `gpt-6-astra` y rechaza modelos mini. ## Fuera de alcance No cambia planes ni precios. La memoria queda al servicio del expediente autenticado. El historial corto del aparato se conserva como complemento, no como fuente única.

author: jjiang193
body:
Answer the user's decision instead of displaying the instrument, and never show a stale or false number as if it were true. Everything here is arithmetic over rows that already existed: no new tables, no SCHEMA_VERSION bump, no requirements change, firmware untouched.

Backend
- Return what was stored and dropped at the API boundary: meal mean salinity and mg per 240 mL, the full label check (severity, ratio, headline, detail), per-day and today low/high ranges (sum of per-bite ranges), a per-product `sources` breakdown on /summary, `sample_age_s` on /api/spoon.
- The live label check judges the open meal's weight-averaged salinity, not the single bite, so the flag no longer flickers near 2x.
- A self-reported item is bounded at 5,000 mg and may not be in the future; `ts_utc`/`source` exist so Undo restores an entry on its original day and a seeded row stays seeded. Idle meals close on a 30 s timer, not only lazily.
- range=week is eight rows: the seven full days the averages cover, then today.
- seed: a topped-up day no longer writes its health reading twice.

Dashboard
- Trust layer: useTelemetry exposes spoonLive/silentForS/notFound/lastDip/ dipsNotCounted on the same single 200 ms flush; a spoon silent mid-meal is a critical banner with dashed-out sensor values and a paused projection; server unreachable, spoon silent, no spoon yet and busy elsewhere each have their own copy; the interlock banner is role="alert" at its true tier; the `?? 2300` fallbacks are gone; errors carry no URL path; Vite's proxy answers 502 rather than 500 when the backend is down.
- Patient Today leads with what is left (TodayHero, with the day's range and an over-limit state) and puts it in this bowl's terms (BowlCard: cups and spoonfuls that still fit, withheld while the label is in question). One alert slot at the top, the label declared only in SessionCard, one-tap "log again" for solids with bounds, confirm from 2,000 mg, labels and Undo. DailyMeter removed; LabelCheckCard is display-only.
- Clinician: "Where the sodium comes from" (measured and self-reported never merged, only a flagged product coloured), a meals table with the bowl's mean salinity and the server's label headline instead of a hard-coded "Consistent with label", every reason a patient surfaced, a "Today so far" tile, roster tiles that filter and count from the same rosterReasons as the chip, TargetEditor that accepts "1,800" and keeps its saved note.
- One time axis: today drawn faded as "today so far", day tooltips carry the range, and VitalsTimeline draws blood pressure and weight on the sodium chart's days in neutral ink - drawn, never interpreted.
- Per-view document.title, focus to the view heading on navigation, muted text at AA contrast, no type under 11px.

Docs: HANDOFF (state, new decisions with reasons, where things are), README, demo script and the telemetry contract updated to match.

author: edwarfonseca
body:
Implementa el componente `publisher/` completo: tareas T-PUB-001 a T-PUB-008
del roadmap, sobre los contratos ya definidos en `common/`.

## Qué incluye

| Archivo | Qué hace |
|---|---|
| `normalizer.py` | Extrae la lectura de `DemandaTiempoReal` y la reparte en las 5 zonas + SIN |
| `xm_client.py` | Cliente httpx async, 3 reintentos con backoff, excepciones del dominio |
| `simulator.py` | Paseo aleatorio acotado sobre curva circadiana + los 4 escenarios de stress |
| `source_selector.py` | Conmuta a simulador tras 3 fallos y reintenta XM con backoff 5/10/20/30 min |
| `main.py` | Bucle async: PUBLISH + XADD (MAXLEN 1000) + HSET (TTL 24h), cierre limpio |

Van 3 commits separados a propósito. El primero (`fix(tests)`) es
independiente del resto: si lo necesitan con urgencia, se puede tomar solo
ese sin mergear el Publisher.

## ⚠️ Arreglo que afecta a todo el equipo

**La suite de tests no corría. Ninguna, ni el smoke test de la Fase 0.**
`conftest.py` aplica los marcadores `unit` e `integration`, pero no estaban
declarados en `pyproject.toml` y con `--strict-markers` activo pytest
abortaba la colección entera con `INTERNALERROR`.

Se agrega también un filtro para la deprecación de `event_loop_policy` que
pytest-asyncio <1.0 dispara en Python >= 3.14, donde `filterwarnings = error`
la volvía un fallo. Sin eso la suite no arranca en Arch ni Fedora.

## Decisión de diseño que necesita visto bueno

El endpoint `DemandaTiempoReal` **solo publica el agregado nacional**: no trae
desglose por zona ni por recurso de generación, que es lo que pide el taller.

La solución fue un modelo de reparto explícito y documentado en
`normalizer.py`: cada zona consume una fracción fija de la demanda nacional, y
dentro de la zona la generación se despacha por orden de mérito real (primero
renovable no gestionable, luego hidráulica, y la térmica cubre el faltante).

**La magnitud del sistema sí es real cuando la fuente es XM; el reparto es un
modelo.** Conviene que quede dicho así en el documento técnico para no
presentarlo como dato medido. Si prefieren datos por zona reales, la vía es
`pydataxm`/SINERGOX detrás del flag `XM_USE_PYDATAXM`, que está previsto pero
no implementado.

## Dos comportamientos reales de la API de XM

Ambos verificados contra el endpoint en vivo y cubiertos con tests:

1. **El último punto de la serie llega con `"Valor": null`.** Tomar
   `Datos[-1]` a ciegas devuelve `None` y rompe aguas abajo.
2. **Hay una segunda serie, `"Pronóstico"`**, que es proyección y no debe
   publicarse como medición.

## Cómo probarlo

```bash
pip install -e ".[dev]"
pytest tests/unit -q          # 68 tests

# Modo simulador (no necesita internet)
FORCE_SOURCE=simulator PUBLISHER_INTERVAL_SECONDS=2 python -m publisher.main

# Modo automático, contra XM real
python -m publisher.main

# En otra terminal
redis-cli SUBSCRIBE energy-events
redis-cli HGETALL state:sin
redis-cli GET health:mode
```

Probado end-to-end contra XM real y Redis real: 6 eventos por ciclo, los tres
destinos escribiéndose, TTL correcto en los hashes y cierre limpio con
SIGTERM. `ruff` limpio y `mypy` sin errores en `publisher/`.

## Notas para cada uno

- **Alejandro**: al canal `energy-events` llega un JSON con el discriminador
  `type: "tick"` más la estructura del `Event` de `common/models.py`. También
  se emite `type: "source_switch"` cuando cambia la fuente.
- **David**: para el banner, `health:mode` vale `real` o `simulator`, y
  `health:failures` permite distinguir el estado DEGRADADO (modo real pero con
  fallos acumulados).
- **Jonathan**: el publisher arranca con `python -m publisher.main` y solo
  necesita `REDIS_URL`. Listo para el `Dockerfile.publisher`.

## Fuera de alcance / detectado pero no tocado

Cosas preexistentes que no modifiqué por estar fuera de mi componente:

- `common/config.py:125` falla `mypy`.
- `[tool.mypy]` declara `discover_untyped_supports`, que no es una opción real.
- `ruff check .` reporta 39 errores en código previo.
- El formatter de logs imprime la hora con doble `Z` (`...T22:30:54ZZ`).

author: deonmenezes
body:
## What gap this closes

Recurring maintenance run on the Mantis detection stack. While reviewing the DLP/secrets-handling code (`.codex/mcp-servers/findings/server.js` and `.codex/mcp-servers/http-audit/server.js`), I found the two servers each kept their **own copy** of the "does this look like a raw secret" pattern list, and the copies had drifted:

- `http-audit`'s `redactValue()` (used to build evidence packs) redacted: AWS keys, GitHub tokens, Slack tokens, JWTs, PEM private keys, `user:pass@` URLs, **and** generically-named `token=`/`api_key=`/`password=`/etc. query/form params.
- `findings/server.js`'s `scanForSecrets()` guard (which decides whether `finding_create`/`finding_update` **refuses** a payload outright, per PRD section 9/11) only covered AWS keys, GitHub tokens, Slack tokens, JWTs, and PEM key headers.

Net effect: a finding/update payload containing something like `?api_key=live_abcdef...` in a claim or evidence string would be **accepted** by the findings guard even though `http_audit` would have redacted that exact string. That's a false-negative in the tool's own safety backstop — the weaker of the two checks is the one that actually gates writes into the append-only findings log.

Neither list covered several very common real-world credential shapes either: Google API keys, Stripe keys, Anthropic/OpenAI API keys, npm tokens, SendGrid keys, GitLab tokens, AWS STS (`ASIA...`) keys, or Slack webhook URLs.

## What changed

- Added `.codex/mcp-servers/lib/secret_patterns.js`: a single shared pattern list (`SECRET_VALUE_PATTERNS`) with `redactSecrets()` (replace-based, for `http-audit`) and `containsSecret()` (boolean guard, for `findings`) built on top of it, plus the additional credential shapes above.
- `http-audit/server.js` and `findings/server.js` now both delegate to this shared module instead of keeping forked copies, so the redactor and the refusal guard can no longer silently diverge.
- Added `.codex/mcp-servers/lib/secret_patterns.test.js` (Node's built-in `node --test`, zero dependencies, matching this directory's existing "pure Node" style) covering every pattern shape, PEM bodies, `user:pass@` URLs, generic key=value params, non-string inputs, and regex-statefulness (shared `g`-flag regex objects reused across `.test()` calls needed an explicit `lastIndex` reset in `containsSecret`, which the tests pin down).

Verified: `node --test .codex/mcp-servers/lib/secret_patterns.test.js` (6/6 passing), `node -c` on all three touched/added server files, and `prettier --write` per the repo's `.prettierrc.toml`.

Scope was kept intentionally small — this is a targeted parity/coverage fix in the DLP backstop, not a rewrite of the findings or http-audit servers.

## Scan findings (authorized target)

author: mmtigers
body:
Closes #747

#792 でステップ1（検知）とステップ2（NOT NULL 化）を済ませ、`PRAGMA foreign_key_check` が使えるようになったので、ステップ3の FK 追加を行う。

> ⚠️ **マージしても実機には自動適用されません。** Issue 本文の「テーブル再作成は DB をロックするため**バックアップ直後のタイミングで行うこと**」に従い、実機への反映（`git pull` + `systemctl restart`）は **04:00 の DB バックアップ直後**に行う想定です。

---

## 対象を実機データで確定しました（当初案から縮小）

候補11関係すべての孤児行を実機で実測し、**張ってよいものだけ**に絞りました。

### 張るもの（6関係・いずれも孤児0件）

```
quest_history.user_id / reward_history.user_id / user_inventory.user_id /
routine_progress.user_id / routine_step_events.user_id /
quest_cancellation_audit.user_id   →   quest_users.user_id
```

`ON DELETE` は既定（NO ACTION）です。リポジトリ内に `DELETE FROM quest_users` は存在せず、`admin/reset_user` も残高をゼロ化するだけで行は消しません。ユーザー行が消えるとすれば異常な操作なので、**静かに孤児を作らずその場で失敗させる**のが狙いです。

### 意図的に張らないもの

| 関係 | 理由 |
| --- | --- |
| `quest_history.quest_id` → `quest_master`（実機 **1,219行**） | `sync_master_data` が退役クエストをマスタから消しても、`quest_title` を非正規化保持して履歴を残す設計。RESTRICT では**退役が永久にできなくなり**、CASCADE では**家族の記録が消える**（#762 と衝突） |
| `reward_history.reward_id` → `reward_master`（実機 1行） | 同上 |
| `quest_cancellation_audit.history_id` → `quest_history` | 監査行は**削除された履歴の控えそのもの**。`approval_service` は監査行を書いてから履歴を DELETE するため、FK を張ると**取消フローがその場で壊れる** |
| `quest_history.linked_history_id` → `quest_history`（自己参照） | 兄妹連携の履歴は**相互に**指し合う（実機で `3632 ↔ 3633` を確認）。取消は主履歴 → 相方の順に削除するため、RESTRICT では最初の DELETE が相方からの参照で失敗する |

後ろ2つは Issue のコメントで「張る」と書いていたものを、実装中に**取り下げた**ものです。`quest_cancellation_audit` は当時0行だったため孤児検査が素通りしており、自己参照の相互リンクも測定していませんでした。

この整理は `health_watch` チェック11 の2層構成（`_ORPHAN_CHECKS_STRICT` は通知 / `_ORPHAN_CHECKS_EXPECTED` は記録のみ）と対応しており、`migrations/README.md` に方針として残しました。

## 検証：本番DBのコピーでリハーサル

6テーブルすべてについて、**列定義・索引・行数・全行のデータ**が適用前後で完全一致することを確認しました。

```
quest_history:            3408 行 / 索引 2 / FK [('quest_users', 'user_id', ...)]
reward_history:            595 行 / 索引 1 / FK [...]
user_inventory:            571 行 / 索引 2 / FK [reward_master, quest_users]  ← 既存FKも維持
routine_progress:           60 行 / 索引 1 / FK [...]
routine_step_events:        99 行 / 索引 2 / FK [...]
quest_cancellation_audit:    0 行 / 索引 2 / FK [...]

integrity_check: ok
foreign_key_check: 違反なし
```

FK が実際に効くこと、そして**張らない関係が従来どおり動く**ことも確認しています。

| 操作 | 結果 |
| --- | --- |
| 未知ユーザーの履歴を挿入 | `IntegrityError`（FK が効く） |
| 参照が残るユーザーを削除 | `IntegrityError`（FK が効く） |
| マスタに無い `quest_id` の履歴を挿入 | **成功**（退役後も履歴を残せる） |
| 監査行を書いてから履歴を削除 | **成功**（取消フローが壊れない） |

## そのほか

- `init_unified_db.validate_schema_integrity` の `expected_schemas` から `users` / `quests` を削除しました。#792 で DROP したのにリストに残っており、**起動のたびに `⚠️ Schema Integrity Issue: Missing Table: users` の警告**が出ていました
- `pytest tests/`: **1914 passed**。FK により孤児行を作れなくなったため、`check_orphaned_rows` の回帰テストは `PRAGMA foreign_keys=OFF` で「FK を迂回して壊れた DB」を再現する形に変更しました（手動SQL・FK導入前の残存行などを想定した検知機能なので、テスト自体は残す価値があります）
- 仕様書ドリフト: 検知事項なし / ruff: 新規指摘なし

body:
## Why it is not needed

`MarvinJsModule` was imported in `app.module.ts` but `<app-marvin-js-editor>` appears in no template, so the editor never rendered. The only things that consumed the package were the `assets`/`styles`/`scripts` entries in `angular.json` (which copied the MarvinJS distribution into `assets/marvin-js/` and bundled `marvinjslauncher.js`, `util.js`, `webservices.js` into `scripts.js`) and the `MarvinJsEditorComponent` that called `MarvinJSUtil.getEditor` on an iframe pointing at `/demo.html`. That iframe URL was only proxied in `proxy.conf.json` for `ng serve`; in the nginx image `/demo.html` falls through to `index.html`, so the editor could not have worked in a deployed container even where it was reachable.

The fleet moved to Ketcher (served through the `/ketcher` proxy) for the structure editor. This PR removes the leftover MarvinJS/Chemaxon plumbing so the repo no longer needs a Chemaxon license, the `NPM_TOKEN` secret, or the Chemaxon Artifactory registry.

## What changes

- `.github/workflows/docker.yml`
- `.npmrc` (deleted)
- `README.md`
- `angular.json`
- `docker-compose.marvin.yaml` (deleted)
- `package-lock.json`
- `package.json`
- `proxy.conf.json`
- `src/app/app.module.ts`
- `src/app/components/somn/marvinjs/index.ts` (deleted)
- `src/app/components/somn/marvinjs/marvinjs-editor.component.ts` (deleted)
- `src/app/components/somn/marvinjs/marvinjs.d.ts` (deleted)
- `src/app/components/somn/marvinjs/marvinjs.module.ts` (deleted)

- `package.json`: `@chemaxon/marvinjs` removed.
- `package-lock.json`: its entry removed, and 262 `resolved` URLs that pointed at `hub.chemaxon.com:443/artifactory/api/npm/npm/` (the Artifactory *proxy* of npmjs, which the old `.npmrc` had made the default registry) repointed at `registry.npmjs.org`. Tarballs and `integrity` hashes are unchanged; Artifactory serves npmjs tarballs byte-for-byte, and `npm ci` verifies every hash.
- `angular.json`: the 12 MarvinJS `assets`/`styles`/`scripts` entries (6 per configuration).
- `.npmrc`: Chemaxon registry lines removed (file deleted; nothing else was in it).
- Workflows: the `hub.chemaxon.com` auth line and its `NPM_TOKEN` comment. Where that line was the only thing creating `$HOME/.npmrc`, it is replaced by `touch $HOME/.npmrc` so the Docker build secret mount still has a file.
- `docker-compose.marvin.yaml`, the MarvinJS backend entries in `proxy.conf.json`, the README's Chemaxon registry setup block.
- The MarvinJS editor component (`marvinjs/` directory: editor component, module, type declarations) and its `MarvinJsModule` registration in `app.module.ts`, since it existed only to host the package.

## Verification

`npm ci --userconfig /dev/null` (no registry credentials at all) followed by `ng build` succeeds locally on this branch (Angular 15, webpack builder): every repointed tarball downloaded from npmjs with its original integrity hash, and the production bundle builds without the MarvinJS scripts. `grep -rl chemaxon` over the repo (excluding `node_modules`, `dist`, `.git`) is empty.

## After merge

The `NPM_TOKEN` repository secret is no longer referenced by any workflow and can be deleted.

author: tripandcode
body:
**Origin:** Interactive session

27+ z-index literals were picked ad hoc per component, so nothing told a new overlay where it stood
relative to the rest — `HelpHint`'s fixed toast (`drawerBackdrop - 1` = 299) sat above several
"modal" overlays whose old literals (80, 100, 200) were all below it. Extend the shared `Z_INDEX`
ladder to cover every stacking tier, mirror it as `--z-*` custom properties in `global.css`, replace
every hardcoded literal with the matching rung, define two undefined CSS custom properties, drop
three unused ones, and add a static CI check so this can't silently drift again.

## What changed
- `frontend/src/styles/zIndex.ts`: extended `Z_INDEX` from 2 keys to the full 13-rung ladder (`base`,
  `raised`, `mapOverlay`, `dropdown`, `popover`, `sticky`, `tooltip`, `drawerBackdrop`, `drawer`,
  `modalBackdrop`, `modal`, `contextMenu`, `toast`). Documents why `contextMenu` (500) intentionally
  outranks `modal`/`modalBackdrop` (400/401): a context menu can be opened from inside a modal and
  must render above it.
- `frontend/src/styles/global.css`: added a `--z-*` mirror of every `Z_INDEX` rung in `:root`.
- `frontend/src/styles/zIndex.test.ts` (new): asserts every `Z_INDEX` key has a matching `--z-<kebab>`
  entry in `global.css` with the same value, so the two can't drift apart again.
- Replaced every hardcoded `zIndex`/`z-index` literal (21 in TSX/TS, 11 in CSS) across
  `ThreadSidebar`, `OnboardingGate`, `PeakHourModal`, `AdminAgenciesPage`, `RouteForecastSection`,
  `RangeBadge`, `TabFilterBar`, `InsightHint`, `AgencyPicker`, `SidebarUserMenu`, `PresetMenu`,
  `LimitPill`, `SegmentedPill`, `SettingsDrawer`, `MapStyleControl`, the landing-page preview
  components, `global.css`, `overview.css`, `investigation.css`, `stopEvidence.css`,
  `operationsMap.css`, and `RoutePickerPill.css` with the matching `Z_INDEX`/`var(--z-*)` rung.
- `frontend/src/pages/admin/AdminOpsPage.tsx`: `var(--radius-md)` (undefined) → `var(--radius-lg)`.
- `frontend/src/components/RouteForecastSection.tsx`: `var(--text-2, var(--text-secondary))` →
  `var(--text-secondary)` directly (`--text-2` was undefined, only ever used with this fallback).
- `frontend/src/styles/global.css`: removed `--bg-soft-hover`, `--space-5`, `--space-6` (both theme
  blocks) — zero remaining `var(...)` references to any of the three.
- `frontend/scripts/check-css-tokens.mjs` (new): scans `src/**/*.{css,tsx,ts}` and fails if a
  `var(--x)` reference has no fallback and no matching declaration in `global.css`, or if a CSS
  `z-index:` declaration is anything other than `var(--z-*)`. Wired as `npm run check:css-tokens`.
- `tests/frontend/check_css_tokens.test.mjs` (new): 7 fixture-based positive/negative cases for the
  script above, mirroring `check_entry_chunk.test.mjs`'s pattern. Wired as `npm run
  test:check-css-tokens`.
- `frontend/eslint.config.js`: added a `no-restricted-syntax` rule forbidding a `Literal` value on a
  `zIndex` object property (message points at `Z_INDEX`).
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: added "CSS tokens checker unit tests" (`npm run test:check-css-tokens`)
  and "CSS tokens check" (`npm run check:css-tokens`) steps to the `frontend` job.

## Findings addressed
- F-54 (z-index ladder) — `frontend/src/styles/zIndex.ts`, `global.css` mirror, all listed call
  sites converted to `Z_INDEX`/`var(--z-*)`.
- F-56 (undefined tokens) — `AdminOpsPage.tsx` (`--radius-md` → `--radius-lg`),
  `RouteForecastSection.tsx` (`--text-2` → `--text-secondary`).
- F-57 (stray tokens) — removed `--bg-soft-hover`, `--space-5`, `--space-6` from `global.css` (both
  theme blocks). `--below`, `--github`, `--google`, `--local` were **not** real custom properties
  anywhere in the codebase (see Observations) — nothing to remove for those three.

## Verification (static only — no DB, no live data)
- `npx vitest run src/styles/zIndex.test.ts` → RED (2 failed, `--z-drawer-backdrop`/`--z-drawer`
  missing) before the mirror was added; GREEN (13 passed) after.
- `node --test tests/frontend/check_css_tokens.test.mjs` → RED (7 failed, script missing) before
  `check-css-tokens.mjs` was written; GREEN (7 passed) after.
- `npm run typecheck` → clean (exit 0).
- `npm run lint` → 0 errors, 4 pre-existing warnings unrelated to this change (`any` in two admin
  test files, one `react-refresh` fast-refresh warning in `MarkdownMermaid.tsx`).
- `npm run test` → 107 test files, 629 tests passed (jsdom `HTMLCanvasElement.getContext` console
  noise from an unrelated landing-page animation hook is pre-existing, not a failure).
- `npm run lint:i18n` → clean (exit 0).
- `npm run lint:i18n-strings` → clean (exit 0).
- `npm run deadcode` → clean (exit 0).
- `npm run check:css-tokens` → OK, 287 files scanned, no undefined `var(--x)`, no non-ladder
  `z-index`.
- `npm run build:bundle && npm run check:entry-chunk` → build succeeded (pre-existing >500kB chunk

  stays out of the entry closure (505.0 KiB, within budget).
- Not run: DB-backed suites (`tests/api`, `tests/pipeline`, `tests/db`, `tests/query`) — this task

author: clevervi
body:
## What changed

An issuer write now records **which grant authorised it**, not merely that one
did. `lifecycle_event.grant_id` has existed since the column was designed for
this; nothing wrote it.

## Why

Refs #152 — the fifth of its five acceptance criteria. The other four shipped in
#155, which carried no closing keyword; checking whether the issue should close
found a better reason to leave it open.

`registerProduct` reads the grants an actor holds, refuses unless one is an
`issuer` grant over the named organization, and then threw the grant away. The
event recorded `actor_kind: 'issuer'` — a claim about a **capacity**, a role.
ADR 0011 §3 asks for the **authority**.

Measured against the development database before this shipped:

```
actor_kind=issuer events: 8133, of those with grant_id: 0
```

The authorisation was correct and left no evidence of itself. That is invisible
until it is needed: a grant is revoked or expires, `grantsHeldAt` will never
return it again, and an event saying only `issuer` can no longer be traced to
what permitted it — or show that anything did.

## The decision worth challenging

`RecordingActor` gains `grantId: number | null` — **required and nullable**,
not optional.

Optional compiles everywhere and lets a future write path omit it, landing
another null nobody decided on, which is exactly how the current 8,133 got
there. Required forces every call site to answer, and TypeScript named all 26 of
them instead of leaving them to be discovered.

**`null` is a real answer.** A holder enrolment is somebody entering a serial on
nobody's authority: no organization, no capacity claimed, no grant to name. So

- `grant_id IS NULL` on a `holder` event means *none was needed*;
- the same null on an `issuer` event means *the record lost something*.

Both readings had to stay available, which is why there is a test for each.
Asserting only the issuer half would pass against an implementation that wrote a
grant onto everything.

## `.some()` became `.find()`

The grant that decides is the grant that is recorded. Asking a second time would
be asking at a second instant, and the two can disagree.

## Mutations

| Mutation | Named test that went red |
| --- | --- |
| the grant is not written at all (`grantId: null` in `insertProduct`) | `records which grant authorised the write` |
| the wrong grant is chosen (`held[0]` instead of the matching capacity) | `records which grant authorised the write` |
| an enrolment is given a grant it never had | `records no grant for an enrolment` |

All three restored to green.

**The second mutation required changing a fixture to be detectable at all.**
`authorised` held exactly one grant, so `held[0]` and "the grant matching
`issuer`" were the same row and the mutant survived. It now holds two grants
over the same organization with the `authority` one written **first**, because
`grantsHeldAt` orders by id. A test that cannot tell the right grant from the
first one is not testing the thing it names.

The assertion is also two-sided for the same reason: `toBe(held.id)` alone would
pass against an implementation writing any non-null number, and `not.toBeNull()`
alone would pass against one writing somebody else's grant.

## The measurement was wrong again, for the fifth time in this series

The third mutation first reported `NOT CAUGHT`. The patch replaced the string
`grantId: null`, and the **first occurrence in the file is inside a comment** —
so it mutated the prose explaining why null is correct and left the code alone.
A test that caught the mutation perfectly was reported as worthless.

Recorded because the pattern is now unmistakable: in this series the measurement
has been wrong five times and the guard zero times.

## Found by the review, filed rather than fixed here

**The grant is validated at one instant and recorded at another.**
`grantsHeldAt` is called with `new Date()` — this process's clock — while
`insertProduct` stamps `occurred_at` with the database's `now()`, inside a
transaction the lookup has already returned from. A grant revoked in that window
produces an event whose `occurred_at` is later than the moment its own
`grant_id` stopped being valid.

Before this change the grant was a boolean that vanished, so a stale read
produced a write that should not have happened. **Naming the grant is what turns
it into a claim in the permanent record**, which is why this pull request is
where it surfaced. It is #174, and the call site now says so rather than leaving
the next reader to find it.

Not fixed here because every option moves the boundary between `apps/api` and
`packages/db`, and `changeProductStatus` will ask the same question the moment
it records a grant — so it should be decided once, with the rejected options
written down.

## What is deliberately not here

A database constraint making an issuer event without a grant impossible. That is
the structural version of this guarantee — the code-level fix depends on one
call site being written correctly, forever.

It would break 23 fixtures across 7 files that write issuer events, each of which
would need a real `capacity_grant`. That is a separate argument and it is the
one #153 is already circling: *the API requires an actor, the database does not.*
Commented there rather than folded in here.

## Existing rows

They stay `NULL`. History is append-only, and backfilling would mean inventing a
grant for acts recorded before anything was pinned. `grant_id IS NULL` on an
issuer event means "recorded before this landed", and that is written down in the
schema rather than left for somebody to infer.

## Tests

`pnpm test`: 458 in `packages/db`, 146 in `apps/api` (+2), 121 in `apps/web`.
Four consecutive clean runs of the full monorepo suite.

**One thing I cannot account for.** The first full run after the mutation script
finished reported 6 failures in `packages/db`, and my own grep dropped the test
names before I saw them.

Chased rather than re-run until it went away: **20 runs of `packages/db` alone,
full output captured each time, 20 passed and 0 failed.** That is the honest
claim — twenty captured runs did not reproduce it — and it is a different
statement from "it passes now". The cause is unidentified. If it returns it will
have names, because the output is no longer being filtered before anybody reads
it.

## Security impact

Positive and narrow. Nothing new is trusted from a request: `grantId` comes from
the grant lookup and cannot be supplied by a caller. What changes is that a
revoked grant's role in past acts stops being unrecoverable.

## Breaking changes

`RecordingActor` gains a required field. Internal to the workspace; every call
site is in this diff.

---

- [ ] CI is green
- [x] `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test` and `pnpm build` pass locally
- [x] `pnpm-lock.yaml` — no dependency changed
- [x] No secrets, keys or production data in the diff
- [x] Documentation updated if behaviour changed — the reasoning sits on the
      field and on the event write, next to the code

author: christiangrogers
body:
This pull request introduces a comprehensive set of improvements to the project's GitHub repository configuration, focusing on issue reporting, code review routing, pull request guidance, and continuous integration (CI) reliability. The changes aim to streamline collaboration, clarify responsibilities, and ensure robust quality checks before releases reach end users.

**Issue Reporting Improvements:**

* Added a dedicated annotator bug report template (`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/annotator-report.yml`) to guide annotators in reporting issues with the SegQueue module, including structured prompts for version, case, frequency, and blocking status.
* Introduced a general bug report template (`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug.yml`) for defects in the server, training pipeline, or CI, with prompts to specify affected components, reproduction steps, and environment details.
* Created a configuration file (`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml`) enabling blank issues and providing direct links to key documentation for installation, server operation, and model training.

**Code Review and Ownership:**

* Established a CODEOWNERS file (`.github/CODEOWNERS`) to enforce review routing, ensuring that changes to critical paths (e.g., `src/segqueue/`, `slicer/`, `server/`) are reviewed by the designated owner before merging.

**Pull Request and CI Process Enhancements:**

* Added a pull request template (`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`) that prompts contributors to explain changes from the user perspective, justify the reasoning, and verify testing steps, with special attention to compatibility and versioning for the labelling app.
* Overhauled the CI workflow (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) to clarify job purposes, enforce branch naming conventions, and add robust checks for linting, testing, Slicer compatibility, server integration, and end-to-end acceptance. The workflow ensures that only well-tested changes can reach `main`, which triggers releases.
* Updated the release workflow (`.github/workflows/segqueue-release.yml`) to always run the portability test (`tests/test_segqueue_portability.py`), ensuring the shared package remains compatible with Python 3.9 and Slicer's environment.

These changes collectively improve the reliability of releases, the clarity of collaboration, and the user experience for both annotators and operators.

author: abhishek9639
body:
Refs #7576

The rest of group 5 from #7576, following #7596. With this the list in the issue is finished.

## Proposed Changes

  - `examples/transpose/*`: carry the matrix order, the tile and block sizes and the loop indices as `std::size_t`.

## Any background context you want to provide?

Every one of these files looks like this:

```cpp
std::uint64_t order = vm["matrix_size"].as<std::uint64_t>();
// ...
std::vector<double> A(order * order);
for (std::uint64_t i = 0; i < order; ++i)
    A[i * order + j] = ...;
```

The values size and index a `std::vector<double>`, so they are `std::size_t`. Two things deliberately stay `std::uint64_t`.

**The reported byte count.** Each file has

```cpp
std::uint64_t bytes =
    static_cast<std::uint64_t>(2 * sizeof(double) * order * order);
```

which multiplies in 64 bits today only because `order` is a `std::uint64_t`. Once `order` is as wide as `std::size_t`, that product would be computed in 32 bits on a 32 bit host and overflow before the cast ever ran, so the first factor is widened instead:

```cpp
std::uint64_t bytes =
    2 * sizeof(double) * static_cast<std::uint64_t>(order) * order;
```

I checked it rather than assuming, with `std::uint32_t` standing in for a 32 bit `std::size_t`:

```
order=1024     old=16777216        new=16777216        same
order=100000   old=160000000000    new=160000000000    same
order=1000000  old=16000000000000  new=16000000000000  same
```

The last of those is well past what a 32 bit multiply would hold.

**The serialized types in the two component based variants.** `sub_block::size_` is written to an archive with `ar & size_`, and the arguments of `get_sub_block` and of the `block_component` constructor travel with the action. Their type decides the wire format rather than the host, so they stay `std::uint64_t` for the same reason the serialization module keeps its sizes at a fixed width, and they are converted where they become a memory size:

```cpp
sub_block get_sub_block(std::uint64_t offset, std::uint64_t size)
{
    HPX_ASSERT(!data_.empty());
    return sub_block(&data_[static_cast<std::size_t>(offset)], size);
}
```

That is the same shape as #7594, which felt like the right thing for an example to be demonstrating.

### A file that reports no warnings today

`transpose_await.cpp` is built only when its own CMake condition holds, so it contributes nothing to the 1586 while having the identical structure. It is converted too rather than left as the odd one out in its own directory.

### Verification

The 32 bit job here is the check for the warnings. Beyond the byte count above, I re-ran the check from #7596 over every file touched, comparing each `("name", value<T>())` declaration against its `vm["name"].as<U>()`, since a mismatch there fails at startup rather than at compile time. No mismatches, and the includes line up.

## Checklist

Not all points below apply to all pull requests.

- [ ] I have added a new feature and have added tests to go along with it.
- [ ] I have fixed a bug and have added a regression test.
- [ ] I have added a test using random numbers; I have made sure it uses a seed, and that random numbers generated are valid inputs for the tests.

author: michel-onstein
body:
Inside a terminal reply's string, an OSC, DCS or APC, the detector forwards every byte without looking for the escape key until a `BEL` or ST arrives. An earlier fix added a 100 ms idle timeout so that Alt+`_`, which sends the same two bytes as an APC introducer, does not leave command mode deaf.

That timeout only fires once the bytes stop, which an adversary simply does not do. A remote can set a multi-megabyte clipboard with OSC 52 and query it back in a loop: the terminal streams one enormous, continuously arriving reply, the detector never goes idle, and `Ctrl-] Ctrl-] d` is swallowed into the string and forwarded to the attacker. The session then cannot be detached without killing the terminal, and keys meant as local commands go to the remote.

So the string state is bounded by bytes as well as by silence: past 64 KiB it is abandoned and keys are heard again. Real replies are far smaller, and a clipboard read that is genuinely larger loses nothing but its tail.

Tested: `scripts/verify.sh` passes, covering fmt, clippy with `-D warnings` on both targets, the full suite, shellcheck and markdownlint. New tests: an unterminated OSC arriving without a pause no longer swallows the command key, and an ordinary reply is still read as a string with the command key working immediately after it. The first was confirmed to fail without the cap.

author: arena-ai-coding-agent[bot]
body:
## 團長回報

> 「但為什麼我無痕和普通視窗還是同步不到，更過份的是我登入帳戶後 老說我沒有後端，我沒有後端如何登入」
> 「另外我需要瘦身」

## 真正死因：三個環，唔係一個

### ① 單據相片「直上 Drive」由頭到尾都未行得通 ← 呢個先係資料庫變大嘅源頭

`api/proxy.js` 嘅 `ALLOWED_ACTIONS` **漏咗 `uploadPhotos`**。代理一律回 `400 不支援的操作`
→ `finance.js` 嘅 `if (up?.ok)` 永遠 false → 跌返落「本地存做後備」
→ 每張單據相以 **base64 `dataUrl` 寫入 `db.claims[].photos[].dataUrl`**（base64 脹大約 33%）。

> 所以「單據係直上 Drive 嘅設計，點解會大過 4.5MB」—— 因為條 Drive 路喺正式站上面
> **一次都未行通**。後端 `Code.gs` 由 v2.3.0 起一直有 `uploadPhotos`（`tests/gas.mjs` 有測），
> 錯嘅係代理白名單。測試捉唔到，因為測試全部直打假 GAS，冇一個經代理白名單。

### ② 資料庫大過 Vercel 4.5MB 回應上限 → `loadDb` 回 500 純文字

Vercel 爆上限時回嘅係純文字 `FUNCTION_RESPONSE_PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE`，唔係 JSON。

> **更正上一輪嘅錯誤講法**：呢種情況**唔會**跌落自助路線變「未設定後端網址」。
> `postJson` 只在 `status===404` 或者回應係 HTML 嗰陣先 set `noApi:true`；
> 500 純文字兩樣都唔係 → `noApi:false` → `postBackend` 直接 return。
> 真正會講「未設定後端網址」嘅係另一條路（`/api/proxy` 真的 404／回 HTML）。
> 兩條路都係「把真正死因蓋住」，今次一齊修。

### ③ 每部機讀唔到後端 → 各自儲存自己嗰份 → 兩邊永遠對唔到料

## 改咗乜

| 檔 | 改動 |
|---|---|
| `api/proxy.js` | ★ 白名單加 `uploadPhotos` ＋ `loadDbPart`；刪死碼 `BIG_BODY_ACTIONS`（由頭到尾冇被讀過） |
| `gastemplate.js` → `Code.gs` **v2.6.0** | 新 action `loadDbPart`（每段 1,000,000 字，每段帶 version）；抽出 `dbRawText()` 做 `loadDb`／`loadDbPart` **共用嘅唯一讀法**；`SUPPORTED_ACTIONS` 改陣列（舊嘅手寫字串漏咗 `constitution`） |
| `lib/remote.js` | `pullDbSegmented()`（逐段拼、version 撞咗由頭再讀、段號超範圍明確報錯）；`pullDb({bytes})`；`remoteDiagnose()` 加「整份資料庫讀取」一格 |
| `lib/gateway.js` | `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE_RE` ＋ `reason:'too_large'`，**一定唔會**跌落自助路線；錯誤訊息直接講 4.5MB 同分段讀 |
| `dev-server.mjs` | 本機模擬 Vercel 4.5MB 回應上限（實測：3MB→200 JSON，6MB→500 純文字） |
| `scripts/lint.mjs`（新） | 零依賴：語法／JSON／HTML 引用／**代理白名單 vs 前端實送 action**／`SUPPORTED_ACTIONS` 一致性／`.vercelignore` 審計＋部署清單 |
| `package.json` | 加 `lint`／`build`／`check`（之前**三個都唔存在**） |

**點解唔係「先問體積先決定」**：`dbInfo` 喺後端內部會行一次 `loadDb`，每次開機多問一次
＝ 白燒一倍 GAS 配額。所以 `pullDb()` 預設先試單一讀，失敗先退去分段；
只有呼叫者已知體積（`pullDb({bytes})`）先直接分段。

## 部署瘦身

| 項目 | 之前 | 而家 |
|---|---|---|
| `.vercelignore` | **冇** | 有 |
| 部署上傳 | 125 檔 · 2,427 KB | **73 檔 · 1,494 KB**（排除 38%） |
| Vercel `npm ci` | 裝埋 jsdom（16 MB） | `--omit=dev`，**零套件** |
| 死重檔 | 根目錄有個名叫 `\|` 嘅檔（1,879 B，內容係一次 grep 輸出） | 已 `git rm` |

排除：`tests/`(555KB)、`docs/`(233KB)、`apps-script/`(78KB，生成物 —— APP 內「下載 Code.gs」係瀏覽器即刻生成，**唔會** fetch 呢個檔)、`README.md`、`MD`、`DEPLOY_GUIDE_FOR_TROOPS.md`、`dev-server.mjs`、`*.bak/*.tmp/*.old/*.log`、`.env*`。

**注意**：repo 本身得 2.37 MB，而且**一個圖片檔都冇**（UI 全部 inline SVG）。
所以「Vercel 儲存空間爆滿」唔會係靜態產物引起 —— 真正食空間嘅係
**Google Sheet「資料庫」分頁 ＋ Drive 入面嘅單據相**。

## 測試

`npm run check`（lint → build → test）exit 0。**1,976 → 2,037 通過 / 0 失敗**（+61）；lint 14/0。

- `tests/gas.mjs` 92→**114**：真係行生成出嚟嘅 `Code.gs`。5MB 資料庫 → 分件寫入 →
  `loadDbPart` 逐段讀返 → 拼埋 parse 得到、同成份 `loadDb` 同一個 version／bytes；
  段號超範圍明確報錯；負數 `partIdx`；空後端 `found:false`；分段讀都有旅團隔離；冇 key → 未授權。
- `tests/remote.mjs` 190→**229**：代理放行 `uploadPhotos`／`loadDbPart`（白名單以外照樣擋住）；
  5MB 分段讀返；`loadDb` 撞 500 純文字 → 自動退去分段；讀緊嗰陣撞正有人儲存 → 由頭再讀；
  舊版後端 → 提示更新 Apps Script（**唔係**「未設定後端網址」）；`reason:'too_large'`；診斷新格。
- 順手修好 `tests/gate-env.mjs` 三個 case 漏 stub `data/units.generated.json`
  （跑過 `npm run build` 之後會假紅燈 —— 既有嘅 test hermeticity bug）。
- 順手修好一個脆弱斷言：`doPost` action 由「比對成句字面」改成逐個驗。

author: rileymccarthy
body:
A repo that wants Vibes can now depend on it like anything else and run `npx vibes`:

```json
"devDependencies": { "vibes": "github:RileyMcCarthy/vibes" }
```

The Rust binding already resolved as a git dependency. This makes the CLI and the TypeScript binding reachable the same way, so a consumer needs no submodule. Verified end to end against a scratch Rust consumer — binding from git, CLI from `node_modules`, `collect` and `report` both working — and a scratch TypeScript consumer.

## Three lines, three failures closed

| line | without it |
|---|---|
| `"prepare": "npm run build"` | npm hands the consumer the source tree; `bin/vibes.mjs` fails on its first import of `dist/` |
| `"files": [...]` | npm packs using `.gitignore` as the fallback — `dist/` is gitignored — so it **builds the output and then leaves it out of the package it just built** |
| `"exports": {...}` | a nested `package.json` is not reachable through its parent; `import from 'vibes/behaviour'` fails to resolve |

The second one bit me during verification: the build visibly ran and the CLI still couldn't find `dist/cli.js`. CI now has a pack check that asserts the tarball carries `dist/`, the bin and all three bindings, and does not carry `src/`, so that can't come back silently.

`"."` in the exports map points at the library entry, not the bin wrapper — importing `bin/vibes.mjs` would run the CLI as a side effect of the import.

## What this means per language

| | via `npm install vibes` |
|---|---|
| Rust | binding from git, CLI from `node_modules` — verified |
| TypeScript | `import { behaviour } from 'vibes/behaviour'` — verified |
| C | `-I node_modules/vibes/bindings/c` — verified compiling and emitting |
| Python | no binding yet — separate work |

MaD stays on its submodule; nothing here changes that.
