author: rsh1k
body:
## `agents` was linked and unguarded

`sections.txt` is one half of a contract with the application: the admin's Help link sends each screen to an anchor named in `docSections`, and `check-anchors.sh` refuses a build where `index.html` has stopped carrying one.

`agents` was in the app's list and in this manual and **not in `sections.txt`** — so that section was the one this check did not cover. Removing it would have passed here and landed the Agents screen's Help on nothing.

## Design had no section at all

The admin's Design screen sent Help to `#templates`, which explains the template language and its four refusals and says nothing about the thing that screen is for. The theme is thirty-odd named values and seventeen contrast pairs computed in both schemes; it is the part of the product an operator is most likely to change, and the manual did not mention it.

The new section covers why the token set is closed rather than a stylesheet upload, why contrast can be a *gate* at all — it is arithmetic over two hex values, so there is nothing to judge and nothing to guess — what `theme generate` is for, and typefaces served from the site's own origin.

It also covers the part people ask for by name and cannot have. A design system has two licences and people read the first: the code licence usually permits a derived palette, the trademark policy does not permit the name, and two of the large ones separately forbid copying the look. So `theme import` reads the file the design system publishes, in the W3C Design Tokens Format Module 2025.10, on the machine of somebody entitled to use it.

The mapping is written down rather than guessed, and the section says why: `primary` means the brand colour in one system and the body text colour in another, and a matcher that swapped them would produce a palette that is coherent, plausible and **inverted** — every value real, every value looking right on its own.

## Agents could not call anything, and now can

A manifest may name tools, each naming one exact host. When a model asks for one, the manifest and the install's own declarations both have to agree about the host or nothing is called, and **a host the model supplied is dropped rather than forwarded** — that was the thing worth not taking instruction about.

Calling a tool taints the run for the same reason reading stored content does, and more so: a third-party result is whatever that host returned on this request, reviewed by nobody here.

Also new: an agent can ask the search indexes rather than listing every page and reading them one at a time, and `agent check` walks the whole manifest without a model.

## Media stopped at stills

Focal points, derived crops that leave the original alone, orientation applied to the pixels, captions required before a video publishes, range requests that read only the bytes asked for, `quilzo studio`, and `media verify` over every C2PA manifest — ours and theirs.

---

Checked locally: `./check-anchors.sh` passes, no dangling in-page anchors, every referenced image exists, and the HTML parses balanced (40 sections, 40 closes).

The other half is Quilzo/Quilzo#200, which points the Design screen at `#design`. **This one merges first** — the app-side list is the one that decides where Help goes.

author: go-to-k
body:
Closes #2854

## The defect

`cdkd import` takes no parameter values, so every template parameter is bound to its `Default`. A CloudFormation stack deployed with `--parameters DbPassword='{{resolve:secretsmanager:...}}'` over `Default: CHANGEME` (and a nested child supplied the same way by its parent) leaves no reference in any template the import reads. Nothing threw, both opener counts read 0, the discard walk saw no discard, so the resource was captured and the DECRYPTED AWS readback was persisted as `observedProperties` - no throw, no warning.

## The fix: remedy (c), generalized to every level of the tree

When a CloudFormation stack backs the import - the `--migrate-from-cloudformation` source, each nested child (addressed by its ARN from the resource tree), or on ANY other import (selective mode included) a CloudFormation stack with the cdkd stack's name - cdkd reads its deployed parameter values with `DescribeStacks` and compares them with what the import BOUND. A new ARM 4 in `resolveImportedProperties` refuses the observed baseline (and sets `observedBaselineRefused`) for every resource that depends on a parameter that is not provably equal. One warning per stack names the parameters and the count.

- **Premise-independent.** The issue flagged as unmeasured whether `DescribeStacks` returns a reference-valued parameter literally or resolved. The API reference documents `ParameterValue` as "the input value", but the comparison never relies on that: it never pattern-matches `{{resolve:`. A literal reference, a resolved value, a parameter missing from the response and a failed call all differ from the bound placeholder, and a `NoEcho` parameter is divergent unconditionally (its `****` proves nothing, and a `Default` of literally `****` would otherwise compare equal).
- **Deployed values are comparison-only.** Never bound into the resolve, never logged, never in an error message, never persisted. `DeployedParameters` holds them in a `#private` field, and a `DescribeStacks` failure is reported by error NAME only. The one place an SDK message is READ is to classify "stack does not exist" on a non-migrate import (gated on `ValidationError`), which means "no deployed values exist", silently; it is never rendered.
- **A child's own `DescribeStacks` answer IS what its parent supplied**, so remedy (b)'s parent-parameter plumbing is unnecessary, and the ROOT case (the ordinary one) is covered by the same code.
- **One per-stack verdict** (`computeParameterTaint`): every resource is judged on its TEMPLATE definition (`Properties` + `Condition`) unioned with the state bag - a record preserved by a selective merge holds the resolved literal and names no parameter. Seeds are direct dependents and bags that cannot be classified; the refused set is then closed, to a fixpoint, over ATTRIBUTE reads (`Fn::GetAtt`, `${A.Attr}`), because `{Fn::GetAtt: [SsmParam, Value]}` - what CDK's `param.stringValue` emits - resolves without throwing. A plain `Ref` of a resource is not followed.
- **Dependence walk** (`collectParameterDependencies`): generic recursion into every value, with dedicated arms for the bare-string namings (`Ref`, `Fn::Sub` text, `Fn::GetAtt` target, condition names); conditions followed transitively; the resource-level `Condition`. Non-string `Ref`, malformed `Fn::Sub` / `Fn::If`, unknown condition and unknown `Fn::` keys are unclassifiable and refuse.
- **Only parameters something NAMES count.** CDK's `BootstrapVersion` is never bound (nothing but `Rules` names it), so it would otherwise be "divergent" on every stack. The same test gates the `DescribeStacks` call, which keeps it off imports that cannot need it.
- **Comparison mirrors the resolver's binding**: same coercion for `Number` / `CommaDelimitedList` / `List<>`; an SSM-typed parameter compares `ResolvedValue`, since the resolver binds the VALUE; a non-string scalar `Default` compares by string form; `NaN` never proves equality; an unbound parameter is divergent.
- **New IAM requirement**: `cloudformation:DescribeStacks`. Without it the import still succeeds, warns once naming the action, and refuses every parameter-dependent baseline. Documented in `docs/import.md`.

Remedy (a) (resolver provenance) remains the structural fix for #2850 / #2852 and is not attempted here.

## NOT closed here - and one of these blocks treating the class as done

- **#3462 (filed from this PR's security review, severity high): the NEXT `cdkd deploy` clears the marker.** `cdkd deploy` binds the same placeholder `Default`; an UPDATE that does not rewrite the parameter-bound property rebuilds the record (dropping `observedBaselineRefused`) and captures the readback against the placeholder. Nothing `cdkd import` writes survives that rebuild, so the fix belongs in `src/deployment/deploy-engine.ts`, which another lane holds. This PR closes the IMPORT writer #2854 is scoped to, removes the warning's promise that the next deploy captures the baseline, and adds a `docs/import.md` qualifier telling the user to put the real reference in the template first.
- **#2872 is widened**: a record PRESERVED by a selective merge that a pre-#2854 import already gave a plaintext baseline is now refused, and a refusal leaves that old baseline in place (#2872 owns whether deleting it is right; a row was added there). `cdkd scrub` is the existing remedy.
- An import with NO CloudFormation stack of that name has no deployed-parameter source (#2868's class).
- Taint across the nested-stack `Outputs` boundary (parent reading `Fn::GetAtt: [Child, Outputs.X]`) is not followed.
- The `attributes` bag residue of #2847 / #2868 is unchanged.

## Tests

- `tests/unit/cli/import-deployed-parameters.test.ts` - real resolver + real capture, both polarities, every dependence route, fail-closed shapes, comparison parity, the multi-resource verdict (loop continues, fixpoint pinned by declaring the reader-of-reader first, preserved-record seed, unclassifiable seed, in-state count), and sentinel assertions that a deployed value reaches neither a log line nor the record, including through an SDK error message and a hostile error name.
- `tests/unit/cli/import.test.ts` - command-level wiring for root migrate, selective, auto (including a degraded resource-map lookup), nested child by ARN, absent stack, rejected call. Its default CloudFormation answer is the cdkd-native "does not exist", so pre-existing tests keep the arm they fence.
- Mutation probes, one at a time with byte-exact restore, across three rounds: every one red at a dedicated case except two `catch` fallbacks that are shadowed by ARM 1 (the resolver fails on the same input first); the test comments say so rather than claiming a fence.

## Review

3-axis + security. Declined, with reason: a suggestion to purge `all` object versions in the fixture's failure-path `cleanup` - `tests/unit/scripts/integ-s3-versions-harness.test.ts` forbids it, because an `all` purge after a failed destroy deletes the state.json a later `state destroy` needs; the failure path keeps `noncurrent` and the success path sweeps `all` and asserts zero.

## Integ

New fixture `tests/integration/import-deployed-parameter-secret` - WRITTEN, NOT RUN in this lane (the orchestrator serializes real-AWS runs). It deploys root + nested child via upstream `cdk deploy` with the reference as the deployed parameter value, asserts the premise, prints only the SHAPE CLASS of what `DescribeStacks` returned per parameter (the live measurement the issue asked for; to be recorded on #2854), then asserts no plaintext in root or child state, the refused / captured verdicts with a deployed-at-Default negative control, the warning naming all four parameters, and a zero-version S3 sweep.

Needed before merge: `import-deployed-parameter-secret`, `migrate-from-cfn`, `import-nested-stack`, `import-auto-mode`, `import-secret-observed`.

Not edited (held by other lanes): `.claude/rules/layout-cli-import-export.md` deserves one bullet naming `import-de

author: kokhlo
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #116556: `_profile_owns_catalog()` made the profile-owned catalog an early positive check in `_validate_live_listing`, but on a miss validation still fell through to the generic `{base_url}/models` probe — so for a relay that re-shapes its product line (#101705), a model present in the generic listing but **excluded** by the profile's own catalog was still accepted (#116667).

Root cause: `hermes_cli/models_validate.py` `_validate_live_listing` consulted the profile catalog only as `_profile_owns_catalog(...) and _match_in_catalog(...).exact` — early-accept on hit, silent fall-through on miss.

Fix: a new `_profile_owned_catalog()` resolves the profile's catalog **only when the profile serves it from an endpoint of its own** — `models_url` pointing somewhere other than the generic `{base_url}/models`. For those relays the generic listing is a different product line, so the declared catalog now decides authoritatively: exact hit → accept, miss → reject with the catalog's closest suggestion, and the generic probe (plus its curated/Nous soft-accepts) is never consulted.

Deliberately unchanged:
- profiles with **no** separate catalog endpoint (bare `fetch_models` overrides that re-shape the generic listing — openrouter, kimi-coding, meta-ai, …) keep the previous behavior entirely;
- a profile-owned catalog that resolves **empty/unavailable** keeps the generic-listing fallback (the issue's explicit carve-out).

## Testing

- `python -m pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_model_validation.py -q` → **75 passed** (3 new regressions: generic-only model rejected with suggestion; profile-catalog hit still accepted; empty profile catalog keeps the generic fallback).

author: myklob
body:
One commit on top of #175.

A page that supports itself has no score worth reading, so the verdict now leads with that when it applies, ahead of everything else.

Which exposed that the clause could never fire. The scorer refuses a cyclic corpus by design, and everything built on it refuses too, so a loop stops the build long before any page is rendered. The refusal is right. Arriving as an exception part way through a render is a bad way to learn it.

`integrity.py` now runs on the two tables directly, without the scorer, and says the same thing in one line before anything is rendered: how many loops, and the path around each. CI runs it first. On a deliberately circular pair it prints `a -> b -> a`; on the published corpus and on a synthetic one of 14,480 pages it reports none.

## The scorecard stopped repeating itself

Truth, confidence, what the answer rests on, whether acting pays, and any structural fault were each printed twice in different words within a few lines of each other, once in the new verdict and once in the readout below it. What remains under the verdict is the working: the share of weight, the confidence components, how much of the corpus depends on the page, the kind of dispute, and coverage.

```
149 tests, all passing
conformance: conforms
workbook and CSVs: in step
no circular arguments in content (261 pages, 884 rows)
261 pages -> broken internal links: 0
```

author: copilot
body:
This adds the first Web UI slice for Issue 10: users can create a conversion job, watch stage/event progress over SSE, and inspect diagnostic/report output in one place. It also introduces the App Router API surface needed to stream job events with replay and connection lifecycle handling.

- **Web app workspace**
  - Adds `apps/web` as a new Next.js App Router workspace.
  - Wires the root workspace scripts so the web app builds against `@wptossg/shared`.

- **Job creation and monitoring UI**
  - Replaces the scaffolded landing page with a focused dashboard for:
    - job submission by site URL
    - current status / stage / percent complete
    - event log timeline
    - diagnostic summary
    - final `report.json` summary
  - Uses shared job/event/report types end-to-end.

- **SSE API surface**
  - Adds:
    - `POST /api/jobs`
    - `GET /api/jobs/[id]`
    - `GET /api/jobs/[id]/events`
  - Streams typed SSE events with:
    - `Last-Event-ID` replay support
    - heartbeat comments
    - terminal-state close handling
    - race-safe replay/subscription behavior

- **Server-side job/event adapter**
  - Introduces a lightweight in-memory job store for the web layer.
  - Simulates stage progression, page completion events, diagnostics, and final report generation without moving worker-class processing into the web app.
  - Derives simulated report/event counts from per-job state rather than fixed constants.

- **Runtime polish**
  - Removes remote font dependency from the layout so the app does not rely on external font fetches at build/runtime.
  - Tightens form semantics with URL-specific input handling.

Example SSE route shape:

```ts
for (const event of listEvents(id, lastEventId)) {
  sendChunk(controller, serializeSseEvent(createJobEventEnvelope(event)));
}

resources.unsubscribe = subscribe(id, (event) => {
  sendChunk(controller, serializeSseEvent(createJobEventEnvelope(event)));
  if (event.type === 'completed' || event.type === 'failed') {
    close();
  }
});
```

author: moiseszeleny
body:
Stacked on #4; GitHub retargets it to `main` when #4 merges.

## Why
#4 moves the pin to feynlag `efffdb0`, whose writer gives every `VSS1` vertex an unconditional `-1`. That flips **ten shipped 2HDM couplings** (a vertex-by-vertex numeric diff of all four UFOs shows exactly ten sign flips and nothing else). No test pinned any VSS vertex: the SM UFO has none in unitary gauge, so `models/sm/tests/test_l3_ufo.py` cannot, yet `REPORT.md` tagged the claim with that file.

## What the test pins
In the Higgs basis the second doublet couples to the gauge bosons like the SM doublet, with rho_perp = cos(b-a) h - sin(b-a) H. Each 2HDM VSS vertex is therefore a stock MadGraph Goldstone vertex times cos(b-a) or -sin(b-a). Charged Goldstone legs are divided by i^q, because H+- carries no Goldstone phase.

| pinned | against |
|---|---|
| `[a,h-,h+]`, `[Z,h-,h+]` | stock `GC_3`, `GC_61` (convention-free) |
| four charged `W` vertices | stock `GC_37` (non-conjugate-pair, so they tell an unconditional `-1` from a pair-only one) |
| four vertices with an A | one shared sign |

The A vertices depend on the sign of A relative to MadGraph's G0, a field convention, so the test asserts only that it is a sign and the same for all four. It also asserts that these ten are the only VSS vertices in the UFO. The stock values were transcribed from MadGraph 3.7.2's `couplings.py` and `vertices.py`.

## Mutation checks (outside the repo)
| variant | result |
|---|---|
| pre-`efffdb0` UFO (nothing applied) | fails all six absolute pins |
| pair-only rule | fails the four `W` pins; the two conjugate-pair vertices alone pass |
| one A vertex flipped | fails the other three |
| current UFO | passes |

The A vertices pass a uniform revert by construction, because flipping all of them looks the same as flipping A's sign. The six absolute pins cover that case.

Also: the fixture saves and restores `sys.path` and `sys.modules` (the `sm` test's fixture does not; left untouched), the `REPORT.md` tag now cites this test, and the README suite count is updated.

Not included: a resolved `FG-5` row in `FEYNLAG_GAPS.md` for the upstream VSS sign defect. That is a judgment call for you.

## Test plan
- [x] new test passes; `uv run pytest -q -m "not slow"`: 116 passed, 1 skipped, 1 xfailed
- [x] `build_outputs.py --check`, `build_genealogy.py --check`
- [x] `tests/test_markdown_math.py` after the doc edits

In a thread the bot has already joined, a Discord message that @mentions another user (but not the bot) is now processed like any other message in that thread, and when the admission gate does drop a message it says so at debug level.

- `_discord_message_admission()` now consults `_in_bot_thread()` before applying the `DISCORD_IGNORE_NO_MENTION` drop, the same exemption `_handle_message()` and `_dispatch_recovered_message()` already grant. `thread_require_mention` still wins for multi-bot threads because it lives inside `_in_bot_thread()`.
- The drop path logs `admission: dropping message <id> — mentions others, not self, not a bot thread, channel not free-response` instead of returning silently.
- Salvages #116581 (@hardwork9047) — cherry-picked with authorship; tests trimmed to two invariants in a follow-up commit.

## Live repro (real `DiscordAdapter` + real `_in_bot_thread()`, `Mock(spec=discord.Thread)` channel; no bot credentials — the Discord gateway cannot be faked locally, so the admission gate was driven directly on the unmodified adapter class)

| message in a bot-joined thread | before (origin/main) | after |
|---|---|---|
| no mention | admitted | admitted |
| `<@OTHER> test` (third party only) | **dropped, no log line** | admitted |
| `<@BOT> test` | admitted | admitted |
| control: `<@OTHER> test` in a plain channel | dropped silently | dropped + debug log |

Root cause: the admission gate runs on every ingress path and can veto what the two dispatch paths admit, but it never checked the bot-thread exemption those paths use.

author: makenowjust
body:
Fixes #4596. Independent of the other open PRs — this branch sits directly on master.

The `File.open` emitter picked between the flags helper and the mode-string helper by the mode argument's **static type** alone. A poly mode — a value read out of a mixed container, an untyped accessor, a flags word assembled across branches — is neither `TY_INT` nor a `#to_int` object, so it fell to the string branch, whose strict String coercion raised *"no implicit conversion of Integer into String"* for the flag word CRuby accepts:

```ruby
h = { mode: File::RDONLY, name: "r" }
File.open(path, h[:mode])   # raised; CRuby opens it
```

`File.new`, the block form and `Kernel#open` share the emitter and failed the same way. `IO.sysopen` and a boxed mode *string* were always fine, as were an inline constant and a typed local — which is why the shape only shows up where the mode's type is erased.

CRuby asks `#to_int` before `#to_str`, so the decision belongs to the value, not to the call site. The typed arms stay exactly as they were (a mode the analysis can classify still compiles to the direct call, no new branch on the hot path), and a poly one goes to `sp_File_open_val`, which makes that decision on the boxed value: Integer or Bignum is a flag word, nil is the default `"r"`, anything else takes the same strict string coercion the old branch used.

The new test pins the four spellings through a boxed mode, a boxed mode *string*, the inline constant and the typed local, and a write mode that really writes, against CRuby's output in both modes.

`make test` on this branch: raise 3703 pass / 0 fail / 0 error; promote 80 ERR + 26 FAIL, exactly the same-machine master baseline — nothing added. (Two of those are not this change's: `nullable_num_compare` is pre-existing on clean master — verified on 5680dddd — and `int_arg_into_bigint_param` is flaky in a full parallel run, passing 3/3 when run alone.)

author: dukevuzz
body:
Two regressions found by AIO e2e run 35490481743.

Resume answered 409 in 38 ms after a successful pause. The hibernation flip did a bare read-then-write of the CNPG Cluster, and the operator writes that object throughout hibernation, so the version the resume had read was already stale and the API server refused the write. Observation never ran. The flip now re-reads and retries while the conflict lasts; a conflict that never clears, and every other error, still fail. Pause used the same helper and had the same gap.

The second refusal is an ordering hole left by EXC-421: with the limit taken at insert time, a full cluster answered first, so an organisation at its project limit was told 400 instead of 409. The early capacity answer is restored ahead of the cluster check; the atomic slot at insert is unchanged.

Both were reproduced by a failing test first, neither of which needs a cluster.

author: lennysnaider
body:
Arregla el fallo reportado: **tres avatares distintas salían idénticas**, con la
cara y el pelo de la foto del Clone Ref. Raven, que es pelirroja, salía morena.

## Dos causas, las dos mías

**1. Borré la identidad y no puse lo que la sustituye.** La ruta llamaba a
`stripIdentityRedundancy` copiando a Qwen 2 —que borra el preámbulo de edad,
`[BODY:]` y `[FACE:]`— pero sin copiar el ancla con la que Qwen 2 lo compensa.
`hairEmphasis`, `eyeEmphasis` y `bodyEmphasis` del contexto **ni se leían**.

**2. El orden de las imágenes.** Qwen **edita la PRIMERA**, así que con Clone Ref
el lienzo tiene que ser el clone y la cara de la avatar entrar SEGUNDA con un
face-swap explícito. La ruta mandaba la cara primero.

Lo segundo estaba medido desde julio en la ruta de Qwen 2 — *"con la cara como
imagen 1, Qwen anclaba la composición del RETRATO"* — y esta ruta repitió el
intento que ya había fallado. Viene directamente de una decisión del plan: "no
heredar los prompts de clone de Qwen 2 en v1".

## Verificado en vivo

Tres generaciones contra la API real, con una cara pelirroja de referencia y un
Clone Ref moreno:

| Configuración | Resultado |
|---|---|
| cara primero, sin ancla | morena, cara del clone — **el bug** |
| cara primero + ancla de identidad | castaña con puntas cobrizas — a medias |
| **clone de lienzo + face-swap** | **pelirroja, ojos verdes y pecas**, con el vestuario y el sitio del clone ✅ |

## Qué cambia

La función queda con los dos caminos separados y sin contradecirse: con clone
manda el face-swap desde la SEGUNDA imagen; sin clone, la cara es el lienzo y las
cláusulas indexadas de `planExtraRefs` vuelven a encajar. El peso del slider
sigue los mismos tramos que Qwen 2.

## Tests

Los de antes miraban la **forma** del request (que `image_urls` fuese un array,
que el model no se reescribiera) y **ninguno miraba si la persona seguía ahí**.
Se añaden siete que sí: pelo, ojos y cuerpo presentes; el orden de las imágenes
según haya clone o no; y que no conviva la orden contraria.

`tsc` limpio · `eslint` 0 errores · 691/691 tests · snapshot en verde.

## What this fixes

Nothing in shipped behaviour. One comment, its twin in a test file, and one ledger row.

PR #6910 applied the honesty cure to **both** copies of the key-fact grid — which is why the live pages are correct — and then described the extracted copy as a dead twin that no canonical record reaches. The live HTML says the opposite: `/kbli/93114`, `/kbli/49213` and `/kbli/93191` render `LicensingQuickFacts` (the `gap-1 p-4` cells and the "under Licensing Data below" wording are that file's; `KeyFacts` uses `gap-1.5 px-4 py-3.5` and "under PP28/2025 Licensing Data below").

## Why the census was wrong

It counted gold membership with `GOLD_CODES` — the 428 entries of `kbli-gold-all.json`. The page does not. It asks `discloseKbliEditorial`, which returns `gold: null, intel: undefined` whenever `isPmaVerdictVerified` or `hasPublishablePmaCap` fails. So an unverified PMA verdict withholds the gold *layout* as well as the gold *prose* — and every record whose licensing provenance is unverified is, by construction, in that set. | branch | codes |

The ledger row `kbli-page-prints-unverified-licensing-values-at-full-weight` is closed, with all three corrections on the record: the row's predicate covered 1 of 3 reachable codes, the cure keys on the positive gate instead, and this reachability claim was backwards.

author: jakechampion
body:
One typed-path increment toward goal 2, with an rc-log entry.

## A template's argument is typed off the destination

After #9825 the fuzz census had 33 programs the typed path refused, and two of the root leaves were one thing: a literal handed to a template. `var m: Map[i32, i32] = id(Map {})` refused as `unsupported map shape: no destination names one` (seven seeds) and `var fs: ((i32) => i32)[] = id([cw3_a, …])` as `unresolved array literal type` (three).

`invoke_rest` produces each argument at its parameter's type under the bindings the earlier arguments made, and for `id[T](x: T)` the first argument's parameter is the bare variable. A literal has no type of its own (an empty literal has no element to name one; an array of lambdas is typed by what receives it), so `expr` reached `map_construction` or `array` with nothing concrete. The destination knows: the binding's type names T through the contract's result. `destination_binding` binds the result against the call's expected type once, and `invoke_rest` substitutes from it only for an argument whose parameter is still unconcrete after the earlier arguments' bindings. An argument naming its own type binds the variable itself, left to right, as before; a destination the result cannot fit binds nothing.

Fifteen programs produce whole, not three: the array literals were the visible leaf, and a literal handed to a template sat behind the "is a function value … builds" consequences of a dozen others. The map seeds move one leaf deeper, to a real limit: `id$$map$i32$i32: map unit is not shared`. The instance returns its parameter, a map, and a map box carries no reference count on the register backends, so a unit of one is only ever moved (`ssarc.shared_map_error`). `same(m: Map[i32, i32]): Map[i32, i32] { return m; }` refuses the same way with no template in sight, so that leaf is the map representation's, not this change's.

Case: `literal-argument-typed-from-the-destination` (an empty array, a literal of locals and an array of one capturing lambda, all through `id`, fifty rounds, with the absolute leak pin).

rc-log: `2026-09-20-a-templates-argument-is-typed-off-the-destination.md`

## Validation

All green locally on the full tree: the semantic production suite with the new case, the semantic-source RC and print suites, `TestSelfHostCheckerCodes`, tail recursion, the fixture corpus through the self-host compiler on the x86-64, arm64 and wasm legs (`FERN_SELFHOST_FIXTURES=1`), `internal/lint`, and the compiler's own sources producing whole (8625 of 8625). author: dev-jonghoonpark
body:
## 부록 · 왜 하필 "빔"인가

차례 아래와 §5 본문에 앵커를 걸고, 퀴즈 다음에 본문을 두는 각주 형태입니다. 부록 끝에서 §5로 돌아가는 링크도 달았습니다.

내용:

- **1976년 HARPY** — CMU의 Bruce Lowerre가 박사논문에서 음성 인식 시스템을 만들며 붙인 이름. 상태 1만 5천 개짜리 네트워크를 전부 열어 볼 수 없어서 유망한 것만 남긴 데서 나왔습니다.
- **원래 빔은 개수가 아니라 점수 창이었다** — "1등 점수에서 일정 폭 안에 드는 후보를 전부 남긴다". 그러면 살아남은 후보들이 1등 주변으로 띠를 이루고 그게 시간축을 훑고 지나가죠. **"빔 폭(width)"이라는 말이 자연스러운 이유**가 여기 있습니다.
- **그래서 §4의 `top_k`는 엄밀히는 빔이 아니다** — 고정 폭 변형입니다. Kaldi가 `--beam`(임계값, 원래 의미)과 `--max-active`(개수 상한)를 아직 **따로** 받는다는 점을, §7에서 논문이 `p=0.99` 말고 "최대 40자" 하드 리밋을 하나 더 둔 것과 같은 동기로 이어 놓았습니다.

마무리는 "빔은 가능한 경우 전부가 아니라 그 반대 — 일부러 좁게 비춘 범위"로, §4 트레이스의 `top_k` 한 줄과 연결했습니다.

## §2 · CTC 약자 풀이

`CTC = Connectionist Temporal Classification` (Graves et al., ICML 2006, 원문 링크 포함).

단순 약자 풀이로 끝내지 않고, 논문 제목의 **unsegmented**가 왜 핵심인지까지 붙였습니다 — 음성은 프레임과 글자의 대응을 미리 잘라 둘 수 없으니 "가능한 정렬을 전부 인정하고 확률을 합치는" 쪽으로 우회한 게 CTC이고, 축약 규칙과 `blank`가 그 장치라는 것. 글 전체의 동기와 이어집니다.

## 검증

- HTML 태그 균형 확인
- 320 / 390 / 768 / 1280px에서 `documentElement.scrollWidth == clientWidth`
- `note-beam` / `fnref-beam` / `s2` / `s5` / `s7` 앵커 5개 모두 해석됨
- 라이트/다크 렌더링 확인, README 절 표에 부록 행 추가

author: immaculatecross
body:
Closes #153453

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes delayed WhatsApp replies when the agent's plugin registry selects an unconnected channel adapter after the inbound message was accepted by a connected one.

## User Impact

Replies use the inbound transport on the first attempt, avoiding the observed 5–10-second delivery-recovery wait. Model response time is unchanged. No configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Capture the inbound channel registration before agent dispatch and carry it only into durable reply delivery. Capability checks and sending use that same adapter. Keep the current request scope so caller authority and agent policy hooks remain current, and keep managed adapter lifecycle checks so a revoked connection owner cannot be revived or replaced by a same-ID sender.

The binding is channel-generic; there is no WhatsApp-specific state store or retry-timer change. Unrelated channel sends keep their normal registry selection.

## Evidence

- On unmodified main `4e002cf7`, the new DM/group integration regression fails through the real durable reply pipeline with the synthetic unconnected adapter's missing-listener error. Both pass with the fix and send exactly once via the connected adapter.
- Five new tests cover those two flows plus current caller scope, unrelated-channel selection, and adapter revocation. Existing delivery, durable-delivery, and channel-resolution tests also pass: 62 tests across five files in total.
- A version-specific equivalent was tested live on OpenClaw/WhatsApp 2026.9.5: three replies sent on the first attempt; two warm requests took 3.726 and 3.828 seconds. This source revision itself has not been deployed to the live WhatsApp account.
- Full `pnpm build`, core TypeScript check, formatting, and diff checks passed. Independent source review found no further concerns.
- The broader `check:changed` run and automated Codex review were not completed before submission. The automated review was stopped at the operator's request to publish; no automated clean verdict is claimed. CI and maintainer review remain pending.

AI-assisted with Codex. Maintainer edits enabled.

author: me-frankan
body:
## Scope

Opening a channel or a thread landed the reader above the message they were going to read, so every visit started with a long scroll down. A thread never showed an unread divider at all.

## Three causes, each confirmed in a browser

1. **A thread pane never read its own cursor.** Thread read state lives in `thread_reads`, one row per root message, and the server already sends it as `threadReadThrough`. The pane was reading the *channel* cursor while filtering out every message carrying a `threadRootId` — which is every reply. So a thread drew no divider and never positioned on unread.
2. **The open scroll ran before `scrollMargin` was measured.** The virtualizer positions rows against that margin; the measurement can only happen after layout, and a `setState` from a layout effect lands after the whole commit. The first scroll was therefore always short by the height of whatever sits above the list — a thread's root message, the load-older control.
3. **The router's scroll restoration overwrote the result.** `scrollRestoration: true` (`router.tsx:23`) tracks every scrolled element and rewrites this container's `scrollTop` in its `onRendered` pass, after this child's layout effect, inheriting the previous route's offset. Instrumentation caught `scrollToIndex` landing at `scrollTop=482` synchronously and being rewritten to `0` on the very next frame. The open-at-latest path already reasserted itself one frame later for this exact reason; the unread path did not.

## Changes

- New `features/conversations/conversation-open-position.ts`: `unreadBoundary` + `conversationOpenPosition`, framework-free, shared by the pane, the divider snapshot and the tests. A thread pane passes its own cursor, a channel pane the member cursor.
- `scrollMargin` becomes `number | undefined` — "not measured yet" instead of a zero that is corrected later — and is measured from layout offsets rather than viewport rects. A rect-based measurement taken while the container is being scrolled mixes two moments; it was observed reporting 1254 before settling at 102.
- The unread open goes through the virtualizer's own `scrollToIndex`, reasserted once on the next frame against the router's restoration. The estimate→measured drift below the anchor stays the virtualizer's job: `@tanstack/virtual-core@3.17.8` already compensates `scrollTop` for every row first measured above the fold (`defaultShouldAdjust`).
- Fixes an existing bug: `firstUnreadConsumedRef` was never reset when the pane switched conversations, so only the first conversation of a visit could land on its unread boundary.
- Default preference `newest-read` → `first-unread`, with a migration that also backfills rows still holding the old default. The column shipped two days ago (`20260918193000`) carrying the previous fixed behaviour as its default, so those rows hold that default rather than a user's choice.
- The unread divider becomes the same neutral rule the day divider uses, with its label at the end, instead of a brand-coloured bar across the middle of the pane.

## Approved decisions

- Landing on the first unread reply, and drawing the divider in both the channel and the thread, was chosen over "always newest" and over following the preference only in channels.
- The schema change (default + backfill of `users.conversationOpenMode`) follows from that choice.
- The divider restyle was requested directly: the coloured bar read as the loudest element on screen.

## Official sources

- Slack, [Manage your Mark as Read preference](https://slack.com/help/articles/360043037853-Manage-your-Mark-as-Read-preference): the three options under "When I view a channel" map one-to-one onto `first-unread` / `newest-read` / `newest-unread`; the first is "Start where you left off and mark the conversation as read". The help centre does not document which is the default.
- Slack, [Navigate Slack with your keyboard](https://slack.com/help/articles/115003340723-Navigate-Slack-with-your-keyboard): ⌘J moves focus to the first unread message.
- Discord has no official spec page for this; the standing feature request [Option to always start at the newest message](https://support.discord.com/hc/en-us/community/posts/360043598192-Option-to-always-start-at-the-newest-message) is the evidence that its default is to start where you left off.
- `@tanstack/virtual-core@3.17.8` source (`dist/esm/index.js:857-889`) for the size-change scroll compensation and `shouldAdjustScrollPositionOnItemSizeChange`; `@tanstack/router-core@1.171.27` `src/scroll-restoration.ts` for the tracked-element restoration described above.

## Verification

Measured in a real browser against local dev data (a thread with 13 long replies, cursor left mid-thread):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| channel with unread | `scrollTop=0`, divider 506px below the fold | `scrollTop=482`, divider 24px from the top |
| thread with unread | pinned to the bottom (`scrollTop=4152`), divider 2024px above the fold | `scrollTop=2006`, divider 24px from the top |
| nothing unread | 156px short of the bottom | flush with the bottom |
| 390px viewport | same as above | divider at the top, first unread reply right below it |

Checks: `bun run check` clean. `bun run test`: web **1453 pass / 0 fail**. `packages/daemon` reports 5 failures and `packages/coforge` 0 on this branch; a baseline worktree on `main` reports 6 and 1 respectively, with a different failing set each run — 5s/20s timeout flakes, in packages this branch does not touch.

No UI unit tests, per `docs/agents/testing.md`.

## Manual verification todo

- [ ] Channel, DM and thread: with unread, the view opens on the first unread message with the divider above it; with nothing unread, it opens at the bottom.
- [ ] Switch between several channels without a page load — each lands on its own unread boundary.
- [ ] Divider appearance on desktop and mobile, light and dark.
- [ ] A notification deep link (`#message-…`) still jumps to that message rather than to the unread boundary.
- [ ] Expanding or collapsing a long message does not drag the view back to the unread boundary.
- [ ] Switching the preference to "newest message" in Settings changes the behaviour accordingly.

## Risks and follow-ups

- The backfill overwrites `newest-read` for every existing user, including anyone who picked it deliberately in the two days the setting has existed.
- Reopening a thread pane that is still mounted keeps its scroll position rather than re-positioning on new unread replies; that matches how the panes are kept alive today and is out of scope here.

author: lilseyi
body:
Adversarial pass on #752 at `e8c701b8`. **A read-only member can edit the note.** Not on `main` — this is a pre-merge catch, and the fix ships with its tests.

## The chain

The room lets an `ask` past the write gate **on purpose**, and the reason is right: asking what a note says is a read, and a `member` of somebody else's context holds exactly that. Gating it left a reader unable to sync from anybody.

It then relayed the frame as a `y`. On the receiving side a `y` goes to `readSyncMessage`, which chooses between *answering* a question and *applying* an update on a **type byte inside the payload** — and the payload is supplied entirely by whoever sent the frame.

So:

1. a read-only `member` opens the socket (allowed — `canWrite: false`);
2. sends `{"t":"ask","d":"<base64 of an ordinary Yjs update>"}`;
3. `decodeClientFrame` accepts it — non-empty base64, ≤32 KiB. **The gateway cannot tell a state vector from an update**: it holds no Yjs and the bytes are opaque there *by design*;
4. the write gate matches `y` and `snap` only, so `canWrite` is never consulted;
5. the room broadcasts `{t:"y", d}` to every peer;
6. each peer's `readSyncMessage` applies it, because the embedded byte says update;
7. the elected writer flushes the result to the customer's bucket.

**Non-negotiable #4** — *"write access to someone else's context is never implied by read"* — and it is the same boundary this branch already fixed once, two commits earlier, by gating `y` and `snap`. A new frame arrived carrying the same payload to the same sink. That is **"a gate is sized for the callers it had"** in its sharpest form: the gate enumerates frame *types*, and a type was added.

## The fix keeps the type instead of erasing it

The gateway genuinely cannot narrow this, and should not try — the opaqueness is what keeps the zero-dependency rule intact.

- **The room** broadcasts `ask` as `ask`.
- **The client** reads one with `readSyncAsk`, which dispatches on nothing but SyncStep1 — a message that cannot modify a document by construction, since `readSyncStep1` reads a state vector and writes a reply. A `y` is unchanged.

A reader still syncs: the non-vacuity check proves a genuine question is still answered and fills an empty document.

## The test asserted the defect

The existing gateway check pinned that a reader's payload reaches the writer as `t: "y"` — one check above *"an edit from the same read-only member still reaches nobody"*. The two sat adjacent, and the first defeated the second. It is replaced, and the replacement says why.

## Sabotage

| edit | FAIL |
| --- | --- |
| the room relabels `ask` as `y` again | 2 |
| `readSyncAsk` delegates to `readSyncMessage` again | 1 (mobile) |

## The non-vacuity check earned its place

My first version of the client test built the forged update from an **independently seeded** document. Yjs correctly buffered it as depending on history the target had never seen, so the refusal passed against an inert payload — the check would have "proved" a fix that did nothing. Its own non-vacuity half failed, which is the only reason that was caught.

It now syncs the attacker to its victims first, the way being in the room does, and asserts the same bytes read as an edit **do** rewrite the note.

## Verified

`apps/mcp` — **3941 PASS, 0 FAIL**. Mobile presence suites (`presence`, `presenceContract`, `liveMergeTyping`) — 55 passed. `@context/mobile` typecheck clean. `check-no-identifiers` OK.

author: pattch-openclaw
body:
## What

Perf-gate spike **PR 1 of 5** (FLAC.md → "Perf gate spike — concrete plan and validation process", merged in #46): the scaffold crate + embedded clips for the Phase 1 step 4 go/no-go measurement. **Nothing is measured yet** — PR 2 gates every perf number (correctness-before-speed).

## Landed

**Crate `examples/flac_spike/`** — standalone workspace, cargo config **inherited** (never re-declared; the `-Tgba.ld` rule). `#![no_std]` lib + GBA `[[bin]]` behind `cfg(target_arch = "arm")` (agb is a target-gated dependency so the host witness gate compiles without agb's graph; bin is `test = false`).

- `assets` — generated manifest: per-frame region-relative offset table (the GAFP stand-in), sizes, FNV-1a pins, measured censuses, `include_bytes!` of the regions
- `checksum` — FNV-1a 64, shared host/ROM; unit vectors **derived** (see findings)
- `driver` — the seek-table frame-loop seam every later PR plugs into: PR 2 hashes via it, PR 3 times `decode_one`'s window, PR 4 alternates buffer halves. Decode logic never changes underneath.
- `main` — ROM: boots, logs arm metadata, verifies region hash pins; blue/red screen verdict (BitReader-PoC convention)

**Assets** — `scripts/gen_spike_assets.sh` → `frame_vectors.py spike_assets` (the plan line's "spike-assets", landed with the module's underscore convention). Committed 10 s deterministic source, both arms at `-b 2048 -m -1`, 16-bit stereo 32 kHz. Measured censuses, exactly Correction 3's arms:

| Arm | Encode | Census (both slots) |
|---|---|---|
| `L0_FIXED` | `flac -1 -l 0` | `fixed0 ×157` |
| `L4_LPC` | `flac -1 -l 4` | `lpc4 ×156 + lpc3 ×1` |

Fail-closed layers: `check_stream` invariants, a **both-slot** subframe walk whose per-frame footer gap must land on the next frame's offset (witnesses region slicing + the bps+1 side seam on all 314 frames), and arm censuses that refuse to write if `-l 0` ever stops being FIXED-only or `-l 4` stops being majority LPC. Regions byte-stable across regenerations (sha256 pins in `assets.rs`). Reference PCM blobs are host-test ground truth only — the ROM pins them by hash, never embeds them.

**Witness suite** (`make spike-test`) — 4 checksum unit + 6 integration:
- Rust FNV-1a reproduces the Python generator's pins on both regions and both PCM blobs (cross-language hash meeting on committed bytes)
- driver decode of the **exact embedded bytes** is **bit-exact vs `flac -d`** on both arms (320,000 stereo samples each)
- the two arms' PCM is byte-identical (same source ⇒ one ground truth — free cross-arm witness)
- seek-table structural invariants
- **negative control**: offset +1 byte must fail the walk, pristine control decodes — proves the driver consumes the table rather than chaining by bytes

**Gates** — Makefile: `spike-rom` / `native-spike-rom` / `podman-spike-rom` / `spike-test` (same out-of-tree `--manifest-path` pattern as flac-test), spike workspace added to format/check/clean/clean-cache; container cache volume added. `.gitignore`: spike target dir + `flac-spike.gba` (assets deliberately tracked — committed generator output).

**Docs** — spike README rewritten (placeholder false the moment the crate existed; its "62,500 cycles/frame" units error corrected to ~1,048,750 cycles/frame, derived — the correction was scheduled for PR 5 but a false README is worse than an early one). FLAC.md: completion entry + PR 1 marked done in the plan.

## Findings (same failure mode, new costume — recall without a witness)

- The first draft's FNV unit-vector "published values" were wrong **from memory**; the implementation disagreed and was right. Pins now in the test were derived in two independent runtimes (Python big-int, Node BigInt) and anchored against the 32-bit definition vectors FNV publishes (`fnv1a32("a") = 0xE40C292C`), which the same loop reproduces exactly.
- Found by the compiler in the **generated file**, not review: Python `json.dumps` escapes non-ASCII as `\uXXXX` (valid JSON, invalid Rust — fixed with `ensure_ascii=False`); a const struct-literal needs `};` (a lexer error earlier in the file masked it — generated files need compile gates too).
- `usize::from(u32)` doesn't exist on any platform (core never implements it; target-dependent width) — driver routes through `try_from` with clean out-of-range rejection.

## Gates run

- `make spike-test` ✅ (4 unit + 6 integration)
- `make native-spike-rom` ✅ builds/links/fixes `flac-spike.gba`
- `make flac-test` ✅ unchanged (flac-lite untouched; 91 unit + 24 integration)
- `make check` ✅ (spike workspace included)

On-target boot check (blue screen) is the manual step from here on — this ROM, like the integration ROM, is an infinite-loop gfx ROM, so the `#[test_case]` runner doesn't apply; PR 2 makes the on-target proof a checksum.

## 図鑑から追加にタイプ表示

チーム管理の「＋ 図鑑から追加…」の候補にタイプを並べた（`フォレトス [むし][はがね]`）。

どのフォルムのタイプを見せるかは**メインタイプを持つフォルムを優先**する。メガで初めて付く系統（グソクムシャ等）は通常フォルムのタイプを見せても「なぜ入れられるのか」が分からないため、`メガではがね` と補足を添える。

## 畳めるパネル

絞込みや設定が縦に伸びると、スマホでは肝心の一覧が画面の下半分に追いやられていた。共通コンポーネント `Panel` に切り出して各所へ適用。

| 画面 | 畳めるパネル |
| --- | --- |
| チーム管理 | チーム / 追加・入出力 / 弱点チェック / 攻撃範囲チェック |
| 図鑑 | 絞り込み（既定で畳む）|
| ダメージ計算 | 戦闘条件 |
| 素早さ比較 | 手持ち・控えの素早さ設定 / 絞り込み（既定で畳む）|

- 開閉状態は localStorage に保存する
- 見出しは button（`aria-expanded` つき）なのでキーボードでも開閉できる

弱点チェック・攻撃範囲チェックは既に独自の開閉を持っていたので `Panel` に寄せた。ただし**警告バナー（「半数以上が弱点」「誰も抜群を取れないタイプ」）は畳んでも出したまま**にする必要があるため、`Panel` に「畳んでも残す領域」（`always`）を足して見落とさないようにした。

- `npm run build` 通過
- 412px で横あふれ0
- 全パネルの開閉、要約の表示、開閉状態の保存を確認
- 弱点チェックを畳んでも警告バナーが残ること（3件 → 3件）

author: naman0r
body:
## What

**Weekly receipt at `/receipt`.** The last seven days of agent sessions drawn as a paper receipt: sessions per agent, prompts, tool calls, fresh input tokens with cache reads on their own sub-line, output tokens, lines changed, the top five projects by cost, a Cleaned up section, and a total. Project names show as "project 1", "project 2" unless you switch them on, since the point is to share it. Copy image and Download PNG draw the same lines onto a canvas, so the image matches the page. It is in the sidebar and linked from Agent Watch's Last 7 days header. Local-only; needs Agent Watch on.

**Cleanup actions are now logged.** A successful Clean up on `/cleanup`, Stop on Ports, Remove on Worktrees, or Clean on Disk appends to `~/.dockmaster/actions.json` (kind, count, KB freed), written atomically and trimmed to 90 days. The receipt reads this week's entries. Nothing logged these before, so the counts start at zero.

`buildReceipt` in `lib/receipt.ts` is pure and unit tested.

## Agent Watch token count fixes

Checking the receipt's numbers against the raw transcripts turned up three counting bugs that also affected the Agent Watch cards.

- **Resumed Codex sessions lost their earlier usage.** Codex writes a running total per session, and the total starts over when a session is resumed. Only the last total was kept. All four of my Codex sessions this week had been resumed once, and they showed 2.7M tokens where the transcripts hold 13M. A drop in the running total now banks the previous one. Verified two ways against the files: the reset-aware total and a de-duplicated sum of per-turn usage agree exactly on three sessions and within 3% on the fourth.
- **Codex cached tokens were counted twice.** Codex includes cached tokens inside `input_tokens`; Claude Code and OpenCode report them apart. Input is now input minus cached, and "in context" is the last turn's input. One card had been showing 380k in context.
- **Claude Code subagent transcripts were never read.** They live in `<session>/subagents/agent-*.jsonl`, one level deeper than the scan went. They now fold into their parent session. A subagent's opening prompt does not count as a prompt and its context does not overwrite the parent's. This week that was 8 files and 67k output tokens.

## Verified by hand

- `/receipt` renders on the dev server with live data, and Download PNG produced a 944 x 1580 image.
- Summed `output_tokens` straight from the week's Claude Code transcripts: 910,822, matching the scanner before the subagent fix. Logged output is about 2.4 times the visible text, the difference being thinking whose text is not stored, so the logs are not undercounting.
- `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` (182 tests), and `npm run build` pass. The build ran in a throwaway copy so the dev server's `.next` was untouched.

Not verified: Copy image, since browser automation cannot reach the clipboard. A cleanup action showing up on the receipt was not exercised end to end either; the log write and the weekly tally are covered separately.

Known limits: the receipt total only adds up costs the agent CLIs recorded themselves, so it is partial, and the note under the total names the agents it leaves out. Agent Watch reads at most the 60 most recent sessions. Remote Macs keep the old Codex numbers until the companion is updated; the companion version was not bumped.

author: acmaster03
body:
Follow-up to #42 and #44. `/live` was Home a second time — same title, same stay line, same progress bar, same Next row, same full-width Check in button — which is why pressing Check in read as nothing having happened. It is now a redirect to `/dashboard`.

Five commits, each independently reviewable.

## What moved, so nothing was dropped

| `/live` had | now |
|---|---|
| check-in sheet | `components/checkin/CheckInProvider`, mounted above every screen |
| Note | a mode of that sheet, placeless on purpose |
| Arrived | Home, arrival day only, gone once recorded |
| Plan vs actual | `components/trips/PlanVsActual`, rendered on Home |
| edit / delete / queued marker | Home's feed rows via `SocialRow`, author-only |
| pre / post phase screens | Home already had its own, `BeforeYouFly` included |

A **redirect, not a deletion**: installed apps hold their last URL, the service worker caches documents by path, and phones carry bookmarks. `app/(app)/live/` keeps its name because `CheckInModal`, `EditEventModal`, `FollowerNudge` and `Sheet` still live there and are imported elsewhere.

## Bugs that fell out of the merge

- **Home's "Arrived" was a `<Link href="/live">`.** It recorded nothing and moved you to a screen with another Arrived button on it.
- **`/live`'s Arrived showed every day of the trip** with no already-recorded check, so it wrote duplicate events while its toast claimed "the button is done for this stop".
- **"Check-ins ›" in the feed header linked to `/live`.** Home's feed *is* the check-ins, so it pointed at a rearranged copy of its own page.
- **`scrollLock` recorded offset 0** when a lock was taken over a leaked one, throwing the reader to the top of the page on close. Unreachable only because #44 removed the path there.
- **`useSearchParams` in a layout-level provider** needs a Suspense boundary as soon as any page under that layout is statically rendered. The `?checkin=1` shim it served was dead anyway — `/live` redirects and Next drops the query string — so it was removed rather than wrapped.

## The offline outbox

`lib/trips/outbox.ts` is **byte-untouched**. The mutations moved into `lib/trips/useTripEvents.ts` but import `CHECKIN_MUTATION_KEY` and `EVENT_MUTATION_KEY` rather than retyping them, and nothing else in the app writes events. A check-in queued on a phone before this ships replays identically.

## Verification

Build, typecheck and 75/75 tests pass; lint is unchanged from before this branch (one pre-existing `SettingsClient.tsx:183` error).

Unlike the earlier PRs, the UI here was **driven in a browser**, against a production build:

```
home:  {"hydrated":true,"planVsActual":true,"checkInBtn":true,"overflowX":0}  errors: 0
       url unchanged: true | dialog: 1     ← raised tab opens the sheet, no navigation
sheet: mode switch flips aria-checked, dialog retitles to Note, Save disabled while empty
nav:   button is transparent, borderless, Work Sans, 58px, no overflow at 320px or larger text
```

A layout regression was caught this way and fixed: folding the trip percentage and date home into the card kicker pushed "ON PLAN" onto two lines at 390px.

Worth recording for the next person: the **dev server cannot be driven in this environment** — its HMR websocket never connects, so React never hydrates and every control is inert. `next build && next start` works. That is also why the `/dev/*-preview` routes looked like they were waiting on Supabase earlier in this branch; they were not.

## Still open, in `docs/NOTES.md`

- An unticked stop still owes money for its bookings (`computeBudget` drops it, `bookingsSummary` does not). Left for the Money round.
- `moneyModel` and `whereAmI` disagree about the day you leave a stop — closed vs half-open interval. Reconciling them changes budget numbers, so it is written down rather than done in passing.
- Whether Check in / Arrived / Note / Activity / post become one vocabulary.

author: proshunsuke
body:
## Background and purpose

Closes https://github.com/proshunsuke/tab-position-options-fork/issues/20

Add the original extension's External Links feature: an ordinary click can open a link in a new tab while page exclusions and explicit navigation rules control exceptions. The feature is disabled by default.

## Changes

- Add all seven page/link rule types, with priority: page exclusions → link URL rules → page URL rules → exact-origin comparison (protocol, hostname, and port). The first match within each category wins.
- Preserve modified/middle clicks, downloads, same-document anchors, and non-HTTP(S) links. Evaluate dynamic links and SPA URLs at click time, including HTTP(S) frames.
- Create tabs with their intended position and activation immediately. Explicit foreground/background rules override New Tab activation settings; New Tab positioning, Tab on Activate, and Loading Page positioning still apply. Warm handling uses cached settings and snapshots without storage reads, tab queries, or waits before creation.
- Handle Chrome's delayed opener metadata and links originating in pop-up windows so regular new-tab handling cannot overwrite explicit activation rules.
- Add the options section, all ten locale translations, settings persistence, and strict import/export support.
- Request HTTP/HTTPS site access at installation through WXT-generated `content_scripts.matches`. The API `permissions` list stays unchanged; no additional `scripting` or `host_permissions` declaration is needed. Update the privacy policy and repository-managed store submission copy accordingly.

## Validation

- Type checking and lint pass; all 132 unit tests pass, including synchronous API dispatch, origin/rule precedence, event ordering, and settings validation.
- The three-shard full E2E run passed 178 of 179 tests. The sole failure was an existing storage assertion missing the new default settings section; its expectation was updated and the settings suite passed on rerun.
- After the final runtime fix, the headed external-link and settings suites passed 21 tests. The pop-up case was then expanded to verify both foreground/background activation and window focus; both cases passed.
- Browser coverage includes live settings updates, dynamic/SPA links, frames, native modifier/download/anchor behavior, pinned boundaries, placement-rule interactions, worker state reinitialization, and settings import/export. The generated manifest and options layout were also inspected.

author: sergiovalle3121
body:
Cuarta ola del plan de cierre de brecha con AutoCAD. Cuatro carriles en paralelo, cada uno con un escéptico que intentó refutarlo; los cuatro escépticos encontraron defectos reales y están corregidos aquí.

**Anotación que sigue al dibujo**
- `ANNOSCALE`, `OBJECTSCALE` y `ANNORESET`: la escala anotativa ya se controla desde la línea de comandos. El motor existía desde hace tiempo y **ninguna orden se lo daba al usuario**. Medido: un texto anotativo cambia de tamaño en el modelo al cambiar de escala y **conserva su tamaño impreso**.
- `CENTERMARK` y `CENTERLINE` ahora **siguen al círculo** cuando se mueve o se escala, y se declaran huérfanas si se borra el objetivo. Antes se quedaban pegadas donde nacieron.
- `HATCHORIGIN`: alinea la fase del patrón entre sombreados vecinos. Medido con el desfase peor posible: de media separación a cero.
- *El escéptico encontró* que `HATCHORIGIN` perdía en silencio el segundo clic al designar sombreados uno a uno. Corregido.

**Tablas y texto que hacen el trabajo**
- Fórmulas de celda: `=SUMA`, `=PROMEDIO`, `=CONTAR`, con recálculo al cambiar la celda de origen.
- `TINSERT`: insertar y borrar filas y columnas, y fusionar celdas. `TABLEEXPORT` a CSV.
- `MTEXT` con viñetas y listas numeradas reales.
- *El escéptico encontró* que fusionar celdas no miraba el tamaño real de una celda ya fusionada, así que dos fusiones solapadas se pisaban. Ahora se rechaza el solape.

**La lámina: capas por ventana**
- `VPLAYER`: congelar y fijar color, tipo de línea y grosor **solo dentro de una ventana**. Sin esto hay que duplicar el dibujo.
- `CHSPACE`: mover entre modelo y papel conservando el tamaño aparente. Medido: 8 m a 1:50 son 160 mm de papel exactos.
- `VPORTS` en espacio modelo, y congelar por ventana desde el gestor de capas.

**Bloques con atributos, que es como se rotula un plano**
- Se arregló el modo **predefinido** de `ATTDEF`, que se perdía al definir el bloque.
- `ATTEXT` / `EATTEXT`: extracción de atributos a CSV (la lista de luminarias, de puertas…).
- *El escéptico encontró* que el nombre del CSV perdía los acentos y la Ñ: «CLIMATIZACIÓN» salía roto. Corregido normalizando, no borrando.

El registro queda en **382 comandos**, todos con icono y resumen. Gates locales: typecheck, lint, trinquete de lint, presupuesto de monolito, integridad de comandos, manifiesto, cobertura de cinta, alcance de UI y localizadores e2e, todo verde.

author: dycuong03
body:
Clean replacement for #375. Answers #371, unblocks the cost side of #372.

## Why a new branch

#375 carries the same finding but was opened **against `main`**, not `develop`. Its 479-file / +102,095 / −4,042 diff is not accidental payload added by the author — it is the entire `develop` → `main` backlog showing through the base choice. Against `develop` the actual change is **2 files, +96 lines**, and that is what this PR contains. #375 is also `CONFLICTING`, so it has run no CI at all.

Docs-only. No code changed.

## The finding

With `GAMESERVER_REPLICATION_SCHEDULE=off` every dirty entity is sent every world tick, so an enemy and a remote player are replicated identically — yet enemies render **3.9%** frozen frames against remote players' **0.0%**. The cause is spawn/despawn churn: each fresh entity id starts with one interpolation sample, which cannot be interpolated, so the view holds it still until the buffer fills. A persistent remote player pays that hold once and amortises it to ~0; an enemy pays it every ~4.2s.

## What the evidence establishes

**#371 hypothesis 3 (the instrument artefact) is ruled out — from the code, not by preference.** This is the load-bearing result, because hypotheses 1 and 3 predict the same number:

- `EnemyReapSystem` despawns at radius 2.5; `EnemyMoveSystem` stops at radius 0.1 (`distSq <= 0.01f`) — 25× apart.
- `EnemyMoveSystem` applies a constant `EnemySpeed` with **no deceleration term**, so the "enemy decelerating into the centre" premise hypothesis 3 rests on does not exist in this code.
- Tick order is `Spawn → Move → Reap` (`EnemyAiPhase`), reap in the same tick after move.

Therefore an enemy is destroyed at full speed, `EnemyMoveSystem.cs:174` is unreachable under `EnemyAiTuning` as shipped, and there are no legitimately-still enemy frames for `ParkedTravel` to miscount. All constants verified against `EnemyAiTuning.cs` in this tree.

**The population arithmetic closes.** Lifetime `(13 − 2.5) / 2.5` = 4.2s; spawn rate `2 / 1.5` = 1.33/s; steady alive ≈ 5.6, matching the `/status` 4↔6 oscillation.

## What it does NOT establish

**The 3.9% is not partitioned.** Churn is established as the driver; the share attributable to it is not measured. A per-spawn hold of one 66.7ms send interval predicts only **1.6%** — about 40% of the measured value. The measured 3.9% inverts to a **~164ms** hold (~2.5 send intervals), which matches a 2–3 sample interpolation buffer but not the one-sample-to-two-samples reading. Which of the two the client actually does was not measured here. Part XVII now states this gap with the arithmetic in a table rather than asserting "that asymmetry is the whole gap", which is what the original text claimed.

No measurement in this PR excludes an entity's first N frames after spawn or separates `fresh` from `steady` frames. That quantitative split is Cuvara/Netcode#157 and remains open.

## Consequence for #372

The cost side is real rather than artefact, which removes the "cost is untrustworthy" caveat #372 was carrying. It does **not** move the recommendation: `tiered` stays `off` by default and the cheaper staleness-free levers still dominate. The two ship gates on #372 are unchanged.

Refs #371, #372. Supersedes the content of #375 — leaving that one for the author/lead to dispose of.

author: rsh1k
body:
NEWS stopped at v0.2.1 on 8 September. Eighty-two commits later it still did — so the file whose first line says *"only what somebody running this would notice"* had noticed nothing for twelve days. The README had gone stale in three specific places, and the Design screen's Help link went to the page explaining why the template language has no `eval`.

**No tag.** This is the record of what happened, not a release.

## NEWS

An unreleased section, grouped the way the work actually went rather than by component. Most of it came out of two sweeps — driving the running program through a browser and a terminal, and an audit for things declared and never executed — and the second found more, because in every case the code was correct about its own job and wrong about what another part was doing with it.

Sixty-two entries, under: *Declared and never executed*, *Found by using it*, *Agents*, *The design system you already use*, *Pictures and video*, *Writing and the interface*, *Speed*, *Honesty*.

## README

**The three processes were four.** `quilzo studio` has existed since [#174](https://github.com/Quilzo/Quilzo/pull/174) and the section listing the processes did not mention it. It is also the most interesting one to explain: the admin's policy is `default-src 'none'` and a test asserts its screens execute nothing, but `getDisplayMedia` and `MediaRecorder` are JavaScript APIs. Rather than open a nonce route and weaken the claim everywhere else, the capture surface is its own process.

**The agents paragraph predated tool calling.** A manifest names tools and the hosts they may reach; a host the model supplied is dropped rather than forwarded; a tool call taints the run. None of that was there. Neither was the fact that an agent can reach a declared MCP server at all — "Reaching other systems" described the client as something only the command line used.

**Pictures and video, and speed.** Two new paragraphs. The media work of the last fortnight — focal points, derived crops, orientation applied to the pixels, captions required before a video publishes, range requests, C2PA verification — was not described anywhere. Neither was any of the performance work, which is the kind of claim that is worthless unless the numbers sit beside it:

```
a page on a 211-page site   6.83 ms -> 2.66 ms
the escaper, per page       714 KB/1163 allocs -> 234 KB/737
a page over the wire        6,443 B -> 1,955 B
the sitemap and the feeds   1,054 B -> 304, and no body
```

## The Help link on the Design screen

`docSections` here and `sections.txt` in the manual are the two halves of a contract: neither proves the other, each fails on its own side, and the failure a reader suffers — Help landing on nothing — needs both to be wrong at once.

The Design screen pointed at `templates`. That section is about the template language and its four refusals; it says nothing about the theme, which is what the screen is for. The manual now has a `design` section covering the token set, the contrast gate, `theme generate`, typefaces and the design-token import.

**Found while comparing the two lists:** `agents` was in `docSections` and in `index.html` and *not* in `sections.txt`, so the manual's own guard did not cover the Agents section — removing it would have passed CI on both sides.

Quilzo/quilzo.github.io#4 is the other half and **merges first**.

## The repository description

Updated to say that a manifest covers the tools an agent may call and the hosts it named first, which is the part that changed.

author: dinah-gh
body:
A comment stops being minted whole. `dinah comment <ref>` with no text mints
the entity, writes an empty body and prints its reference, which is the form an
editor calls: the comment exists from the first keystroke, so nothing has to
decide when an author has finished composing one, and an author who says
nothing after all deletes it.

A comment's body is written through a verb, which records a SHA-256 over the
body exactly as the anchor parser returns it. Every verb that writes the anchor
recomputes the digest, not only those that write the body, because rendering
re-serialises the file whole and a header-only write would otherwise be
reported as an edit nobody made. A write over a body that has already diverged
is refused rather than absorbing it, and `dinah accept-divergence` ratifies
what is on disk and takes no text.

A checklist item's answer stops being a free-text note and becomes a reference
to one of that item's own comments. `resolve`, `verify` and `fail` take that
reference and refuse any other; `--text` mints a comment and designates it in
one act; naming both is refused rather than resolved by precedence. `reopen`'s
reason stays free prose, and reopening clears the designation, which is what
frees a designated comment for deletion.

`dinah-migrate-notes` carries every live store across. It writes in place and
claims no atomicity, which is what every other migration here does; its
idempotence rests on the converted comment's identity rather than on the note
key, so a rerun cannot write a second copy. An item whose settling the journal
cannot attribute is named in a manifest and nothing is written, and
`--unattributed` records the comment with no author at all rather than with an
invented name.

The storage format moves to 6 and the conformance claim to dinah-core/0.18. A
store below the format is refused by name as `dinah.store-awaiting-migration`.

The extension deletes dinah-506's draft apparatus: creation calls the empty
form and opens the file, saving writes the body through the verb, and a settled
item's row draws the answer it designates.

Twenty acceptance criteria, each verified against a test armed by writing the
wrong implementation it names and confirming a genuine assertion failure.
Eighteen such breaks in all. Two defects the tests found and the work fixed: a
digest taken over the caller's bytes where the writer normalises on the way to
disk, and a forced deletion handing a bare identifier to a verb that resolves
references. Both are promoted to the counterexample corpus.

author: sauersml
body:
Refs #3020 (partial; the Bernoulli marginal-slope remainder is tracked in #3430)

## Problem
The same formula meant different things depending on the family. With an explicit `length_scale=` on every spatial term, the Bernoulli marginal-slope entry point (`bms/block_specs.rs`) and the location-scale entry point (`gamlss/builders.rs`) called `all_spatial_terms_kappa_fixed` and turned κ optimization **off**. Survival, single-surface and location-scale-survival fits went through the generic `spatial_length_scale_term_indices` enrollment and **searched** κ from that value.

The documented contract treats the value as a start ("Global length-scale init"; `matern_length_scale_sensitivity` expects REML to refine it). The short-circuit's own comment says it existed to dodge an ARC stall. SPEC: "In general, do not paper over solver issues."

## Change
- Delete the GAMLSS short-circuit. κ enrollment for location-scale fits is now decided by the term spec, as for survival and single-surface fits.
- **BMS keeps its pin for now.** Removing it makes the explicit-ℓ BMS integration fits (`binary_outcome_shape_bms_*`, `bms_covariance_declined_2718`) fail with the n-block ARC stall of #3430, the same stall that already reds the omitted-scale BMS Matérn fits. Dropping those fits isn't allowed, and loosening the solver would paper over #3430. So the pin stays, its comment names #3430 as the reason, and it is to be deleted with that fix. `spatial_term_has_locked_kappa` is now private and documented as serving only that pin.
- Matérn provenance (Auto vs explicit) is kept. It still stops re-planning from overwriting a user value.
- Tests assert that an explicit Matérn or Duchon scale is enrolled and that its κ slot starts at ψ̄ = −ln ℓ. For Duchon: one isotropic slot at the declined power, per-axis ψ at the enrolled power.
- The GAMLSS Matérn fixture now runs the joint κ+ρ search with the production outer budget instead of the four-step smoke budget.
- docs/formulas.md:
  - fixes the TPS, Matérn and Duchon `length_scale` rows;
  - adds a "Kernel scales" section that lists the three fits holding a scale at its seed: BMS with explicit scalar scales (#3430), BMS `residual_columns` (#2924), and the marginal-slope `mjs` range.

## Validation
- `cargo check --workspace --tests` passes on the merged tip.
- focused-rust-proof on the tip: gam-terms `matern_length_scale_provenance`/`term_builder::tests`; gam-models `explicit_duchon_aniso_length_scale_seeds`/`design_assembly_constraint`/`gamlss::tests`; gam integration `binary_outcome_shape_bms`, `production_like_binary_outcome` and `bms_covariance_declined_2718`.

author: deptr-softwares
body:
v0.19 batch 6. Ctrl-click a block's header to select it; the selection can then
be copied, pasted, deleted and moved as one piece, from the bar above the list
or from any selected card's own buttons.

Rebased onto `next-update` after #196 merged. The 65 conflicts were stamped
script tags and were resolved by regenerating, not by hand — see the note at the
bottom, because that resolution had a trap in it.

## The design was already in the file

The carried spec says *a selection model, not a keybinding* and says nothing
about shape. The shape came from `expandedBlocks`, twenty lines above the new
code: collapse state is a **WeakSet keyed by the block object**, and the comment
there already states the three reasons — index changes under reordering, a flag
on the block would be serialised into `desc_data` and shipped to every reader,
and object identity survives `renderBlockList`.

All three apply harder to a selection, because **every operation a selection
offers changes the indices of the blocks around it**. Held as indices, a
selection would be wrong the instant it was used.

**No order is stored either.** It is derived from the live array each time, so
"copy these five" and "move these five up" still mean the same five blocks after
the array has been rewritten under them — there is no second copy to go stale
because there is no copy at all.

## Three rules chosen rather than fallen into

- **A selection beats the hover.** Hover copy is what this was before C2 and
  still works untouched with nothing selected — but once an author has said
  which blocks they mean, the pointer resting on a sixth must not overrule them.
- **A card in the selection hands its ▲▼✖ to the whole selection**; a card
  outside it still acts on itself. Otherwise the card buttons and the bar
  quietly come to mean different things.
- **v0.18 F9's gallery early return is kept**, not routed around.

Ordering that matters: `moveSelectedBlocks` decides whether anything *can* move
before touching the array, so the history snapshot is of the state being left
and a selection already against the end cannot push a duplicate undo step. And
folder membership is positional, so every position an operation disturbed is
reconciled, not only the block that moved.

## The bug eighteen passing tests could not see

**`stopPropagation` does not stop listeners on the same element.** All three of
this file's click listeners are bound to `#block-list`, so every selection-bar
button *also* reached the general button handler — which resolves buttons via
`closest('.block-card').getAttribute(...)` and, by its own comment, throws on
anything outside a card. Four exceptions per pass, one per button.

Nothing caught it because the bar's work had already been done in the first
listener: the document was correct, the selection was correct, and the exception
surfaced in a second listener where nothing was watching. The test that found it
asserts on `pageerror` rather than on the document, which is the only place this
was ever visible. `stopImmediatePropagation` is the fix.

**A test that accused the stylesheet.** A hover assertion failed comparing
`rgb(219,168,13)` against `rgb(231,176,8)` — both yellow. Not a specificity bug:
`.block-card` carries `transition: border-color 0.1s`, so it had compared two
frames of the same animation.

## Tests

`tests/block-multiselect.spec.js`, 19 tests. **Falsified on committed code**,
three independent breaks, each caught by the test named for it:

| Break | Caught by |
|---|---|
| selection keyed by index | *the selection names blocks, not positions* (+4 others) |
| `#block-list` dropped from the CSS selector | *a selected card is painted* |
| gallery early return removed | *gallery mode is left alone* |

The CSS one is worth a line: the rule has to beat `.block-card.collapsed:hover`,
which is three classes, so the id in the selector is load-bearing. Without the
hover step in that test it could have been dropped and nothing would have
noticed.

Derived set by grep, **204 passed** before the rebase; **146 re-run after it**
(including batch 5's editor-tutorial, colour-preset and multicolour specs, since
the rebase pulled batch 5's changes into the same file). `npm run validate`
clean, 65 modules.

## One thing worth flagging about the conflict resolution

"Regenerate, never hand-merge" recovers whatever a generator owns and **silently
discards anything in the same files that it does not**. Batch 5 had added a
script tag and the MoS button to `edit.html`, which is hand-authored. Before
resolving I checked that this branch's HTML changes were *stamps only* — they
were — then took `next-update`'s side and regenerated, so batch 5's additions
survived. Both were verified present afterwards rather than assumed.

## For the owner, after merge

- Nothing to probe: no SQL, so `Supabase Preview` will report `SKIPPED`.
- The two accordion bugs you reported are **not** in this PR; they are going
  into batch 7 with C3, and the preview-reset one is being kept in front of the
  SectionedBox work as you asked.

body:
Refs #63
Tracking plan: .ai/runs/2026-09-20-extension-package-manifest.md
Source doc: .ai/specs/2026-09-20-extension-package-manifest.md
Status: in-progress

## 🎯 What changes

Adds the installable extension package manifest contract and pure compatibility decision described by the design spec. Cezar can validate `cezar.extension.json` documents and refuse unsupported API generations, release ranges, or entrypoint kinds before an installer executes extension code.

## 📋 Scope

The change is isolated to `packages/extension-api`: a dependency-free semver subset, generation-aware package-manifest validation, the ordered host compatibility verdict, tests, public exports, documentation, and a worked JSON example. It intentionally adds no installer or runtime consumer. `cezar` and `entrypoints` are strict for API generation 1; top-level metadata remains forward-compatible.

## 💥 Compatibility

Existing `ExtensionManifest` validation and compiled-in extension behavior remain unchanged. The new strict rules apply only to package manifests for this validator's API generation; newer generations are reported as unsupported rather than interpreted.

## 🧪 Validation

Passed: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:unit`, `npm run build`, `npm run test:package`, and the focused extension-api manifest/range/surface tests (88 tests). `npm test` reached the suite but remains red on unrelated base failures: a stale Jira compatibility expectation, process-dependent server/open-in-app/route-parity failures, and existing web task-header/automations/task-files failures. No UI surface is changed; browser QA is not applicable and this PR uses `skip-qa`.
