author: n1tzankl
body:
`{ fence: false }` returns the table alone, with `bytes: 0` and nothing shed.

### Why

A second fence on one pull request is a second comment. `githubStore.list`
reads every issue comment that carries one, so the summary `sync` is about to
write — repeating every comment's fence — would be read back as **one more
comment**, with an id nothing can resolve: it points at the summary, not at
what a reviewer clicked.

That comment would hold the gate for ever. A reviewer resolving everything they
wrote would not clear it, because nothing they can click owns that id. It is
the exact failure `runGateContract` exists to prevent, arriving through the
door nobody was watching.

Found while wiring `sync` in `maple-action`, before it was written rather than
after it shipped.

### The alternative

Give the action its own table renderer. That is the drift this sequence of work
exists to remove, so: core renders, the action asks for what it needs.

`docs/connectors.md` records the rule where a connector author meets it. 890
tests, `lint typecheck test build format:check` green.

body:
Makes the HoReCa digest genuinely useful and honest about its data. Three parts, all built:

> **Note:** stacks on #20 (branched off `feat/aspirational-districts` for the stylesheet cache-busting fix). Merge #20 first and this diff reduces to just these changes.

## 1. Commodity picker (the dropdown)
`/digest` now reads `?item=...` and renders a grouped multi-select. `commodity_options()` splits choices by evidence: **6** with wholesale + quick-commerce (full spread) and **~230** wholesale-only (which show the real Agmarknet price, honest *"No retail offer / Not comparable"* — never a fabricated retail). Board, tiles, and text payload follow the selection.

## 2. "Getting real-time prices" explainer
States the truth instead of implying a live feed: **wholesale is near-live** (Agmarknet, daily), **quick-commerce has no open/licensed API** and the connector already refuses to scrape (`ScraperForbiddenError`), so retail is a manual panel.

## 3. Manual price-entry panel (the daily workflow) — NEW
`/panel` (Operations → Price panel, linked from the digest): a human checks the apps and types what they see — commodity, platform, pack size, selling price, optional MRP + product link, date — with a recent-entries table. Each submission flows through the **same `QuickCommerceConnector.ingest()`** the CSV importer uses, so a typed entry gets identical ₹/kg normalisation, the `retail_offer` class, a `RetailOfferDetail`, and mandatory provenance (product link, or a generated `manual-panel://` URI — never blank). Entries hit the board immediately and are never averaged with wholesale.

## Tests
`commodity_options` split; the panel form records a normalised, sourced ₹/kg observation and rejects a non-numeric price with an error (nothing saved). All quick-commerce/digest tests green; ruff clean on new code.

author: jj20love
body:
## #213 没修对

上一版的判据写成 `resumeStatus != null`——「本届有任何简历记录就照常渲染进度」。

但社员在投递页**根本提交不了**，本届会出现的只有早年自动建出来的空草稿（`status=1`）。拿它当「有申请记录」，这一屏就对社员显示：

> 草稿（尚未提交） / 继续填写并提交

正是要藏掉的东西。

线上核查，cycle 14 挂着 **4 个** `status=1` 的社员空草稿：

```sql
SELECT r.status, COUNT(*) FROM resume r JOIN user u ON u.user_id=r.user_id
WHERE r.cycle_id=14 AND u.is_member=1 GROUP BY r.status;
→ status=1  条数=4
```

四个人全都没被拦住，修了等于没修。

## 改动

判据改成「**没有真的提交过**」，和本页 `submitted` 的定义保持一致：

```ts
const submitted = (resumeStatus ?? 0) >= 2;
if (submitted) return false;
```

提交过的仍照常渲染真实进度——典型是本届投递后被录取、回来看面试结果的人。这个分支是有意保留的，不能因为「是社员」就把人家的结果页吃掉。

## 测试

`memberGate.test.ts` 补了一条专门锁这次回归的：**只有草稿时仍显示社员态**（`status` 0 和 1 都断言）。原有 5 条不变，共 6 条全过。

全量 411 passed；`resumeFieldDrag.test.tsx` 仍是已知的既有 flaky（未改动的 origin/main 上同样复现）。

author: alimuzzaman
body:
Pairs with WPDevelopers/wp-scheduled-posts-pro#18. Merge that one first, or merge both together.

## What this does

Google Business Profile is marketed as a Pro feature in `readme.txt:26`, but it was implemented end to end in this plugin and gated by one client-side check in `GoogleBusiness.jsx:271`. Anyone hitting the REST or AJAX endpoints directly got the feature for free. The implementation now ships with SchedulePress Pro 5.4.0, and what stays here is the upsell.

## Audit result

Google Business was the only misplaced feature. The rest of the free/Pro boundary was already correct:

| Feature | In free | Where it runs |
|---|---|---|
| Missed Schedule handler | settings toggle only | Pro |
| Auto and Manual Scheduler | settings toggle only | Pro |
| Advanced Schedule | settings toggle only | Pro |
| Republish and Unpublish | settings toggle only | Pro |
| Elementor section schedule | settings toggle only | Pro |
| Publish now with future date | settings toggle only | Pro |

Multi-profile sharing was already gated on the server, not just in the UI: `Helper::get_social_profile()` runs the `wpsp_social_profile_limit_checkpoint` filter and slices to one profile without Pro.

## The seam

Rather than cutting a Google-Business-shaped hole, this adds a registry any social network can describe itself through. `WPSP\Social\Platforms` reads `wpsp_social_platforms`, and every consumer reads the registry: Share Now dispatch, character limits, custom templates, AI caption budgets, the reconnect maintenance job, the settings card, the template tab, the Elementor modal, the classic editor share box and the post panel. The next network Pro adds needs no change here.

New hooks:

| Hook | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `wpsp_social_platforms` | describe a platform |
| `wpsp_instant_share_{platform}` | share one post to one profile |
| `wpsp_social_fetch_profile_response` | answer the connect AJAX for a platform free does not ship |
| `wpsp_social_profile_fields` | replace the Social Profile card |
| `wpsp_social_template_tabs` | replace the Social Templates tab |
| `wpsp_el_modal_social_platform_fields` | render the Elementor block |
| `wpsp_calendar_delete_event` | clear an advanced schedule |
| `wpsp_social_platforms_loaded` | ordering marker after the built-ins boot |

## What free users see

A platform listed in `Platforms::PRO_UPSELL` with nothing serving it renders locked on all five surfaces it appears on today: the Social Profile card, the Social Templates tab, the classic editor share row, the Elementor modal header, and the Manage Social Sharing tab in the post panel. Each carries a name, a logo, a sentence and a link to pricing.

The entry retires itself the moment Pro registers the same slug, so one build serves both tiers with no `is_pro` branching in the UI. Without Pro the card opens the pricing popup. With a Pro too old to have claimed the platform it says "update SchedulePress Pro" instead, because selling someone a licence they already hold is the wrong answer.

The Google Business images stay in this plugin, since all five locked surfaces render them and Pro reuses them through `WPSP_ASSETS_URI`.

## Version mismatch

`WPSP_MIN_PRO_VERSION` is new, and it is what the admin notice reads. Bump that constant, not the check, when a future feature moves out. The notice says nothing about which feature is affected, because that list changes every time.

It now fires only when Pro is active. The old check used `is_plugin_installed()`, which nagged anyone with an inactive copy sitting in their plugins folder.

Pro 5.4.0 stays dormant against this plugin's predecessors, so release order does not matter.

## Bugs fixed

- `Calendar.php` did `use WPSP_PRO\Scheduled\Published` and instantiated it with no guard. Deleting an advanced-scheduled post from the calendar was a fatal error on a site without Pro. It now asks through a filter and returns a 400 when nobody answers.
- `npm run pot` walked `node_modules` and exhausted PHP's memory parsing bundled JavaScript. It only stayed hidden while nobody had run `npm install`.

## Verification

100 unit tests pass, up from 82. New coverage for the registry, the version notice and the reconnect merges. The stub `add_filter()` became a real in-memory hook store, because a registry built entirely out of a filter cannot be tested against a no-op.

Checked on a local sandbox site rooted at this branch, with Pro pointed at its matching branch:

With Pro active, the settings card renders as `social-platform`, the registry reports `google_business` at 1500 characters, the locked entry retires, and exactly one card and one tab exist. Every Google Business hook is registered once and comes from Pro.

With Pro deactivated, `WPSP\Social\GoogleBusiness`, `WPSCP_GOOGLE_BUSINESS_OPTION_NAME` and the token-refresh listener are all absent, the card and tab revert to the locked placeholder, the locked entry reports a label and a resolving icon URL, and `/` and `/wp-json/` both answer 200 with no fatals.

That live check is what caught the one real bug in this branch: the platform filters ran after `normalize()`, which `array_values()` every `fields` map, so Pro's replacement appended a second card instead of taking the placeholder's place and the placeholder won. Fixed in 7d4c3733 with a test that pins the ordering.

Not verified: this plugin's 5.3.4 with Pro 5.4.0, and the integration suite, which needs the WordPress test library.

## Data

Saved settings and post meta are left alone. A free-only site keeps its `google_business_profile_list` and its orphaned `wpsp_google_business_token_refresh` events. The hook name has not changed, so Pro reattaches to the same events rather than rescheduling from scratch.

Full write-up in `docs/specs/free-pro-separation.md`.

author: michalprusek
body:
Follow-up to #553 — the three items it listed as "recorded, not fixed here", plus two asked for directly.

## Owner-only controls

`ProjectService.updateProject` narrows with `findFirst({ id, userId })`, so **rename, type and model are owner-only**. `ProjectDetail` passed all three handlers unconditionally, so a shared annotator's click came back as a 404 *after* the optimistic update had already painted the new value. The type pill has had this shape far longer than the model pill; one ownership gate fixes both.

The chain had a hole at every layer:

- `getProjectById` did not return `isOwned`/`isShared` at all — unlike `getUserProjects`, whose shape its own comment claims to match.
- `mapProjectFields` would have stripped them anyway. That is the enumerative-mapper hazard for the **third time in two PRs**, so it now has its own tests.

`verified` stays ungated — the backend deliberately lets an accepted-share annotator set it.

`undefined` counts as owned: treating "not loaded yet" as not-owned would flash a read-only header at the real owner on every page load.

## Hole detection, only where it means something

Offered on **`spheroid` and `wound`**, hidden everywhere else.

| Type | Why |
|---|---|
| `microtubules` | Produces polylines; `detect_holes` never reaches polygonisation, so the toggle could not apply at all |
| `sperm`, `microcapsule`, `neurite`, `spheroid_invasive` | **Do** honour it in the ML service (`predict`, `predict_neurite_soma`, `predict_disintegration`), but an interior hole in a sperm head, a capsule, a soma or a disintegrating corona is noise rather than structure |

Where the toggle is hidden the request carries the default `true`, **not the per-user global**: a parameter the user cannot see must not be one they are silently subject to — a `false` set on a spheroid project would otherwise follow them into a neurite one, with no control to turn it back on.

Normalised on **both** sides (`resolveDetectHoles`). Doing it only in the browser would leave the rule cosmetic: a stale tab could still POST `false` and the ML service would obey it — the same lesson as #553's backend resolver with no call sites.

## Header status is a bare dot

The words beside it were asked to go. The tooltip and `aria-label` keep them and `role="status"` keeps it announced, so nothing is lost for anyone who needs it.

## The i18n validator now refuses a file that does not parse

It matches keys with regular expressions and reported **"Complete (2102 keys)" for six files with unbalanced braces** — measured last session, caught only by `tsc`. `ts.createSourceFile` collects syntax errors on `parseDiagnostics` rather than throwing, and nothing was reading them. Verified by breaking a file:

```
❌ src/translations/cs.ts does not parse.
   2785:14 Property assignment expected.
   Key validation is regex-based and would report this file as complete.
```

The guard fails loudly if a future TypeScript version stops exposing `parseDiagnostics`, rather than going quietly back to accepting broken files.

## Production migration history — repaired separately (already done)

`prisma migrate deploy` had been **broken on production since 2026-06**: `20260516_add_project_folders` sat in `_prisma_migrations` as started-but-never-finished and blocked everything after it. **12 migrations existed in the repo with no record at all**, having been applied by hand.

Before touching anything I verified every one of them against the live schema — **24 of 24 objects present** (5 tables, 12 indexes, 7 constraints, plus the column and check-constraint changes). That found one genuine gap: `20260828_default_preferred_lang_en` had **never been applied**. `schema.prisma` declares `preferredLang @default("en")`; production still had `'cs'`.

So: applied that one ALTER, then recorded all 13 via `prisma migrate resolve --applied` (after dumping `_prisma_migrations` so the step is one command from reversible). Result:

```
26 migrations found in prisma/migrations
No pending migrations to apply.
```

Every repo migration is now recorded. One orphan remains — `20250921133009_add_remember_me_to_session` is recorded but its directory is gone from the repo; `migrate deploy` tolerates it.

## Verification

- frontend **5396 / 5396**, backend **4015 / 4015**, `make ci` green
- every new rule mutation-tested; one survived first (`mapProjectFields` stripping `isOwned` — the same blind spot as `segmentationModel`) and now has tests
- three suites failed honestly on the behaviour change and were updated to assert it rather than to restore the old value: the per-type queue table now pins `detectHoles` per type, `getProjectById` asserts the ownership fields, and the queue schema test states that `model` has no default on purpose

## What and why

Builds the Categories screens on top of the existing `categories` table and `CategoriesRepository`, replacing the four `/categories…` stubs in the router.

- **Categories page**: Expenses / Income tabs with the group count, groups that expand to their categories, reordering by drag or the "Move up" / "Move down" semantic actions. First launch shows an intro line and every empty group says "No categories yet" with an "Add category to …" button; the list ends with "New category group".
- **Category editor**: name, type (create only), group (required, with a "New group" shortcut), icon, colour or "Group", hidden, and what already uses it.
- **Group editor**: name, type locked once the group has categories or transactions, hidden (which hides its categories from the pickers too), and its categories to open, reorder or add to. Groups have no icon or colour field, as DESIGN.md asks: a new one takes the next palette colour.
- **Delete**: counts transactions, reminders and the budget that goes with it, and asks where they go — to its group (default), to another category picked in a sheet, or uncategorized. A group has to be emptied first.
- **Category picker sheet**: accent-insensitive search, groups selectable as "Whole group", hidden items left out, "New category" and "Manage" at the bottom (off where leaving the sheet would drop the caller's flow).

Data layer, kept minimal: `CategoryUsage` plus `watchAll`, `reorder` and `usage` on `CategoriesRepository`. `remove` now moves **reminders** as well as transactions in the same database transaction (budgets already cascaded). `reorderIds` moved from `features/assets_accounts/models/` to `core/`, since both features reorder the same way — no behaviour change, the existing test moved with it.

No schema change, no backup format change, no new dependency.

Closes #<issue>

## How to test

All data below is synthetic; a fresh install seeds only the default groups.

1. Fresh install → drawer → **Categories**. The Expenses tab shows the seeded groups with the intro line and "No categories yet" under each one.
2. Tap "Add category to Food", name it `Groceries`, pick an icon and a colour, save. It appears inside Food; the group now says "1 category".
3. Drag `Groceries` and a second category to reorder them, then reorder two groups. Reopen the page: the order stuck. Repeat with a screen reader using "Move up" / "Move down".
4. Open `Groceries` → change its group to another expense group → save. Its transactions stay with it. The type field is locked with an explanation.
5. Open the group `Food` → its type is locked ("already has categories or transactions") and "Delete group" is disabled with "Move or delete its category first."
6. Add an expense to `Groceries`, then open `Groceries` → **Delete category**. The dialog counts the transaction and offers: to `Food` (default), to another category (opens the searchable sheet — try `rént` to find `Rent`), or Uncategorized. Confirm and check the transaction moved.
7. Mark a group as hidden and reopen the picker from step 6: neither the group nor its categories are listed.
8. Repeat steps 1–2 in Spanish and French (Settings → language) and in dark mode.

## Checklist

- [x] `fvm flutter analyze` reports no issues
- [x] `fvm dart format .` leaves no diff
- [x] `fvm flutter test` passes (138 tests)
- [x] New logic is covered by tests — `test/features/categories_test.dart` (grouping, colour inheritance, list, editors, delete with reassignment, picker search) and `test/data/repositories_test.dart` (`usage`, `reorder`, reminder reassignment)
- [x] Schema change? None — no migration needed
- [x] Backup format change? None
- [x] New strings added to `app_en.arb`, `app_es.arb` **and** `app_fr.arb`, screen checked in the three locales — 45 keys in all three, `l10n_untranslated.txt` empty, and `test/features/categories_test.dart` renders every screen in en/es/fr on a 360×780 surface (an overflow fails the test).
- [x] No new dependency with network access, telemetry or ads
- [x] No real financial data in the diff, the screenshots or the tests
- [x] `CHANGELOG.md` updated under "Unreleased"

author: sammachin
body:
The catalog build is supposed to run every 30mins, however this morning it had not been run for 12 hours despite there being new nodes.

I think the problem is the timings, the action is scheduled to run at 0 and 30 mins past the hour
GitHub's scheduled workflows are best-effort with no guarantee: the schedule event gets delayed during high load, and under enough load it's dropped entirely, not just deferred. And */30 lands on the two single most popular scheduling times on all of GitHub, so :00 and :30 are the most congested and the most likely to be delayed or skipped. We don't see any failures in the actions log it just looks like the job gets skipped.

This PR adjusts the times to 07 and 37 which will hopefully avoid some of the peak rush times on jobs and improve the sucess.

body:
Priority: P2 | Area: area:render | Labels: feat,area:render,P2 | Milestone: v0.1.0 | RFC: terminal-feature-gap-analysis.md P2 row | Task: CTX-0583

Closes #1145

## Summary

`UnderlineStyle::Single`, `Curly`, `Dotted`, and `Dashed` all painted one
identical full-width bottom strip; only `Double` differed. This change maps
each SGR `4:x` style to its own deterministic paint while keeping
`Single`/`Double` byte-identical to the previous output.

Recon:

- `bitty-vt` already parses every style (`parse_underline_style`, `SGR 4`,
  `4:0..4:5`, `21`, `24`); `bitty-term-state` persists it on the cell.
- The only paint path is `bitty-render` `emit_decorations`; both the GPU
  present/headless RGBA path (`gpu.rs`) and the `sw-fallback`
  `draw_list_onto` (`software.rs`) consume `DrawList::fills` rectangles, so
  one Core-owned emitter owns distinctness for every backend.

## Change

- `crates/bitty-render/src/grid.rs`: `push_underline_pattern` emits per-style
  geometry from an `UnderlinePlacement` (absolute cell origin, span, cell
  height, thickness, resolved color):
  - `Single`/`Double`: unchanged full-width bars.
  - `Dotted`: `thickness`-wide dots, pitch `2 * thickness`.
  - `Dashed`: `thickness + 1`-wide dashes, pitch `2 * (thickness + 1)`.
  - `Curly`: 4-segment stepped wave, crest `2 * thickness` above the strip.
  - Patterns are anchored to absolute pixel columns so adjacent cells
    continue one run; every rectangle stays inside its cell.
- `MAX_DECORATION_RECTS_PER_CELL = 64` bounds the emitted rectangles; hostile
  cell widths widen the pattern step instead of growing the fill list.

No new dependencies, no new public API beyond the documented bound, all
arithmetic saturating, no panics on production paths.

## TDD evidence

Pre-fix red (`cargo test -p bitty-render --lib grid::tests::underline`):
`underline_styles_paint_distinct_geometry` failed because `Dotted` emitted
`[(0, 12, 8, 2)]`, byte-identical to `Single` (the collapse).

Post-fix:

- `cargo test -p bitty-render --locked`: 209 lib tests + suites green.
- `cargo test -p bitty-render --features sw-fallback --locked`: green,
  including `underline_styles_composite_to_distinct_rgba`, which asserts the
  four composited RGBA surfaces are pairwise distinct.
- `cargo test -p bitty-runtime --test present_golden --locked`: 10/10 golden
  digests unchanged (no golden matrix contains SGR `4:x` paint).
- `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --locked`: green.

## Gates

- `just check`: exit 0
- `cargo check --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu --workspace --all-targets --locked`: exit 0
- `just ci-local`: exit 0
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`: exit 0

## Docs

`terminal-feature-gap-analysis.md` P2 row describes the current partial state;
the gap remains tracked there until the follow-up docs sync updates it.

## Risks

- Curly/dotted/dashed are rectangle approximations of procedural sprites
  (ghostty draws them with curves); they are distinct, deterministic, and
  bounded, not pixel-identical to ghostty.
- Sub-thickness pattern steps degenerate to partial bars when a cell is too
  narrow to hold one pattern cycle; covered by the bounded/inside-cell tests.

author: smaug123
body:
Stage E2c-1 of `docs/plans/2026-09-01-ipv4-only-locked-v1.md`, following #490.

`Ipv6IsolationMode` gains `Ipv4OnlyLockedV1` and the state schema gains its
spelling, so a locked session can be *recorded*. It still cannot be *reached*:
`ConfiguredIpv6Profile::admit` refuses the profile, so nothing builds a plan
carrying the mode.

## Why E2c became three PRs

Building it found that the locked start does not fit the machine the legacy
one runs on. `start_agent_vm_session` is synchronous, iterates
`AgentVmStartStep`, and is the entry point for *both* the daemon and
`writ-agent-vm-runner`. The locked tail fits neither constraint: waiting for
the guest's `security-ready` record is a bounded async poll, and the release
is minted by the state store rather than constructed by a caller. Adding
locked variants to `AgentVmStartStep` would have handed that interpreter steps
it has no way to carry out.

So the locked sequence is its own ordered type, `LockedStartStep` (create →
verify → start → final firewall → await `security-ready` → release), each step
naming the `LockedPhase` it establishes, so the order the sequence walks and
the order Stage E1 records are the same order. `AgentVmStartStep` is
untouched.

E2c-2 has the daemon interpret that sequence; E2c-3 does the post-release
migration off `container exec`, points `admit` at `admit_locked`, and opens
the profile on an empty host-placement pin list.

## A locked session is managed-only, structurally

Its release signal exists only once the state store has recorded the attempt
to send it (Stage E1's one door). A start path with no store could therefore
start a guest, confine it, and never release it. `start_agent_vm_session`
refuses the mode before creating anything, and a test asserts that no
container command ran — the refusal has to come at the one point where
refusing costs nothing.

That is precisely the case that function's own doc comment anticipated: it
said its "a plan cannot carry a closed profile" reasoning would break when a
closed profile got an active mode. This is that profile, and the refusal is
the answer.

## What the variant buys today: the compiler

Five exhaustive matches had to answer for it. More to the point, five
`== Ipv4OnlyNoGuestIpv6` comparisons would have quietly handed a locked
session the legacy answer — the compiler says nothing about those. They are
now `Ipv6IsolationMode` predicates named for the question each site asks:

- `requires_guest_command` — both IPv4-only profiles hold the workload until
  the host says go, so both need something to release.
- `has_firewall_ipv6_cidr` — only dual-stack derives a PF IPv6 rule from the
  session's `/64`.
- `startable_without_a_state_store` — only the locked profile cannot.

A mode added later has to decide rather than inherit whichever branch it falls
into.

## Oracles

- The sequence establishes the phases in order and never goes backwards;
  `Claimed` is absent (a start begins there rather than reaching it) and the
  release step establishes `ReleaseAttempted`, not `WorkloadReleased`.
- Create precedes verify precedes start; the final firewall precedes the guest
  handshake, which precedes the release; and no step in the sequence is an
  `exec` into the guest.
- The release step's invocation is the `container kill --signal USR1` a dry
  run prints, and nothing more — the one that may actually be sent is minted
  by the store.
- A storeless start refuses the locked profile and runs nothing; the other
  modes are unaffected.
- A profile that holds its workload cannot be planned without a guest command,
  asserted per mode against written-out answers with a length check, so a new
  mode fails here until someone decides.
- Two weakenings were injected and fail these tests: a storeless start that
  runs the locked profile, and a locked mode that does not require a guest
  command.

## One test rewritten rather than extended

Stage D's `the_locked_spelling_parses_here_and_is_unknown_to_an_older_binary`
used this build's `Ipv6IsolationMode` as the stand-in for an older binary —
valid only while that type lacked the variant. The stand-in is now an explicit
two-variant enum in the test, so the rollback property is still tested rather
than quietly lost.

## Gates

`cargo fmt`, `clippy --all-targets --all-features -D warnings`, `cargo test`,
the `vm-client` lib+bins build, `cargo doc` with warnings denied,
`scripts/test-proof-helpers.sh`, and `nix build .#checks.aarch64-darwin.tests`.

author: caesarakalaeii
body:
The static warm list was the flimsiest part of the pure-node transport's resilience story: handles verified at audit time are stale in hours, and this session already needed two manual re-audits (warm-room diversification, then overnight additions from the connect log). The curator automates the audit, with the constraints that made the manual process safe:

- **Cadence**: every 30 min, liveness-probe tab-less warm rooms (api-live route, fail-open; warm tabs count as coverage — a captured session outlives its stream).
- **Acquisition** (only under coverage floor of 2): ONE live-feed discovery pass on a pool-lane page (same UA/request-blocking as a capture — `ViewerPool.withDiscoveryPage`), filter (never canary, never listed, 6h cooldown after failed verification), liveness-check, capture-verify at most 2. The capture IS the classic-ness test — a passing capture proves the harvestable im/fetch AND leaves the room warm.
- **Budget encoded**: any 403 (discovery or capture) benches all acquisition for an hour — the operator's manual rule since 2026-09-19, now in code. Worst case ~4-6 TikTok requests/day.
- **Fail-conservative**: uncertainty (probe errors, discovery failures, exhausted candidates) leaves the list untouched. The curator only ever ADDS; removal stays a human call (breaker + NoWarmSession alert cover failing rooms).
- **Off by default**: `SIGNER_WARM_AUTOCURATE` — the caesar flag flip is a separate decision after this soaks on main.

Tests: 71/71 (6 new — coverage floor respected, live+classic acquisition, candidate filtering, non-classic cooldown, 403 bench mid-cycle and on discovery). Signer README rows updated.

author: arena-ai-coding-agent[bot]
body:
## Summary

- carries forward the standalone Windows desktop runtime from #686
- fixes the failed packaged Windows end-to-end run by starting PostgreSQL through bundled `pg_ctl.exe` on Windows instead of spawning `postgres.exe` directly
- keeps PostgreSQL loopback-only, validates the generated port, and captures bounded PostgreSQL startup diagnostics
- makes packaged smoke failures exit immediately instead of hanging behind an interactive recovery dialog
- adds a regression test for the Windows startup strategy and exact `pg_ctl` arguments

## Root cause

Run 35503150362 reached the real packaged executable, initialized the UTF-8 cluster, and then PostgreSQL rejected its direct server launch:

> Execution of PostgreSQL by a user with administrative permissions is not permitted.

The GitHub Windows runner's `runneradmin` account carries the Administrators group. PostgreSQL's `pg_ctl.exe` uses its native restricted-token launch path for this case; `embedded-postgres.start()` bypassed that path by spawning `postgres.exe` directly. The app now uses `pg_ctl start -w` on Windows and retains the existing `pg_ctl stop` shutdown.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit`
- `npm test -- --run` — 345 files / 4,953 tests passed
- focused desktop posture tests — 9 tests passed
- `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high`
- `npm run build`
- `npm run desktop:runtime`
- `cd electron && npm run verify:runtime`
- local real PostgreSQL lifecycle smoke via `pg_ctl`: initialize, start, connect, assert `listen_addresses=127.0.0.1`, stop, and assert no `postmaster.pid`

This replaces #686 so the packaged Windows check can validate the corrected runtime.

body:
> Where do I find this text? 'THE FRONT PAGE ... Title, Strapline, The Sprint loop - heading, Plan, Build, Open, Review, Retro'. I can't actually find it

The words are all still there. The **directions** were wrong.

There is no front page any more. The way in became **Before you start** (two tabs) and then **Your Product Goal**, and these labels were left describing the game as it used to be. A `where` that names a screen nobody can reach is worse than no `where` at all, because it sends somebody looking.

## Where that text actually is

| In the editor | On screen |
|---|---|
| Title ("Build a Zoo") | **Your Product Goal**, at the top |
| Strapline | **Your Product Goal**, under the title |
| The Sprint loop, heading and all five steps | **How the zoo works**, and again on **Your Product Goal** |

The loop now says *both* screens, because it is on both: the same five lines from one source, read once against when each step happens, and once beside the Goal they aim at. Somebody editing it should know they are changing both.

The group is called **The way in** now, which is what those screens are, and the five steps are labelled "The Sprint loop - Plan" and so on rather than bare verbs, so they are recognisable in a list.

## Three tests hold it

- Everything in the group names a screen that exists.
- Nothing anywhere points at a front page.
- The Sprint loop admits to both of its screens.

## One thing for you to decide

The Sprint loop being on two consecutive screens is a real duplication, not just a labelling problem. It reads better on **How the zoo works**, where each step is shown against when it happens; on the Product Goal screen it is reading matter beside the one thing that screen asks you to write, which is what you had me move to the top in the first place.

I have left it, because removing it is a content decision rather than a fix. Say the word and it comes off the Product Goal screen.

## Gate

`tsc` clean, 1695 tests passing across 168 files (3 new), lint at 134 warnings, build clean.

author: amirbiron
body: ## ✨ תיאור קצר שני טסטים ב-`tests/test_redis_safety.py` נפלו ב-CI על `3.0` במקום `2.0` או `1.0` ועברו כשהריצו אותם לבד. הסיבה לא הייתה בטסטים: ההכרעה מי קובע את ה-timeout של Redis התפצלה לשני מקומות עם ברירות מחדל סותרות, והתשובה נקבעה לפי איזה מודול `config` הספיק להיכנס ל-`sys.modules`. מתחת לזה התגלה באג פרודקשן: `SAFE_MODE` לא הוריד את ה-timeouts לשנייה כפי שהתיעוד הבטיח, אלא נתן 3 ו-5. ## 📦 שינויים עיקריים - [x] קוד (Backend) - [ ] בוט טלגרם - [ ] מסד נתונים/מיגרציות - [x] תיעוד (docs/) - [ ] DevOps/CI/CD פירוט נקודות: - **`runtime_settings.py` (חדש, חסר תלויות):** `resolve_redis_timeouts(explicit_connect, explicit_socket, safe_mode)` — פונקציה טהורה שמכריעה לפי סדר קדימות אחד: ערך מפורש ← `1/1` ב-`SAFE_MODE` ← `3/5`. לצידה `redis_timeouts(cfg, env)` כנקודת כניסה אחת שמחברת קונפיג ו-ENV, ו-`safe_mode_enabled()`. - **`config.py`:** `REDIS_CONNECT_TIMEOUT` ו-`REDIS_SOCKET_TIMEOUT` הפכו ל-`Optional[float] = None` עם `ge=0` ו-`allow_inf_nan=False`. עד עכשיו ברירת המחדל שלהם נקבעה בזמן import דרך `float(os.getenv(...))`, ולכן השדה **לעולם לא היה `None`** — וזה מה שהפך את מסלול ה-`SAFE_MODE` ב-`cache_manager` לקוד מת. משתנה סביבה מפורש עדיין נקרא, כי pydantic-settings קורא אותו לפי שם השדה. - **`cache_manager.py` ו-`main.py`:** שניהם קוראים רק לפונקציה הזו. ברירות המחדל הכפולות נמחקו, וגם הנפילה ל-`0.25` ב-`main.py` שהייתה מתה מאותה סיבה. **הערך האפקטיבי בפרודקשן לא משתנה** — הוא נשאר 3 כפי שהיה, וזה נבדק. - **איחוד קריאת `SAFE_MODE`:** הדגל נקרא בחמישה מקומות בשלוש רשימות ערכים שונות — חלקן קיבלו `"y"` וחלקן לא, ורק אחת עשתה `strip()`. עכשיו זו פונקציה אחת. - **`REDIS_CONNECT_TIMEOUT=` ריק כבר לא מפיל את הבוט.** ערך ריק פירושו "לא הוגדר", במקום `ValidationError` שמונע מהשירות לעלות. - **טסטים:** שני הטסטים השבורים נכתבו מחדש כקריאות ישירות לפונקציה הטהורה — בלי `importlib.reload`, בלי `os.environ` גלובלי, ובלי תלות במה שכבר נטען בתהליך. נוסף טסט שמוכיח ש-`SAFE_MODE` נותן שנייה אחת גם כשהקונפיג טעון, וטסט חיווט שמוודא שהערך שההכרעה מחזירה הוא זה שמגיע ל-`redis.from_url`. - **תיעוד:** `GUIDES/GUIDE_CONNECTION_POOLING.md` הצהיר `5`/`5` בזמן שהקונפיג הצהיר `3`/`5` — יושר. `docs/environment-variables.rst` ותיאורי ה-Config Inspector חודדו. ### מה היה שבור, בשפה פשוטה היו שני פקידים שמחליטים כמה שניות מחכים ל-Redis, וכל אחד מהם החזיק דף ברירות מחדל משלו. הפקיד הראשון (`config.py`) מילא את הטופס **תמיד**, כבר ברגע שהתוכנית עלתה, ולכן הפקיד השני (`cache_manager`) — זה שהיה אמור להגיד "רגע, אנחנו ב-SAFE_MODE, תוריד לשנייה" — מעולם לא הגיע לדבר. בטסטים הפקיד הראשון לפעמים לא היה בחדר, ואז התשובה יצאה אחרת. עכשיו יש פקיד אחד, והוא ממלא את הטופס רק כשבאמת ביקשו ממנו. ## 🧪 בדיקות - [x] Unit - [x] Integration - [ ] Manual **שחזור הכשל לפני התיקון.** ריצה מלאה של הסוויטה על commit ההורה, עם `-n auto --dist=loadscope` כמו ב-CI, שחזרה את שני הכשלים של CI מילה במילה: ``` FAILED tests/test_redis_safety.py::test_connect_respects_env_timeouts - Asser... FAILED tests/test_redis_safety.py::test_connect_safe_mode_defaults_to_1s - As... ``` **מדידת הבאג עצמו.** טסט שהריץ את `CacheManager` הישן עם `SAFE_MODE=1` ובלי משתני ENV מפורשים הדפיס `OLD CODE SAFE_MODE -> 3.0 5.0`, כלומר `assert (3.0, 5.0) == (1.0, 1.0)` — הטסט החדש נופל על הקוד הישן, כפי שנדרש. **אחרי התיקון.** `tests/test_redis_safety.py` ירוק בכל אחד מהמצבים: לבד, בתוך הריצה המלאה, עם הקונפיג האמיתי טעון מראש ל-`sys.modules` (התנאי שהפיל אותו קודם), ובשלושה זרעים של `pytest-randomly` יחד עם טסטים שמייבאים את הקונפיג. **אימות מול המקור.** התנהגות pydantic-settings 2.11 נבדקה בהרצה ולא מהזיכרון: שדה `Optional[float] = None` אכן נקרא מ-ENV, `ge=0` חל דרך ה-Union ופוסל ערך שלילי ו-`nan`, ו-`allow_inf_nan=False` פוסל `inf`. ## 🧪 בדיקות נדרשות ב‑PR - 🔍 Code Quality & Security - Unit Tests (3.11) - Unit Tests (3.12) ## 📝 סוג שינוי - [ ] feat: פיצ'ר חדש - [x] fix: תיקון באג - [ ] docs: שינוי תיעוד בלבד - [ ] refactor: שינוי קוד ללא שינוי התנהגות - [ ] perf: שיפור ביצועים - [ ] chore/ci: תשתית/CI - [ ] breaking change: שינוי שובר תאימות ## ✅ צ'קליסט - [x] הקוד עוקב אחרי הסגנון (flake8 על הקבצים שנגעתי בהם נקי; `mypy` ו-`ruff` נקיים על המודול החדש) - [x] בדיקות רצות ועוברות - [x] תיעוד עודכן - [x] לא נוספו ג'ובים חדשים - [x] משתני סביבה: עודכנו `docs/environment-variables.rst` **וגם** `services/config_inspector_service.py` - [x] לא נוספו/השתנו טוקנים של ערכת נושא - [x] אין סודות/מפתחות בקוד - [x] אין מחיקות מסוכנות - [x] הודעת הקומיט תואמת Conventional Commits - [ ] CHANGELOG — לא נדרש - [x] עיינתי במסמכי אתר התיעוד — נתיב: `docs/environment-variables.rst`, `docs/configuration.rst`, `docs/performance-scaling.rst`, `docs/doc-authoring.rst`, `GUIDES/GUIDE_CONNECTION_POOLING.md` | המשפט: "``REDIS_CONNECT_TIMEOUT``/``REDIS_SOCKET_TIMEOUT`` שמרניים. ב-``SAFE_MODE`` ברירות מחדל נמוכות יותר." ## 🧩 השפעות/סיכונים - **`SAFE_MODE` משנה התנהגות — וזו הכוונה.** מי שמפעיל אותו בלי להגדיר timeouts מפורשים יקבל מעכשיו `1/1` במקום `3/5`. זו ההתנהגות שהתיעוד מבטיח מאז ומתמיד; מה שהיה עד היום הוא הבאג. מי שרוצה את הערכים הישנים מגדיר אותם במפורש, והם מנצחים. - **במצב רגיל (בלי `SAFE_MODE`) שום ערך לא זז** — `3` ו-`5` כמו קודם, וגם `main.py` ממשיך לבדוק זמינות Redis עם אותן 3 שניות שהיו לו בפועל. - **הידוק ולידציה:** ערך שלילי, `nan` או `inf` ב-ENV יפילו את טעינת הקונפיג בזמן עלייה במקום לעבור בשקט ל-redis. ערך שאינו מספר הפיל כבר קודם. ## 🔗 קישורים - Issues קשורים: — - מסמכים/מפרטים רלוונטיים: [Branch Protection & PR Rules](../docs/branch-protection-and-pr-rules.rst) ## 🧯 סיכון / החזרה לאחור (Rollback) - `git revert` של הקומיט מחזיר את המצב הקודם במלואו. אין מיגרציה, אין שינוי סכימה, ואין מצב מתמשך שנכתב. - אם מתגלה בעיה רק עם `SAFE_MODE` — אפשר להגדיר `REDIS_CONNECT_TIMEOUT=3` ו-`REDIS_SOCKET_TIMEOUT=5` ב-ENV ולקבל בדיוק את ההתנהגות הישנה, בלי revert. --- 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_012HhLQAmzYQhruqGVYJXhiv --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_012HhLQAmzYQhruqGVYJXhiv)_ ## Summary by Sourcery Centralize Redis timeout and SAFE_MODE handling so production behavior is consistent, documented, and deterministic across services. Bug Fixes: - Unify Redis timeout resolution so explicit values take precedence, SAFE_MODE uses 1-second defaults, and normal defaults remain 3/5. - Ensure SAFE_MODE is interpreted consistently across cache, maintenance, file cleanup, and predictive actions. - Treat blank Redis timeout environment values as unset while rejecting invalid negative or non-finite configured values. Enhancements: - Centralize runtime setting resolution in a dependency-free module and use it across Redis integrations and configuration inspection. - Use the resolved Redis connection timeout for the availability probe while retaining separate probe bounds. - Replace order-dependent Redis safety tests with deterministic unit, configuration, and wiring coverage. Documentation: - Update Redis timeout and SAFE_MODE documentation and configuration inspector descriptions to reflect effective defaults. Tests: - Add coverage for timeout precedence, SAFE_MODE parsing, blank and invalid values, real configuration loading, and propagation to the Redis client.

author: max1874
body:
## Problem

`packages/protocol/src/operations.ts` has carried `update_room` and `rename` since the rewrite, and the website uses both for room settings and member management, but the agent-facing tool table stopped at nine. An owner's conversation could not rename its own member — a name it proposed at join, before it knew the work — or adjust the room it sits in. `04-codebase.md` §11 records the fixed nine as a deliberate v1 decision and names `tools.ts` + `stdio.ts` as the place to change it.

## Resulting behavior

Two tools join the shared table in `packages/protocol/src/tools.ts`:

| Tool | Parameters | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `update_room` | `name?`, `description?`, `rotateCode?` | the room's name, description or code |
| `rename` | `name` | this conversation's own member |

- **Neither takes a room.** The binding supplies it, as it already does for message IDs, the workspace and the conversation: a local bridge reads the joined marker, a connector reads the conversation handle.
- **Both are `connector: true`.** The definitions exist once so the local and remote surfaces cannot drift (02 §17 decision 16). `login` stays local-only because it writes a local credentials file and needs no conversation; neither applies here. The connector's surface grows from 8 to 10.
- **`rename` sends no `member`**, so a conversation can only rename the member it backs. That matches the Hub's authority, which passes `allowRoomOwner=false`: a room's owner may remove another account's member but not rename it. The tool description says so rather than implying broader reach.
- **Both refresh the joined marker.** It caches the member address and the room name, both of which these calls change, and `status` plus the local `already_in_room` message read it. A new narrow `Session.remark(patch)` does that; reusing `enter()` would reset unread state and reopen the link. `update_room` also refreshes the marker's code after a rotation, normalized, because the marker's copy is what lets a repeated join of the same room through: leaving it stale would pass the local check and reach the Hub as `no_such_room` for a room the conversation is sitting in.
- **`update_room` with no fields is refused** with `invalid_input`. Every field is optional so a caller can change one, but a call that changed nothing reported an update that never happened. No existing caller sends an empty patch.

Deliberately **no `notifications/tools/list_changed`**: `serveStdio` serves a list computed once at startup and `stdio.ts` does not declare the capability, so a static addition changes the list between processes rather than within one. That hook belongs to the deferred "expose fewer tools before joining" item.

No schema or protocol-version change, so there is no deployment ordering to observe.

## Validation

- `pnpm typecheck` — all packages, 5 clients and the website.
- `pnpm build` — notices, web, protocol and all five plugin bundles, plus the marketplace export; the new tools are present in every built bundle.
- `pnpm check:source`, `pnpm check:packages`.
- `pnpm test` excluding `@tandryio/opencode`: protocol 15, web 4, bridge 24, hub 42 + 5 workerd, dsh 8, codex 4, pi 7, claude 5. All pass.
- `pnpm test:e2e`, `pnpm test:marketplace`, `pnpm test:tooling`, `pnpm test:npm` all pass.
- New tests cover the two renderers, the tool schemas (no room parameter; the handle required on the connector), three bridge behaviours (the marker rewrite, the code shown only when rotated, and that a rename leaves the room, the code, the link and unread mail untouched), and that the marker's code stays current and normalized across a rotation.
- **CI is green on both jobs**, which includes `clients/opencode`. That suite cannot run on the machine that wrote this — it needs the opencode CLI and Bun, and the `opencode-ai` postinstall cannot fetch its platform binary there — so its tool-list assertion was updated alongside the other hosts and validated here instead. A parallel session ran it against a real CLI as well: 15/15, including `standalone bundle loads eleven native tools`.

## Follow-up

- `01-concepts.md` and `02-architecture.md` need the matching amendment, on the private side: the tool table is why `04` §11 records the fixed nine, and the room/member management boundary in 01 (the website manages rooms and members) is now shared with agents. The joined marker's `code` changes meaning from "the code the conversation joined with" to "a code that admits to this room", which the amendment should record.
- The coverage and the observed-vs-declared check for `join`'s undeclared `already_in_room` are separate work; see #2.

author: iret77
body: Closes #190. ## What was broken `releases/latest/download/latest.json` is what every installed aiui polls. `release-macos.yml` wrote one carrying a single platform key: ```json "platforms": { "darwin-aarch64": { "signature": …, "url": … } } ``` …and published the release immediately. The `windows-x86_64` entry was added afterwards by `release-windows.yml`, a **separate, manually dispatched** workflow. A missing target is not "no update available" — `tauri-plugin-updater` raises `TargetsNotFound`, so a Windows client's update check lands in the **error path**. Between the two workflow runs every Windows install was broken, and if the second dispatch was forgotten, permanently. That is what shipped in v0.10.1. The invariant was being maintained by a human remembering a second step. This makes it structural. ## What changed **The release is created as a draft.** `releases/latest/download/…` does not serve drafts, so clients keep resolving the previous **complete** feed while this one is half-assembled. `release-windows.yml` attaches the Windows half, validates the assembled feed, and only then un-drafts. **`release-macos.yml` dispatches the Windows workflow itself.** Completing a release is no longer something anyone has to remember — and forgetting now costs visibility (the release stays a draft) instead of silently breaking one platform. `workflow_dispatch` is kept so a failed run can be repeated by hand; the run is idempotent. **A Windows build failure now holds back the whole release, macOS included.** That is the correct coupling for a two-platform product: a release that only half exists is precisely what produced this bug. **`scripts/check-updater-feed.sh`** refuses a feed that is missing a shipped platform, carries an empty signature or url, points an entry at a **different release's** artifact, or advertises the wrong version. The shipped-platform list lives in that script alone, so adding `darwin-x86_64` later is a one-line change. ### Two tempting fixes this deliberately avoids **Carrying the previous release's Windows entry forward** is worse than the bug. The feed would say `"version": "0.11.0"` while `platforms["windows-x86_64"].url` points at the 0.10.1 installer — and the signature matches that older artifact, so it downloads, verifies and installs *cleanly*. The client restarts still on 0.10.1, the check offers 0.11.0 again, and round it goes. Worse, `/update` reports success with the **feed's** version (`http.rs` returns `available: Some(to_version)` from `latest.json`), so an agent is told "updated 0.10.1 → 0.11.0" while the machine never moved. A false success is harder to debug than an honest error. The guard rejects exactly this shape. **Swallowing `TargetsNotFound` client-side** would convert a loud wrong state into a silent one, telling a user several versions behind that they are current. ## Verification The release path itself needs macOS and Windows runners plus signing secrets, so it cannot be executed here. What *can* be verified was: - **`scripts/test-check-updater-feed.sh`** — 13 fixture cases, run in CI on every PR, all passing locally. They include the exact v0.10.1 shape (windows entry absent), a carried-forward entry pointing at `v0.10.1` while the feed claims `0.11.0`, empty signatures, missing urls, version and tag mismatches, unparsable JSON, and that an unknown platform is a note rather than a failure. A guard that quietly stopped guarding would be worse than none, which is why it is tested rather than trusted. - All three workflow files parse as YAML, and every embedded `bash` `run:` block passes `bash -n`. ## Compatibility - **`latest.json` is a wire contract** with clients from 0.1.2 onward, and its schema is fixed by `tauri-plugin-updater`. This change only ever *adds* the platform key that was missing — no client changes, no older client affected. - Asset URLs in already-published feeds keep resolving; nothing on past releases is renamed or removed. - No config-schema change, and no change to the agent-facing `update` tool. - **Operationally**: nothing is visible until the Windows run finishes. `CONTRIBUTING.md` now says so, including how to recover when that run fails. One note for the maintainer: the project's agent instructions still describe the Windows workflow as a manual second step, and that file lives outside this repo, so it is not updated here. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. Autofix is disabled.

author: kayibabe
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1 and #2 from the 2026-09-20 full-system audit (Codex-reviewed).

### 1. Auth/CORS fail-open outside development (High)

`backend/core/security.py` and `backend/main.py` gated every relaxed
security default (no API key required, wildcard CORS + credentials, docs
exposed) on `environment == "production"` — an allow-list of one. Any other
value (unset, `staging`, a typo) silently inherited dev-mode laxity. Codex
reproduced this live with `ENVIRONMENT=staging`: protected routes bypassed
API-key validation and CORS allowed any origin with credentials enabled.

**Fix:** inverted the gate to `environment == "development"` (a deny-list of
one) via `Settings.is_development`, and added
`backend.main._validate_environment_config()` so `create_app()` refuses to
boot for any non-development environment missing `API_KEY`, `SECRET_KEY`, or
`CORS_ORIGINS` — fail loud at startup, not per-request. CI now sets
`API_KEY`/`CORS_ORIGINS` (previously only `SECRET_KEY`) since `ENVIRONMENT=ci`
is not `development` either.

> **⚠️ Deploy note:** before this is deployed, the `qwantej-api` Railway
> service's Variables tab must have `CORS_ORIGINS` set (and `API_KEY`/
> `SECRET_KEY` confirmed already set) or the service will fail to boot.
> `/health` has no auth dependency, so the healthcheck itself is unaffected,
> but the process won't come up at all without these.

### 2. Forecast archive invariant broken (DEVELOPMENT.md §4)

`scripts/run_signal_pipeline.py` computed a full forecast (features, model
probabilities, calibration) and then returned before `publish_prediction()`
whenever the value gate rejected it in production mode — silently
discarding a computed forecast instead of archiving it, contradicting
DEVELOPMENT.md §4's "every prediction is archived" rule. A
`PredictionPublicationError` was also caught and downgraded to a warning,
swallowing an archival failure instead of failing the run.

**Fix:** every computed, lineage-verified forecast is now archived
regardless of gate outcome. Added `predictions.gate_passed` (migration
`b8d0f2a4c6e8`): `True` for a live, stakeable signal; `False` for a
value-gate rejection archived for audit/calibration evidence only. The
accumulator phase filters on `gate_passed` instead of relying on
gate-rejected rows never existing. `publish_prediction()` failures now
propagate (the run's transaction rolls back and the fixture is retried next
run) instead of being logged and swallowed.

## Tests

- New: environment fail-closed matrix (development/staging/production/ci/
  typo/empty, both configured and unconfigured) — `tests/test_security.py`
- New: gate-rejected forecast is archived with `gate_passed=False` and
  `reason_codes=["MARKET_STALE"]`, never executable — `tests/test_signal_pipeline.py`
- New: accumulator phase excludes `gate_passed=False` rows from qualified
  selections — `tests/test_signal_pipeline.py`
- Updated the pre-existing "empty API_KEY in production" test to assert
  `create_app()` itself raises, since misconfiguration now fails at
  startup rather than producing a per-request 500.

## Verification

- `pytest -q` (SQLite, no local Postgres this session): **1101 passed**, 68
  Postgres-only integration tests skipped
- `ruff check backend src tests`: clean
- `mypy backend src`: clean, 138 files
- `alembic heads`: single head (`b8d0f2a4c6e8`)
- Migration **not yet run against a real Postgres instance** (no local
  Postgres available this session) — will apply cleanly via the normal
  DEVELOPMENT.md §6 flow (`railway run --service qwantej-api -- alembic
  upgrade head`) after merge; it follows the identical
  add-boolean-column-with-server-default pattern as the already-proven
  `c6d8e0f2a4b1_add_prediction_research_mode` migration.

## Out of scope (tracked separately)

- Dependency pinning across `pyproject.toml`/`requirements.txt`
- `/health/ready`'s Telegram-config exposure to unauthenticated callers
- Stale `.claude/worktrees/affectionate-cori-d8c6dc` worktree (6 commits
  ahead of its own remote branch, pre-dates the Render→Railway migration)
- Root `.env.example` missing `NEXT_PUBLIC_CURRENCY_SYMBOL`
- Stale "Neon production database" wording in migration
  `0cded7a40ae5`'s docstring

author: suraciii
body:
Implements #1054 (revised design: agents read their bound Slack thread on demand).

## What changes

- **On-demand instead of automatic**: a first channel-thread mention launches the Agent with its task and stable conversation references; it no longer pre-fetches thread history, and a history read can no longer reject an otherwise valid task. The obsolete no-op thread reader, its startup-context budget options, and the channel ingress import path are removed; the generic `AgentStartupContext` machinery is untouched for other entry points.
- **Narrow read port**: `ISlackThreadQueryPort` plus one `conversations.replies` adapter over the existing `SlackApiTransport` (normalized facts only, wire payloads stay in infrastructure; the boundary-port inventory tests enumerate the new port/adapter). Pagination contradictions fail closed; file/attachment/rich-text content that was not retrieved is marked unread; the thread root is marked. HTTP 429 and in-envelope `ratelimited` classify as `RateLimited` with `Retry-After`, surfaced as 429 + `retryAfterSeconds` — never slept through or auto-retried; the four pre-existing adapters treat the new outcome exactly as before.
- **Binding resolution**: the selected Session's recorded Slack provenance and the durable thread mapping resolve the Connection, workspace, channel, and root. Foreign project, no association, conflicting associations, DM, Manager conversation, and cross-Session mapping each fail closed with distinct codes — no substitute Connection, thread, user token, or transcript. A soft-deleted Connection reports `connection_unavailable` (no retry hint). Reads use the verified managed-App Bot credential through a Server-initiated lease-service path independent of Socket health; disabled/unverified/unprovisioned credentials fail closed; the token is never logged or persisted.
- **Continuation**: stateless HMAC-SHA256 token scoped to purpose/project/session/connection/workspace/channel/root/cursor, keyed by the Connection's Bot credential; malformed, tampered, and differently-scoped tokens are indistinguishable refusals verified before any provider call. Credential rotation invalidates outstanding tokens by design.
- **CLI**: `mo slack thread view --project … --session … [--limit 1-100] [--continuation …] [--json thread,messages,continuation]` with local validation before any request and server error codes surfaced through the existing envelope.
- **Skill**: the collaboration skill (published as 1.0.6 with coordinated Server catalog + Runner hash pins) teaches reading the bound thread when earlier discussion is needed, passing non-null continuations back, treating a failed read as missing context rather than an empty thread, and not presenting an early page with unread continuation as the final agreement.
- **Docs**: `docs/slack.md`, `design/slack.md`, `docs/cli-reference.md` updated first (separate docs commit), including the group-DM boundary (an mpim mention takes the channel-thread path; Slack itself refuses reads beyond the installed Bot's granted scopes).

Reading creates no AgentJob, SessionInput, or AgentTurn, sends nothing, and adds no Slack persistence.

## Evidence

- Server: full suite 7401 passed (base 7351) before review fixes; Slack+Contracts namespaces 762 passed after; L0 binding-resolver/continuation/read-service specs (real SQLite stores), L1 route specs through a scripted Slack API (wire fields, continuation forwarding, 400/404/409/429/502 mapping, transport-failure and stale-cursor cases, no-side-effect assertions), boundary-port inventory, skill digest contract drift test.
- Runner: full suite 2128 passed incl. hash-pinned slack-execution-context and followup-handler contract tests.
- CLI: `npm run test:cli` green incl. new `issue_1054_thread_view_test.go` request-shape/field/validation/help cases.
- Full local gate `npm run verify` on the branch (post-review-fix HEAD): all tracks green; docs/format/filesizes checks clean.
- Reviews: two independent fresh-context reviewers (correctness; tests/boundary) both returned OK with notes; all five P2 findings were applied in follow-up commits with focused re-validation.

Live Slack workspace behavior (installed Bot scope/rate-limit posture) remains untested locally by design; the provider contract is exercised through the scripted transport, and the issue records the authorized-workspace check as separate evidence.

author: bonroi2296-tech
body:
## 왜
감독 판 **C-4**. 문의 #0420c300: 판정기(judge)가 3턴 모두 1.0 을 줬는데 봇은 「코디에게 알렸다」를 두 번 내보내고, 연락처가 없는데 「접수됐어요」라고 말했다. 점수(사실·안전·관련성)는 **절차**를 안 본다. 밤 검사도 «답을 하는가»만 봐서 이 부류는 영영 안 잡혔다. PO — *「이슈 터지기 전에 미리 테스트 못 하니」*. 근거 = `docs/rules/AI_QUALITY.md` 「절차 결함도 «분포»에 넣어라」.

## 무엇을
**`scripts/check-chat-process.ts` 신설** → 밤 검사 `chat-smoke.yml` 에 `if: always()` 단계로 (앞 스모크가 빨간불이어도 따로 돈다 — 가려지면 만든 이유가 없어진다).

| # | 검사 | 통과 조건 |
|---|---|---|
| ① | 6개 언어(ko·en·ru·kz·zh·ja)로 「코디 연결」을 **연락처 없이** 누른다 | 절차 표식 0 |
| ② | 지난 24시간 판정 기록의 절차 표식 수 | 하루 상한 3 이하 |
| ③ | 지난 7일 «진짜» 대화 수(점검 대화 제외) | 하한 2 이상 |

- **판정은 `contactGate.detectProcessFlags` 를 그대로 부른다.** 정규식을 베끼면 저쪽이 바뀔 때 이 검사만 조용히 안 맞게 된다(드리프트 = 거짓 초록불). 그래서 `.mjs` 가 아니라 `.ts` + `tsx`.
- ⚠️ **영역 준수**: `src/lib/chat/**` 는 **읽기만** 했다 — 그 폴더의 고친 파일 **0개**.
- **`--self-test`**: 망·DB 없이 견본 4개(나쁜 2·정상 2)로 판정 배선을 잰다. `ci.yml` 이 매 신청서마다 부른다 → `check:guard-coverage` 가 이 검사를 「진짜 잡는지 확인됨」으로 센다(33개 전부 확인).
- **표식 하루 상한은 이 파일에 둔다.** `qualityStandards.ALERT_ALWAYS_FLAGS` 에 섞으면 점수 경보가 오염된다 — 감독이 짚은 함정 그대로.
- 알림 메일 본문에 절차 검사 요약도 포함(한쪽만 담으면 다른 쪽 실패가 메일에서 사라진다).

## 🛑 ①을 «DB 의 표식»으로 재지 않은 이유 (둘 다 실측)
- 점검 대화는 **설계상 판정기가 건너뛴다**(`isSyntheticThread`) → 표식이 애초에 안 남는다.
- 표식 검출 자체가 **실서비스에 아직 안 나갔다**(실서비스 커밋 `84e3a01b`, #1846 은 그 뒤).

즉 DB 를 보면 「위반 0건」이 나오는데 그건 통과가 아니라 **아무것도 안 본 것**이다. 그래서 실서비스 답변 글자를 받아 이 저장소의 검출기로 직접 판정한다.

## 실측
- **배선 견본 4개 통과**: 안내 되풀이 → `handoff_template_echo` · 거짓 접수 → `false_intake_confirm` · 정상 답변 → `[]` · 연락처 있을 때 접수 확정 → `[]`(인자 순서가 틀리면 여기서 깨진다).
- **오늘 기댓값**(SQL 로 미리 재둠): ② 24시간 표식 **0건**(상한 3) · ③ 진짜 **33건**(전체 69 − 점검 36).
- **③ 하한 2 의 근거** — 주별 진짜 대화: 8/24주 50 · 8/31주 25 · **9/07주 1** · 9/14주 31. 9/07 주가 정확히 PO 가 말한 「7일간 1건」이고 **아무도 세고 있지 않았다.** 하한 2 는 그 주만 울리고 나머지는 조용하다.
- **② 상한 3 은 보정 안 된 임시값**이라고 파일에 적었다: 30일 표본 0건은 깨끗해서가 아니라 검출기가 실서비스에 안 나가서다. 나간 뒤 일주일 보고 다시 정할 것.
- 열쇠가 없으면 「0건 통과」가 아니라 **«못 쟀다»로 빨간불** — 실행으로 확인.
- `check:workflow-pipefail --selftest` · `check:workflow-env` · `check:guard-coverage` · `check:rules` · `check:content` · `tsc` · `eslint` 통과.

## 안 한 것 (정직하게)
#0420c300 의 세 번째 결함 **「6개 언어 버튼 잘림」은 화면 문제**라 창구를 부르는 밤 검사로는 볼 수 없다. 흉내내면 「검사가 있는데 아무것도 안 잡는」 상태가 되므로 **만들지 않고**, 브라우저 검사(e2e) 자리라고 스크립트와 규칙 문서에 적었다.

## 저위험 근거

author: gougoujiang
body:
## What

Adds `docs/proposals/remote-control.md` (+ zh-CN mirror) researching and proposing **Remote Control** for BuildMax: drive a local CLI/TUI or Desktop agent session from another device, with execution and the filesystem staying on the user's machine and the server acting only as an outbound-brokered relay. Status: proposal — under discussion.

## Key points

- **Decomposition (§5):** Remote Control and the [client-surface-convergence](https://github.com/icloudbb/buildmax/blob/main/docs/proposals/client-surface-convergence.md) Environment plane are not competing products but two points on a host-by-surface grid, resting on two orthogonal substrates — a **control plane** (live-session registry, event relay, inbound command delivery, presence) and a **cloud-environment substrate**. The control plane is *required* for a local host (the server can't reach the laptop) and only *unifying* for a cloud host.
- **Recommendation (§13, option C):** build the control plane first as local Remote Control, then the environment substrate to reach the cloud quadrants — an ordering, not a doubling of effort.
- **Feasibility is high:** reuses the run-bridge outbound-proxy pattern, the WebSocket and streaming hubs, the per-device `AuthSession` model, and a mid-run `PendingInput` seam the local runtime already wires.
- Includes a Mermaid architecture diagram of the control plane (§9), a phased plan (§12), security posture (§11), and open questions (§14).

## Notes

- Docs-only; no shipped behavior, so no changelog fragment.
- `TestDocsLinksResolve`, `TestDocumentedFilePathsExist`, and `make check docs` (markdownlint) pass. zh-CN mirror kept in sync per the documentation convention.

author: mroczect
body:
### Summary
This PR introduces a complete stock movement audit trail, rewrites the frontend as a minimal vanilla JS SPA, and restructures the database CLI into a namespaced package. It also hardens backend security around JWT revocation, rate limiting, and transaction validation.

### Motivation & Context
The previous system lacked an audit trail for stock changes, making it difficult to trace inventory discrepancies. The frontend had grown complex with React and Tailwind, and the database scripts were flat and hard to maintain. This change addresses these issues by adding a dedicated stock movement model, simplifying the frontend for faster iteration, and reorganizing the database layer for clarity.

### Detailed Changes
- **.gitignore**: Remove stray blank line and ignore Rust `target` directory.
- **backend/README.md**: Comprehensive rewrite to document new stock endpoints, database CLI, and security notes.
- **backend/app/Controllers/Api/V1/AuthController.php**: Blacklist refresh token on rotation; whitespace cleanup.
- **backend/app/Controllers/Api/V1/ScheduleController.php**: Validate `scheduled_at` format and future date; require active customer and user.
- **backend/app/Controllers/Api/V1/StockController.php**: New controller for listing stock movements and adjusting stock.
- **backend/app/Controllers/Api/V1/TransactionController.php**: Add `paid_amount` validation on create and update; cap at `total_amount`.
- **backend/app/Core/App.php**: Singleton boot; send `Vary: Origin`; add `X-XSS-Protection`.
- **backend/app/Core/Auth.php**: Check JWT blacklist by `jti` instead of raw token.
- **backend/app/Core/Database.php**: Support nested transactions via savepoints.
- **backend/app/Core/Middleware.php**: Deleted unused abstract class.
- **backend/app/Core/Model.php**: Validate `orderBy` clause.
- **backend/app/Core/Response.php**: Handle JSON encoding failures; omit `errors` when null.
- **backend/app/Core/Router.php**: Throw on missing middleware.
- **backend/app/Core/Validator.php**: Cast numeric bounds to float.
- **backend/app/Exceptions/ErrorHandler.php**: Return early on handled exceptions; log PDO errors with driver details.
- **backend/app/Middleware/RateLimitMiddleware.php**: Per-IP bucket; fix file handle leak.
- **backend/app/Models/StockMovement.php**: New model for stock movements.
- **backend/app/Services/AuthService.php**: Use `customer` role; throw if missing.
- **backend/app/Services/StockService.php**: Refactor to support atomic adjustments with movement logging.
- **backend/app/Services/TransactionService.php**: Log stock movements on sale; validate items; derive status from paid amount.
- **backend/app/Support/AppLogger.php**: Honor trusted proxies for client IP.
- **backend/app/Support/Jwt.php**: Add `blacklistByJti` and `isBlacklistedByJti`; fail closed.
- **backend/app/Support/helpers.php**: Add `env()` helper.
- **backend/composer.json/lock**: Add `carthage-software/mago` dev dependency.
- **backend/routes/api.php**: Add stock movement routes; switch admin role to `administrator`.
- **backend/tests/***: Update role names; add per-IP rate limit test; use future schedule times; database test improvements.
- **database/***: Move to root, add bootstrap, namespaced CLI classes (`Database\Cli`, `Database\Migrator`, etc.), migrate all migrations and seeders to new namespace, add `stock_movements` migration, add README.
- **frontend/***: Complete rewrite from React to vanilla JS SPA with hash routing; remove React, Tailwind, and related dependencies; add API client, UI helpers, and page modules.
- **frontend/bun.lock**: Update lockfile for new dependencies.
- **frontend/package.json**: Remove React dependencies; add Vite and Bun types.

### Impact & Breaking Changes
- Role names changed: `admin` → `administrator`, `kurir` → `agent`, `pelanggan` → `customer`. All API consumers must update role checks.
- Database CLI path changed to `php database/db.php`; composer scripts updated.
- Frontend is completely rewritten; any custom React components are removed.
- Stock updates via `PUT /products/{id}` no longer write audit records; use `POST /stock-movements/adjust` for auditable changes.
- `JWT_SECRET` must be at least 32 bytes; boot fails otherwise.

### Testing Recommendations
1. Run `php database/db.php fresh --seed` to verify migrations and seeders.
2. Test stock adjustment endpoint: `POST /api/v1/stock-movements/adjust` with `product_id`, `new_stock`, `reason`.
3. Verify transaction creation deducts stock and creates `stock_movements` rows.
4. Test per-IP rate limiting: exceed login attempts from one IP and confirm another IP is not blocked.
5. Run frontend: `cd frontend && bun install && bun run dev`, then log in and exercise CRUD pages.
6. Run backend tests: `composer test`.

author: dkehne
body:
Behebt #474

## Problem

Der Block „Lizenzen" der Genehmigungskarte (Verwaltung → Lizenzwesen → Verband → Liga, offener Antrag) zeigte drei Zeichen: Haken für erteilt, Kreuz für abgelehnt, Fragezeichen für **alles andere**. Beantragt, zurückgezogen, gelöscht, ignoriert, gesperrt und Transfer sahen damit identisch aus — eine noch offene Lizenz wie eine gelöschte.

## Lösung

Ein Zeichen je Status aus `License::NAMES`, alle im selben Kreis, damit die Spalte ruhig bleibt:

| Status | Zeichen | Farbe |
| --- | --- | --- |
| erteilt | Haken | grün |
| beantragt | Uhr | gelb |
| abgelehnt | Kreuz | rot |
| ungültig: gelöscht | Minus | grau |
| ungültig wegen Transfer | Pfeil nach rechts | blau |
| ungültig: ignoriert | Pause | grau |
| zurückgezogen | Pfeil nach links | grau |
| gesperrt | Schrägstrich | rot |
| unbekannt | Fragezeichen | grau |

Die Farbe sagt weiter, ob der Spieler spielen darf; innerhalb einer Farbe unterscheidet die Form. Der Klartext hängt als `<title>` am Symbol und ist damit Tooltip und Vorlesetext in einem (ein `[title]`-Attribut nimmt ein `<svg>` nicht an, NG0303).

Zuordnung, Farbe und Schlüssel stehen als eine Tabelle in der Komponente statt als Zweige in der Vorlage.

## Nebenbei behoben

- Der bisherige `@switch` verglich streng. Die Status-ID liegt in der JSONB-History nicht typgarantiert vor (`League#build_license_items` schreibt an zwei Stellen `to_i`), eine erteilte Lizenz mit `'1'` als Zeichenkette zeigte deshalb das Fragezeichen.
- Der `viewBox` stand auf 22, die Pfade sind im 24er-Raster gezeichnet — der Kreis war rechts unten angeschnitten.

## Prüfung

`ng lint` sauber, `ng build` erfolgreich, volle Suite grün (1679 Specs). Vier neue Specs in der Datei; die Prüfung „zeichnet jeden bekannten Status anders" fällt nachweislich um, wenn sich zwei Status wieder ein Zeichen teilen. Der Satz wurde zusätzlich als Bild gerendert und angesehen.

Nur Frontend, keine API-Änderung.

author: michalmoronga-alt
body:
## Čo sa mení (z pohľadu používateľa)

`scripts\run_su_tests.ps1` dostal voliteľný prepínač **`-CloseWhenDone`** (predvolene VYPNUTÝ — bez neho sa správanie runnera nemení, idle okno SketchUpu ostáva otvorené ako doteraz).

**Prečo:** pri autonómnych dávkach beží runner 5–10× za deň a každá idle testovacia inštancia drží ~1,5 GB. 20.9.2026 ostalo otvorených 12 inštancií, voľných bolo 5 GB z 32 a nový beh uviazol (Welcome obrazovka bez `su_result.txt`).

**Ako to funguje s prepínačom:**
- Zatváranie beží **vnútri SketchUpu** (modul `NoxunSuClose` v generovanom `boot.rb`, timer každé 2 s), nie zo skriptu — skript proces **nikdy nezabíja**.
- **Brána = koncový marker** `=== KONIEC SUBORU ===` v `su_result.txt`. Bez markera sa inštancia nikdy nezatvorí (visiaci beh ostáva na diagnostiku).
- Po markeri (+3 s na debounce observerov) sa inštancia zbaví príznaku zmien **uložením run-kópie modelu** (kópia žije len v `run_*`, pôvodný `_dev` model sa nedotkne; uložený stav ostáva na diagnostiku). Záloha pri zlyhaní uloženia: `Model#close(true)` — na Windows podľa API dokumentácie File/New, `ignore_changes` potlačí otázku „uložiť zmeny?". Potom v ďalšom ticku `Sketchup.quit` (pýta sa len pri neuložených zmenách; `send_action` je deprecated, nepoužíva sa).
- Poistka: keby bol dokument pred quit stále „špinavý", uloží sa malý stub do run priečinka (nikdy pôvodný model), aby quit nečakal na klik.
- Runner po markeri počká na zánik procesu (max 120 s), vypíše `close.log` a exit kód inštancie (aj hex); ak inštancia neskončí, LEN to nahlási.
- Sentinel `last_run.txt` aj `deploy.lock` logika bez zmeny (zámok sa drží aj počas čakania na zánik procesu).

**Navyše (platí aj bez prepínača):** `load` runnera v `boot.rb` je v `begin/rescue ScriptError, StandardError` — SyntaxError/LoadError nie sú StandardError, rescue v `su_runner.rb` by ich nechytil a beh by skončil 8-min timeoutom bez markera. Teraz dá FAIL riadok + marker (rýchly, čitateľný výsledok). Šablóna `boot.rb` je v single-quoted here-stringoch s placeholdermi (PowerShell v nich neinterpoluje — Ruby `#{}` ani `$` nič nerozbije).

**Docs:** poznámka v `CLAUDE.md` (Testovanie) — pri autonómnych behoch prepínač používať; komentár v hlavičke runnera (prečo prepínač existuje + známy stav); záznam v `SYSTEM/archiv/KRONIKA.md`. Bez bumpu verzie (plugin sa nemení — precedens PR #269).

## Známy stav — pád v teardown SketchUpu (priznané, neizolované)

Po CELEJ testovacej sade (2813 scenárov) končí teardown SketchUpu 2026 pri `Sketchup.quit` kódom **0xC0000374** (heap corruption v ntdll) — **až PO zapísaní výsledku a uložení kópie**. Proces zmizne do pár sekúnd, neostane žiadny helper proces, dialog ani recovery súbor; Windows to len ticho zaloguje do WER; ďalšie behy štartujú normálne. Verdikt testov to nemení (je hotový pred zatváraním) a runner exit kód vypíše s vysvetlením.

Vylúčené sondami a plnými behmi: File/New vs. save (beh 1 vs. 2 — rovnaký pád), otvorený Inspector/Štúdio (sonda: exit 0), overlay add+remove 5× (sonda: exit 0), nástroje, upratanie pluginu pred quit (beh 3: zavreté okná + `EdgeCheck/DirectionCheck.disable!` + `select_tool(nil)` + GC — rovnaký pád, preto v šablóne nie je). Príčina je v stave po celej relácii; ďalšia bisekcia = desiatky 4-minútových behov, vedome odložená.

## Ako testované

- **Sonda 1** (samostatná inštancia SU 2026, plugin načítaný): mutácia modelu → `close(true)` → nový dokument `modified? == false` → `Sketchup.quit` → exit 0 do 3 s.
- **Sonda 2** nad REÁLNOU šablónou z runnera (blok vyrezaný a vykonaný harnessom): parse runnera 0 chýb, `ruby -c` boot.rb OK, marker zachytený, nový dokument ÚMYSELNE zašpinený → stub uložený → exit 0.
- **Sonda 4** (save cesta nad reálnou šablónou): `save run-kopie -> true`, bez stubu, exit 0.
- **Štyri plné behy `scripts\run_su_tests.ps1 -CloseWhenDone`** (beh 1 File/New, beh 2 save, beh 3 save + upratanie pluginu, beh 4 = finálna šablóna): vždy 2813 PASS / 0 FAIL / 0 SKIP, marker → proces SketchUpu zanikol do 8 s, vlastná inštancia nikdy neostala (behy 3 a 4 bežali súbežne s behmi inej session cez `deploy.lock` — 3× odmietnutie `exit 2` a prevzatie zámku fungovali).
- Headless `ruby tests/run_all.rb`: 4232 PASS / 0 FAIL (vrátane docs a encoding guardov).

**Môžeš mergovať** po CI + Codex kole (merge robí Claude podľa workflow).

author: eaxea
body:
## Sorun

Bugünkü vakanın en ağır tarafı buydu: para çekildi, alıcı sonuç sayfasında şunu gördü:

> Ödeme tamamlanmadı. Sepetiniz korunuyor, tekrar deneyebilirsiniz.

Yani sistem, parası alınmış bir müşteriyi **ikinci kez ödemeye davet etti**. Çifte tahsilat, güven kaybı ve mevzuat sorunu.

Sebep: sayfa yalnızca iki durum biliyordu, `paid` ve değil. Oysa üçüncü bir durum var ve bugün tam da o yaşandı: ödeme **başarısız değil, sonucu bilinmiyor**.

## Değişiklik

**1. Sayfa artık önce iyzico'ya soruyor.** Sipariş `pending` ise `conversationId` ile ödeme durumu çekilir; doğrulanırsa alıcı doğrudan "Siparişiniz alındı" görür ve mail gider. Bu sorgu token gerektirmediği için callback anı geçtikten sonra da çalışır.

**2. Sorgu da sonuç vermezse üçüncü ekran:**

> **Ödemeniz kontrol ediliyor.**
> Ödeme sonucunu şu an ödeme sağlayıcımızdan doğrulayamadık. **Lütfen ödemeyi tekrar yapmayın.** Kartınızdan çekim yapıldıysa siparişiniz geçerlidir. Durum netleştiğinde size e posta ile haber veriyoruz.
> Sipariş numaranız MA-… Bize ulaşmak isterseniz info@maiamari.art

Ayrıca "Durumu yeniden sorgula" düğmesi var ve **"Sepete dön" bağlantısı bu durumda gizleniyor**: alıcı tekrar ödemeye yönlendirilmemeli.

"Ödeme tamamlanmadı, tekrar deneyebilirsiniz" metni artık yalnız gerçekten başarısız (`failed` / `cancelled`) siparişlerde çıkıyor.

## Tasarım notları

- Uzlaştırma mantığı panelle **ortak** (`reconcilePendingOrder`). İki ayrı mantık kalırsa biri düzelirken diğeri eskir.
- Tekrar deneme bütçesi çağırana bırakıldı: panelde geniş (kimse beklemiyor), alıcının sayfasında tek tekrar, yoksa sayfa saniyelerce asılı kalır.

## Doğrulama

Gerçek bir bekleyen siparişle yerelde çalıştırıldı: iyzico "ödeme kaydı bulunamadı" dedi ve **sipariş değişmedi**. 123/123 test, lint + build temiz.

author: sven-ericmolzahn
body:
Follow-up to #3, which did this for the README. `SKILL.md` is the file agents actually read, so the same sentence was shaping their answers.

It claimed *"even Apple's prose says `.divisions` where the SDK says `.division`"*. [Preparing your app for iPhone Duo](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/technologyoverviews/preparing-your-app-for-iphone-duo) pluralises in ordinary English ("identify divisions and occlusions") and uses the singular where it defines the term ("A division occurs when a folding region divides a large view"). It never writes `.divisions` as an API name.

Beyond being inaccurate, it was the wrong shape for an instruction file. "Secondary sources get them wrong" teaches an agent to distrust sources; what it should learn is to check against the SDK, which is what the next line already tells it to do. The rewrite puts the reason in the situation instead:

> These APIs were days old when this was written, so there is little to check a spelling against except the SDK itself. The traps survive a plausibility check: the reserved-region kinds are singular (`.division`, `.occlusion`) where prose pluralises them naturally, and a name that compiles can still be the wrong one.

Also names Tech Talk 111465 where the missing camera API was previously "a Tech Talk", so a reader can check it.

`tests/validate-skill.py` passes; the body is 2835 words.

author: norbertbodziony
body:
## What

The account dock fetched each provider's remaining percentage once per target and then held it, so the figure in the Usage popover counted down in the provider's window but never on screen. It now refreshes itself.

- A poll ticks every 30 s while the reading is visible — the hybrid chip, the account menu, or the usage popover — and refetches when the last reading is 5 minutes old. The short tick with an age check stops a manual **Refresh** from pushing the next automatic one out to nearly 10 minutes.
- The poll stays quiet when there is no usage target, when providers are not ready, and when nothing shows the figure, so the lazy load in the Windows/compact account menu is unchanged.
- A hidden window does not poll; `visibilitychange` refreshes at once when the window comes back and the interval has passed.
- `lastUsageRefreshAt` is set in `refreshUsage`, so manual, target-change and automatic refreshes share one clock. The existing request-generation guard and in-flight check still prevent overlapping calls.

Desktop renderer only (`src/renderer/src/features/account/AccountDock.tsx`). No IPC, schema, migration or contract change: it calls the existing `agent.getUsage`. No outbound data change, so `PRIVACY.md` is unaffected.
