author: shaishibear
body:
Item 3 of the [checkpoint review](https://github.com/ShaishiBear/dark-factory-2.0/blob/main/docs/checkpoint-review-275/REVIEW_AND_CONTINUATION.md)'s work order, which was explicit that this is source work rather than a future host fix: *"The current `bind()` actively applies 0700/0600, so merely documenting a future deployment arrangement leaves source work unresolved."*

## The arrangement

`SocketAccess` carries the client group **by name, never a numeric gid**. A gid is a fact about one host, so a number in a repository is right once and wrong afterwards. The name resolves against the host's own group database at bind time, and an unknown name **refuses rather than falling back** — falling back would leave a broker running that its clients cannot reach, with the misconfiguration hidden behind a working-looking process.

| | directory | socket |
|---|---|---|
| no group configured (default) | 0700 | 0600 |
| client group configured | 0750 | 0660 |

The default fails closed, which is what a misconfigured install should get.

**The order in `bind()` is the property.** The inode is created under a umask that makes it owner-only, so it never exists wider than its final mode even for the instant between `bind` and `chmod`; the group is assigned; the mode is set; and only then does it listen. A socket that listened first would serve connections during the window its permissions were not yet the intended ones.

**Private state is a different directory and nothing here touches it.** The review's warning is exact: widening the state permissions, or running every role under one uid, would pass an isolation test by removing the property it tests.

## What same-uid tests cannot do, and what does it instead

Every socket test in this repository runs its client and its server under one uid, because a test cannot create a user. They establish that `SO_PEERCRED` reports the connecting process and that the modes are what the code set. They establish **nothing** about whether `df-web` can open a socket owned by `df-broker`.

`harness/socket_qualification.py` runs as root in a disposable runner, creates four users and a group, starts the broker under one and drives the others at it. Six checks, each named for what it establishes and why the others do not imply it:

1. A mapped client in the group **connects and is served**. The arrangement is the one the deployment needs, not merely a private one.
2. Its **role comes from its uid**: the web identity connects and is refused a coordinator command.
3. A uid deliberately placed **in the group but not in the role map is refused anyway**. This is the one that separates the two mechanisms: filesystem access is not command authorization.
4. A uid **outside the group cannot open the socket at all**, so the group is load-bearing rather than decorative.
5. No client can **read the broker's database or list its state directory**.
6. No client can **replace the socket path**, which would be a client that could impersonate the broker.

## Status, stated exactly

- **Source implemented:** yes.
- **Supported-platform qualification: NOT YET RUN.** GitHub only dispatches a `workflow_dispatch` workflow that exists on the default branch, so this one cannot execute until it merges. The qualification is dispatched against `main` immediately afterwards and its result recorded. **Until that result exists, process isolation remains unqualified and is not claimed.**
- **Installed observation:** none. The systemd unit records the arrangement and says plainly that nothing in this repository installs it; installing needs host access this factory does not have.

## Evidence

- 87 passed, 7 skipped. The `SocketAccess` tests and the two `bind()` ordering tests run on every platform.
- **4 new mutants, all kill-checked, all caught.** Three survived their first kill-check because their only detectors were the Linux socket tests that skip where the mutation family runs — the same trap, for the fourth time in this work. The unknown-group refusal now fakes the group database instead of skipping, and `bind()`'s call order is recorded through a fake socket, so the umask and the listen-after-chmod orderings are pinned everywhere.
- `MUTATION_ANCHORS_OK factory=1038 application=9 detectors=102`; trust-root lint clean.

author: nativa-studio
body:
Marcia spotted it: Ava opened her invite at 8:05 and was sent it at 8:06. Not possible, and not one row. **14 of the 16** guests on Gabriel's party who had both stamps were opened before they were sent, 8 of them inside two minutes.

`get_invite` stamped `opened_at` on every call, and the page's `generateMetadata` calls it. `generateMetadata` is exactly what a chat app runs when it fetches a link to draw a preview card, so the moment Share was tapped and WhatsApp picked, WhatsApp fetched the link and the guest was marked as having opened their invitation seconds before it reached them.

So reading an invite stops being the same thing as recording that it was read. `get_invite` returns the invite and nothing else. Marking is its own call, made by the page and not by `generateMetadata`, and only when the request looks like a person: the same test the calendar tap already uses, now in `lib/guest/is-a-person.ts` so both read one copy.

Proved against a fresh guest, four fetches, one stamp:

| fetch | opened_at |
| --- | --- |
| start | null |
| WhatsApp fetches it | null |
| Facebook fetches it | null |
| a browser prefetches it | null |
| **a real iPhone opens it** | **stamped** |

**The old stamps are left alone rather than cleared.** Some of them are real: a guest sent their link by hand and marked as sent the next morning genuinely did open it first, and blanket deleting every `opened_at` older than its `sent_at` would throw those away with the wrong ones. Marcia's call, not mine.

body:
Constrained Agent 7 one-increment expression-capacity preflight, preregistered in issue #817 before execution and stacked directly on exact PR #810 head `b077eaffabfe66ce0b15ac29601a82bfddeb4cf9`.

## Fresh audit / non-duplication
Reread the latest constrained README, AGENTS, PROJECT_GOAL, CURRENT_CHECKPOINT and AGENT_TASKS; refreshed open PRs, recent constrained commits and exact-head CI. #810 remains queued and owns the recalibrated scalar-amplitude vs radial-shape tangent audit. No newer Agent-7 PR studies a second temporal coefficient. This PR does not touch Kokuno Agents 1–5, Agent-9 delivery/export, pressure/forcing, PDE residuals, or #714 fresh paths.

## Why this is the next minimal basis-growth question
The frozen #775 outer-reservoir child uses one time law only:

`g1(t)=2*(t-0.25)`.

If later fixed visual/source-observable evidence says the *time evolution* rather than the instantaneous spatial shape is wrong, adding a second spatial/poloidal basis would be premature. This preflight therefore asks whether one endpoint-preserving temporal curvature coordinate provides an independent response direction while keeping the spatial reservoir channel unchanged.

Freeze

`g2(t)=16*(t-0.25)*(0.75-t)`

on `[0.25,0.75]`, so `g2(.25)=g2(.75)=0` and `g2(.50)=1`. This is an autonomous repository basis, not an OpenAI-published time law.

## Frozen 3-column identifiability gate
Reuse #810's exact recalibrated family `k={.90,1.00,1.10}` and exact #775 live-alpha semantics. On the same deterministic response cloud and times `.375/.50/.625/.75`, compare normalized columns:

1. live scalar-amplitude tangent `alpha_1*g1*C_1`;
2. recalibrated radial-shape tangent `(u_1.10-u_.90)/.20`;
3. endpoint-preserving temporal-curvature tangent `alpha_1*g2*C_1`.

Preregistered gate from issue #817: rank 3, normalized 3-column condition `<=25`, and every pairwise normalized cosine absolute value `<.995`.

## Visualization-fingerprint diagnostics
Without fitting or selecting a coefficient, record the unit temporal-curvature tangent on the existing visible-tip / axial-stretch semantics: mean cylindrical radial response at `|z|=1.55/1.75`, mean away-from-midplane axial response in the frozen core/annulus bands, and exact zero response at `t=.25/.75`. These are autonomous morphology diagnostics only; no sign/magnitude is called OpenAI correspondence.

## Minimal increment
Exactly 3 commits / 3 added files / 0 behind relative to #810:

- `experiments/root_st052/agent7_st052m_endpoint_temporal_curvature_preflight.py`
- `experiments/root_st052/test_agent7_st052m_endpoint_temporal_curvature_preflight.py`
- `.github/workflows/agent7-st052m-endpoint-temporal-curvature-preflight.yml`

No candidate velocity, basis coefficient, canonical API, serialization, pressure, forcing, held-out residual, public-image target, or scientific threshold changes.

## Routing consequence
A future exact-head PASS would establish only that an endpoint-preserving temporal coefficient is a locally independent, reasonably conditioned morphology lever in addition to scalar amplitude and radial shape. It would justify at most one later frozen temporal-child experiment *if* a preregistered time-evolution mismatch exists. It does not justify a second spatial basis, and it does not directly make `velocity(x,y,z,t)` closer in this increment.

Hard false remains `visualization_ready`, `visual_correspondence_verified`, `source_correspondence_verified`, `pde_validated`, `paper_exact`, `openai_field_identified`, and blow-up proof. Exact-head Actions results are intentionally not pre-claimed; queued/not-yet-run is not passed.

Closes #817.

author: mihailinl
body:
`bot/baseline.mjs`'s `verifyOne` had a **bare `catch`**. `gh attestation verify`
exits 1 whether the attestation is absent, wrong, or **never checked at all** —
no network, Sigstore's trust root unreachable, a timeout — and all three became
`{outcome: "unverified", repository_id: null}`.

That value goes into MIG-20's `migration` record. It is written **once**,
`--write` refuses a second run, and A1, MIG-28 and TRUST-23 all read it. A
five-minute Sigstore outage during the one dispatch would have recorded the
whole catalogue as permanently unattested.

**And nothing would have stopped it.** `--verify`'s only floor was
`facts.length === 0`, so `verified 0 of 41` exits 0, and `--write` never looked
at the facts file. Run today, end to end, on this tree: **41 facts, 0 verified,
exit 0.**

| repair | what it is |
|---|---|
| one owner for the three readings | `classifyVerifyFailure` exported from `bot/lib/attestation.mjs`, which already classified for `verifyAttestation` while `baseline.mjs` classified zero ways. A 404 wins over a stray "connection" in the same stderr |
| `unchecked` is its own outcome | DEC-7's vocabulary untouched; `--verify` exits non-zero naming each, `--write` refuses a facts file carrying any — **checked at the write too**, because the facts file is an artifact between two jobs and "verify exited 0" is the weaker claim |
| a wholesale failure is refused | `--expect-unverified N` takes a **count**, not a boolean: a flag meaning "yes, whatever it is" is one somebody adds to a red run without reading it. The wrong number is refused too |

Watched red with both `--write` guards removed:

```
✖ --write refuses a facts file that records anything as not checked
✖ --write refuses a wholly unverified baseline unless the operator says the number
```

Also: the file's header said three gates were absent and two landed in
`edab81a` — `f1a9d49` edited this file afterwards without noticing — and
`verifyOne`'s docstring still said it was unreachable. A docstring claiming a
function cannot run is not a thing anything executes, which is why it outlived
its truth and why finding the floor took running the tool.

Green: baseline 25, ingest 182, policy 148, detectors 28, workflows 26,
selftest 263/21, validate 22 plugins 0 errors.

author: nolane-x
body:
Improves the BYOK connection experience after the browser-CORS relay repair.

Instead of waiting until the user pastes a key and presses Connect, the modal now probes the verified relay as soon as it opens.

- health-checks the secure relay without sending the user's API key
- retries transient relay startup/network failures
- caches a successful relay health result for 30 seconds to avoid duplicating the health round-trip during Connect
- shows "Secure relay ready" before the user submits a credential
- uses an amber warning state for transient infrastructure problems instead of presenting them like a rejected API key
- keeps red/error state for actual credential/permission failures and relay-identity verification failures
- keeps BYOK memory-only behavior unchanged
- Connect still rechecks the relay if the preflight is stale or failed

This should make the modal fail earlier, more clearly, and without involving the user's key when the infrastructure itself is unavailable.

## Summary

The Javadoc build runs with doclint, which reported 224 missing-comment warnings that never failed the build, so they piled up. This change adds the missing Javadoc and corrects four descriptions that said the wrong thing. It is a backport of #25822 to `25.3`, plus a small follow-up fix.

## What changed

This change is documentation only. No code logic changes, and the public API stays the same, so nothing can break for existing users.

- Added the missing Javadoc in the modules doclint covers: `flow-dnd`, `flow-html-components`, `flow-polymer2lit`, `flow-devloop-daemon`, `flow-dev-bundle-plugin`, `vaadin-dev-server` and `vaadin-spring`.
- Classes that relied on the implicit default constructor now declare it, because a comment needs a declared constructor. Each declared constructor is `public`, exactly like the implicit one it replaces, so callers and the binary API are unaffected. Every empty body carries a comment explaining why it is empty, to satisfy the static analysis rules.
- Fixed four descriptions that were wrong:
  - `VITE_HANDLER` is the key in the user properties of the endpoint configuration, not a registration name.
  - The AOT `Marker` bean guards only the one-time `@Route` bean registration, not the whole processor.
  - `BuildDevBundleMojo.executeInternal` no longer claims it must be public. It is called through `getDeclaredMethod` with `setAccessible(true)`, and the sibling plugin declares the same method `protected`, so the claim would block narrowing that accidentally public method later.
  - `AttachmentType.INLINE` was documented as the default. It is not: the anchor API falls back to `DOWNLOAD` when no attachment type is given. The comment now explains what the value means for the `download` attribute and points out the real fallback.
- Split some enum constants onto separate lines so each one can have its own comment. The constants themselves are unchanged.

anddudkin
body:
## Summary

Implements exact pre-correction of programmed conductances (`precorrect_g_star`) to eliminate the residual IR-drop error in `combined_full` compensation. Since the error comes entirely from a known, deterministic star-branch resistance, it can be cancelled by programming different physical conductances than the target ones, achieving zero error across all array sizes and parameter ranges.

## Key Changes

- **New module `crossbar/calibrate.py`**: Implements `precorrect_g_star(cfg)` which inverts the `closed_form_combined_full` formula to compute physical conductances that produce exact ideal VMM output. Includes feasibility checking (raises `ValueError` when a cell would require non-positive resistance) and optional precondition validation.

- **New validation script `examples/validate_precorrection.py`**: Comprehensive single-point validation that precorrection achieves floating-point-precision agreement with ideal VMM across four independent methods (closed-form formula, dense MNA, sparse MNA, ngspice simulation).

- **New landscape sweep `examples/run_precorrection_landscape.py`**: Systematic evaluation across array sizes (4×4 to 256×256) and R_line/R_cell ratios (0.0001 to 0.001), comparing `combined_full` before/after precorrection. Supports `--variants` flag to include canonical compensation levels for comparison. Handles infeasibility gracefully per grid point.

- **New periphery sweep `examples/run_precorrection_periphery_sweep.py`**: Tests precorrection stability as shared peripheral routing resistance `r_col_end` grows (0 to 100 Ω), verifying the generalized Millman-theorem formula works beyond the pure-star case.

- **Experiment 3 & 4 results**: 
  - Experiment 3: Baseline precorrection validation showing mean relative error reduced from 0.025%–11% down to ~10⁻¹³% across all 35 grid points (0 infeasible cases).
  - Experiment 4: Full compensation progression (baseline → wl_buffer_full → bl_star → combined_full → combined_full_precorrected) on identical axes, demonstrating precorrection as the final step in a complete error-elimination chain.

- **Updated documentation**: README.md and CLAUDE.md sections explaining the pre-correction approach, formula, and usage; experiment READMEs with parameter tables and key results.

- **Package export**: Added `precorrect_g_star` to `crossbar/__init__.py` public API.

## Implementation Details

The precorrection formula inverts the divider relationship in `combined_full`:
```
g_corrected[i,j] = 1 / ( (1 - r_col_end·G_j) / g_target[i,j] - R_star(i) )
```
where `R_star(i) = r_col*(n_rows-i)` is the known star-branch resistance and `G_j = sum_i g_target[i,j]` is the column conductance sum. This is exact (not iterative or approximate) and independent of `v_in`, making it a true pre-correction rather than a measured-input-specific calibration.

Both sweep scripts use the same `--variants` flag pattern as existing comparison scripts, with a reserved near-black color (#161616) for precorrected results to distinguish them from the four canonical compensation levels.

author: amir-shadanfar
body:
## Summary

Step 2 of the brief, first part: **measure before changing anything**. The Acme corpus (six documents, about one chunk each) cannot show a ranking change, so this adds a separate ~100-chunk synthetic corpus, a 16-question dataset, and `evaluation/evaluate_ranking.py`. The Acme corpus, its dataset and its published numbers are untouched.

## The corpus

100 chunks: 91 generic paragraphs that keep repeating a fictional product name ("Zenvora"), 4 distractors that use the same words without answering, 4 fact chunks, and **the technology table of `AGENTS.md` copied verbatim** (19 rows, 975 characters, one chunk) as the long table chunk. Everything else is invented; no personal text.

## The dataset (16 questions)

Short / long x with / without the product name x one fact / two facts in one chunk / two facts in two chunks, plus four controls that answer from ordinary fact chunks. Each expected chunk is identified by a verbatim marker that occurs in exactly one chunk (tested).

## Baseline, before any change (real embedder nomic-embed-text, qwen2.5:7b for the agent)

`POST /search` per mode, top 20; recall@k = fraction of expected chunks in the first k; complete@5 = all of them in the first 5; MRR = 1 / rank of the first expected chunk.

| Mode | recall@1 | recall@5 | recall@10 | complete@5 | MRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| vector | 0.22 | 0.31 | 0.31 | 0.25 | 0.33 |
| keyword | 0.41 | 0.75 | 0.75 | 0.75 | 0.58 |
| **hybrid (the default)** | **0.16** | **0.44** | **0.81** | **0.38** | **0.39** |
| agent (`POST /agent`, its sources) | 0.12 | 0.44 | 0.44 | 0.38 | 0.32 |

By group (hybrid): without the product name recall@5 0.69 (MRR 0.55), **with it 0.19 (MRR 0.23)**; one-fact 0.25; two-fact 0.33; controls 0.75. The agent averaged 2.19 searches per question and scored the same recall@5 as single-shot.

Findings the numbers support:
- The right chunk is usually *found* (hybrid recall@10 0.81) but at rank 7 to 9: the top 5 is filled by generic chunks.
- **The product name is not the only cause.** With no name, the vector arm still finds the long table chunk in the top 5 for 0 of 4 one-fact questions (vector recall@5 = 0.00): a long table embeds badly. The keyword arm without the name is excellent (recall@5 1.00, MRR 0.88) and collapses with it (0.50 / 0.29), because a strict AND on `zenvora` matches only distractors and the table is never a candidate.
- Controls are hurt by the name too: "How do I run the tests for the Zenvora project?" does not find its fact chunk in the top 20.
- Agent mode does not help: each of its searches returns 5 chunks and the table sits at rank 7 to 9.

## Changes per commit

1. `feat(evaluation): add a larger synthetic corpus and dataset for measuring ranking` - corpus builder, dataset, script, and tests (corpus about 100 chunks, deterministic, table verbatim, unique markers, metric arithmetic, smoke run with fakes; five mutations checked).

## How to run

```bash
uv run python -m evaluation.evaluate_ranking --api-key <key> --agent
```
Needs a live server with a real embedder (never in CI). Use a scratch tenant.

## Notes

- Also pushed to PR #39: `evaluate_retrieval` counted `context_only` neighbours as retrieved once #39 lists them in `sources`; fixed there with tests.
- The 16 questions and one corpus are a small sample: numbers are directional, not a benchmark. Scored on synthetic data only.

author: asafgolombek
body:
## Summary

PR 2 of the local-auth-reuse work. PR 1 (#1554) shipped `gh`/`aws`/`kubectl` login reuse via
`nimbus connector detect` + `nimbus init`, deferring `gcloud` to its own follow-up. This PR closes
that gap: a GCP connector (`gcp`/`bigquery`/`cloud_logging`/`vertex_ai` and their four lazy-mesh MCP
servers) can now authenticate as the owner's own `gcloud auth login` session instead of a
service-account key file (`GcpAuth`, `connectors/_lib/gcp-auth.ts`), detected read-only via
`gcloud config list --format json` (`detectGcloud`) and adopted through the same
`connector.adoptLocalAuth` HITL action type the other three sources already use.

This is the closing task of the PR (2.6): end-to-end coverage over a real gateway subprocess, docs,
and gates — plus a whole-branch review round that found two ship-blockers and several smaller
issues, all fixed in this same commit (see "Review fixes" below).

- `connectors/_lib/gcp-auth.ts`'s `resolveGcpAuth`: a configured `gcp.credentials_json_path` always
  wins over `gcp.auth_source = "gcloud"`, even when both are on file — a key is the more specific
  instruction. Adopting gcloud mode unconditionally clears any stored key path so the mode actually
  takes effect; the consent prompt discloses that clear only when a key path is actually on file.
- `detectGcloud` can report `available`, `needs_project` (an active login with no default project),
  `not_logged_in`, or `cli_not_found`. `needs_project` is the one non-`available` status
  `adoptLocalAuth`'s `usable()` still offers — the owner can supply a project id at adopt time
  (`nimbus connector detect --source gcloud --project <id>`, or the interactive prompt), and the
  explicit flag now correctly overrides gcloud's own detected default (see I-1 below).
- Neither `detectGcloud` nor the gcloud arm of `connector.auth` makes an outbound request, so there
  is nothing for `verifyBeforeStoreWithScopes` to probe and no `sync`-class egress row for gcloud
  mode specifically.
- `sync/connector-configured.ts`'s `isConnectorConfigured` now treats GCP as configured when
  EITHER a key path OR `auth_source = "gcloud"` is set, alongside `project_id`.

## This task (2.6)

**E2E.** Extended `packages/gateway/test/e2e/local-auth.e2e.test.ts` (a real gateway subprocess
driven over a real socket/named pipe — the layer that proves `connector.detectLocalAuth` /
`connector.adoptLocalAuth` are actually *routed*, not just handled): added a `gcloud` shim
(`gcloud config list --format json` → an account with no default project), added `"gcloud"` to
`writeShims`, updated the first test's expectation to the resulting four findings including gcloud
`needs_project`, and added an approved gcloud adoption (`{ source: "gcloud", project: "acme-prod" }`)
whose consent prompt and outcome are asserted, with the final vault-check test extended to assert
`gcp.auth_source = "gcloud"` and `gcp.project_id = "acme-prod"` after the gateway process is killed.
Verified locally (Windows, 5/5 pass) and via `bun run verify:docker --changed` (Docker Linux,
matching CI — 856/856 pass across 21 files, `local-auth.e2e.test.ts` included).

**Docs.**
- `docs/cli-reference.md`: `nimbus connector detect`'s example block, source-list prose, and result
  table now include `gcloud`; a new paragraph documents `--project <id>` semantics (required when
  `needs_project`, optional override otherwise, project-id-shape validated); the detection/adoption
  paragraph notes gcloud's local-only detection and network-free adoption.
- `docs/architecture.md`: the `connector.detectLocalAuth`/`connector.adoptLocalAuth` IPC catalogue
  entry now covers all four sources (including the `project` param and the `needs_project` status),
  and a new paragraph documents the `gcp.auth_source`/`gcp.project_id` write and the
  key-always-wins `resolveGcpAuth` rule — `grep -n "credentials_json_path" docs/architecture.md`
  returned nothing BEFORE this change (there was no prior "GCP credential model" section to extend,
  so this is new content rather than an edit to an existing note — the grep now finds this PR's own
  new paragraph, which is the expected and correct outcome).
- `docs/CHANGELOG.md`: new dated bullet (2026-09-20) summarizing this PR, distinct from PR 1's
  existing bullet and the separate same-day "GCP service-account key actually applies" fix; lists
  all four `detectGcloud` statuses (`available`/`needs_project`/`not_logged_in`/`cli_not_found`),
  and spells the CLI flag correctly (`--gcp-credentials-json`, matching `connector.ts:241` — a
  first draft of this bullet had the two doc files disagree on the flag name; both now say the
  same, real one).
- `docs/roadmap.md`: ticked the "Detect-and-reuse existing local auth" row to `[x]`, naming PR 1
  (#1554) and this PR.
- `packages/cli/src/commands/init.ts`: `--no-detect` help text now says `gh/aws/kubectl/gcloud`
  instead of the stale three-source list.
- Two locations were deliberately left untouched because they are correct as written:
  `packages/cli/src/commands/connector-detect.ts` (the `needs_project`-has-no-meaning-for-gh/aws/
  kubectl comment, and the shared-by-gh/aws/kubectl `chooseFromList` comment — gcloud never reaches
  `chooseFromList`) and `detect-local-auth.test.ts` (same `needs_project` claim, in a test).
- **Stale-enumeration sweep, stated as what it actually is:** two spelling-level greps (mine, then
  the reviewer's) each missed real hits; a third, concept-level sweep in the review round found two
  more, both in files this task itself had already edited and simply not re-swept afterward
  (`local-auth-shim.ts`'s file banner, `local-auth.e2e.test.ts`'s doc comment above the loop it
  widened to four sources) — both fixed here. Given that history, this sweep is not claimed
  complete; a fourth pass finding a fifth spot would not be surprising, and any such spot is the
  same one-line fix as the ones already found.

**Manual acceptance — NOT performed, and this is a deliberate, stated gap rather than an implied
result.** `gcloud` is not installed on this machine: `Bun.which("gcloud")` returns `null`. No manual
run against a real `gcloud auth login` session was made, and nothing below should be read as
describing what such a run "would" show — that would not be a real observation. What GCLOUD-MODE
BEHAVIOUR is covered by, instead:
- Unit tests (`detect-gcloud.test.ts`, `adopt-local-auth.test.ts` gcloud describe block,
  `auth.test.ts`'s "connector.auth gcp — gcloud login mode" block, `gcp-auth.test.ts`) against an
  injected fake CLI process — never a real `gcloud` binary.
- The new e2e test above, against a *shim* `gcloud` on `PATH` — a fake binary imitating gcloud's
  `config list --format json` output, run through the real spawn/env/routing path, but still not
  the real gcloud CLI or a real login session.
- What none of the above can prove, and what the closing brief specifically asked to record when
  possible (spec delta 6): whether a sandboxed GCP MCP tool call can actually read gcloud's own
  login store (its credentials cache under the gcloud config directory) when spawned through this
  repo's sandbox confinement. That question is **open** — it needs a machine with a real `gcloud`
  installed and logged in, run through the isolated-`LOCALAPPDATA` acceptance procedure (same rule
  as Task 1.13).

## Review fixes (whole-branch review round)

**I-1 (blocker, fixed) — `--project` was silently ignored whenever gcloud had a default project.**
`connector-detect.ts`'s `chooseOne` read `f.project ?? opts.project ?? ask(...)` — the detected
default beat the explicit flag, the opposite of the gateway's own `resolveTarget`
(`req.project ?? f.project` — request wins). Reordered the CLI to match:
`opts.project ?? f.project ?? ask(...)`. Added tests for both directions of `available` +
`--project` at both layers: `connector-detect.test.ts` ("--project overrides an available finding's
own detected default project" / "without --project, an available finding's own

author: pierreadel
body:
Changes:

**Code splitting + lazy loading + Suspense** - the /search route and the stars chart (pulls in @mui/x-charts, the heaviest dependency) now load on demand via React.lazy() + Suspense instead of shipping in the initial bundle.

Measured before/after:
- Initial chunk: 1,101KB -> 937KB (358.72KB -> 302.06KB gzip)
- Chart: split into its own 161KB chunk, only loads when the dashboard's chart section renders
- Search page: split into a ~2KB chunk

**Virtualized lists** - both the tracked-repos grid and search results list kept accumulating cards via "Load more" without ever unmounting earlier ones, so the DOM grew unbounded (search can go up to GitHub's 1000-result cap). Added @tanstack/react-virtual, but it only kicks in at 20+ items - below that it's the same plain list as before, since a scroll container isn't worth it for the common small case. For tracked repos this also let me drop "Load more" entirely, since all tracked repos' data is already fetched regardless of what's rendered - there was no real fetch being gated, just DOM size.

Adds ~8KB gzip to the main chunk for react-virtual itself (tracked-repos isn't lazy-loaded), but that's small next to the initial-load win above.

author: martinciu
body:
## 🌊 Problem

`~/.cache/ccpulse/ccpulse.log` grew to **427 MB / 1.99 M lines**, 60% of them one repeated WARN: the usage API returning 429. Measured during the incident: **2,596 × 429 in a single hour** — one every ~1.4 s.

The loop:

- tmux runs `ccpulse status --json --index` every **5 s**, plus a Stop hook per Claude Code session — each a fresh, short-lived process.
- `cacheTTL` is 3 min, so a healthy API sees one call per 3 min.
- On a failure, `Fetch` returned `cache_stale` and **never touched `usage.json`** — `UpdatedAt` stayed old, so **every subsequent invocation hit the API again**. Hammering a rate-limited endpoint keeps it rate-limited.

The TUI already handled this (`pollBackoff`: 6→12→24→30 min, `Retry-After` up to 1 h) — but only in-process. It politely waited thirty minutes while the statusline beside it fired at the same endpoint every five seconds.

## 🔧 Fix

**A persisted backoff window, one policy, every caller.**

- 📄 After any failed API call `Fetch` records a retry deadline in a sibling file, `<cacheDir>/usage-backoff.json` (0600, atomic, under the existing fetch flock). A stale-cache attempt before the deadline is **suppressed, not sent**. Success deletes the file.
- 🧠 The policy moved from `cmd/ccpulse` into `pkg/anthro`, so the TUI poller and every `status` process share it. The poller keeps no state of its own; it sleeps until the deadline `Fetch` reports.
- ➕ `FetchResult` gains additive `RetryAt` / `Consecutive429`. `Source` stays `cache_stale`; **the `status --json` schema is unchanged.** With no cache at all, a suppressed attempt returns a typed `*RetryError` — never a zero-value `Usage`, which would render as a perfectly plausible 0%.
- 🔇 The 429 WARN drops `body_snippet` (the status code is the whole message). With the window there is at most one such line per window anyway.
- 🩺 `doctor` reports the window: `ℹ usage API backoff: retry in 19m59s (2 consecutive 429s)`.

### Why a sibling file, not a field in `usage.json`

Writing the data cache on the *failure* path would either bump `UpdatedAt` (stale data masquerading as fresh) or, with no cache yet, create an entry holding zero `Usage`. A sibling keeps the data cache untouched and resets by deletion.

### The state file is untrusted input

Corrupt, wrong-version, or unreadable → **fails open** (no window), surfaced by `doctor`. A `retry_at` beyond the 1 h ceiling is **discarded, not capped**: capping on read looks like a fix and behaves like a wedge — every read would slide the ceiling forward and fetching would never resume. The ceiling carries one minute of read-side slack so a legitimate maximal window survives a small backward clock step.

### Cancellation is not an API failure

`context.Canceled` (TUI quit mid-fetch, SIGINT to `status`) records nothing — it would otherwise open a 3-minute window against an endpoint that did nothing wrong **and zero a live 429 escalation**. `context.DeadlineExceeded` deliberately still records: `status` wraps `Fetch` in a 5 s timeout, so that is exactly how an offline machine surfaces, and exempting it would bring back the 5-second loop.

## 🖥️ Verified on the real binary

Built from a clean `git archive`, isolated cache dir:

| scenario | runs | API attempts |
|---|---|---|
| stale cache + open window | 3 | **0** |
| stale cache, no window, API healthy (200) | 4 | **1** — then `cache_fresh`, no state file |
| stale cache, dead proxy (transport failure) | 3 | **1** — window written (0600), next two suppressed |
| SIGINT 918 ms into a hung fetch (`context canceled`) | 1 | window **not** written |
| same hung fetch to the 5 s timeout (`deadline exceeded`) | 1 | window **written** |

## 🧪 Test plan

- ✅ `go test ./...` (19 packages), `-race` on `pkg/anthro` + `cmd/ccpulse`, `make lint` → 0 issues. stdlib `testing` only, no new deps, frozen clock — nothing sleeps out a window.
- 🔬 Reviewed through four skill lenses (security, concurrency, testing, error-handling). The testing lens ran **23 mutations**; the 7 survivors are all closed in the last commit, and each new guard was confirmed to fail when its behaviour is broken — including by an independent re-run on an isolated copy (cancellation exemption, non-429 persistence, poller delay floor, ceiling slack).
- 🧵 Concurrency: state is re-read **after** lock acquisition; 16 concurrent callers on an expired window → exactly 1 API hit, all observe the same new deadline.
- 🛡️ Security: no Critical/High/Medium. State file fuzzed (MaxInt64, `1e400`, year 9999, 100k-deep nesting, ESC bytes) — no panic, no suppressed fetch; hostile `Retry-After` bounded to one request per hour at worst; sentinel bearer token never reaches a log line.
- 🔌 Call sites, not just helpers: the poller's outcome→delay step is extracted into a pure, table-tested `nextPollDelay`; the doctor line is asserted end-to-end.

## 📎 Notes

- `CLAUDE.md`: `pkg/anthro` package-map row updated; stale test name fixed (`TestFetch_NoCredentialFieldsInLogs`).
- Filed separately, deliberately not bundled: **#534** — a future `updated_at` in `usage.json` is served as `cache_fresh` forever (pre-existing, found by the security lens).

Closes #529

author: nadaverell
body:
Replica count could make a single workload's startup failures look independently corroborated by its node. Correlation now requires caller-visible Pods from at least two known workload owner UIDs, on the same node, with the exact same emitted network/startup failure class. Every underlying issue remains.

The Issues view keeps the original failure text once and exposes corroboration as a neutral context fact with up to five deterministic links to contributing Pods and a neutral evidence cue with an icon. The fact identifies the representative Pod, node and failure class, reports complete counts and any link truncation, and does not claim node causality. Existing message-only dashboard and MCP consumers retain the factual hint.

- ReplicaSet→Deployment and Job→CronJob links use cached intermediate objects and matching UIDs; missing or custom ownership stays unknown. Root ReplicaSets/Jobs with valid identities remain known workloads; standalone Pods do not corroborate.
- Only already-emitted namespace-visible failures contribute. Duplicate input scopes cannot inflate counts, volume failures do not corroborate network failures, and no new cluster-scoped resource links or authorization behavior are introduced.
- Structured context survives grouping and repeated enrichment without replacing existing rollup facts. No new public Issue fields or incident-grouping model.

Validation: `make test`, `make tsc`, full `make build`, the full k8s/issues/MCP suites, focused post-bind tests and 45 shared rendered-UI tests pass. Tests cover one owner/rolling revisions/CronJob runs, independent owners, missing or mismatched UIDs, unknown owners, mixed classes, scope, duplicate inputs, termination/recovery, deterministic references, five-link truncation and repeated grouped enrichment.

Live proof on existing kind used actual controller-created owner UIDs and a real missing-ConfigMap volume stall, with explicitly synthetic network Events (not a reproduced CNI outage). Same-owner before/after retained all six scheduling rows and removed the unsupported hint. HTTP/MCP returned three Pods/two owners for the partial reader versus four/three for the broader reader, with hidden identities absent from the restricted payload. `get_dashboard` and `diagnose` retain positive evidence. Real UI captures cover keyboard expansion, opening a contributing Pod, and readable 1280/856px layouts. Creating the missing ConfigMap verifies recovery and removal of the hint/context; the hidden namespace's unresolved issue remains.

Limits: corroboration retains the >10-minute age, ContainerCreating and no-IP eligibility floor. Fresh event-classified failures retain their own issues without a hint; exact-class event aging can remove corroboration without recovery. Unknown/custom ownership is incomplete rather than inferred. The app's existing minimum width is 856px; this does not add mobile support. Distinct owners with matching symptoms do not prove a node cause.

author: serroc
body:
## Поля `TYPE` + `EXPR` типизированы как методы

### Проблема

Ряд полей в `.xmd`, объявленных как `TYPE="..." EXPR="..."` (без `PROPERTY="1"`),
у нас затипизирован как функции — `time(): XmlElem<number | null>`, `name(): string`.
На самом деле это обычные элементы документа, а не методы.

Проверялось на `wtv_active_learning.xmd`, поле `time` (`TYPE="integer" EXPR="сумма parts.time"`),
на документе, у которого в `parts` нет заполненного `time` (реальная сумма = 0).

**1. Присвоение работает в памяти**

```js
doc = OpenDoc(UrlFromDocID(<id>));
s = 0;
for (p in doc.TopElem.parts) s += OptInt(p.time);
doc.TopElem.time = 99999;
alert('after assign: ' + doc.TopElem.time + ' / real sum: ' + s);
// after assign: 99999 / real sum: 0
```

Поле не getter: присвоенное значение хранится в элементе и читается обратно.

**2. Но до XML/каталога присвоенное значение не доходит**

```js
doc = OpenDoc(UrlFromDocID(<id>));
doc.TopElem.time = 99999;
doc.Save();
alert(ArrayOptFirstElem(XQuery("for $e in active_learnings where $e/id = <id> return $e/Fields('time')")).time);
// 0
```

Перед сериализацией при `Save()` движок пересчитал `EXPR` и затёр `99999` реальной суммой.

**Вывод.** Для полей с `TYPE` + `EXPR` (без `PROPERTY="1"`):
- `EXPR` вычисляется движком при открытии документа (`OpenDoc`) и повторно перед сохранением (`Save()`);
- присвоение живёт только в памяти до `Save()` и никогда не попадает в XML и в каталог;
- код, который присваивает таким полям значение (например, `teAL.state_id = 1`,
  `docLearning.TopElem.last_usage_date = ...`), не влияет на сохранённые данные;
- чтение поля в той же сессии после присваивания вернёт присвоенное, а не вычисленное значение —
  источник расхождений между тем, что видит код, и тем, что окажется в базе.

С точки зрения типов: это поля вида `XmlElem<T>`, а не `(): T`. Текущая типизация
заставляет писать `doc.TopElem.time()` — что в рантайме не работает, — и скрывает, что
поле можно (пусть и бесполезно) присвоить.

### Что сделано

Функции заменены на поля `XmlElem<...>` в 15 файлах (17 объявлений):

| Файл | Поле | Тип |
|---|---|---|
| `ms_general` | `used_fulltext` | `XmlElem<string \| null>` |
| `active_learning` | `last_usage_date` | `XmlElem<Date \| null>` |
| `active_learning` | `state_id` | `XmlElem<number, typeof common.learning_states>` |
| `active_learning` | `time` | `XmlElem<number \| null>` |
| `digital_signature`, `efficiency_grade`, `personnel_reserve`, `potential_grade` | `name` | `XmlElem<string \| null>` |
| `dn_program_discipl` | `laboriousn_all_term`, `all_laboriousn_audit`, `all_laboriousn_indep` | `XmlElem<number \| null>` |
| `file_source` | `path_filling_expr` | `XmlElem<boolean \| null>` |
| `host`, `server_agent` | `converter` | `XmlElem<boolean \| null>` |
| `invoice` | `total_price` | `XmlElem<number \| null>` |
| `poll` | `is_multiple_select` | `XmlElem<boolean>` |
| `poll_procedure` | `equal_hash` | `XmlElem<string \| null>` |
| `qa_test` | `lib_name` | `XmlElem<string \| null>` (было `boolean`, в `.xmd` — `string`) |
| `wiki_base` | `process_embedding` | `XmlElem<boolean>` |

### Проверка

- `npm run check` (eslint + tsc для `lib` и `tests`) — проходит.
- Поведение в рантайме проверено скриптами выше на `wtv_active_learning.time`.

author: danielstewart77
body:
Recurring tasks stop being one-shot sends into Telegram. A task that names a `discord_channel` in its frontmatter fires as a nudge into the session already bound to that channel — the same `("discord", channel_id)` binding the Discord bot resolves for an inbound message — so the conversation holds every previous fire and everything Daniel said back to it. The session is not killed, and the response is posted into the channel.

The skill is the whole configuration: it names its own channel and carries its own behaviour, so the fire carries no instructions. A week of fires is a week of briefings rather than a week of briefings plus seven copies of the instructions, and a reply typed later needs nothing re-established.

Nothing could push into a Discord channel through the bot — it only ever replies to something it received — so delivery calls the platform API directly with the bot token, the shape the Telegram path already had. Text first; the voice note follows as its own message so a channel without Attach Files still gets the briefing. Rate limits are waited out. A refused post is reported as a failure and never as a completion.

A task channel also stops demanding an at-mention, and stands outside `discord_allowed_channels` — that gate is ours, not Discord's, and requiring it on every reply would price the continuity the channel exists for at a keystroke nobody would keep paying.

The reaper is gone rather than exempted. A session ends when somebody ends it.

Design and accepted risks: `docs/architecture/channel-resident-scheduled-tasks.md`.

**Inert until configured.** No skill names a channel yet, so behaviour is unchanged until a `discord_channel` line is added to Ada's `7am` skill.

Three adversarial reviewers ran against the diff; their surviving findings are in the second commit. 1017 tests in the main suite and 249 in comms, all green.

author: timveil
body:
Tests and fixtures only; nothing under `src/main` changes, so this does not trigger a release.

## What
Pins current behaviour, against a real Postgres (Testcontainers, FK enforcement on), for the schema shapes in #613, and turns the "trace" claims from the code audit into verified results. Cases that fail today are written as `@Disabled` desired-outcome tests linked to their follow-up issue, so each fix PR just removes the annotation.

- `create_partitioned.postgres.sql`: one schema per scenario plus a `saas` schema mirroring #613 (range-partitioned `orders`, tenant-scoped composite FKs, first-of-month CHECKs, rollup table).
- `create_fk_shapes.postgres.sql`: self-reference, mutual cycle, serial and identity PK targets, unconfigured-parent cardinality, partial-failure.
- `PostgresSchemaFixture`: one container per class, a Hikari pool pinned to each scenario schema, and `assertForeignKeysEnforced` (checks FKs are validated and triggers are on).
- `PostgresPartitionedSchemaTest`, `PostgresForeignKeyShapesTest`, plus one `@Disabled` unit test in `PostgresConstraintsTest`.

## Results
13 tests pin current behaviour and pass; 12 `@Disabled` tests assert the desired outcome. I ran the disabled ones with the disabled condition deactivated to confirm each fails for the stated reason, and ran the same assertions against hand-filled valid data to confirm they will pass once fixed. The full ten-claim table is in [this comment](https://github.com/timveil/bloviate/issues/614#issuecomment-5749995112). Highlights:

- Partitioned parent is skipped and its leaves are filled directly, failing on partition bounds (#615).
- FK to an auto-increment/identity PK is broken, not just unverified (#617).
- `CHECK (date_trunc('month'::text, d) = d)` is mis-parsed as allowed values `["month"]` and crashes a plain fill (#619).
- Mutual FK cycle: sequential path throws, parallel path silently skips the tables (#618).

The end-to-end `saas` test is disabled under #613 and needs #615, #617 and #619 together.

Closes #614

author: mahaloz
body:
## The problem

`libctypes` names a libc struct only where the image IMPORTS the function that
declares it. gnulib's obstack is linked into the program instead, so the widest
aggregate in the corpus's ground truth after `FILE` — 431 pointer variables — is
never named, and the declaration that would have named it is in the binary's own
symbol table. Seventy-odd other libc slots are simply missing from the table.

`/usr/bin/grep` on any glibc box, on `main`:

```
$ kuna decompile-all /usr/bin/grep | grep -E '_obstack_newchunk'
void _obstack_newchunk(struct_14 *a0,unsigned long a1) // ternary
      _obstack_newchunk(a0,0x20);
      _obstack_newchunk(a0);          <- one argument; the second was never recovered
```

After: `void _obstack_newchunk(obstack *a0,unsigned long a1)`, both arguments at
every call, and its callers take an `obstack *` — `sub_f210(unsigned long *a0)`
and `sub_ed20(void *a0,...)` become `sub_f210(obstack *a0)` and
`sub_ed20(obstack *a0,...)`.

## The fix

- Seven named aggregates, sized from `sizeof`/`_Alignof` and cross-checked
  against the corpus's own DWARF: `obstack` 88, `spwd` 72, `utmpx` 384,
  `utmp` 384, `re_pattern_buffer` 64, `lconv` 96, `statfs` 120.
- About seventy-five slots on names the table already had — the rest of the
  stream surface, the three account databases, more `tm`/`timespec`/`termios`/
  `sigset_t`, the regex entry points. Every signature comes from
  `gcc -aux-info` over the installed headers, and `libctypes off` stays
  byte-identical to `main` (9 whole binaries, `cmp -s`).
- The five `_obstack_*` entry points are the one thing matched against a name the
  image DEFINES — the reserved half of `obstack.h`, so a definition can only be
  glibc's or gnulib's. They get two tables, because the publishers disagree:
  gnulib's size type is `size_t`, the installed glibc header says `int`, so a
  defined name takes the first and an import the second.
- Which slots to add came from mining the corpus's ground truth rather than from
  reading headers; the ranked table is in `docs/features/libcstructs/`.

## The tests

Four assertions on a new fixture in `tests/stages/kuna-libctypes.xml` (`void` →
`obstack *` through a defined entry point, `void` → `spwd *` and `FILE *`
through imported ones) and six unit tests over the table invariants, the two
obstack channels and the account-database argument lists.

444-slice typesweep, two builds of this tree: **1,349 → 1,353 perfect, mean
.3405 → .3419, 91 functions improved / 1 worse**, `ptr_struct` 422 → 496,
exported variable counts identical on both arms. Whole-corpus hunk
classification over 14 binaries and the speed block are in
`docs/features/libcstructs/analysis.md`.

Two regressions ship knowingly, both the same shape — a named sub-object splits
a frame slot its neighbour owned — and both instances of a rendering `main`
already prints. gzip `-O2` `lutimens`: a 144-byte `stat` local becomes
`char v5 [80]` handed to `lstat`, and three words of its tail detach into
`v9`/`v10`/`v11`, which **the emitted body reads with nothing writing them**.
Over the 30 slices that import `utimensat`/`futimens` those rows win 122
functions a `timespec` against that one, and `main` already prints 7 such
under-declared `stat` frames to this branch's 8 — so they are kept. openssh
`ssh_signal` splits a `sigaction` the same way through `sigfillset`, and
`main`'s `sigemptyset` prints the identical split. Ablations in `analysis.md`.

## Changes

Import Nilay Knowledge as a private Next.js workspace with its complete source history, attribution, license notices, shared configuration, and build/test integration.

This is the first of three pull requests splitting #101 to respect GitHub's 100-commit rebase merge limit while retaining every original commit in `1.x`. It contains the original first 99 commits, followed by a commit deferring the incomplete Nilay About snapshot. The resulting file tree contains the Knowledge integration, with its existing Vitest 4 / Vite security fixes brought forward from the later About integration so this intermediate revision has no audited dependency vulnerabilities. The batch also waits for Lane initialization and Vista source acquisition before asserting the loaded UI, fixing startup races exposed by Windows CI. Remove unused MathJax, Lightbox, and jQuery script imports from the four legacy legal-text pages and their public copies, addressing the CodeQL review findings while preserving the text, images, title, and navigation. The next pull request restores the identical About snapshot before continuing its remaining history and integration; the third retains the repository validation changes.

## Validation

- Verified: exactly 100 commits above `1.x`; all original commits are retained.
- Passed after bringing forward the existing toolchain fixes: `npm ci --ignore-scripts --dry-run`; npm dependency audit reports zero vulnerabilities.

author: zkochan
body:
## Summary

Closes pnpm/pnpm#15161.

Every linker but one reports a direct dependency as it creates the symlink for it under `node_modules`. The hoisted linker writes the package into `node_modules/<alias>` itself and creates no symlink there, so nothing reported it, and `@pnpm/cli.default-reporter` fell back to diffing `package.json`.

That fallback knows the range a dependency was asked for, not the version it resolved to, and it sees nothing at all when `package.json` did not change. Measured against the isolated linker, a hoisted install:

| | isolated | hoisted, before | hoisted, after |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| `pnpm add pkg` | `+ pkg 100.1.0` | `+ pkg ^100.0.0` | `+ pkg 100.1.0` |
| version change | `- pkg 100.0.0` / `+ pkg 100.1.0` | nothing | `- pkg 100.0.0` / `+ pkg 100.1.0` |
| `install` after deleting `node_modules` | `+ pkg 100.1.0` | nothing | `+ pkg 100.1.0` |
| `pnpm remove pkg` | `- pkg 100.1.0` | `- pkg ^100.1.0` | `- pkg 100.1.0` |
| `pnpm add -g a b` | both packages | first package only | both packages |
| nothing changed | nothing | nothing | nothing |

The hoisted path now reports the direct dependencies whose resolution changed, by comparing the lockfile the previous install left in `node_modules/.pnpm` against the one this install materializes. That comparison gives the same answer the symlink outcome gives the other linkers: a dependency is reported when this install put it there or replaced it, and a repeat install still reports nothing.

`link:` dependencies are left out of the comparison. They are symlinked even under the hoisted linker, so they are already reported.

### pnpm v12

pnpm 12 has the same bug, with nothing to soften it: `pnpm install --config.node-linker=hoisted` on 12.5.1 printed no summary at all, because pacquet has no `package.json` fallback. The cause matches. `run_hoisted_linker` runs `SymlinkDirectDependencies` with `link_only: true`, which filters every regular dependency out in `collect_resolved_entries` before `emit_root_added` can fire.

The Rust half is the same comparison against `PriorHoistedState::current_lockfile`, the previous install's `lock.yaml`, which the hoisted linker already receives for its orphan diff. Both stacks now emit the same `pnpm:root` events for the same installs, which is what keeps `@pnpm/cli.default-reporter` rendering pacquet's NDJSON the way it renders the TypeScript CLI's.

## Squash Commit Body

```text
Every other linker reports a direct dependency as it creates the symlink
for it under `node_modules`. The hoisted linker writes the package into
`node_modules/<alias>` itself and creates no symlink there, so nothing
reported it. pnpm 11 fell back to diffing `package.json`; pnpm 12 has no
fallback and printed no summary at all.

That fallback knows the range a dependency was asked for, not the version
it resolved to, and it sees nothing at all when `package.json` did not
change. So a hoisted install printed `+ pkg ^1.0.0` where every other
linker prints `+ pkg 1.2.3`, printed nothing for a version change or for
the dependencies it put back after `node_modules` was deleted, and listed
only the first package of a `pnpm add -g` that installs several.

Both stacks' hoisted paths now report the direct dependencies whose
resolution changed, by comparing the lockfile the previous install left
in `node_modules` against the one this install materializes.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#15161.
```

## Checklist

- [x] I checked the referenced issue and verified that none of the PRs
  already linked to it solves it.
- [x] New features are implemented only in the Rust pnpm v12 CLI. Bug fixes
  are implemented in every affected version.
- [x] Added a changeset (`pnpm changeset`) if this PR changes any published
  package. Keep it short and written for pnpm users — it becomes a release note.
- [x] Added or updated tests.

---
Written by an agent (Claude Code, claude-opus-5).

author: jaggerxtrm
body:
## Why v0.13.0 failed to publish

The publish job died at **"Check payload hygiene"** — *before* it ever reached npm:

```
Forbidden packed paths:
- .xtrm/skills/optional/xtrm-maintenance/sync-docs/evals/evals.json (eval output)
```

`check-payload-hygiene.mjs` forbids `/(^|\/)evals?(\/|$)/` and `/(^|\/)workspace\//` paths, but `package.json`'s exclusions covered **only the default tier**:

``"
!.xtrm/skills/default/**/evals/**
!.xtrm/skills/default/**/workspace/iteration-*/**
!.xtrm/skills/default/*-workspace/**
```

The optional tier had no equivalent, so **any** optional-tier skill carrying eval or workspace output is packed and fails the release. The offending file is tracked and arrived 2026-09-12 with the vendored `sync-docs` skill.

## Change

Mirrors the three default-tier patterns for the optional tier. Three added lines, `package.json` only.

## Verification

| Check | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `check:payload-hygiene` | exit 1, forbidden path reported | **exit 0**, `Payload hygiene ok` |
| Packed files | 325 | 324 |
| `npm pack` paths matching `evals`/`workspace/iteration-` | 1 | **NONE** |
| `sync-docs` real content still packed | yes | **yes** (references, scripts, SKILL.md) |

Verified with an actual `npm pack --dry-run --json` listing, not just the hygiene script — the skill still ships; only its eval artifact is dropped. `package.json` parses; diff is limited to the `files` array.

## Process note (not fixed here)

`check:payload-hygiene` runs **only** in `publish.yml` and `prepublishOnly` — never in the pull-request CI job. That is why this sat undetected from 2026-09-12 until the release attempt, and it's the same *publish-only gate* class as CORE-2326 (fresh-machine smoke). Two independent release blockers, both invisible until publish. Worth addressing together.

author: fakechris
body:
Closes #485
Involute: INV-623

## Summary

A source row and a reader pack could not say where they came from without `index.json`.

- **`SourceRow.capture_path`** — the intake record's `from`, the capture location *before* the sweep normalized and moved the file. Kept beside `rel_path`, whose meaning is unchanged (current location). First intake record wins, matching `captured_on`: a re-ingest of the same bytes is not a new origin.
- **`run-status.json`** gains `source_url`, `source_sha256`, `source_rel_path`. Two sources with the same title are no longer indistinguishable from inside a pack, and a pack that outlives an index rebuild still names its source.
- **`ovp2 doctor` → `pack-provenance`** cross-checks each pack's self-declared sha against the sha the index joined it to. Until now that join was the only link from a claim back to its source and there was no second opinion to check it against. A mismatch is a Fail — the claims citing that pack point at the wrong note. Packs predating the field are Info, not a failure.

All fields serde-additive, per the "additive evolution only" rule in `docs/product-state-layout.md`.

## Design calls worth flagging

**The source title moved into `SourceProvenance`.** Adding a parameter pushed `write_reader_pack` to 8 arguments, over clippy's limit. Rather than allow the lint, I folded `source_title` into the struct — it is exactly the "which source is this" fact the struct exists to carry, and `run-status.json` already wrote it next to the three new keys. `run_reader_pipeline` refills the title from the `SourceDoc`, so a caller cannot disagree with the source about its own name.

**Key naming.** The keys are `source_url` / `source_sha256` / `source_rel_path`, not bare `url` / `sha256` / `rel_path`. They sit beside the existing `"source"` title key, and `source_sha256` matches `PackRow.source_sha256` — the same name on both sides of the comparison `doctor` performs.

**`read-source` records no `rel_path`.** It takes an arbitrary path and has no `--vault-root`, so it cannot anchor one. Writing the argument verbatim would put an absolute or cwd-relative value in a field whose contract is vault-relative. Absent beats wrong.

## Gates

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test --workspace --exclude ovp2-desktop` | exit 0 — 85 result blocks, 0 failed |
| `cargo clippy --workspace --exclude ovp2-desktop --all-targets -- -D warnings` | exit 0, zero warnings |
| `codex review --uncommitted` (gpt-6-astra, high) | clean on the third pass; P1 + P2 below fixed |

`ovp2-desktop` is excluded because its Tauri build script needs a staged sidecar binary and `console-ui/dist`, neither present in a fresh worktree. That matches how the gates are already run on this branch series.

## Codex findings, both fixed

**[P1] `capture_path` leaked into published artifacts.** `PublicView::from_model` clears `rel_path` but I added a new field and did not clear it, so `ovp-publish` serialized private vault paths into public `api/model.json`. Worse than `rel_path`: the pre-move path names the capture mechanism and the producer's own filename on top of the vault layout. Now cleared, and the redaction fixture carries a non-null `capture_path` so the assertion can actually fail — verified by temporarily removing the fix and watching the test go red.

**[P2] `read-source` wrote a non-vault-relative `source_rel_path`.** Fixed as described above.

## Note

`cargo fmt` is not run. The repo is not rustfmt-clean, so formatting any touched file reformats unrelated code in it and buries the diff; I reverted an accidental sweep to keep this reviewable. The diff is semantic-only.

One unrelated flake seen and confirmed harmless: `evolve_ab_e2e::paired_cli_executes_accepts_rejects_and_preserves_evidence` fails with "input fixture or executable changed during paired run" when another `cargo` build runs concurrently. It passes in isolation and in the clean full run above.

  - Added `pack-provenance` diagnostics to identify mismatches between indexed sources and reader packs.
  - Older packs without provenance are clearly identified as legacy.

- **Documentation**

author: daniel-t-s-adams
body:
Four findings from #72, which auto-merged before they could be answered here.

## The unit test could not fail for the mutant it named

`route_layer` wraps only the routes registered *before* it runs. `the_control_group_is_capped_by_the_same_number` registered its probe after `control_routes` had applied its bound, then applied a second `RequestBodyLimitLayer` beside it — so the probe was capped by the test's own layer, and the test passed with the group's bound deleted. I confirmed that directly: deleting `control_routes`' `route_layer` killed only the integration test.

The bound now goes on through `bounded(routes, limit)`, which takes the group. `control_routes` hands it the real route; the test hands it the probe. Deleting the bound inside `bounded` now fails the unit test as well.

## The 64 MiB ceiling was not a limit this service could apply

`axum` caps every body-consuming extractor at 2 MiB (`axum-core`'s `DEFAULT_LIMIT = 2_097_152`) unless `DefaultBodyLimit` says otherwise. `LARGEST_PROTOCOL_BODY_BYTES` let a deployment name up to 64 MiB, so anything above 2 MiB would have been refused at 2 MiB while the configuration said something else — a limit nobody chose, which is the failure `[member_api]` exists to prevent, and it would have appeared only once the §5 JSON routes landed.

The control group now disables that, so `max_control_body_bytes` is the only bound on it, and the constant's doc says so. `the_configured_limit_is_the_only_one_that_applies` sends 3 MiB through a 4 MiB limit and reads the whole body back.

The alternative — deriving a smaller ceiling from the control contract — was available, but the ceiling is the operator's memory decision and §10.3's chunk is the one number the protocol supplies for "a body this protocol defines at all". Making the whole range usable seemed better than narrowing it to what the framework happened to allow.

## The error module claimed an absolute the same PR had broken

`error.rs` said every failing response from this service carries the pinned shape. The bodyless `503` that #72 introduced for an unrepresentable clock does not. The module doc names that exception now, and points at `service::no_server_time`.

## A fixture used a value its predecessor had made invalid

The hostname case in `a_member_api_section_with_an_unusable_value_does_not_load` passed `max_control_body_bytes = 262144`, which #72 made invalid, so it isolated the `listen` rejection only because `validate_for` checks `listen` before the body bound. It now passes a valid limit.

**No test can catch this one.** Reordering the two checks is what it guards against, and the old fixture still passes today — so it is a latent dependency removed, not a behaviour newly covered. I am flagging it rather than claiming a mutant, because the mutant survives.

## Verification

`make check` and `make db-test` green. The two structural fixes are killed by named tests:

| mutant | killed by |
|---|---|
| the control group's own bound deleted | `the_control_group_is_capped_by_the_same_number` |
| axum's 2 MiB default left in place | `the_configured_limit_is_the_only_one_that_applies` |

The mutants from #72 still hold. No migration, no schema change, no protocol meaning changed.

author: arena-ai-coding-agent[bot]
body:
## What changed

Synchronize KEmulator's virtual `System.currentTimeMillis()` implementation.

Every MIDlet call is rewritten to `CustomMethod.currentTimeMillis()`. Before this change, two MIDlet threads could interleave the updates of its shared wall-clock snapshot and accumulated virtual time. A delayed caller could overwrite the newer snapshot, causing the following call to add an already-counted interval again.

## Why this fixes the Bluetooth symptom

Art Of War uses a UI thread plus a Bluetooth/L2CAP worker. Its worker polls `L2CAPConnection.ready()` and measures a 60-second receive deadline with `System.currentTimeMillis()`. A raced virtual clock can make that deadline (and other game timers) expire early even when TCP/L2CAP traffic is healthy. The client is the first side waiting for a host packet in the game's ping-pong protocol, so it can lose input/control while the host still appears to continue locally.

The synchronized method makes each clock advance atomic and preserves the existing speed and paused-step semantics.

## Scope

This is intentionally one commit and one source file on top of `bluepop2`; it does not bring in the earlier Bluetooth implementation/history.

## Validation

- `git diff --check`
- Build/runtime test not run because this environment has no JDK installed.

## Purpose

Improve coordination and measurement without another model-tuning pass. This PR targets `personal`, not upstream `main`. It does not change model/effort defaults, concurrency, approvals, service tiers, `research_verifier`, or the guarded apply implementation.

## Changes

- Give reviewers a ready snapshot, return findings, then resume for a ready delta instead of short-interval polling.
- Share validation evidence tied to the actual working-tree state, command, and relevant environment. Retain purposeful independent final verification.
- Probe critical parser/runtime/configuration assumptions early and read-only; never publish private configuration.
- Add paired `--since`/`--until` response-record scope, clearly separated from full recorded session/thread spans.
- Label allowance windows from recorded metadata, flag changed/unknown resets, and distinguish counted, excluded automatic-review, and all-recorded token subtotals.
- Mark reasoning as included in output and mixed/legacy effort attribution honestly; refuse unsupported scoped cumulative data or missing timestamps instead of guessing.
- Add `mise run orchestrator:usage` and a focused `PERFORMANCE.md` reference with official OpenAI and Artificial Analysis research links. No new telemetry service, cost calculator, forced compaction, or upstream profile import.

## Verified here

Original edited-file bytes were checked against GitHub blob hashes. In an isolated source snapshot, `python -m pytest -q tests/test_token_usage.py` passed **21 tests plus 13 subtests**. `python -m py_compile scripts/token_usage.py` and whitespace checks passed. Changed role TOMLs parse, their non-instruction fields are unchanged, and existing mise tasks/tools are unchanged. The uploaded reporting and test blobs match the tested bytes.

## Local gate before merge/install

The full guarded-sync integration suite, actual mise execution/argument forwarding, private installed-file plan, and current Codex log compatibility were **not** run here. Local Codex should review the diff, validate/test through mise, and rerun a known task interval privately. Preserve drift and unrelated local work. Do not publish logs, reports, receipts, or configuration dumps.

After those checks pass, merge into `personal` and use the documented guarded sync/apply/status workflow. A simple sync cannot install an unmerged PR. Start a new Codex session after changed role/skill files are applied.

There is no measured speedup claim: these are targeted workflow improvements plus tested reporting corrections. The selected interval counts whole timestamped response records, not inferred compute time or an attributable subscription bill.

author: jktzhitrl
body:
## Summary
This PR introduces a complete local camera management system that integrates Reolink and Blink cameras into a unified Home Assistant dashboard with local recording via Frigate, eliminating the need for cloud subscriptions.

## Key Changes
- **Docker Compose setup**: Added orchestration for Mosquitto (MQTT broker), Frigate (local NVR), and Home Assistant services
- **Frigate configuration**: Configured two Reolink cameras with dual-stream setup (main stream for recording, sub-stream for object detection) with 7-day motion-based retention
- **MQTT integration**: Set up Mosquitto broker to connect Frigate with Home Assistant
- **Environment configuration**: Added `.env.example` template for camera credentials and `.gitignore` to prevent accidental credential commits
- **Comprehensive documentation**: Added detailed README with setup instructions, security considerations, and hardware recommendations

## Notable Implementation Details
- Frigate uses CPU-based object detection by default with optional Google Coral USB accelerator support
- Blink cameras leverage Home Assistant's native integration with local USB storage on Sync Module 2 to bypass cloud recording requirements
- MQTT runs in anonymous mode (suitable for trusted home networks only) with guidance for production hardening
- Home Assistant uses `network_mode: host` for simplified local network access
- Frigate container includes 256MB shared memory allocation for video processing
- All services configured with `restart: unless-stopped` for reliability
- Credentials injected via environment variables to keep sensitive data out of version control

author: alexratmanpl
body:
## What changed

Three documentation repairs, found by checking every instruction file in this repository against every other after five pull requests in two days moved the file layout, replaced the word cap, and changed its counter.

| File | Was | Is |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `README.md` | listed four of `build_skills.py`'s checks | lists all five |
| `docs/adr/README.md` | silent on how a record relates to the rule it records | says `AGENTS.md` holds every operative rule |
| `CHANGELOG.md` | a word count with no counter named | names it |

No behaviour changes. Nothing in `skills/` is touched.

## Why

**`README.md`.** #31 added the budget check and the README's Development section was not updated with it. That section is the one place a contributor reads to learn what the build enforces, and the check it omitted is the one most likely to stop them.

**`docs/adr/README.md`.** ADR 0001 states inside itself that `AGENTS.md` carries the operative rule and the record only says why. ADR 0002 does not. So the repository had two files that both read as normative on the word budget, and nothing saying which wins — while `RUN.md` in the control repository asserts that `AGENTS.md` is the only place the rule is stated. The index now says it once, for every record present and future. ADR 0001's own sentence stays: a record is not edited after it is accepted, and the index is not a record.

**`CHANGELOG.md`.** The first `Unreleased` entry gave `1,925 → 1,119` with no counter named, directly above the entry explaining that the counter had just changed. Two figures for the same file exist in this repository — 1,165 by `wc -w`, 1,119 by the build's counter — so an unqualified one is a trap.

## Checked

- `python3 scripts/build_skills.py --check-only`: four skills, exit 0, unchanged figures.
- Every backticked file path in `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, both records and `.github/pull_request_template.md` resolves to a file that exists — checked by script, not by eye.
- Every bold **Section** reference across both repositories checked against the headings that actually exist. That is what caught a stale pointer in the control repository's `REVIEW.md`, fixed there.
- A sentence-similarity scan across `AGENTS.md`, the pull request template, ADR 0002 and the control repository's three instruction files: seven cross-file pairs before, one after. The one that remains is in the control repository and pre-existing.
- `scripts/check_no_session_links.sh`: OK.
- Blob SHAs of all three pushed files against the locally tested copies, and `git diff HEAD origin/<branch>` is empty.

## Review

Not put through the two-axis review. `REVIEW.md` measures a change against a finding in the control repository's `feedback/`, and this change has none — it came from a cross-check of the instruction files against each other, which is a source that review has no axis for.

What that cross-check found and fixed in the control repository, since it is the other half of the same pass: `REVIEW.md` told the reviewer that `interview-prep` states its twenty-five word ceiling in **The brief**, which stopped being true when #30 moved it to `references/brief.md`; `REVIEW.md` step 4 said to run every checker against both versions without saying against what, which is how a measurement of `SKILL.md` alone reported a relocation as an improvement in #30's first body; and `RUN.md` restated three things it explicitly says it does not restate.

Two pairs of restated text were left alone rather than collapsed, and both are worth knowing about:

1. `RUN.md` and `CAPTURE.md` both state the promise-versus-behaviour bar — one for writing a finding, one for acting on it. `CAPTURE.md` is guidance to a person and `RUN.md` is a gate, so a person writing a wish-shaped finding anyway still has to be caught. Both load-bearing.
2. `AGENTS.md` and `README.md` both say that installing flattens the categories so names must be unique. Same fact, two audiences. Pre-existing.

## Why
In the installed 0.8.48 the apple provider still answered "I cannot access external applications or sessions" to "now you see muxa agents?". The helper itself works — called directly with the same socket it lists the real sessions — but the question was asked in a conversation started before the workspace tools existed, whose replayed history holds the model's own earlier refusal. The on-device model then repeats itself instead of calling a tool it has since been given (3 runs: 3 refusals, 0 tool calls).

## What
The helper's instructions now say that an earlier "cannot access" answer predates its tools and is out of date, and that a question about the user's agents means calling `list_agent_sessions` rather than answering from memory. Against the same poisoned history: tool called on every run (6/6 across helpers built with the 26.5 and 27.0 SDKs).

Workaround meanwhile: start a New Conversation before asking.

author: delphykmc
body:
## Goal

WP-Help-D — **Agent interface / offline canonical documentation retrieval**. Base is merged WP-Help-C `main@408f53f1f44574682b0db348e4dd0d2c02a3c5a2` (PR #91). This slice makes the *existing* searchable User Guide useful to repository-aware agents without adding a chatbot or any new application/network dependency.

## Implementation

- `docs/user-guide/llms.txt`: complete entrypoint for all **35** canonical MkDocs navigation routes, question-to-page routing, and explicit repository-side search instructions; no invented hosted URL or separate content authority.
- `scripts/search_user_guide.py`: Python 3.10 stdlib-only, deterministic lexical search over checked-in canonical User Guide Markdown. Text or `--json` results include source-relative Markdown path, exact 1-based source line, heading, brief excerpt and corresponding generated HTML route. Bounded 1–20 results, no network, model, embeddings, tokens, local image content, index cache, runtime dependency, or screenshot-notes indexing. Code fences are excluded from answer snippets.
- `scripts/check_docs.py`: ensure `llms.txt` enumerates every MkDocs critical navigation route once; generated-site checker already requires referenced HTML routes to exist.
- `tests/unit/test_user_guide_agent_search.py`: source attribution, deterministic ordering, fenced-code exclusion, excluded screenshot asset docs, JSON output, Unicode, empty and out-of-bounds input, real corpus sanity.
- Docs: `docs/USER_GUIDE_AGENT_INTERFACE.md`, `docs/USER_GUIDE_FOLLOW_UP.md`, `docs/USER_GUIDE.md`, `AGENTS.md` maintain source authority and distinguish agent search from future, **not yet approved**, Ask PixelScope/RAG/LLM UI. `.github/workflows/user-guide.yml` runs the focused tests on both OSes.

## Security and scope

Canonical Markdown is unchanged; offline site, existing local Help, manual Pages/artifact publication, and the P7 exact four-file release contract remain unchanged. CLI is repository-side only; installed users already have offline MkDocs search. No new PySide6 UI, F1 help routing, provider API, implicit cloud access, credentials, image/IQA indexing or service dependency.

`Ask PixelScope` is explicitly evaluated and **deferred** until there is an owner-approved UX/provider/security contract. This is WP-Help-D's useful static/local agent interface, not a claim that a chatbot has shipped.

## Validation

GitHub User Guide validation (Windows/Ubuntu): focused docs/agent retrieval tests, `check_docs`, strict blocked-network cold-cache MkDocs, generated-site contract, repository-wide Ruff; Windows also runs mypy `src` and release packaging regression tests. Report only completed exact-head run evidence in the PR discussion. Owner-local focused test command:

```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest -q tests\unit\test_user_guide_agent_search.py tests\unit\test_docs_contract.py tests\unit\test_user_guide_site_contract.py
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts\search_user_guide.py "RAW14 stride" --json
```

Independent latest-head review requested; do not merge automatically. Commits are ChatGPT co-authored.
