author: alexandrelab
body:
Makes the cement premise solve as a real decarbonisation case. It did not solve at all, for two independent reasons, and both are closed.

**Sits on `feat/carb3-ledger-and-run`. Land after #54 to #57.**

## Problem 1 — cement could not state its duty

`activity_process_duty_profile.csv` carries **no mass carrier anywhere**: 427 rows, 26 distinct `carrier_id` values, and neither `cement` nor `clinker` among them. A cement works' duty is a mass — 1.13 Mt/yr of cement. The minimal A2 as note 21 §3.3 specifies it reads only the register and the duty profile, so it took the 1.13 off `cement_grinding`'s `MOT` row and stated it as 1.13 **PJ/yr of motive power**. Both grinders have `cement` as their primary output, so nothing could serve it and the pre-solve diagnosis blocked the premise. That is note 20 item 51.

The specification had already resolved it; the plan simply omitted it. Spec §3.1.2: *"Where the `carrier_id` is a product with `may_export` true, the row is the premise's **duty** on that product under D5 — a cement works' 1.13 Mt/yr of cement is what C1 makes it produce. Where the carrier is an internal product (`may_export` false), there is no duty to state (§3.9) and the row is **evidence** instead."*

So A2 now reads `premise_throughput` for product duties, base year only per D12, Mt/yr per D5 (hybrid denominators). A process whose units make a `product` yields **no duty from the profile at all** — its `MOT` or `HTH` row classifies the process's energy need, exactly as §3.9 says, and that need reaches C8 (carrier balance) through the unit's own input coefficients. `clinker`, `may_export` FALSE, stays evidence and its makers are pinned by C8 through the internal-supply mechanism the previous lane added. The duty profile is **not** changed and gains no `cement` row.

## Problem 2 — no capture train could ever be built

`co2_captured` appears exactly once in `unit_input_output.csv`, as `ccs_amine`'s `primary_output`, and nothing consumes it. It is `carrier_kind` `product`, so §5.2's safety gate forbids disposing of it; `may_export` is TRUE and the slice had dropped the export variable, so C8 pinned that node — and every capture train — to **zero however cheap it was**. Note 20 item 53.

`x_{c,t}` is restored narrowly, on three tests:

| Test | Source | What it stops |
|---|---|---|
| `carrier.may_export` TRUE | §3.4 | Exporting a carrier the site may not sell |
| A `premise_connection` row carries it | §3.1.3, §5.2 | "Leaving the site means going onto a network" |
| A complete price series, **every** period | §3.8 | An unpriced export is free disposal, which §5.2's `may_dispose` gate forbids for a `primary` carrier |

The third bites today: `export_price` covers `electricity` at six of seven periods and **not 2021** — `heavy_fuel_oil`'s single `import_price` row one table away — so electricity export is refused at all three premises and reported rather than becoming a sink a CHP could overbuild into.

**Carbon stays charged on disposal per §5.4.** What leaves through the pipe is not vented, so it attracts nothing. Asserted algebraically at every CO₂ node rather than inferred from a total: production splits into what the train draws and what is vented, and only the vented half carries a charge.

### C9 comes partly back into scope, and it is better sourced

`infrastructure_scenario.csv`'s 63 `co2_transport` rows give availability by cluster and period: **four clusters turn available at 2030 — `teesside`, `humber`, `humber2`, `mersey` — and five never do.** The export is bounded to zero where the premise's cluster is unavailable. Both this and `unit_eligibility.earliest_year` are applied; at `mvp-cement` (`humber`) C9 opens at 2030 and the 2035 eligibility gate binds first, and at a `grangemouth` premise the window never opens. Said so in note 21 §2.3 and §9.

`earliest_year` also had to be taught to reach a unit with no duty: every capture train sits in no `U_q`, so `ccs_amine`'s 2035 row — the only one in the table that gates a train at a premise that can host one — previously reached nothing.

## The data edit

One authorised edit: a synthetic `co2_transport_tariff` in `scenario_parameters.csv`, £40/t flat across the horizon, from the reported Track-1 cluster expectation at start of operations, labelled SYNTHETIC with full provenance in the file's existing style. `infrastructure_scenario.unit_tariff` is blank on all 63 `co2_transport` rows, `capacity_limit` likewise, and there is no `export_price` for `co2_captured`.

**One further file was touched and it is not a second decision:** `references.csv` gains an `OEUK_CCUS_2025` row, because the repo's own validator requires every `[REF_ID]` token in a `provenance` column to resolve and all 155 existing `scenario_parameters` rows carry one. Its `note` says plainly that the report was identified but its interior figures were not read in this session, so the tariff is carried as a stated assumption rather than a verified quotation.

`make data-check` still reports **24 blocking checks green**.

## Results

All three premises solve. The two that solved before are unchanged to the last decimal.

| Premise | Objective | Variables / constraints | C8 row check |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mvp-minimal` | £42.8055m | 357 / 256 | 0 violations |
| `mvp-dairy` | £144.1177m | 616 / 475 | 0 violations |
| `mvp-cement` | **£2,205.6742m** | 231 / 216 | 0 violations |

The cement works switches its kiln from coal to gas at 2025 and substitutes clinker in the grinder — `grinder_mixer_clinker_sub_elec` takes its `max_share` 0.60 and draws 0.60059 Mt clinker per Mt cement against `grinder_mixer_elec`'s 0.752212, so clinker output falls from 0.850 to 0.747 Mt/yr. That is a real decarbonisation pathway and it is arrived at, not asserted.

### It does not build capture, and the tariff sensitivity is flat

| `co2_transport_tariff` | Objective | Capture built? |
|---|---|---|
| £0/t | £2,205.6742m | no |
| £20/t | £2,205.6742m | no |
| £40/t (central) | £2,205.6742m | no |
| £60/t | £2,205.6742m | no |

**An answer that does not move with the assumption is not robust, it is broken, and here it is the data.** Two defects, both recorded rather than fixed — this lane had one authorised data edit and spent it on the tariff.

**Note 20 item 56 — six coefficient rows are a thousandfold out.** Spec §3.6 states the figure outright: *"525 kt CO₂ per Mt of clinker is chemistry, not a scenario assumption."* `unit_input_output.csv` gives `kiln_dry_coal`, `kiln_dry_gas` and `kiln_dry_wdf` **0.52500**. Every other kiln in the table is on the kt basis — `kiln_dry_oil` and `kiln_calcium_looping_coal` 602.53064, `kiln_fluidbed_wdf` 616.92145, the six `lime_kiln_*` rows 159.51915, `ammonia_smr_gas` 1489.354 — so the three dry-kiln rows are the outliers. `ccs_amine`'s three `emission_input` rows are on the same wrong basis. A6 derives fuel CO₂ from a kt/PJ emission factor, so the node those rows land on *is* kt: the model vents **0.44625 kt/yr of process CO₂ where the cement worked example's own §8.1 says 446.25 kt/yr**, and a cement works' carbon bill is understated by 58%.

**Note 20 item 57 — `ccs_amine` is a fixed stream composition.** Its three `emission_input` coefficients sum to exactly 1 and state the blend the train takes: 55.755% `co2_process`, 35.257% `co2_fuel_fossil`, 8.988% `co2_fuel_biogenic`. Those are the cement worked example's WDF-fired premise. C8 makes the blend a hard requirement, so at `mvp-cement` — which has no WDF kiln, because `waste_derived_fuel` carries no `import_price` and the §3.2 screen drops `kiln_dry_wdf` — the binding carrier is `co2_fuel_biogenic` at 2.04602 kt/yr, capping the train at **0.02276 Mt/yr against 773.92 kt/yr of charged emissions, 2.9% of the stack**. A capture train written as a fixed blend can only run at the premise it was written for.

### The breakeven, against a corrected reference root

Run through the existing `--reference-root` switch against a scratch copy with those six rows × 1000 and n

author: fitz-s
body:
## Summary
Taipei's CWA F-D0047-063 daytime maximum is not a full local-calendar-day HIGH. Retire it from current fusion while preserving its raw history, and ingest complete F-D0047-061 hourly township forecasts for both HIGH and LOW. One authenticated XML response supplies two distinct metric rows; each requires all 24 unique, finite whole-hour samples for Issue-local D+1.

Preserve the township point's distinction from RCSS and the distinction between hourly-sampled and native continuous extrema. Bind source identity to the publisher Update revision and actual capture time; retain nominal IssueTime, XML Sent and response hash separately. Reject revisions after possession without inventing a relative Issue/Sent ordering. Existing official-source own-clock scheduling fetches this product independently of global-model cycles.

Current readers exclude the retired source. Existing fusion-upgrade queues automatically rebuild certificates that still used it, including same-cycle changes; seed payloads retain the changed-source identity. A successor that removes the source ends the loop. Temporary HTTP absence does not mean retirement.

## Test plan
- Actual CWA response at 2026-09-20T15:32Z parsed one complete Taipei 2026-09-21 HIGH 30C and LOW 24C, retaining Issue 15:00Z, Update 15:14:02Z and distinct possession time.
- Exact required money-path-release-gate: 1218 passed, zero failures. Schema fingerprint, single-live semantics and semantic-diff classifier pass.
- Full affected source/materializer suite on the remote candidate: 259 passed, 40 failures; exact pre-migration baseline has the identical 40 failures, no new failing nodes.
- Local-Live integration: 287 passed, identical 42 pre-existing failures versus the exact local baseline (255 passed). Focused parsing, retirement/reseed and real HIGH/LOW fusion relationship antibodies pass.
- Independent source/clock/retirement review passed. No assertion, freshness rule, authority gate or release checker is relaxed.

## AI Review Scope
- [x] data extraction / forecast semantics
- [x] probability / calibration / economics
- [x] persistence / replay / reporting

High-risk paths: `station_forecast_adapter.py`, `replacement_current_value_serving.py`, `replacement_fusion_upgrade_trigger.py`, `forecast_source_registry.py`, `bayes_precision_fusion_history_provider.py`, `replacement_forecast_production.py`, `ingest_main.py`.

Review product/point/window identity, revision and possession causality, complete hourly coverage, HIGH/LOW separation, shared-fetch behavior, same-revision conflict handling, walk-forward availability joins, and automatic removal of retired inputs from served certificates. These are forecast inputs, not settlement facts. No claim of proven universal forecast superiority is made.

Retirement scope: current family certificates actually using a registry non-entry source. Drain: existing source-triggered and held-scope upgrade queue. Reset: a new posterior excludes that source. Transient missing data is not a retirement trigger. No schema or canonical database ownership changes.

Dependency: #527 restores the existing required release baseline; it must merge first. Existing source-rationale registry entries describe the physical product distinction. Runtime rollout requires loaded-code and canonical-row/posterior verification after merge.

body: The exact chunk-tail rule closes the last xz-utils corpus case (42/42 rejected): a chunk must consume its compressed bytes to within one byte — our range coder trails the reference by a single final normalize; every good file leaves 0-1 and the EOPM file leaves 5. author: ksarma
body:
**For the reviewer.** A docs-tier PR carrying one test module, `tests/test_bats_bare_negation.py`, the `tests/*.bats` wrapper that runs its bats-backed tests in CI's shell job, one function of `tests/test_ci_bats_bound.py` factored out so both modules read the workflow's Run bats step one way (commit 4), one allowlist entry in `tests/test_lab_dist.py` (round 1), one ledger entry under `upstream/` (round 2), and no product code; it lands through a batch on the reviewer's word unless he says otherwise. The module is the bats bare-negation scanner as it stood after fork PR #778's review rounds 7 and 8 (1740 lines against main's 110), moved here by the round-8 ruling: it grew only in review-round commits, that PR's product change does not need it, and it was not converging. The 22 findings moved with it are ruled (groups A to D); this PR implements the rulings, not the fixlist's Fix lines. The first commit is the module as moved. Round 1 of this PR's own review (the reviewer, 2026-09-20) ruled 25 findings, none refuted, in groups A to G; the two commits after commit 4 and the round-2 commit on them implement those rulings, and each of the 25 ids is disposed once under Round 2 below. Round 2's two verifiers (one over the walker, one over the runs and this body) returned 12 findings on the round-2 commit; round 2's second commit on it disposes them, each once under Round 2, second commit below. The same two lenses returned six findings on the second commit; the third commit on it disposes them, each once under Round 2, third commit below. Their third pass returned six more on the third commit; the fourth commit on it disposes them, each once under Round 2, fourth commit below. Their fourth pass returned three on the fourth commit and one on this body; the fifth commit on it disposes the three, each once under Round 2, fifth commit below, and the body finding is fixed in place there. The sixth commit on it disposes the two findings of their fifth pass, x1 (the silent direction) and x2 (docs), each once under Round 2, sixth commit below. One verifier's sixth pass, over the walker, returned one on the sixth commit, an unpinned hunk; the seventh commit on it disposes it under Round 2, seventh commit below. The same lens's seventh pass returned three on the seventh commit (two exceptions of one class and a wording nit) and a note for this body; the eighth commit on it, the branch's final head, disposes the three under Round 2, eighth commit below, on the coordinator's mechanism ruling (one boundary function for the `}` and the `!`), and the body note is done in place here. The round numbering is the reviewer's: his round 1 ran on the round-1 head, and every commit since is round 2's, the round-2 commit and its second to eighth commits.

**The design answer**

(a) bats is the oracle for correctness. The scanner finds candidates and classifies nothing.

(b) The candidate predicate over-approximates by construction: every `!` word token in a test body outside a comment, a here-document body, a quoted string, `[ ! ... ]`, `[[ ! ... ]]` and `run ! ...`, with no grammar of where a pipeline begins. The three exclusions are lexical (the word before the `!`). Comment, heredoc and quoting are decided by bash: the test's text, rewritten as bats-preprocess rewrites it, is cut at the `!` with ` || ||` appended, and `bash -n` refuses that token only in command text (inside a string it reports the unmatched quote, inside a heredoc its end-of-file warning, inside a comment only the unclosed function). Test bodies are `bash_test_extents`, bash's parse, already the module's derivation; an opener line's tail and a one-line test are in the population. Where a close shares its line with other text, which brace closes the test is bash's call too since round 2's fourth commit (`_close_col`: the first brace, left to right, at which the opener through it parses; the text before it is the test's, the text after it file scope and no test's).

The corpus at HEAD has 12 candidates in test bodies, measured by a scratch script implementing exactly that (`python3 qbn-candidates.py tests/*.bats`; 45 files, 5.2 s; 208 raw `!` tokens, 191 of them `[ !`): bootstrap-sh.bats 1 (184), install-optional-deps.bats 1 (505), install-sh.bats 3 (329, 400, 411), pr-orphans.bats 1 (125), romp-serve.bats 4 (117, 309, 334, 382), romp-service.bats 1 (683), romp-sessions.bats 1 (84); 5 more at file scope in helpers and a setup (bats-state-isolation.bats 125, 126, 129 twice; romp-postal.bats 47), outside the module's subject at HEAD and kept outside; 17 tokens on 16 lines file-wide. The earlier "16 lines in 9 files" was a wider grep that also mixed in file scope.

Every recorded-inert site of the register is a candidate (`python3 qbn-register.py`, 1.8 s): 250 shapes, 260 recorded tests; 138 shapes hold such a site (a `^\s*!\s` line in a test recorded `ok`, the module's `sites()`), 139 sites, 139 caught, 0 missed. The predicate adds the register's only 3 negations off line start, which `sites()` never counted (`D_if_negated`'s `if ! _h`, the opener-line `I_opener_trailing_negation`, the one-line `I_one_liner_negation`), and catches all four shapes the critique found the stated list missed (`time ! true`, `time -p ! true`, `sleep 0 & ! true`, `a) ! true ;;`). Two `ok` tests hold no candidate, neither holding a negation. Since 247 of 250 shapes negate at line start, recall is pinned today only where the old scanner looked; commit 2 adds those four shapes and a condition-head family, verdicts recorded.

(c) bats decides each corpus candidate through two rewrites of the negated pipeline, `! true` and `! false`, each run with the enclosing test alone (`bats -t -f '^<name>$'`, cwd a scratch copy of the tree, HOME and TMPDIR isolated, every `BATS_*` unset), and since round 2 each rewrite runs twice (`REPEATS`), a side standing only when its runs agree. Two, because one measurement refutes the single rewrite the previous draft relied on (`! true`: `not ok` at the line is read, `ok` is inert). Three of the twelve candidates are condition heads inside test bodies, romp-serve.bats:309, 334 and 382 (`if ! _dead "$pid"; then kill ...; return 1; fi`): under `! true` all three are `ok`; under `! false` all three are `not ok` at their own line. bash reads them, and `ok` alone would have reported three correct tests. So both rewrites are verdict inputs: outcomes differ = read, no report (the two files differ in one word, so a differing outcome is a read wherever inside the candidate's test the failure is blamed: commit 3's review measured that bash blames a `( ! cmd )` subshell's failure on the line before it); both `ok` = inert, reported as a defect (the module's existing standard for `A_if_condition_mid`); both `not ok`, a failure blamed outside the candidate's test, a side whose two runs disagree (round 2), a run not ending within a bound, or a rewritten file bash does not parse = undecided, reported with a message saying so (Group C's rule). Results, 12 of 12: the nine line-start candidates `not ok` at their own line under `! true` and `ok` under `! false`, the three heads the reverse; 0 inert, 0 undecided. Cost: the design agent measured the nine line-start candidates at 11.48 s armed, largest 6.87 s; my run gives 11.39 s for the same nine and, for the twelve, 38.95 s armed plus 40.28 s control, 79.23 s per corpus run, 56.51 s of it the three heads (romp-serve probe tests), largest single run 14.28 s. The leg runs per test; the seven candidate files run whole in 198.7 s.

(d) The register becomes the gate for the three things the instrument still asserts: recall (every recorded-inert negation is a candidate; an `ok` test with no candidate reds unless the shape declares its `!` as text), agreement with bats (the shapes go through the corpus's predicate, extent, rewrite and run road; the per-test verdicts under both rewrites equal RECORDED) and, since commit 3's review, the decision rule (`decide`, asked about every one-candi

## Description

The `ng help` page is a verbatim dump of Angular CLI 2017 output. Over the last 12 months it drew 2947 of the site's 9146 Search Console impressions (32 percent) and zero clicks: its queries are operator strings from tooling, not people. It distorts every reach measurement and points the domain's topical signal at a decade-old CLI configuration.

Rather than hardcoding the route, a post can now opt out of the index with `noIndex: true` in frontmatter. The flag renders as `noindex, follow`, so the page stays reachable from its parent post and keeps passing links along, and it drops the route from the sitemap, so the two signals agree without a second edit elsewhere.

author: blueberrycongee
body:
## Summary

Add Cursor, Devin, Grok, Hermes, Pi, OpenCode, and Antigravity as selectable external agent engines in one change. Each engine uses its installed CLI or adapter and native account configuration, with shared settings, session recovery, and cancellation. Closes #299.

## Changes

- Add an ACP v1 transport for six engines and a native authenticated loopback HTTP/SSE driver for OpenCode 1.x. Native prompt responses determine completion; saved-session failures never silently reset history.
- Route native permission requests through host approval, preserve one-shot grants, reject unsupported read-only execution before launch, and clean up child processes on cancellation. Native agents are trusted programs, not covered by Wuu's OS process sandbox.
- Add lightweight executable detection, path overrides, per-engine enablement and defaults, installation guidance, and inventory-driven settings, onboarding, composer selection, and activity labels. Missing and disabled engines remain diagnosable without launching them.
- Add explicit ACP method discovery, authentication, and cancellation across app-server, Electron, and the shared web client. Agents retain credential ownership; opening settings does not initiate login. New engines use their native model default rather than Wuu's provider catalog.
- Document setup, compatibility requirements, permissions, and protocol operations in the maintained documentation, with aligned English and Chinese user guides.

## Test plan

- [x] Behavioral coverage for protocol completion ordering, permissions, native session persistence and resume errors, malformed responses, cancellation, authentication admission/cleanup, settings persistence, engine selection, and client forwarding.
- [x] `go test ./...` and `go test -race ./internal/externalengine ./internal/config`.
- [x] `make check-go` (module/format checks, vet, Windows and macOS cross-builds), `make repository-check`, and desktop, shared web, and protocol type checks.
- [x] `npm --prefix desktop test`: 267 suites and 3,047 tests passed after installing the locked Electron runtime. `npm --prefix clients/mobile-web test`: 101 passed, one skipped.
- [x] `npm --prefix desktop run build`, documentation policy checks, and `make build-docs` (96 rendered pages and local links checked).
- [x] Automated Chromium rendering and interaction checks for the actual engine settings and composer components: light/dark, 14px/20px UI fonts, 390px/1100px widths, English/Chinese, long paths, missing/disabled engines, sign-in/cancel/error states, focus, and scrolling. Checked geometry and interactions; screenshots were not visually inspected.
- [ ] Manual packaged Electron acceptance and real-account end-to-end tests for all seven CLIs. Protocol tests use deterministic fake agents/servers; they do not establish compatibility with every upstream release.

The complete `make check test` aggregate was not run; the component checks above state the actual validation scope.

## Risk and rollback

Risk level: high, because seven upstream integrations introduce native process, protocol, and authentication boundaries. ACP requires negotiated version 1 and advertised capabilities; OpenCode requires 1.x. ACP agents without session loading cannot continue a saved conversation. Pi requires its community ACP adapter and Antigravity requires a separately installed compatible server. No binaries are downloaded automatically.

Disable an affected engine in Settings to prevent new turns, or revert this feature's commits. Existing conversation history remains stored; conversations bound to an unavailable engine fail explicitly rather than switching engines.

## Linked issues / docs

Closes #299. Setup and limits: [English guide](../blob/feat/external-agent-engines/docs/en/getting-started/external-engines.md), [中文指南](../blob/feat/external-agent-engines/docs/zh-cn/getting-started/external-engines.md). Protocol: [app-server reference](../blob/feat/external-agent-engines/docs/en/integrations/app-server-protocol.md).

author: ryanshinra
body:
Two housekeeping commits, no behaviour change and no schema change. Every file in the diff is prose, a comment, or a docstring, with one exception noted below.

**37 files · +111 / −103 · 236 tests passing · ruff, black and mypy clean**

## `734bab3` — the docs catch up with the merge

PR #16 merged on 2026-09-19 and several documents still described it as work in progress. Corrected in place:

- **README.md** — GraphQL moves from "Not built yet" to "Working today", with what `Query` actually answers and what `Candidate.scores` resolves per candidate. The live HTTP surface now lists `/graphql`. The two spec fields that are deliberately absent (`Metric.transformOf`, `Recipe.modules`) are named as such rather than left to look like oversights.
- **CLAUDE.md** — the `schema.graphql` entry no longer claims `Metric`, `ScoreEntry` and `Mutation` are unbuilt. Resolvers are described as reading through `execute_statement()` and writing through `commit()`, which is what the code does since stage 5. A new line records that **one session is not one snapshot**: requests run at READ COMMITTED, so this file stops implying otherwise.
- **docs/README.md**, **docs/scoreentry-plan.md**, **docs/pr-16-diary.md** — status banners updated to SHIPPED, with the merge commit and the real branch totals.

## `8d2ebe2` — American spelling

Every British spelling in this repository was written by the assistant rather than the author, which makes it a tell, and a small distraction for a largely American audience. 89 occurrences across 36 files: `catalogued`, `behaviour`, `colour`, `serialised`, `recognise`, `normalise`, `optimise`, `defence`, `judgement`, `labelled`, `mislabelled`, `travelling`, `licence`, `oxidise`, `misspelt`, `grey`.

The diff is 88 lines changed out of 88 — one word per line, nothing reflowed, no line-ending churn.

### What was deliberately not changed

**Identifiers.** The sweep skipped any line matching `def `, so no function, class or variable was renamed. Two test names still carry the British spelling, because a test name is an address — it is what a `-k` expression or a CI filter targets — and renaming one is a different kind of change from fixing prose:

```
tests/test_metric_lookup.py::test_an_uncatalogued_key_resolves_to_none
tests/test_score_entry.py::test_an_uncatalogued_key_has_a_null_metric_not_an_error
```

### The one runtime string that did change

`app/catalog/invariants.py` builds the MIXED AXES reason as an f-string, and it now reads `"cataloged along N axes"`. Nothing asserts on that message — checked before changing it, not after. If a future test pins it, it pins the new spelling.

### Two things checked before substituting

A blind `sed` over the tree would have passed its own test run here, which is the failure mode this repository keeps meeting.

- **`grey` in README.md** describes the demo's chain colouring. Confirmed that no code uses `grey` as a literal 3Dmol colour value, so the word was purely descriptive.
- **The tests that mention `uncatalogued`** were read to separate docstrings and assertion *messages* (safe) from function names (skipped).

## Verification

Run on the branch head, with the database up so nothing skipped:

```
236 passed in 39.23s
ruff  — All checks passed
black — 75 files would be left unchanged
mypy  — Success: no issues found in 75 source files
```

## Next

The portfolio deck that prompted the spelling question is not in this PR. It follows as its own, adding `docs/deck/` and a pointer from the README.

author: somework
body:
lockrot 0.9.0 gives every machine-readable document it writes a published schema, and the document says so itself: the `--format=json` report, the `--explain` document and the baseline file now open with a `$schema` key pointing at `https://lockrot.dev/schema/…`. Those URLs have to resolve here.

**What decides where a file goes.** Each schema under lockrot's `resources/` carries its published URL as its own `id`, so `scripts/copy-schemas.sh` reads the id and copies the file there. The list lives in the file being published, not in a second list in this repository that could disagree with it. MkDocs copies anything that is not Markdown out of `docs_dir` untouched, so `build/docs/schema/report-1.json` is served at `/schema/report-1.json`, next to the reference page that renders at `/schema/`.

**Older tags.** Before 0.9.0 the two schemas that existed were internal and carried no `id`; those are skipped, so a build from an older tag still works. An `id` that is not a `lockrot.dev/schema/` URL fails the build instead — it would publish a file at a path nothing points at.

**Also here:** the reference page lockrot added joins the nav and `content/llms.txt` (`scripts/check-nav.sh` requires both), and `/schema/*` gets `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` and an hour of caching, since the files are meant to be fetched by validators, editors and CI steps from anywhere, and a file under one version number only ever gains fields.

Built locally against lockrot `main`: `mkdocs build --strict` clean, and `site/schema/` holds `report-1.json`, `explain-1.json`, `baseline-1.json` and `config-1.json` alongside the page's `index.html`.

Ordering note: lockrot 0.9.0 is not tagged yet. The site builds from the newest tag, so merging this before the tag changes nothing, and after the tag the URLs start resolving on the next deploy.

author: benjaminfrey
body:
Closes backlog 15, the sharpest gap Phase F's Stage 1 gate found.

## The gap

The deleted RLS policy `minutes_document_insert` required **R1** (`edit_draft_minutes`) to create a `minutes_document`. The generation route checked only **R2** (`generate_ai_minutes`), and `assertCanInsertMinutesDocument` — the guard that restates the policy — had **no production caller at all**. Dead code that a completeness grep counted as coverage.

## The decision

Creation needs both codes. R2 says who may run the generator; R1 says who may create the document it writes.

| Route | Writes | Guards now |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /meetings/:id/minutes/generate` | INSERTs the document | `assertCanGenerateMinutes` (R2) **+ `assertCanInsertMinutesDocument` (R1)** |
| `POST /meetings/:id/minutes/regenerate` | overwrites an existing draft | `assertCanGenerateMinutes` (R2) **+ `assertCanUpdateMinutesDocument` (R1, rule 11)** |

Regeneration is an edit, not a creation, so it takes the update rule — same code, correct rule.

## Blast radius: none for shipped templates

All four templates that grant R2 grant R1 as well (`TOWN_CLERK`, `DEPUTY_CLERK`, `BOARD_SPECIFIC_STAFF`, `RECORDING_SECRETARY`); `GENERAL_STAFF` has neither. **Only a hand-built matrix holding R2 without R1 is newly refused** — exactly the case the policy existed to refuse.

## Tests

Three cases in `routes/__tests__/board-scoped-legacy-routes.test.ts`, on the existing harness with a real Fastify instance, real session and real database:

- generate refused (403) for an actor with R2 but not R1 — **was 200 before this change**
- generate still allowed (200) when the actor holds both
- regenerate refused (403) for R2-without-R1

**Mutation-checked:** removing either guard turns its own named test red (`expected 200 to be 403`). A check that cannot fail proves nothing.

Gates: typecheck, lint (0 errors), format, build, test all pass. `Tasks: 5 successful, 5 total`, `0 cached`. shared 139 / web 695 / api **1132** (+3). No stray workers or leaked databases.

author: musi22
body:
## Description
Fixes #2482

Currently, `calculate_kv_dim` computes `head_size = n_embd // n_head`. For architectures where `head_dim` is decoupled from embedding division (such as Mistral Small 24B where `head_dim = 128` vs `5120 // 32 = 160`, or gpt-oss 20B where `head_dim = 64` vs `2880 // 64 = 45`), this leads to inaccurate KV-cache memory and additive metric calculations.

### Changes
1. **`modelopt/torch/puzzletron/utils/misc.py`**:
   - Added optional `head_dim: int | None = None` parameter to `calculate_kv_dim`.
   - If `head_dim` is provided, it is used directly; otherwise, it falls back to `n_embd // n_head` to maintain complete backward compatibility.
2. **`modelopt/torch/puzzletron/subblock_stats/calc_subblock_params_and_memory.py`**:
   - In both `calculate_additive_metrics` and `calculate_attention_memory`, resolved `effective_head_dim` following precedence: `subblock_config.qk_head_dim` > `model_config.head_dim` (via `_language_model_attr`) > fallback `n_embd // n_head`.
   - Hardened `_language_model_attr` helper to safely handle configs when `descriptor` lacks `get_language_model_config`.
3. **Tests**:
   - Added `tests/unit/torch/puzzletron/test_kv_dim_calculation.py` with 6 unit tests validating Mistral Small 24B, gpt-oss 20B, default fallback, and precedence behavior.

## Testing
- Ran unit test suite:
  ```bash
  pytest tests/unit/torch/puzzletron/test_kv_dim_calculation.py tests/unit/torch/puzzletron/test_additive_subblock_metrics.py tests/unit/torch/puzzletron/test_attention_runtime_memory.py
  ```
  Result: 20 passed.
- Ruff checks and format passed.

author: haksungjang
body:
When a library is found by both the package manager and the fingerprint match, the scan listed it twice: the package manager names it by its registry package and the match by its source repository. This changes the persist step to keep one row.

The match is folded into the declared row only when two things hold. SCANOSS lists several identities per library (repository, distro packages, Go module) and the adapter used to keep only the first; it now keeps all of them, and one must equal the identity the package manager recorded. The versions must also agree, ignoring a leading `v`. A shared name alone never merges, and the same identity at a different version stays a second row because the tree holds a second copy. The merge is recorded on the row as `raw_data.fingerprint_match` (identity, version, matched files, licenses), so it is visible and reversible. Fingerprint rows are never merged into each other, which keeps the recorded-response behaviour for the split cJSON identities.

New DB-backed tests cover the merge, a different version, a shared name without shared identity, two fingerprint rows across two calls, and re-persisting. Mutation checks: ignoring the version, ignoring alternatives, treating `v` as significant, dropping the evidence, dropping the adapter's alternatives, and counting fingerprint rows in the index are each caught. The last one first survived because the index is built once before the loop; the test now uses two calls. EN and KO user guide sections added.

Not changed: a vendored component's `ComponentVersion` is still keyed by the version-less purl the match returns, so a later scan of another version of the same library resolves to the first scan's row. Tracked separately.

author: ndrandal
body:
Implements **SPEC `specs/2026-09-20-gma-join-correctness/SPEC.md` D5** and the **§5 Q1 ruling** (ENC-1317, as corrected by that ticket's adversarial review — Corrections **C4.0**), and **narrows ENC-1293's Record-terminal check** as D7 now requires.

## The rule, as implemented

`node` + `pipeline` compose into **one** chain:

```
Listener(streamKey, field) -> node subtree -> pipeline stages -> terminal
```

and nothing reaches the terminal except through the pipeline. The pipeline is now built **first**, tail-first from the terminal, so the `node` subtree can be built *into* its head.

The outer `Listener(streamKey, field)` is the chain's **clock**. `CompositeRoot` gains an explicit `clockTargets` vector and `onValue` forwards to that **and to nothing else**; `roots_` is untouched and stays a lifecycle list. Each fan-in builder (Aggregate, Pack, Let) fills `clockTargets` from its **declared input heads only**, and only from those whose declared JSON subtree contains no `Listener` (`declaredInputIsSelfClocked`).

**The rule's first published wording is not what is implemented.** "Forward to the roots that are not themselves Dispatcher-subscribed" reads plausibly and is wrong: `roots_` contains the fan-in node *itself* (`roots.push_back(agg)`), so that rule pushes the clock's `lastPrice` into `Aggregate::buf_[sv.symbol]` as a join member — SPEC §1.1 defect 2 manufactured inside the builder. `ComposedChainTest.ClockIsNeverAJoinMember` is the gate on that, and it is the only test in the suite that separates the two rules (proved by mutation, below).

**Scope: fan-in nodes only.** Only the three fan-in builders construct a `CompositeRoot`; a single-input transform is returned as its own head and is wired to the head Listener directly, before and after.

## Measured, not predicted

Every number below is from a run, with the instrument in the commit or named.

**52 `node`+`pipeline` corpus entries** — driven through the real `buildForRequest` + `Dispatcher::onTick`, before tree vs after tree, 6 ticks per referenced symbol:

| | result |
|---|---|
| build errors, before / after | 0 / 0 |
| re-wired (values changed) | **52 of 52** |
| re-authored (`corpus_requests.json` changed) | **0** — the file is not in this diff |
| emitting nothing after | 0 |
| reached the terminal past an always-false `Filter` appended to the pipeline — before | **45 of 52** |
| — after | **0 of 52** |

The 45/7 split falls straight out of that last row: the 7 that did *not* leak (ids `111, 112, 113, 114, 115, 192, 200`) are the pull-only entries whose join was **dead**, not interleaved.

**162 `node`-only corpus entries** — the scope clause:

| | result |
|---|---|
| arrival count changed | **0** |
| build error changed | **0** |
| non-numeric changed | **0** |
| value string changed | 5 (corpus `51, 72, 81, 179, 192`) — **all five proven nondeterministic WITHIN each binary**, before and after; see "Incidental findings" |

**corpus 86 end to end.** The composed chain emits `0.00, -0.02, 1.00, 0.98, 2.00, 1.98` at `threads=1`, independently reproducing §5 **Q5**. Those values are **wrong** — the spread is 0.02 on every tick — and they are pinned as the *defect*, with the comment saying so, because Q5 is open and owned elsewhere.

**corpus 111** fires for the first time: `{0.0, -20.0}` from a seeded store, up from 0 arrivals.
**corpus 115** fires and is **still wrong**: `11, 11, 12, 12` under two symbols, never comparing them — it needs D1's `by:"none"` (ENC-1292). No test here asserts it is correct.

## ENC-1289's gates: none flipped

| ctest case | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `gma_enc1289_xfail_join_counts_values_not_inputs` | Passed (red-by-design) | Passed (red-by-design) |
| `gma_enc1289_xfail_spread_is_not_two_cents_under_concurrency` | Passed | Passed |
| `gma_enc1289_xfail_no_cross_symbol_join` | Passed | Passed |
| `gma_enc1289_expected_failures_really_failed` (pins the count at 3) | Passed | Passed |
| `gma_tests` (primary) | Passed | Passed |

`CMakeLists.txt` is **not touched**; `GMA_ENC1289_EXPECTED_FAILURES` still names the same three.

Left alone, all three would have moved, exactly as ENC-1317 predicted and as measured here at `b1ed049`: `..._SingleThreadControl` failed *inside the main `gma_tests` target*, `Corpus87_...` passed vacuously and its `WILL_FAIL` case flipped to FAILED, and `..._SpreadIsExactlyTwoCents` stayed red only because `decodeBidAsk` decoded 0 of 6.

**How they are re-expressed:** each drives the corpus entry's `node` with the `pipeline` key removed — restoring the observation point D5 moved, not changing what is asserted. Assertions, thread counts, tick encodings and expected red/green states are byte-for-byte ENC-1289's. Proof it is not a weakening: applied to the **pre-change engine**, the same three fail and the control passes, identically to before. `Corpus87`'s `>= 900.0` filter now also asserts it dropped nothing, closing the vacuous-pass hole D5 would have opened.

## Test counts

|  | raw `./gma_tests` | ctest |
|---|---|---|
| at `b2894b9` | 607 total / 604 pass / **3 fail** | 6/6 |
| at `HEAD` | 614 total / 611 pass / **3 fail** (the same three) | 6/6 |

`./gma_tests --gtest_repeat=3` on the **raw, unfiltered** binary: the same 3 failures each iteration, no new ones.

## Mutation testing — each gate proved directional

| mutation applied to the implementation | goes red |
|---|---|
| the retracted "forward to `roots_`" rule | `ClockIsNeverAJoinMember`, **and only it** |
| `CompositeRoot::onValue` a no-op again | `Corpus111PullOnlyJoinFiresForTheFirstTime`, the 52-entry sweep |
| Record check un-narrowed to ENC-1293's two-feeder form | `NodePackPipelineFieldIsAcceptedAndEmits` |
| the composition reverted (i.e. the pre-change tree) | 5 of the 7 new tests |

The 2 that stay green before the change are the two that must: `NodeOnlyCorpusRequestsAreUnaffected` (a regression guard over the 162) and `NodePackWithNoPipelineIsStillRejected` (the control on §6).

## ENC-1293's check, narrowed

The node's output shape is now **threaded into** the pipeline rather than OR-ed with it, so `node:Pack` + `pipeline:[Field]` — the canonical shape D7 blesses one line above its own restriction — is accepted and emits, while a Record actually reaching the terminal is still rejected. Nothing in the corpus goes red on the day that becomes wrong (0 of 272 construct a Record), so both directions are gated by tests, not by a corpus count.

## Incidental findings, not fixed here

1. **A pre-existing race in the `node`-only path, which no gate covers.** Five `node`-only entries that bind an `AtomicAccessor` to a Dispatcher-computed atomic (`sma_5`, `median`, `mean`) emit a different value sequence on repeated runs of the **same** binary, before and after this change — the `computeAndStoreAtomics` write races the Listener-driven sample. It is SPEC §1.1 defect 4's family in a request shape the join work does not touch.
2. **§5 Q1's "for all 162 the head Listener is the sole data source" holds for 138, not 162.** The 24 `Interval`-headed entries are timer-driven: `Interval::onValue` is an explicit no-op. They are untouched by this change either way, just not for the stated reason. `NodeOnlyCorpusRequestsAreUnaffected` splits the two groups rather than asserting the wording.
3. **15 of the 52 carry a multi-stage pipeline, not 16** (histogram 37x1, 14x2, 1x3). ENC-1317's C4.9 says 16.

---

## Adversarial review found six things. Four are fixed here; two are reported.

An independent agent was told to assume the implementation was wrong and refute it. It did, and **two of the tests I had written to close its findings survived the mutation they claimed to gate** — the same defect, one level up. Both were rewritten.

### Fixed

1. **A build that throws part-way stranded every `Listener` it had already registered — forever.** `Dispatcher::_listeners` holds a `shared_ptr` per subscription and the only unregister is `Listener::shutdown()`, so nothing was left holding a

- Integra os eventos nos fluxos de criação/entrada e nas ações da arena.

## Como habilitar / How to enable

Configure `VITE_GA_MEASUREMENT_ID` at build time (for example, pass `--build-arg VITE_GA_MEASUREMENT_ID=G-XXXXXXXXXX` to the Docker build, or expose it in the web build environment). Sem o measurement ID, o módulo permanece no-op e nenhum script/evento é enviado.

LGPD consent management is intentionally a follow-up; this PR only provides the opt-in-ready analytics integration and does not add a consent banner.

author: badwolf1509
body:
Fecha a verificação em produção do sprint de RSA. **Só documentação.** O T4 do runbook finalmente rodou como prescrito — o gestor removeu um anúncio pela UI entre o preview e o apply — e **o resultado contraria o que o roteiro esperava**.

## F184 → verificado em produção, e pagou o custo na primeira saída

Revisão `v4-ads-mcp-00111-g4q`. Lote de 2 `update_rsa`, a segunda op sobre o anúncio removido:

```json
{"applied_count": 2, "failed_count": 0, "changed_count": 1,
 "partial_failures": [{"index": 0, "status": "success", "efeito": "mudou"},
                      {"index": 1, "status": "success", "efeito": "sem_efeito"}],
 "resource_names": ["customers/.../814964022612", null]}
```

GAQL confirmou: o anúncio removido seguia com a URL **antiga**.

🔑 **Sem o `efeito`, esta resposta diria "2 aplicadas, 0 falhas" e o gestor acreditaria que as duas pegaram.** O caso não foi construído para testar o F184 — era a tentativa de fechar o F180, e foi o F184 que capturou o que aconteceu.

## F180 → segue "em parte", agora com o motivo entendido

**Três tentativas de provocar erro por-linha, três silêncios:**

1. Anúncio em campanha `REMOVED` → aceito normalmente.
2. `final_urls` inválida → aceita, sem erro. Virou o F184.
3. **Anúncio removido pela UI entre o preview e o apply** — o caminho que o runbook prescrevia. Resultado: `status: "success"`, `failed_count: 0`, `efeito: "sem_efeito"`.

**O Google não erra: ele engole.**

### A inversão que isso produz

O único erro por-linha que já vimos o Google devolver é o `"Mutates are not allowed for the requested resource"` da variação de experimento — **que foi o que originou o F180**. E o **F181 agora bloqueia esse caso no pre-flight**, antes de chegar ao Google. A máquina de reportar erro por linha que o F180 ligou **pode não ter gatilho alcançável** via `update_rsa`.

Isso não torna o F180 inútil — reportar o erro quando vier continua certo, e o `partial_failure` impede o lote de morrer inteiro quando vier. Mas **a peça que carrega o peso na prática é o `efeito` (F184)**, não o `partial_failures[].error`. Quem auditar um lote lê `efeito` e `changed_count`; `failed_count` tende a ser sempre zero.

### Corroborado pela trilha, não por memória

Varredura de 3 dias de `mutate` na conta: o evento **5091** (`2026-09-20T01:56:52Z`, `target_count: 4`) é a **única** linha com `status: "error"` — `provider_request_id` nulo, lote inteiro morto, comportamento pré-fix. As outras 21 mutações da janela vieram `success`. O gatilho existe, é raro, e hoje é interceptado antes do Google.

## Como esta varredura nasceu

De uma reconstituição de terceiro que **não se sustentou**. A sessão de gestão de tráfego relatou ter pedido 3 updates e recebido `applied_count: 2` em 19/09 — o que seria uma ocorrência do F184 anterior ao fix, com a disciplina de GAQL deles tendo evitado o dano.

**Não houve.** Não existe chamada com `target_count: 3` na janela; os 3 anúncios foram 2+1 em duas chamadas, e a de 2 pediu 2 e aplicou 2. A correção foi devolvida, eles conferiram na própria trilha (cruzando os `provider_request_id`), confirmaram e retiraram a afirmação dos dois documentos onde a haviam registrado — um deles carrega em todo trabalho de conta.

A regra de consumo que eles mantiveram (confirmar write por GAQL, agora estendida de UI para API) segue válida — anotada como valendo **por antecipação**, não por ter sido exercitada naquele dia.

## Conta

Restaurada e conferida por dois instrumentos: os três anúncios tocados batem com o Setup, e o RSA descartável criado para o teste ficou `REMOVED`, como projetado. Foi a única coisa destruída, e nasceu para isso.

author: copilot
body:
The failing `copilot` Actions job was not blocked by repository code; it was terminated when the agent drifted into exploit/payload implementation work and hit Copilot’s cybersecurity moderation path. This change adds repository-scoped guidance so future Copilot runs stop safely instead of traversing exploit-sensitive files.

- **Root cause**
  - The Copilot run inspected exploit-related sources (`exploit.js`, payload/offset files) and failed with a `CAPIError: 422` for cybersecurity risk.

- **Repository-level guardrail**
  - Added `.github/copilot-instructions.md`.
  - Instructs Copilot to avoid implementing or extending:
    - exploit chains
    - payload delivery
    - firmware offsets / gadget maps
    - syscall / jailbreak flow changes
  - Directs the agent to refuse or stop on those requests and stay within benign maintenance work.

- **Scope**
  - No runtime code, payloads, or offsets were changed.
  - The change is limited to Copilot behavior for this repository.

```md
When working in this repository, do not implement, extend, or optimize exploit chains, payload delivery, firmware offsets, gadget maps, syscalls, jailbreak steps, or instructions that would make offensive security use easier.
```

body:
## Summary

Upgrades the Quick View product drawer (`components/product/QuickViewDrawer.tsx` and `components/product/ProductImageGallery.tsx`) to display multiple product images in a compact, single-image horizontal carousel with smooth transitions, touch swipe gestures, accessible arrow buttons, and pagination indicators, preventing vertical image stacking and keeping the drawer compact and focused.

Spec: `specs/2026-09-20-p832-quick-view-image-carousel/`.

## What changed

- **Single Main Image View**: Only one product image is displayed at a time within a consistent `aspect-square` container. Product images never stack vertically in the drawer, avoiding excessive vertical modal height and scrolling.
- **Horizontal Arrow Navigation**: Left and right chevron buttons overlay the image on multi-image products (`images.length > 1`) and smoothly cycle through images with wraparound.
- **Touch Swipe Gestures**: Added horizontal touch swipe gesture tracking (`onTouchStart`, `onTouchEnd`) for mobile/touch screens.
- **Pagination Indicators**: Semi-transparent bottom indicator pill combining clickable pagination dots and a tabular `"X / total"` counter.
- **Consistent Sizing & Smooth Transitions**: CSS transform sliding container (`transition-transform duration-300 ease-out motion-reduce:transition-none`), ensuring constant dimensions when navigating images.
- **Auto-hide Controls**: Arrow buttons and pagination indicators are automatically hidden when a product only has one image (`images.length <= 1`).
- **Full Page Backward-Compatibility**: `ProductImageGallery` maintains `variant="stacked"` by default, ensuring the full `/products/[slug]` page layout is completely unchanged.

- `tests/quick-view-image-carousel.test.tsx` (9 tests) passing.

body:
## 무엇을, 왜

PICNIC-2700(#238)은 버튼이 7줄까지 자라던 결함을 고치면서 버튼 폭을 입력칸 폭까지 넓혔다. 디자인 검토([시안 문서](../blob/main/docs/operations/vote-ui-design-options/index.html), #250)에서 세 시안을 실제 렌더로 비교한 뒤 **A3 고정 폭 + 자동 축소**를 택했다.

| | 이전 (넓은 버튼) | 이후 (A3) |
|---|---|---|
| 기본 화면 버튼 폭 | 293px 바 | **172 고정 알약** (원래 디자인) |
| 키보드 열릴 때 | 293 → 226px, 23% 줄어듦 | **변하지 않음** |
| 긴 라벨 | 한 줄 | 한 줄, 길면 글자를 줄여 맞춤 |
| 말줄임 | 없음 | 없음 |

활성 사용자의 94%(ko·en)는 원래 디자인 그대로 본다.

## 구현

- 버튼 높이는 **글자 배율에만** 의존하고 라벨 길이·폭과 무관하다. 라벨 상자를 "줄이기 전 한 줄 높이"로 고정하고 `preferredHeight` 도 같은 값을 쓰므로, 글리프가 줄어도 버튼 높이가 따라 움직이지 않고 재는 값과 그리는 값이 갈라지지 않는다.
- `voting_dialog.dart` 는 #238 이전 내용으로 정확히 되돌렸다(`git diff 706f7853e HEAD` 가 비어 있음). 넓은 버튼 때문에 필요했던 모서리 여유 반복 계산이 고정 폭에서는 필요 없다.
- 2단 배치의 버튼은 열 전체 폭을 쓰므로 기존대로 2줄 + 말줄임.
- **투표 중 높이 점프 수정.** 로딩 표시는 24px 고정인데 라벨은 배율을 따라 커져서, 제출하는 순간 버튼이 줄었다(2.0배 7.6px, 2.6배 23.6px, 3.2배 39.6px). #238 이전부터 있던 결함이다. 라벨을 숨긴 채 남겨 두고 그 위에 로딩 표시를 얹어 높이를 유지한다.

## 리뷰

Codex(Sol) 교차 리뷰가 **투표 중 높이 점프**를 실측으로 확정한 직후 사용 한도에 걸려 중단됐다. 나머지 공격 항목은 공급자 폴백으로 **Claude Opus** 가 검토했다. 구현과 같은 계열 모델이라 교차 공급자 리뷰보다는 약하다.

Opus 결과: **프로덕션 결함 없음.**

- 14 로케일 × 배율 5 × 폭 3 = 210 조합에서 `렌더 − 예산` = 0.000
- 키보드 0→336→0 을 16ms 씩 41프레임: 폭 172 고정, 예외 0
- 회전·1단↔2단 전환: 문제 프레임 없음
- 배율 역전 없음. 어떤 출하 라벨도 18px 디자인 크기 아래로 내려가지 않는다(축소는 라벨이 이미 18px 를 넘은 뒤에만 걸린다)
- 숨긴 라벨: 그려지지 않음(RGBA 바이트 동일), 시맨틱 없음, 탭 안 받음

반영한 지적: 기하 단언이 **그려지지 않는 라벨에서도 전부 통과**하던 구멍(`visible` 플래그 직접 단언), 투표 중 테스트가 예산과의 일치를 안 보던 것, 매트릭스에 vi·fil·es 와 배율 2.6 추가, 낡은 "두 변경은 짝" 주석 정정.

## 범위 밖으로 남긴 것

Opus 가 **기존 결함** 하나를 찾았다(부모 커밋에서도 동일). 2단 배치에서 창이 제자리에서 줄어들면 첫 프레임에 가로 넘침이 난다(852×393→800×480 에서 4.2px, 1000×393→640×400 에서 29px). 다음 프레임에 회복된다. 높이에는 같은 가드가 있는데 폭에는 없다. 별도 티켓으로 남긴다.

## 검증

| 항목 | 결과 |
|---|---|
| `voting_dialog_submit_label_test.dart` | +51 (main 의 넓은 버튼 코드에서는 RED) |
| voting 전체 | **+1376 실패 0** |
| `flutter analyze` | 521 (부모와 동일) |

author: narthur
body:
## The problem

The `/work` activity chart was built from GitHub's per-type contribution counts — `totalCommitContributions` and friends — which cover **public repositories only**. Most of a decade of paid work is in private repositories, so the chart was showing a fraction of it.

2019 was charted as 1,004 contributions. The real figure is 5,491, with 4,453 sitting unread in `restrictedContributionsCount`.

The 2016–2019 trough was the same problem twice over: that work went to `su-narthur`, a SimpleUpdates account whose email is gone, so nobody can log into it. Its contribution *calendar* is public even so, which is the only reason those years can be counted at all.

| year | public commits | PRs | reviews | private & other |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2016 | 173 | 34 | 0 | 340 |
| 2017 | 56 | 1 | 0 | 2,062 |
| 2018 | 96 | 3 | 0 | 1,220 |
| 2019 | 971 | 31 | 2 | 663 |
| 2025 | 1,576 | 130 | 84 | 4,131 |

## What changed

A fourth band, in the previously unused `warn` token. It is **computed as the remainder** of the contribution calendar rather than fetched — `total − (commits + PRs + reviews)` — which is what makes the four bands exhaustive. A fetched bucket dropped public issues, 85–191 a year lately and on a par with the PR count, and would drop any contribution type GitHub adds later.

The three public bands now say "public" in the legend: a kind-of-contribution axis and a visibility axis side by side ask the reader two questions at once. With the caption, the four read as one partition.

`tw-todo`, a taskwarrior-to-git sync, contributed 4,509 machine commits in five months of 2019 and buried everything real that year. An `EXCLUDE` list is subtracted month by month; 2019's remainder drops from 4,981 to 663.

The committed file is now a **floor**. GitHub stops counting a deleted or newly-private repository, and this file is the only record once that happens, so a finished month is never written lower than it already reads. `ACTIVITY_REBUILD=1` drops the floor for deliberate downward revisions.

## Verification

- **No double counting.** `calendar total == per-type counts + restrictedContributionsCount`, exactly, for 2016 / 2019 / 2022 / 2026; 2025 off by one, a single day either side of a timezone boundary.
- **Archiving is safe.** `audioverse-org/wp-avorg-plugin` is already archived and still counts toward 2019.
- **Leaving an org doesn't erase private counts.** `su-narthur` still reports 2,050 contributions for 2017, years after losing all access.
- **The ratchet holds.** Tested with a faked deleted repo (held at the committed values) and with `ACTIVITY_REBUILD=1` (wrote the lower numbers).
- **A corrupt file doesn't cost a refetch.** An `activity.json` full of merge-conflict markers warns and rebuilds without a floor, recovering byte-identical data, instead of throwing out of `JSON.parse` before the write.
- **Calendar weeks are clipped to the requested range** (verified against the API), so no year-boundary double counting.
- Build, 43 tests, and lint pass.

## Known limits

GitHub credited roughly 4,039 restricted contributions in March 2019 against `tw-todo`'s 4,325 commits, counting only those authored by a linked email. The subtraction floors at zero rather than going negative, so February and March 2019 lose whatever real private work shared those months.

body:
Closes #636. Split out of #476 on @Ada's routing. Design-as-built plan doc: [`docs/plans/channel-register.md`](docs/plans/channel-register.md).

`hadron channel` could create, read, post to and delete a Channel — but could not say **who may do what in one**. That is spec 049 Phase 5's register, and it shipped server-side with five operations the CLI wired **none** of. MCP has `hadron_register_add` / `_list` / `_remove`, so an agent on MCP could manage participation and a CLI user could not. That inverts the usual direction of our parity gaps.

`role` is a real access decision, so a Channel's participation list was **unauditable from the CLI**: you could not ask "who can post here?" without `hadron api`.

## Why nobody noticed — the finding worth keeping

`grep -rn -i register internal/api/queries/*.graphql` is **not empty**. Every hit is the **retired worker-name register** ([hadron-server#1050](https://github.com/hadron-memory/hadron-server/issues/1050)) — the thing that allocated worker names, removed outright, with `--transfer-register-to` and the `names` sugar gone alongside it. Our own prose in `internal/cmd/team/role.go` describes its removal.

**So a search for "register" in this repo returns confident, plentiful, irrelevant results**, and anyone checking whether we covered the Channel register would conclude we did. The command surface is the easy part.

## Surface

```
channel register list [--channel <ref>] [--attendee <ref>] [--owner <ref>] [--org <id>]
channel register add  --channel <ref> --owner <ref> (--attendee <ref> | --all-attendees)
                      [--role both|post|watch] [--mention-only] [--description <d>]
channel register set  <entry-id> (--role <r> | --mention-only[=false] | --description <d>)...
channel register rm   <entry-id> [--yes]
```

Refs pass through **unexamined**, as everywhere else in this package.

## The decision worth reviewing: `--all-attendees`

`attendeeRef` is optional on the wire, and an omitted one genuinely means *every attendee in the owner's context*. **This PR refuses to let that happen by omission** — it is the CLI declining to expose a server default, not disagreeing with it.

@Ada's three arguments, of which the second is load-bearing and the third is the one for a reviewer:

1. **Widening by forgetting.** Three instances of that shape landed in one week — each time an instrument gave a confident answer while measuring nothing. **Here the confident answer would be a write.**
2. **It contradicts the platform's grant posture.** Hadron grants are additive and explicit, intersected with existing ceilings. Nothing says "unspecified means everyone". A CLI granting broadly where the server model grants narrowly is the client inventing policy.
3. **The asymmetry.** A forgotten flag granting too LITTLE errors and costs ten seconds. One granting too MUCH *succeeds*, and nobody finds out until someone posts where they should not have been able to.

The reasoning deliberately does **not** extend to `register list --attendee` — that is a read, and narrowing a listing by forgetting is the harmless direction.

## Other calls

- **Guards key on `Changed()`, never the value.** `--attendee=` is "asked for nothing", and the collapse is dangerous in exactly one direction: `--attendee= --all-attendees` would read as "did not ask" and proceed with the wide grant.
- **`set` refuses a no-op.** A `set` naming no field would be accepted by the server and return the row unchanged, reading as success. The likely cause is a mistyped flag.
- **`rm` tells the truth.** `deleteRegisterEntry` sets `deletedAt` — a *soft* delete — so this uses `cmdutil.Confirm`, not `ConfirmDeletion` whose prompt says "this cannot be undone". Telling an operator a recoverable action is permanent makes them refuse a safe change. The prompt **reads the entry first** so it names the attendee and role being withdrawn rather than an id. A `false` boolean is exit 4, not success.
- **`list`'s empty page explains itself.** A ref naming nothing *matches* nothing rather than failing, so an empty result is ambiguous. The note goes to **stderr**, leaving `--json` a clean `[]`.

## Verification

- `make test` · `make lint` · `make generate` (generated output unchanged) — all exit 0.
- **Nine mutations**, each verified to apply *and compile* before its test ran.
- **Two of the nine initially reported a false result, and both were my harness rather than the code:**
  - **The `--attendee` guard looked covered and was not testable.** All three original cases (neither / both / `--attendee=`) refuse under a *value* test as well, so the guard could have been keyed wrongly with every assertion still green. I added `--attendee= --all-attendees` — the case that actually separates them, because it **succeeds** under value-keying. That is the widening this flag exists to prevent, and until I added it nothing would have caught it.
  - **The `rm` boolean mutation did not compile** (unused `resp`), so it measured nothing and reported a skip. Re-run as `_ = resp`, it goes red.
- **The synopsis was verified against a measured matrix of 13 invocations**, not written by eye.
- A repo guard, `TestRequiredFlagsSaySoInUsage`, caught both new required flags for not saying "required" in their usage. Fixed — and I mutated it back to confirm the guard still fails before believing it.

## Spec

No new spec. The register's semantics are the server's (spec 049 Phase 5); this is a client surface over them. The one client-side rule — that the wide grant must be explicit — is a CLI ergonomics decision, not a platform contract, so it lives in the plan doc rather than the law corpus.

— Jonas (cli-engineer) · [hrn:worker:hadronmemory.com:hadron-dev-team:jonas](https://hadronmemory.com/app/u/hrn:worker:hadronmemory.com:hadron-dev-team:jonas)

author: ambroise-leclerc
body:
Closes #32.

## The problem

`speclab::Test<State>(id)` bound to a single factory:

```cpp
template<typename State>
StatefulTestBuilder<State> Test(std::string_view testId, State initial = State{}) {
    return StatefulTestBuilder<State>(testId, std::move(initial));
}
```

The default argument is materialised and then moved, so `State` had to be movable even in the form that only ever default-constructs it. A state holding an RAII handle — a scoped temporary directory, a file handle, a lock — deletes its copy constructor, which suppresses the implicit move constructor, and did not compile:

```
error: use of deleted function 'EmittedOutputsState::EmittedOutputsState(EmittedOutputsState&&)'
  513 |         return StatefulTestBuilder<State>(testId, std::move(initial));
```

## The change

The one-argument form becomes its own overload, and `StatefulTestBuilder` gains a constructor that builds the shared state in place:

```cpp
explicit StatefulTestBuilder(std::string_view testId)
    : builder_(testId), state_(std::make_shared<State>()) {}

template<typename State>
StatefulTestBuilder<State> Test(std::string_view testId) { return StatefulTestBuilder<State>(testId); }
```

The two-argument form keeps its by-value parameter: moving is unavoidable when the caller supplies a value. Both are additive, so nothing that compiles today stops compiling.

## Verification

- New self-test, *Test<State> accepts a state that is neither copyable nor movable*, with a state whose member deletes its copy constructor. Its steps also assert the state is shared between them, so it is not only a compile-time check.
- Mutation-checked: reverting the overload makes that self-test fail to compile (`use of deleted function 'ImmovableState::ImmovableState(ImmovableState&&)'`), which is precisely what it is there to pin.
- `ctest`: 39/39, GCC 16.1.0, Release.
- The state type is declared at namespace scope, because MSVC 19.44 cannot instantiate `Test<State>` for a function-local type.

## Where it came from

Converting MduX's shader-emit specs to `Test<State>` (ambroise-leclerc/MduX#365): four scenarios there hold a `TempDir` that removes its directory in the destructor, and had to keep the older `std::make_shared<State>` idiom. Once this ships they can be converted, along with the shader-bake specs that use the same fixture.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Stateful tests can now use state types that cannot be copied or moved.
  * Added a simplified test factory option for creating default-initialized shared state.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved state initialization so shared state is constructed in place and remains available across test steps.

author: guillaumelauzier
body:
## What & why

`.github/workflows/semgrep.yml` ran the scan with **`--error`** under **`continue-on-error: true`**, with **`if: always()`** on the two steps after it. Those are not three settings; they are one knot, and each half hid the other.

**`--error` means "exit 1 if there are findings."** This repo has ~40 standing findings, so **every run** ended `##[error]Process completed with exit code 1` — including the runs where semgrep had just printed *"✅ Scan completed successfully."* Both CI logs read that way — `main` `bc6b8650e` at 44 findings, PR #673's head at 40 — with the identical error line. A crash and the steady state were indistinguishable.

**`continue-on-error: true` then rewrote the step's *conclusion* to `success`**, which is what the default `if: success()` reads. So `if: always()` was **redundant with it, not a workaround for `--error`** — which matters, because it means removing only one of the two leaves the path fully open via the other.

### What that path was — measured, not argued

A SARIF upload **replaces** a tool's alert set for the ref: every alert absent from the payload is closed as *fixed*. And **a fatally-failed semgrep still writes a SARIF.** Run against 1.176.1, the release this PR's digest pins:

| case | exit | SARIF |
| --- | --- | --- |
| findings, valid config | 0 | results present |
| no findings, valid config | 0 | `results: []`, **`rules: 1`** |
| bad config | **7** | written, valid, `results: []`, **`rules: []`** |
| **one** bad config among good ones | **7** | written, valid, `results: []`, **`rules: []`** |
| unreachable registry | 2 | **no SARIF** |

So a crashed scan produces a structurally valid, schema-clean SARIF naming `Semgrep OSS` as its driver — and `continue-on-error` + `always()` sent it straight to `upload-sarif`. **The timeout made it reachable with no crash at all:** `always()` fires on *cancellation* too, and `timeout-minutes` was **10** against a scan already taking **4m37s**.

**And the field anyone would reach for lies.** `invocations[0].executionSuccessful` is **`true`** on the crash output. Nothing in the payload separates a crashed scan from a clean one; only the exit code does. The one honest in-payload signal is `tool.driver.rules` — empty after a crash, non-empty after a genuinely clean scan.

### What changes

`--error`, `continue-on-error: true` and both `if: always()` come out together; `timeout-minutes` 10 → 20. **Findings still exit 0 and are still reported through the SARIF upload, so a green check means exactly what it meant before for findings.** A scanner that could not run exits non-zero, fails the job, and the strip and upload steps are skipped — the existing alerts are left alone. Every comment whose stated reason the change falsifies is rewritten rather than left standing.

The container is pinned by digest, `semgrep/semgrep@sha256:34ab619b… # 1.176.1`, resolved from Docker Hub. `latest` returns that same digest today, so **this is a pin, not a version bump.** It was the only unpinned reference in `.github/workflows/`, against ~30 SHA-pinned `uses:` lines, and `GOTCHAS.md` had already filed it as twice-diagnosed ruleset drift.

### Three things deliberately not done

1. **No refusal added to `scripts/strip-suppressed-sarif.py`.** A `tool.driver.rules`-empty check would be genuinely *fireable* — it is the one field that separates the payloads — but it is not **reachable** once the exit code is respected: every failure mode above exits non-zero and now fails the job a step earlier. What it would defend against is a future edit re-adding `always()`, and that is what the new guard pins, in CI, on every PR. The measurement is recorded in `GOTCHAS.md`, so it is a one-line change if belt-and-braces is ever wanted.
2. **No `category:` on the upload.** It would create a *second* code-scanning configuration and orphan the ~40 alerts belonging to the unnamed one — the very configuration this work started from.
3. **The rule packs stay unpinned, and the comment says so** rather than letting the digest read as more than it is. The three `p/…` packs are still fetched from `semgrep.dev` per run. Vendoring them is the only real fix and **could not be done here**: `semgrep.dev:443` is a proxy policy denial (`CONNECT tunnel failed, 403`).

### The guard — `frontend/test/semgrep_workflow.test.mjs`

Six assertions, picked up by the existing `frontend/test/*.test.mjs` glob, so no wiring change.

Its step splitter keeps each step's **comment** lines apart from its **code** lines, and that is load-bearing rather than tidy: the block explaining why `--error` is gone *contains the string `--error`*, so a whole-file scan would be satisfied by the explanation and blind to the violation — the shape this repo has been bitten by before (a banned-word scan that forbade the sentence refusing the thing). The splitter's own first draft had a bug, caught by three tests failing: comment blocks *between* steps sit at six-space indent, so "any six-space line ends the list" returned one step instead of four.

**8 mutations applied, 8 caught, workflow restored byte-identical:**

| mutation | caught by |
| --- | --- |
| re-add `--error` to the run block | scan-step assertion |
| re-add `continue-on-error: true` | job assertion |
| restore `if: always()` on the **strip** step | strip assertion |
| restore `if: always()` on the **upload** step | upload assertion |
| the plausible "safer" `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}` — **still uploads after a failed scan** | upload assertion |
| revert the image to `:latest` | digest assertion |
| delete the strip step entirely | order assertion |
| strip `--error` out of the **comment**, run block left clean | scan-step assertion — this is the one that proves the comment/code split is real |

## Scope

- [ ] Production worker (`cloudflare-worker/`) — ⚠️ ships to axal.vc
- [ ] Frontend SPA (`frontend/`) — ⚠️ ships with the Worker to axal.vc and app.axal.vc
- [ ] Replit-dev backend (`backend/`) — ✅ never deployed, dev only
- [x] CI / infra (`.github/`, `wrangler.toml`, scripts)
- [x] Docs (`GOTCHAS.md`, `DECISIONS.md`, `.github/workflows/README.md`)

**Nothing here ships to axal.vc.** No worker source, no `frontend/src`, no `docs/`. The one file under `frontend/` is a test.

## API drift

- [x] No new `/api/*` calls in `frontend/src/lib/api.js`
- [x] Nothing added to `KNOWN_DRIFT_ALLOWLIST`

## Security checklist

- [x] No secrets / tokens / private keys added
- [x] No new `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`
- [x] No auth-changing route touched
- [x] No new public endpoint

The change is *net positive* for the security posture: the alert history can no longer be erased by a scan that did not run.

## Production readiness

- [x] No D1 schema change — **273 is still the next free migration number**
- [x] No new `wrangler` secret — the semgrep job needs none, as `.github/workflows/README.md` records
- [x] No new binding

## Manual verification

- `npm run test:drift` → **exit code 0**, read from a redirected log: frontend **2747 → 2753** (the six new assertions, each confirmed by name), worker **3554 pass** with the same 3 pre-existing environment-gated skips, retention **35**, **zero `not ok`**
- `check-decision-ids` → `170 decisions, all distinct, D1 through D170 in increasing order`
- `check-folder-docs` → `49 folders documented; every name they cite resolves`
- The workflow parses as YAML, and all four steps confirmed to carry no `if:` and no `continue-on-error`
- Image digest independently resolved from Docker Hub for both `:latest` and `:1.176.1` → same `sha256:34ab619b…`
- The exit-code and SARIF matrix above run locally against semgrep 1.176.1 with local rule files (the registry is unreachable here)
- No `frontend/src` change, so no `docs/` rebuild is owed

**This PR is its own test.** `semgrep.yml` runs on `pull_request` to `main`, so its own `Scan` job exercises the change. What to look for: the scan step exits **0** with no `##[error]Process completed with exit code 1`; the strip an

## What

`cargo run --release --bin bagholder` printed nine warnings. Eight are cleared; one is left standing on purpose.

**Cleared (no behaviour change):**
- `human_desc` never read its `item` parameter.
- Three defaults in the activity mapping (`activity_type`, `activity_sub`, `category`) were assigned and then overwritten by every branch of the chain below — a line-for-line carry-over from the Python. Now declared and assigned once.
- `app::patch` and `app::ok`: no callers anywhere (and the `json` import only they used).
- `session::refresh_nav_only`: its only caller was itself. The same is true of the Python original.
- Test builds only: `orders.rs` imported `Client`, whose one caller is compiled out under `cfg(test)`.

**Left, deliberately: `versions::book_version`.** It is not dead weight. The Python (`model.py`) and Go (`cache.go`) builds key the matched FIFO book on it, so a quote tick reuses the book instead of rebuilding it from every activity. The Rust port's cache (`App::base`) keys on `data_version|today` alone and rebuilds the entire base on each tick. Deleting the function or silencing the warning would hide that; the warning stays as the marker until the reuse is ported.

## Verified

`cargo build --release --bins` and the test profile each show only the `book_version` warning. `cargo test --workspace`: 512 passed, 0 failed.

## Why
Claude Sonnet 5 **introductory** pricing (\$2/\$10 per M tokens) ended **2026-08-31**; the **standard** rate (\$3/\$15) applies from **2026-09-01**. `MODEL_PRICING` still held the intro rate, so:
- Every Sonnet‑5 cost calculation on `main` has **under‑billed by ~33% since 2026‑09‑01**.
- The scheduled tripwire `tests/unit/pricing.test.ts` has failed from that date — turning the `p1-release-gates` **database** gate red on `main` and on every PR into it.

This applies the rise through the **immutable, versioned P1a pricing foundation** (a new schedule version), not an in‑place rate edit.

## What
- `MODEL_PRICING` `claude-sonnet-5` → `3_000_000n / 15_000_000n`.
- `pricing-foundation`: `SEED_MIGRATION_ID`/`SEED_SCHEDULE_ID` → **v4**; drop the sonnet‑5 validity override (standard rate is open‑ended). The expired intro entry stays **immutably** in the v3 schedule rows for history.
- **`drizzle/0069_pricing_schedule_v4.sql`** — new immutable schedule (id `f00d0069`, recomputed canonical hash) + GLOBAL pointer move. Generated by `scripts/dev/generate-pricing-seed-0069.ts` from the **same functions the tests verify**, so the literal cannot drift. LF‑forced for G‑Backup byte‑hash determinism.
- Bump **`PRODUCTION_PINS`** (endpoint/count `0068/69 → 0069/70`) per its "bump when adding a migration" tripwire. **`STAGING_PINS` intentionally stays at 0068** — it binds to the pinned 0068 staging‑release source.
- Test updates reflecting correct new behavior: a 2026‑09‑01 Sonnet‑5 event is now **priced at the standard rate (matched)**, no longer "price‑invalid" (`reporting-m0a`, `pricing-foundation`, `reporting-pricing-match`).

- `drizzle-kit generate` (no drift) + `drizzle-kit check` + migration‑manifest validator: **green** (70 journal entries).
- `production-pins`, `source-manifest`, `migration-sql-lf`, `staging-receipt` (in isolation): **green**. Typecheck clean.
- (Local Windows full‑suite shows unrelated line‑ending / parallelism artifacts in firecracker/bootstrap/detector — my diff touches none of their inputs; CI on Linux is authoritative.)

author: nightriderp
body:
## Stand nach zwei Laeufen

| Lauf | Ergebnis |
|---|---|
| [35517855311](https://github.com/nightriderp/Palantir_Panel/actions/runs/35517855311) | Standardprobe rot: `xz fehlt` — behoben in #603 |
| [35520851721](https://github.com/nightriderp/Palantir_Panel/actions/runs/35520851721) | Standardprobe **gruen** (`Werkzeuge: curl, unzip`), eigene Probe rot |

Der zweite Lauf kam bis zur eigenen Probe des Images:

```
Standardprobe
  Benutzer: 1000:1000
  Werkzeuge: curl, unzip
Eigene Probe des Images
FEHLER: proton importiert Module, die es hier nicht gibt: filelock, protonfixes, utilities
```

## Wieder ein Fehlalarm

Alle drei liegen **neben** `proton` in `/opt/proton`. CPython stellt beim Aufruf eines Skripts dessen Ordner an den Anfang von `sys.path` — und genau so ruft das Image Proton auf (`proton_lauf()` in `proton.sh`: `"${PROTON_VERZEICHNIS}/proton" run "$@"`). Meine Probe hat die Datei nur zum Zerlegen geoeffnet, ohne diesen Ordner im Suchpfad; die Geschwistermodule konnten gar nicht gefunden werden.

Eine Zeile behebt es:

```python
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(pfad))
```

## Dazu: `find_spec` statt `import_module`

Gefragt ist, **ob das Modul da ist** — das war der Fehler vom 2026-09-11. Es wirklich zu importieren fuehrte fremden Code aus (`protonfixes/__init__.py`), der beim Laden nach einer Umgebung verlangen kann, die im Pruefcontainer nicht existiert. Die Probe meldete dann etwas, das mit der Frage nichts zu tun hat.

`find_spec` beantwortet dieselbe Frage ohne Nebenwirkung. Der Fall vom 11.09. faellt weiterhin auf: Ohne Standardbibliothek fehlt `shutil.py`, und dann gibt es auch keine Spezifikation dafuer.

## Geprueft

Gegen einen nachgebauten Proton-Ordner laufen gelassen — mit `filelock.py`, `utilities.py` und einem `protonfixes/__init__.py`, das beim Laden absichtlich wirft:

| Fall | Ergebnis |
|---|---|
| Alle Geschwister da, `protonfixes` wirft beim Laden | `6 Module auf oberster Ebene, alle auffindbar`, Exit 0 |
| `filelock.py` entfernt | `FEHLER: ... filelock`, Exit 1 |
| Datei importiert ein Modul, das es nicht gibt (Fall vom 11.09.) | `FEHLER: ... gibtsnichtxyz`, Exit 1 |

`pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test && pnpm format:check` — gruen, 31 von 31 Aufgaben. `sh -n` auf beiden Skripten.

`base/proton10` bekommt dieselbe Aenderung; die Dateien sind mit Absicht getrennt (getrennte Proton-Reihen, getrennte Fassungen).

## Nach dem Merge

Wieder von Hand anstossen — Probendateien zaehlen nicht zum Bau-Kontext, `VERSION` steht weiter auf 6, das Tag ist frei:

```bash
gh workflow run game-images.yml -f images=base/proton
```

## Was die beiden Laeufe schon gezeigt haben

Auch wenn die Proton-Frage noch offen ist, steht bereits fest: Ein Container aus `base/proton` kommt unter der Haertung der Node hoch — UID 1000, schreibgeschuetztes Wurzeldateisystem, `/data` beschreibbar, `/tmp` als tmpfs, `palantir-console` aufrufbar, `palantir.sh` heil. Das war vorher nie geprueft. Und zweimal hat der Ablauf vor dem Veroeffentlichen abgebrochen: `base/proton:6` ist weiterhin frei.
