body:
## What changed

Phase 2 correction PR for the page-by-page audit (`/dashboard/vragen`, the notification path, `/dashboard/messages`, `/dashboard/messages/[id]`, `/dashboard/klaar`). One narrowly scoped PR started from `main` @ 6c88d80ac0b287c801e2f93057665df64cba7930 (main @ e1387e2 merged in while it ran): four MUST FIX defects, two same-PR fixes and four small bounded fixes.

- **VR-01 — invoice status and invoice question no longer contradict.** The one application entry point (`setAccountantStatus`, the door) now makes ONE write: the new database function `accountant_set_invoice_status` moves `invoices.accountant_status` and the asking accountant's own `accountant_subject_status` row in one transaction, scoped to (accountant, invoice). Asking writes both; resolving (`verwerkt`, `in_behandeling`, `te_verwerken`, clearing) closes the question in the same statement; the client answering never touches it; another accountant's question on the same invoice is never altered; a failed second write rolls the first back (proven with breaker triggers in `tests/sql/accountant_invoice_question_sync.test.sql`). EXECUTE is revoked from `PUBLIC`, `anon`, `authenticated` and granted to `service_role` only; SECURITY INVOKER; the door's session-side checks (who is asking, is the invoice visible to them) stay in front of it, and the existing `invoices_accountant_door` trigger still refuses every session write. `/api/accountant/invoice-question` lost its separate text upsert. The owner is told when a question is closed ("Vraag afgehandeld", NB-01), for invoice and document questions alike.
- **VR-02 — the owner may have two accountants.** No uniqueness added, no second invite refused. Every question carries its own `accountant_id` through the model; links are read as a collection (`accountant-links.ts`: failed / zero / one / many, never collapsed, never `.limit(1)`); the answer goes to the asker; an asker who is no longer linked keeps the question visible with an honest state and no composer; a failed link read says so; names are read with service_role only for ids the owner's own rows and links prove. The home's and the rail's "Berichten" door use the same collection (one link → that thread; otherwise the inbox).
- **VR-03 — the invoice door follows the invoice's direction.** `invoiceQuestionHref` decides from the `direction` column, or ownership when it is null (the closing package's rule), never from the number or the name: incoming → `/dashboard/incoming/manage?focus=<id>&from=vragen`, outgoing → `/dashboard/invoice/<id>?from=vragen`; both parent rules know the way back to `/dashboard/vragen`.
- **KL-01 — availability may degrade, financial truth may not.** Every read in `/api/readiness` is inventoried and classified in the route's header (A essential → 503 and no verdict; B supplemental → the verdict is marked incomplete, `ready=false`, never green, the unread input named on the screen and the home; C schema-absent → the zero is the truth). A failed `kor_active` read is essential (503); failed continuity/coverage is not "no gaps"; failed review counts are not zero; a failed evidence lookup accuses nobody. The route takes its clients injected; `readiness-route.test.ts` fails every read on its own against a READY baseline and proves what each does.
- **KL-02** — a period that has not begun (Amsterdam day, one rule for route, page and picker) gets no verdict: route 400 `period_not_started`, page non-verdict state, boundary tests around New Year and a summer quarter transition.
- **KL-03** — the period lives only in the URL (`klaarPath` writes, `quarterFromParams` reads); the picker navigates; refresh, copy, back/forward and deep link name the same period.
- **TH-01** — `/api/messages` reports `linked`; a stranger's thread renders an honest state with no composer; a former partner's thread is read-only. The server stays the boundary.
- **MS-01/MS-02** — an expiring session on the message screens comes back to the same screen (`withRedirect`); the inbox dates in the owner's language.

Not fixed by decision: NB-02 (no e-mail for a question) and VR-04 (all-or-nothing questions list) — both recorded in the PR report. Eight singular `accountant_clients` reads outside the audited journey are recorded there too, not changed here.

Runtime: all nine required smoke cases pass on the local replica (production build of this branch + emulator); nothing touched production.

- [x] Identifiers, comments, test names and this PR body are in English
- [x] Dutch is only used where a user reads it (UI text, PDF/e-mail, legal content, URL
      segments, stored database values)

New screen text is in `messages.ts` with Dutch and English; Arabic falls back to Dutch for the new keys, as AGENTS.md allows. Existing Dutch comments in files touched for another reason were left in place (forward-looking rule).

## Migrations

`supabase/migrations/accountant_invoice_status_sync.sql` — creates `public.accountant_set_invoice_status(uuid, uuid, uuid, text, text)` (plpgsql, SECURITY INVOKER, `search_path = public, pg_temp`), revokes EXECUTE from PUBLIC/anon/authenticated, grants service_role. **Applied to production on 2026-09-20 as migration `20260920185242`** (Phase 2 rollout, Step 1, owner-authorised) and measured there: SECURITY INVOKER, owner postgres, `search_path=public, pg_temp`, ACL `{postgres=X/postgres,service_role=X/postgres}`, EXECUTE anon/authenticated/PUBLIC false, service_role true. body:
Adds the implementation plan for carrying the flushed file paths in the `scan-progress` event so the filmstrip can request only the thumbnails that actually became available, instead of re-requesting every visible placeholder on each event.

Four steps:

1. Make `index::run_scan` report, per progress callback, the paths whose rows `write_batch` committed since the previous callback — and cover the trailing flush with a final callback, which today's `done == total` emit misses.
2. Carry that list as `ready: string[]` in the `scan-progress` payload and narrow `strip.ts` to request only those cells (plus close the in-flight race where a request answered `Err` just before its batch committed would otherwise sit in `missing` until `scan-done`).
3. Remove the now-pointless `REFRESH_INTERVAL = 1000` throttle, whose only remaining caller is `scan-done`.
4. Close the two `todo.md` items this work covers and record the design rationale in `docs/agents/tauri-app.md`.

Three design questions were put to the user and are settled in the plan's "Decisions settled before implementation": no cap on the `ready` array, full paths rather than names relative to `dir`, and full removal of the throttle rather than a shortened interval.

## Summary
- Reported live: running `bootstrap.sh` as root on a real Ubuntu 24.04 machine, the root->brewuser handoff worked (user created, password set, dotfiles copied) but then failed at `sudo: a terminal is required to read the password; ... sudo: a password is required` on brewuser's first `sudo apt-get`.
- Root cause: `su - "$BREW_USER" -c "..."` runs the command without a controlling terminal, so nested `sudo` calls can't prompt.
- Fix: `su --pty - "$BREW_USER" -c "..."` — util-linux's `--pty` flag (confirmed present, util-linux 2.39 on 24.04) allocates a pseudo-terminal for the handed-off shell, giving `sudo` something to prompt on.

## Test plan
- [x] `bash -n ubuntu-setup/bootstrap.sh`
- [x] Confirmed `su --pty` is supported by this util-linux version
- [ ] Not re-verified end-to-end on the reporting machine yet

## Summary

Adds the first TypeSafe evidence-reranking package for PolicyLens.

- Deterministic retrieval remains the recall and safety boundary.
- TypeSafe evaluates only the deterministic top-three candidates.
- Shadow mode is the default rollout; visible answers remain deterministic.
- Active mode is implemented behind candidate-membership and confidence gates, with deterministic fallback.
- Primary and comparison policy requests remain independent.
- Exact citation validation, provider fallback, rate limits, request limits, and security headers remain code-owned.

- `npm.cmd run verify`

- `npm.cmd audit --omit=optional --audit-level=moderate`

author: k-k1
body:
ADR 0093 段 2 の Console 側。kind `lcpp` を**識別できる存在として**登録し（ラベル・短縮名・10 色目・アイコン・CSS・i18n）、決定 2 の「Terminal(CLI) 経路が無い」を読む箇所を実装する。Go・guide は無変更。

## 起動の選択肢には出していない

`lcpp` は managed driver がまだ無く create が 400 で落ちるので、`available: () => false` と `repoLaunchKinds` からの除外で**起動導線に出していない**（`guide/ref/agents.md` 脚注 ⁹ と一致）。

🔴 **「出ないはず」で済ませず、実描画で確認してある**——headless Chromium で**実の `LaunchModal` コンポーネントに実の `repoLaunchKinds` を食わせて**、kind ボタンが 8 個しか描画されず `llama.cpp` が無いことを**両テーマで**確認（スクリーンショットあり）。

## 🔴 10 色目: 一度やり直している

**初回は赤 `#f85149` を選んでいた。これは Console の事実上のエラー色とバイト単位で同一だった。**`--err` はどこにも宣言されておらず（`--err:` は 0 件）、`var(--err, #f85149)` は常にこの literal に落ちる。同じ値が diff/codegrid の削除行マークと admin/tenant のエラー文にも直書きされている。**同じ画面の中で、同じ赤が「エラー」と「llama.cpp というセッション種別」の 2 つを指すことになる。**

原因は測定対象の取り方で、CIEDE2000 の比較相手が**既存 9 つの kind 色だけ**で、**意味色が入っていなかった**。比較集合を「9 つの kind 色 ＋ 同じ画面に出る意味色（`--warn`・`--ok`・`--accent`・diff-add / codegrid-modify / codegrid-add の literal・`--err` のフォールバック literal）」に広げて選び直した。

結果は**オリーブ/マスタード系の黄**（dark `#d9c952` / light `#5c5400`）——色相を全部マップすると claude と warn が ~30-40°、ok/diff-add/codex が ~100-142°、青紫系が ~200-262°、cursor が 330°、err が ~3° で、**空いている色相帯は ~55-58° だけ**だった。マゼンタ系も試したが kiro/cursor から ΔE 6〜13 しか取れず却下。

- 最近傍は両テーマとも `--warn` で **ΔE 17.1（dark）/ 14.4（light）**。rovo の先例（docs/log/74 §8.2・ΔE 7.5/6.3）を大きく上回る。
- `--bg`/`--panel`/`--bar`/`--active-bg` に対するコントラスト **8.04（dark）/ 6.10（light）**。既存 9 kind の最悪値は agy の 3.81/4.86 なので、**既存の床を下回らない**。
- **実の `diff.css` の追加/削除行・`var(--err,…)` バッジ・`--warn`/`--ok` と並べて**両テーマで headless 描画し直して確認済み（子が実施）。
- `tokens.css` のコメントに**赤を却下した理由と広げた比較集合**を残した。次の読み手が同じ穴を開け直さないため。

駆動役が独立に確認したこと: `#d9c952` / `#5c5400` は**コードベースのどこにも既存使用が無い**（初回の失敗モードがまさにこれだった）。

## アイコン

codicon `chip`。`server-process` は**既に LaunchModal/SessionMenu で「managed」駆動選択のアイコン**なので、kind バッジに使うと同じモーダルの中で同じグリフが 2 つの違うものを指す。両方を headless で並べて描画した上で `chip` を採用。

## 端末経路のフラグは 6 箇所中 2 箇所だけ直せば足りた

`AgentDescriptor.terminalDriver?: boolean`（静的宣言。サーバ側の `agents.Caps.ManagedOnly` はまだワイヤに載っておらず、載せるのは Go の変更なので範囲外——`registry.ts` にコメントとして残した）。

**ADR の古い行番号ではなく現在の develop の実コードを当たった結果**、ガードが要るのは `LaunchModal.tsx` の駆動選択トグルと `SessionMenu.tsx` の切替メニュー項目の 2 つだけだった。駆動役も実コードで裏を取った:

- `StartModal.tsx` — `driver: agentOf(kind).managedDriver ? "managed" : ""` で**元から強制**、トグル自体が無い。
- `RepoRowConnected.tsx` — 同じく managed を強制し、`driver_unsupported` の処理まで既存。
- `HandoffModal.tsx` — `repoLaunchKinds.filter(… available({conns}))` 由来なので `available:()=>false` で除外済み。
- `useSessionActions.tsx` — `SessionMenu` の項目を塞げば到達しない（到達してもサーバ側が 400 で拒む＝二重防御）。

## 検証

`cd console && npm test`（node 1931 ＋ dom 1262 ＝ **3193 passed / 1 skipped**・両プロジェクト個別にもパイプ無しで exit code を確認）、`tsc --noEmit` clean、oxlint clean。**陽性対照**は 3 つのガード（LaunchModal のトグル・SessionMenu の項目・registry の `terminalDriver` 値）それぞれを個別に戻して該当テストが赤くなることを確認し、`git checkout` ではなく **Edit で復元**。

## 範囲外として触っていないもの

接続カード（`lcpp` はサインインが無い。shell/ssm と同じ）・`mcpWire` の `MCP_KINDS`・`ScheduleDetailModal`・`ProjectActionPanels`・`ASSISTANT_AGENT_KINDS`・`agentModels.ts` の `isDynamic`・`termcolor.ts` の `KIND_BASE`（**色を付ける端末ペインが原理的に存在しない**ため）。

author: sultanalhabsi
body:
💡 **What:**
Memoized expensive derived state calculations and array filtering/sorting in `src/screens/HomeScreen.tsx`. Introduced a `habitStatsCache` `useMemo` map to avoid calling `calculateHabitStats` for every habit on every re-render. 

🎯 **Why:**
In a React Native list view, computing stats and filtering arrays inside the component render cycle (or `.map()`) creates significant CPU overhead on every re-render. As the number of habits grows, this causes noticeable frame drops and slow responsiveness.

📊 **Impact:**
Reduces re-renders overhead and CPU utilization by a significant margin. Expensive array iterations and date parsing logic inside `calculateHabitStats` are now cached per render cycle instead of running O(N) times where N is the number of habits whenever local component state changes.

🔬 **Measurement:**
Measure the render time of `HomeScreen` before and after adding a large number of habits using React DevTools Profiler, specifically observing the commit time when toggling UI state like `isSearchVisible` or expanding the off-schedule section.

author: suitably
body:
⚡ [optimize player array lookups in Storyteller engine]

### 💡 What
Replaced O(N^2) nested `.find()` searches inside `.map()` and `.some()` operations with pre-computed `Map<string, StoryPlayer>` lookups in `LocalStoryEngine.importSnapshot` and `LocalStoryEngine.updateGameDetails`. Added a dedicated benchmark in `engine.perf.test.ts`.

### 🎯 Why
When processing player channel updates or updating game details, `LocalStoryEngine` performed linear `.find((p) => p.id === ...)` searches over existing player arrays for every player in incoming snapshots/payloads. For games with larger player rosters or frequent snapshot syncs, this resulted in O(N^2) complexity and unnecessary CPU churn during state sync.

### 📊 Measured Improvement
Tested with 500 players and 1,000 operations in Vitest benchmark (`engine.perf.test.ts`):
- **`importSnapshot` (500 players, 1000 ops)**:
  - Baseline (scaled O(N^2)): ~3,150 ms
  - Optimized (O(N) Map lookup): **906.07 ms** (~3.5x speedup)
- **`updateGameDetails` (500 players, 1000 ops)**:
  - Baseline (scaled O(N^2)): ~1,433 ms
  - Optimized (O(N) Map lookup): **179.08 ms** (>8x speedup)

All existing unit tests and architecture checks pass without regressions.

author: makewhatis
body:
## Summary

Two board defects (STUDIO-955) with one root: STUDIO-925 made a **card** a ticket and STUDIO-930 made a **lane** a run status, so a review run belongs to a ticket sitting in another lane.

1. **A reviewer chip opened the author's run, not its own.** The card is `role="link"` with `onClick={open}` targeting the ticket; the reviewer chip was a bare `<span>` with no handler and no `stopPropagation`, so a click bubbled to the card. A chip reading `running` opened the ticket's implementation run, which was `done`. The PR link at the same spot already stops propagation — the chip just never got the same treatment.
2. **The Running lane counted runs but rendered tickets.** Five live reviews rendered as `Running 5 / 6` beside zero cards and a sentence claiming agents were "shown on their tickets in other lanes". A lane's number must describe what the lane shows.

## Changes

`web/` only.

- **`web/src/lib/console-board.ts`**
  - `ReviewerChip` now carries `issue` — the review RUN's own `pr:<owner>/<repo>#<n>@<reviewer>` key (what `job/:key` routes on). The old `key` stays the stable React key.
  - New `runningRuns(rows)` + `RunningRun`: one compact row per **live review run**. A running *ticket* is already a card in the lane (`boardLaneOf`), so only review runs — which have no card anywhere — are returned. One run, one representation.
- **`web/src/components/console/views/BoardView.tsx`**
  - `ReviewerChipView` is now a real navigation target: `role="link"`, `tabIndex={0}`, its own `aria-label` (`Open <reviewer>'s review of <ticket>`), `onClick`/`onKeyDown` that `stopPropagation` and open `chip.issue` — mirroring the card and the PR-link precedent.
  - The Running lane renders the compact run rows and treats the lane as empty only when it renders nothing (cards **and** rows). `occupied` falls back to cards **plus** rows when the tally is absent.
  - The rows respect the project Select exactly as the cards do.
- **`web/src/theme/console-views.css`** — pointer/hover/focus-visible for the clickable chip; `.brun` compact-row styles.
- **Tests** — named after the observed case: a chip reading `running` opens `pr:...#reviewer`, never the ticket (`BoardView.test.tsx`); the five-live-reviews lane renders five rows beside `5 / 6` with the free-slot rack intact.

## Verification

```
$ npm ci && npm test        # web/
Test Files  93 passed (93)
Tests       1980 passed (1980)

$ npm run build             # web/ (tsc -b && vite build)
✓ built in 192ms

$ harness/prompt/prompt_test.sh          exit 0
$ .github/scripts/check-plugin.sh        exit 0
$ .github/scripts/check-plugin_test.sh   exit 0

$ harness/release/check-pr-title.sh "fix(web): open a reviewer chip's own run and count runs in the Running lane (STUDIO-955)"
exit 0
```

Mutation discipline (each guard was broken and each reds exactly the test it claims):

- Removed the chip's `stopPropagation` → `a chip reading running opens that review's run…` fails (`onOpen` fires twice: chip then card).
- Made `runningRuns` return `[]` (lane keeps rendering ticket cards while counting running runs) → `counts what it shows: five running reviews render five rows…` fails (`0` rows beside `5 / 6`).

The lint/test/boot-e2e jobs are Rust-only and untouched by a `web/` change; the `web` job runs the same `npm ci && npm test && npm run build` reproduced above.

## Notes for reviewers

- **Which option from the ticket:** option 1 (compact row per running run), chosen to keep the `N / max_concurrent_agents` capacity read and the idle-slot rack. Running **tickets** keep their full cards — a live review has no card anywhere, so it is the run that was missing; rendering the ticket's card twice would break "a card is a ticket" (option 3).
- The Running lane's count stays the daemon's whole-store tally (its `title` already reads "Whole pool, all projects"), so a project filter can still show fewer rows than the whole-pool number — pre-existing and unchanged by this PR; the run rows now follow the same project filter the cards do.
- No repo doc/plan was produced; this is a code fix only.

Fixes STUDIO-955
https://linear.app/studio49/issue/STUDIO-955/the-running-lane-counts-runs-but-renders-tickets-and-a-reviewer-chip

author: emir-hasanbegovic
body:
## Summary

Two commits that have been sitting on this branch since the 2.0.0 push, rebased onto today's main (the only conflict was CHANGELOG.md, resolved by keeping main's Unreleased entries and adding this one under Fixed).

**fix(ui): the wizard banner's compact mode is measured on the window, not the content column.** The setup wizard's stage labels (INPUT / DESTINATION / BINDING) and the banner slots' sub-lines were missing at the default (980x640) and minimum window sizes and only reappeared once the window was made taller. The threshold compared the page's content column (about 150px shorter than the window: title bar, shell header, page padding) against a window-height cutoff, so compact mode was engaged at sizes it was never meant for. It now reads Window.height and engages only below 0.8 x Tokens.minWindowHeight; the attached height is 0 until parented and is not read as short.

**chore(ci): tolerate Inno 6.7.3's per-user ARP suffix; pin the engine at 6.7.1.** Inno 6.7.3 appends " (Current user)" to a per-user install's Add/Remove Programs DisplayName by itself, which would fail the round-trip's strict assertion the day the runner's engine moves (today's runners still carry 6.7.1 preinstalled, see the last main run). The round-trip now accepts either spelling (same correct install; the installed-vs-portable probe keys on unins*.exe, never the ARP name) and both workflows pin the engine so it moves on purpose.

## Verification

- Debug build of this tree, ctest: 2111/2111 pass.
- scripts/check-qml.ps1: qmllint OK (67 files).
- The commit's own note: round-trip re-run locally against a 6.7.3-built dish-setup.exe, 18/18 assertions pass.

author: cheesex-app[bot]
body:
对应 issue #946 的「片 C」：**建项目时问一句「你打算做什么」**，有答案就让它跟着人进房间。

## 为什么

#946 流程图第 1 步是「让用户说明要做什么」，而今天建项目只填名称 + 团队，**没有任何地方问过这件事**——整条引导最核心的信息没有落点。用户建完就落进一个空房间，房间里唯一回答「我该说什么」的是起手区块。

（Q4 已定走路线 a：#1054 正文与改动只涉及落点，没有「不在建项目时多问」这条决定，所以加这一问不推翻任何东西。Q5 已定不做自动 kickoff。）

## 改了什么

- 新建项目对话框加一个**可选**的多行输入：「你打算做什么（可选）」，placeholder 用文科老师的例子「帮我把这学期的课程材料整理成一份大纲」。**不填照样能建**。
- 答案存到项目上的新字段 `intent`（迁移 `9c4e7a1b6d20`）。**不复用 `summary`**：那是 AI 维护的一页纸，两者差在「谁说的」，共用一列会互相覆盖。
- 有值时，`ProjectService.create` 把原话搬进新生 root 房间的文档：一节「这个项目要做什么」+ 一句「下一步：在下面告诉芝士你要做什么」。
- 无值（含只有空白）时什么都不写，房间照旧靠起手区块。
- 落盘走现成的 `seed_brief_doc`，**模板拼装、不调模型**，署名 `system`——该函数的约定是「平台把已有的文字搬个地方，这里没有一句话是芝士说的」。与赛题报名那条路径（`project/services.py:180`）同构。
- 不自动跑第一轮。

## 验证

- `backend/tests/integration/test_project_intent_brief.py` 5 条。前 3 条走服务层：说了 / 没说 / 只敲空格，**改动前 3 条全红**（`ProjectService.create() got an unexpected keyword argument 'intent'`）。后 2 条走 HTTP——说了要能在响应里读回来，压根没提这一问也能建出项目和房间：服务层的用例分不出「字段能用」和「字段接上了」，路由漏传这一句时前三条照样是绿的。
- `frontend/src/App.newProjectIntent.spec.ts` 3 条：答案跟着建项目请求发出去；跳过这一问发 `''`；取消对话框后上一份答案不会漏进下一个项目。**改动前 3 条全红**（「新建项目对话框里没有 textarea」），改动后全过。
- 那 2 条 HTTP 用例的红度实测过：把 `backend/app/api/routes/projects.py:178` 的 `intent=body.intent` 临时换成 `intent=""`，文件里 1 failed / 4 passed；换回来 5 passed。
- `ruff check` + `ruff format` 干净；前端 `typecheck` 0 error；改动文件的 eslint / prettier 干净；alembic 单一 head（`9c4e7a1b6d20`）。
- 全量前端套件 **194 文件 / 1501 条全过**。头一次跑时有一条挂了——`src/plugins/vuetify.theme.spec.ts` 里那条生成 CSS 变量的用例（5s 超时），单独重跑 1.2s 过，与本次改动无关，重跑全量也干净。
- 顺带修了写用例时踩到的测试环境坑：happy-dom 没有 `visualViewport`，VOverlay 挂不起来，补了桩。

## 没验的

- 在浏览器里端到端建一个项目、看房间真的带着那句话开门。
- 迁移在一个已有数据的库上跑——本轮只在一个空库上验证过。
- 本机没有 Redis，`tests/integration/test_project_visibility.py` 有一条用登录 token 的用例连不上 6379；撤掉本次改动重跑是同样的报错，与片 C 无关。

> 附注：这个 PR 是手工开的（不是平台在同步首个提交时建的），因为写这条时平台的 git 服务端点在返 502，`cheese worktree` / `cheese sync` 都走不通。要是平台上这条任务没挂上这个 PR，以 GitHub 为准。

author: alexisbohns
body:
Part 1 of #852. The issue stays open until the last part of the stack lands.

Replaces Navigation 2's string routes and both `NavHost`s with Navigation 3
typed keys and one `NavDisplay`.

**This part is a pure move, and deliberately changes nothing a user can see.**
Every former `ROUTE_*` string becomes the key for the same destination, with the
same information architecture, and every conditionally-composed cover stays
exactly where it is. The four-tab `NavigationBar` arrives in Part 2, and the
covers become entries in Parts 3 and 4. The repo's "separate a move from a
rewrite" rule is why: a reviewer of this PR checks one thing, that each route
became the same destination.

### Key files

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `navigation/PebblesKeys.kt` | 26 `@Serializable` keys — the 12 routes plus the 14 covers Parts 3–5 will promote. `TopLevelKey : BarKey` and `BarKey` make bar visibility a property of the key rather than a parallel list |
| `navigation/Navigator.kt` | The only writer of navigation state. Backed by one flat stack here; Part 2 swaps in four per-tab stacks without touching a call site |
| `navigation/PebblesEntryProvider.kt` | Key → screen, for exactly what the two `NavHost`s reached |
| `navigation/NavTransitions.kt` | Slide-up for modal keys, shared-axis for pushes, both with a `predictivePopTransitionSpec` |
| `RootScreen.kt` | Twelve `ROUTE_*` constants and both `NavHost` functions deleted |

### Two defects fixed on the way through

- **`soulId` / `collectionId` no longer read back with `.orEmpty()`** — they are non-null `String` fields on their keys.
- **`AuthMode` rides the `Auth` key as a typed enum**, replacing a route string parsed by `AuthMode.fromRoute` with a silent `LOGIN` default. `fromRoute` is left in place until Part 5, when nothing calls it.

### Verification

`npm run lint`, `./gradlew lint` (no new findings), `npm run test` and
`assembleDebug` all green. Beyond that, on a Pixel 8 and a Pixel 7 emulator:

- Cold start lands on Path; `Path → Profile → Souls → SoulDetail` carries the id through the typed key
- Sign-in works through the rewritten gate (the branch Part 1 rewrote)
- **Minified-build smoke test passed and needed no ProGuard rule.** R8 can strip `@Serializable` keys silently, failing as a crash on restore rather than a build error. Against a real `assembleRelease`: pushed `Auth(AuthMode.SIGNUP)`, killed the process, and it restored to Auth with **Sign Up still selected**. R8 keeps the generated serializers unaided, even for a key carrying an enum. No `-keep` was added, since a redundant one widens the keep radius and undoes the shrinking.

That last check is also a small improvement rather than parity: the old route-string round-trip would have restored a signup as a login.

### Not in this part, by design

Covers still do not survive process death, and predictive back does not yet
scrub them — they are still covers. Parts 3 and 4 fix that. If you kill the app
on a pebble detail you will land back on Path; that is expected here, not a
regression.

### Design and plan

`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-20-android-nav3-design.md` (11 decisions, incl.
the four-tab IA and the deliberate break from the 1:1 iOS mirror) and
`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-20-android-nav3.md` (37 tasks across six parts).
Both are committed here because the whole stack builds on them.

author: petonwu
body:
## Problem

#117216 — agent-authored tips (`show_tip` tool → `tip.show` event) arrive with **no `tipId`**, so the renderer's ledgers never see them:

- `showTip()` only writes `$tipShownAt` when `tip.tipId` is set — agent tips are never recorded as seen.
- `retireActiveTip()` persists nothing into `$retiredTips` for an agent tip ("an agent tip has no catalog entry, so it just closes").

Net effect: manually ✕-closing an agent tip means *"see you next conversation"* instead of *"never again"* — the same bubble resurfaces in every new session, indefinitely.

## Fix — give agent tips a stable content identity

`tools/tip_identity.py` (new) derives a stable id from the tip's content:

```
agent_tip_id(selector, text, title) = "agent-" + sha256("\x1f".join(...))[:12]
```

Same content → same id across conversations, sessions and restarts; edited content → a new id and a bubble that shows normally. The `agent-` prefix keeps agent ids out of the catalog id space.

The id flows through the existing ledger machinery — no new storage, no new store, no schema beyond one optional event field:

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `tools/tip_identity.py` (new) | `agent_tip_id()` content-id helper |
| `tools/tip_tool.py` | derive the id; send it as `tip_id` on the event; return it to the model in the tool result |
| `tui_gateway/contracts/events.py` | `TipShowPayload.tip_id: str \| None` (+ regenerated `gateway-contract.generated.ts` / `.openrpc.json`) |
| `apps/desktop/.../gateway-event/desktop-bridge.ts` | pass `tip_id` through to `showTip()` |
| `apps/desktop/src/store/tips.ts` | **the actual fix**: `showTip()` drops any tip whose id is already in `$retiredTips`, so a ✕ binds agent tips exactly as it already bound catalog tips; stale comments updated |
| `apps/desktop/src/lib/chat-messages/types.ts` | `tip_id` on `GatewayEventPayload` |

Returning the id to the model also lays the groundwork for the issue's direction 2 (exposing dismissal history to the agent) without widening the tool surface now.

## Tests

- `tests/tools/test_tip_tool.py`: the event payload and tool result carry the id; the id is stable for identical content and content-addressed (selector/text/title all participate); `agent-` namespacing.
- `apps/desktop/src/store/tips.test.ts` (new): the ✕ on an agent tip retires it; a retired agent tip is dropped on re-show (the regression contract); a merely dismissed (timer) agent tip may return; edited content is not swallowed; catalog tips keep their existing contract.
- `tests/tui_gateway/contracts/test_generated.py`: regenerated contracts are in sync.

Verified locally: `pytest tests/tools/test_tip_tool.py tests/tui_gateway/contracts/test_generated.py` (12 passed), `vitest run` on store/tips + components/tips + lib/tips + use-message-stream (230 passed, 38 files), `tsc --noEmit` clean, plus a manual E2E in the dev desktop app (sandboxed `HERMES_HOME` + Electron user-data dir): same tip re-emitted in a new conversation is suppressed after one ✕; a different tip still shows.

author: adrianhelvik
body:
Background terminal services need a process to own their PTY after `fed start` exits. This adds the hidden `fed host` command: it receives a resolved launch spec over stdin, appends terminal output to the service log, and serves framed attach connections without loading configuration, secrets, or the state database.

A persistent socket lock prevents competing hosts and stale-socket cleanup from replacing a live endpoint. Bounded client queues keep a nonreading client from blocking logging or other clients. The host reports startup exits promptly, drains final output before delivering client exit status, and reaps the service on termination. Diagnostic filenames remain safe and bounded for unusual service names.

Validation: formatting and all-target/all-feature clippy passed on macOS and Linux. Host and PTY behavior tests passed on both platforms, including slow clients, blocked input, concurrent hosts, signals, and Linux log-write failure. The full macOS regression suite had four timing failures across three existing targets; all passed isolated reruns.

PR 3 of 6 for [#29](https://github.com/service-federation/fed/issues/29), based on [#38](https://github.com/service-federation/fed/pull/38). The next layer is host state in [#36](https://github.com/service-federation/fed/pull/36). Background launch and the public attach client follow in PRs 5 and 6.

author: antoniantonov
body:
## Summary

Make the Garmin import workflow self-contained in Docker, with one shared GarminDB SQLite source feeding DuckDB, PostgreSQL, or both.

- Separate interactive authentication/MFA, source refresh, backend imports, read-only queries, and validation into Compose services.
- Add `scripts/run_import.sh` with PostgreSQL as the default, backend selection, authentication, download overrides, offline imports, image reuse, and optional validation. Build and refresh once when importing both backends.
- Add `scripts/run_database.sh`, persistent local PostgreSQL, and the DuckDB Web UI. Wait for service health and stop/restart the DuckDB UI around imports to release its file lock.
- Let garth attempt OAuth1-based renewal when OAuth2 expiry metadata is stale, while continuing to fail on actual authentication errors. Replace the host-side token-renewal scripts with containerized authentication.
- Document configuration, schemas, SQL examples, operation, and an AWS/Azure implementation handoff. Cloud deployment and persistence remain follow-up work, not implemented infrastructure.

## Usage

From the repository root:

```bash
# Default: build, refresh, import PostgreSQL, and leave it running.
./jobs/import-garmin/scripts/run_import.sh

# Refresh once, import both destinations, validate, and leave query services running.
./jobs/import-garmin/scripts/run_import.sh --db both --validate
```

## Import evidence

**Historical live run, 2026-08-28:** the Garmin source refresh authenticated successfully, and both destinations were imported, re-imported, and compared with the transformed SQLite source. The [dated implementation report](https://github.com/antoniantonov/workoutdata/blob/62fa430d9c84239895020aaa97d640889b37b609/docs/reports/summary-2026-08-28T19-54-18%2B02-00.md#12-final-live-execution-result) records the outcome.

**Current verification, 2026-09-20:** PostgreSQL matches the current SQLite source. Using the current Python source mounted read-only into the existing Garmin image, a fresh DuckDB import and a second import into the same disposable database both passed source comparison, backend parity, primary-key, and relationship checks.

| Table | Historical live import: both backends | Current source, PostgreSQL, and isolated DuckDB |
|---|---:|---:|
| `garmin_workout_metadata` | 465 | 495 |
| `garmin_timeseries` | 177,532 | 187,687 |
| `garmin_sleep` | 282 | 298 |

The second DuckDB import preserved all totals. Full-row/value comparisons passed, using the validator's `1e-12` floating-point tolerance, with no duplicate keys, orphan timeseries rows, or mismatched workout relationships.

Both current validation passes ended with:

```text
Comparing DuckDB and PostgreSQL...
  - workouts: backend rows match
  - timeseries: backend rows match
  - sleep: backend rows match
Garmin database validation passed.
```

**Existing local snapshot caveat:** the persisted DuckDB file still contains the older 465-workout snapshot, while the current source and PostgreSQL contain 495 workouts. An initial read-only check against that file reported the expected shape mismatch. It was left unchanged; current parity and repeat-import evidence used `/tmp/garmin-pr-validation.duckdb` inside an automatically removed container. No new Garmin download, PostgreSQL writes, or changes to persisted workout data were made while preparing this PR.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce the isolated import and repeat-import check</summary>

Requires the existing Garmin image and the local PostgreSQL service to be running and populated from the current source. Run from the repository root:

```bash
docker compose --project-directory jobs/import-garmin \
  -f jobs/import-garmin/docker-compose.yml \
  run --rm --no-deps -T --pull never \
  --entrypoint /bin/sh \
  -e PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
  -e DATABASE_TYPE=duckdb \
  -e GARMIN_DOWNLOAD=false \
  -e GARMIN_DUCKDB_PATH=/tmp/garmin-pr-validation.duckdb \
  -e 'PGOPTIONS=-c default_transaction_read_only=on' \
  -v "$PWD/jobs/import-garmin/garmin_etl:/app/garmin_etl:ro" \
  -v "$PWD/jobs/import-garmin/main.py:/app/main.py:ro" \
  -v "$PWD/jobs/import-garmin/local_data:/app/local_data:ro" \
  validate-garmin -c '
    /app/.venv/bin/python /app/main.py &&
    /app/.venv/bin/python -m garmin_etl.validate --backend both &&
    /app/.venv/bin/python /app/main.py &&
    /app/.venv/bin/python -m garmin_etl.validate --backend both
  '
```

</details>

## Additional checks

- All **17 launcher regression tests** passed: `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s jobs/import-garmin/tests -v`.
- Both launchers passed `bash -n`.
- Docker Compose configuration validation passed.
- All 12 application Python modules passed syntax parsing.
- The staged diff passed `git diff --cached --check`.

## Scope

This PR contains the Garmin job changes and its historical implementation report only. The unrelated Polar audit at `jobs/import/missing-duckdb-records.md` remains uncommitted. Environment files, Garmin session tokens, database files, and individual workout records are excluded.

author: allday8556
body:
## 1. What changed

**§A — the offline M5 acceptance harness.** `scripts/m5_acceptance.py` and `scripts/m5accept/`
run the seventeen acceptance-plan cases of Issue #89 through the **real production owners** on a
fresh dedicated root, in an exact clean checkout, with every provider transport refused for the
life of the run. The run writes one sanitized report with a SHA-256 digest that `--verify`
recomputes. The M4 root, checkout and guard modules were parameterized rather than copied, so one
accepted implementation of those gates now serves both milestones.

**§B2 — the durable registration preparation (ADR-0014 §27, architect decision `5751540323`).**
`app/register/authoring.py` and migration **0018** own the operator-authored inputs of one
provider-listing unit: the category selection, the listing values and the detail composition, with
the exact Item membership, in append-only revisions, each with its own sanitized fingerprint. A
separate row proves which revision froze a Snapshot. It stores **inputs only** — no readiness,
status or reason code, no Product, price, image, capability or provider fact — the preflight still
derives every verdict, the builder still freezes, and a `register.create` job payload stays a frozen
**execution** copy that nothing needs in order to display or evaluate a preparation.

**§B — Registration Management reads server-owned truth, per provider-listing unit.**
`app/register/service.py` builds the screen from durable rows — one row per **provider-listing
unit** (ADR-0014 §2, R3), never one per Draft. A frozen unit is the newest Snapshot for exactly its
set of Items, with that Snapshot's own Intent, Attempts, conflict scope and actions; its Items and
`registration_item_key`s come only from that Snapshot's `ItemSnapshot` rows. Each unit carries its
category and required-field state, each Item's pinned price beside the current M4 price with the
server's own comparison, the M4 base and pricing readiness with every reason code, the selected
publication assets as exact identities with their QA verdict, and the preflight re-evaluated from
current truth. `app/api/routes/register.py` serves it, every action carries the **server's** verdict
(`enabled` + `reason_code`), each route re-enters the owner that produced it, and
`ui/web/js/pages/register.js` renders that state and decides none of it.

**§C — derived live-canary readiness.** `app/register/canary.py` names every proof a bounded real
canary would still need, counting real provider-listing units. At this head the verdict is
**BLOCKED**, and each unadopted contract is reported as **not adopted** with its endpoint id —
never as absent or unnecessary. A running application cannot prove its own checkout, so
`CLEAN_RUNTIME` stays unsatisfied with `PROOF_NOT_AVAILABLE_IN_PROCESS` rather than being assumed.

**§D — `docs/acceptance/M5.md`** stays **PENDING** and documents the harness contract, the report
schema, what the offline run proves, what it declares and **why each declaration is a declaration**,
the surface and its owners, and the live-canary blockers.

CI gains `m5-offline-acceptance`: the same harness on a clean checkout, the digest verified, and an
asserted outbound marketplace mutation count of **0**.

## 2. Contract

Implements ADR-0014 §17 (endpoint adoption), §22 (registration UI), §24 (execution safety) and §26
(execution-scope send brake) — as a reader and a renderer. It changes no contract: no ADR sentence,
invariant, table set or migration allow-list moved.

## 3. Schema

**One migration: `0018_m5_registration_preparation`**, authorized by architect decision
`5751540323` after PR-F reported the missing durable owner. It adds exactly four tables — the
preparation, its append-only authored revisions, each revision's Item membership, and the
provenance of the Snapshot a revision froze — and touches no existing table, row, trigger or index.
It adds no endpoint adoption, no marketplace asset owner, no M6 state, no second scheduler or retry
state, no stored readiness and no unrelated cleanup. `alembic check` reports no new operation, the
`0017 ↔ head` round trip holds, and the downgrade refuses while any authored row is held.

## 4. External writes

**None.** CREATE, image upload and product search stay `NOT_ADOPTED`; `product_registration.write`
stays `UNVERIFIED`; the execution mode stays `DRY_RUN`. The harness proves the SmartStore caller
cannot even be loaded during a run, that PR-D's real wire projection refuses to send, and that the
measured outbound marketplace mutation count is **0**.

## 5. How it was verified

Exact head **`d99face9a245e16e1b4eea5a2dc683a5f1ed31f9`**, base `main` `5c205e4b`.

| what | command | observed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| full suite | `pytest -q` | **2685 passed**, 0 failed |
| PR-F focused suite | `pytest tests/integration/test_m5_acceptance.py tests/integration/test_m5_register_api.py tests/integration/test_m5_register_ui.py tests/integration/test_m5_registration_foundation.py tests/unit/test_m5_register_contract.py -q` | **195 passed** |
| lint / format / types | `ruff check .`, `ruff format --check .`, `mypy` | clean; 396 files formatted; **224 source files, no issue** |
| migration | fresh upgrade, `alembic check`, `0017 ↔ head` round trip, downgrade with rows held | head `0018_m5_registration_preparation`, **no new operation**, downgrade refused |
| offline harness, fresh dedicated root outside the repository | `python scripts/m5_acceptance.py --root <fresh>` | exit 0, **63/63 checks**, `problems: []` |
| report digest | `python scripts/m5_acceptance.py --verify <report>` | `report digest verified` |
| negative controls | 32 mutations of each harness guard, provider-zero gate, live-readiness gate, unit boundary, preparation rule and server-owned verdict | **32/32 CAUGHT**, each by a test that states that rule; every file restored byte-for-byte (SHA-256), working tree and ignored paths clean |

**What the harness measured** (report `icbm-m5-acceptance-report/v1`, digest
`b8dab612511021b43badd67003779cf0dae5c9f5836c3b76e45aa8678e462b0f`):

- checkout: `tracked_changes 0`, `untracked_files 0`, `hidden_tracked_files 0`, `ignored_sources 0`,
  `code_outside_checkout 0`; `database_revision 0018_m5_registration_preparation`;
  `execution_mode DRY_RUN`
- guards: `external_network_attempts 0`, `egress_grants_opened 0`, `writes_outside_root 0`,
  `forbidden_modules_loaded_during_run []`, `forbidden_modules_preloaded []`,
  `forbidden_imports_blocked ['integrations.marketplaces.smartstore.caller']` — the deliberate probe
  proving the provider transport cannot be loaded
- boundary: **`marketplace_mutations: 0`**, `provider_audit_events: 0`,
  `real_wire_projection_sendable: false`
- endpoint adoption: `SMARTSTORE_PRODUCT_CREATE_V2 false`, `SMARTSTORE_PRODUCT_IMAGE_UPLOAD false`,
  `SMARTSTORE_PRODUCT_SEARCH false`, `SMARTSTORE_ORIGIN_PRODUCT_READ_V2 true`,
  `SMARTSTORE_CHANNEL_PRODUCT_READ_V2 true`
- canary readiness: **`BLOCKED`**
- declarations, each with its own reason: `CREATE_HANDOFF` and `RECONCILE_LOOKUP`
  `ENDPOINT_NOT_ADOPTED`; `READ_BACK` `OFFLINE_SYNTHETIC_PROVIDER_RESPONSE` with
  `endpoint_adopted: true`; `WIRE_PROJECTION` `WIRE_CONTRACT_UNPROVEN`; `PUBLISHED_STATE`
  `PUBLISHED_STATE_UNPROVEN`; `ACCOUNT_BINDING` `OFFLINE_SYNTHETIC_PROVIDER_RESPONSE`

### The GPT exact-head audits, and the architect decision they produced

- **HOLD #5261079291** — B1 (per-unit read model) and B3 (declaration reasons) closed; B2 was
  implemented as far as durable truth reached and the remainder **reported**: the operator's
  preflight inputs had no durable owner, so no migration was created.
- **Architect decision #5751540323** — option (a) selected and **migration 0018 authorized**: a
  REGISTER-owned durable preparation. Implemented at this head (§B2 above and ADR-0014 §27).
- **HOLD #5261280389** — the two remaining collapses closed: a frozen unit is keyed by its own
  Snapshot, so two legal listings of the same Items never hide one another

author: wjrnj9zy72-design
body:
Suite de la PR #14, et **c'est cette version du SQL qu'il faut passer** — inutile de lancer celui de la #14 d'abord.

## Six chiffres au lieu d'une clé de 32 caractères

Une clé de groupe ne se dicte pas au téléphone, et une fois donnée elle l'est pour toujours. Désormais :

1. quelqu'un du groupe touche **Inviter** ;
2. il dit **le nom du groupe et six chiffres** ;
3. en face : onglet Aperçu, le nom, le code, **Entrer**.

L'invitation vaut **une demi-heure et une seule entrée**. Le tout premier appareil d'un groupe — le seul que personne ne peut inviter — part toujours de la clé affichée par l'éditeur SQL ; ce chemin est replié sous *« Je n'ai pas de code, mais une clé »*.

## Une clé par appareil

L'appareil qui entre reçoit **sa propre clé**. Un téléphone perdu, quelqu'un qui quitte le groupe : on coupe **cette** clé, les autres continuent.

```sql
delete from public.marque_points_group_key where id = 'ID_DE_LA_LIGNE';
```

Une étiquette est stockée à côté (« écran d'accueil · 20 sept. 2026 ») pour s'y retrouver. Le renouvellement global reste possible, comme bouton d'alarme.

## Le piège, trouvé par le test

Ma première version comptait les essais **par invitation**. Ça ne protège de rien : celui qui devine tape des codes qui n'existent pas, donc aucun compteur ne bouge. Reproduit sur PostgreSQL 16 — dix essais faux, et le vrai code marchait toujours.

Le compteur est maintenant **par groupe** : vingt essais ratés en dix minutes et la porte de ce groupe reste fermée un moment ; le groupe d'à côté n'est pas gêné ; une entrée réussie efface l'ardoise.

## Et le rattachement de l'existant

Ce qui était déjà partagé n'appartient à aucun groupe : *Tout récupérer* l'ignorerait et l'app ne pourrait plus le supprimer. Le guide donne la requête qui le range dans votre groupe, avec le comportement vérifié avant et après.

## Vérifications

- `npm test` : **176 tests, 0 échec**.
- Navigateur : **182 vérifications** sur quatorze suites, dont 14 neuves sur l'invitation — code à six chiffres, code dit à voix haute, mauvais code refusé, invitation qui ne ressert pas, clé reçue **différente** de celle qui a invité, et partage depuis le nouvel appareil vu par l'ancien.
- **Dix scénarios SQL** sur PostgreSQL 16 avec les rôles de Supabase, dont le blocage après vingt essais, la coupure d'une seule clé, et l'invitation expirée.

author: itakth
body:
### The guest diagnosed this one itself
```
ipv6 iface-state tap... dhcp=Enabled ra=Enabled
ipv6 managedaddress/otherstateful forced exit=1
ipv6 renew6 exit=0
ERROR: still no global IPv6 after 60s - RDP will be unreachable
```

Two corrections to my own previous PR:
- **`dhcp=Enabled` already.** Windows was willing to solicit all along, so the premise behind forcing it was wrong.
- **The netsh call returned exit=1** — it never applied. Nothing may depend on it; it stays only as an advisory nudge.

`renew6` returned 0, so solicits went out and **nothing answered**.

### Cause
The client solicits from its link-local to `ff02::1:2` port **547** — permitted by the egress list. The server answers from *its* link-local to the client on port **546**, and nothing in this security group admitted that.

So the guest solicited forever and held only a link-local address. That presents **exactly** like a firewall blocking RDP, because packets to the global address never arrive at all — which is why three rounds went to the wrong layer.

### Scoping
Unscoped, like the ICMPv6 rule and for the same reason: a DHCPv6 client port isn't meaningful attack surface, and twice now a hand-derived "tighter" prefix has silently broken address configuration. TCP is where the exposure is, and **3389 stays scoped to `rdp_allowed_prefixes`**.

### Cost
`terraform/` only — no image rebuild.

author: lance0
body:
A session drops its outbound receiver before the RIB processes its queued `PeerDown`. During that interval, other peers' route changes can repeatedly prepare and attempt delivery to the closed channel. Large peer shutdowns therefore produce repeated outbound warnings and failed-send accounting for work that cannot be delivered.

Skip per-peer outbound preparation when the currently registered receiver is already closed. Reuse the existing closed-channel and dirty-retry helpers; lifecycle cleanup remains owned by `PeerDown`. Full live channels retain their warnings and retry behavior, and replacement session registrations receive updates normally.

Regression coverage exercises 1,000 closed receivers alongside a healthy peer, including announcements and a real source withdrawal, full live-channel recovery, and replacement registration followed by a stale `PeerDown`. Removing only the new guard makes the closed-receiver test fail with 5,000 warnings; restoring it produces zero warnings and zero failed-send attempts while preserving healthy delivery.

Validation:
- Focused distribution tests: 7 passed.
- RIB library tests: 1,370 passed, 2 ignored.
- Local gate passed: links, developer tooling, fast checks, contracts, strict workspace Clippy, full workspace tests, and private-item rustdoc.

author: m2ux
body:
## Summary

The prism lens routing data moves out of a technique's rule bodies and into a resource, so the three techniques that read it cite one home. This check looked for the goal targets in the technique that used to carry the tables, so it moves with them.

## What happens today

`check-prism-lens-reachability` proves two things: every lens resource on disk is reachable through some prism mode, and every lens named in the selection logic resolves to a file whose index agrees with the catalog. It takes the goal routes from `prism/techniques/plan-analysis.md`, by path, because that is where the goal-to-lens table was written.

That coupling is what blocked the corpus change. The table has three consuming techniques and one of them keeps a divergent copy, so it is reference material rather than one operation's rule — but moving it to a resource made this check read an empty routing text and report all sixty-odd lenses unreachable.

## The fix

The check reads `prism/resources/lens-selection.md` instead. Both halves take their routing text from there: the coverage half looks for a `slug (NN)` goal target, and the name-fidelity half reads the same file for stale names. The portfolio catalog is unchanged on both halves, and the messages name the new home.

Nothing else changes — not the pipeline-internal list, not the non-lens frontmatter test, not the catalog comparison.

## Scope

One file, `guards/check-prism-lens-reachability.ts`: the path, the two reads that consume it, and the three strings that name it. No registry change, no `package.json` change.

## What was verified

Type-checking is clean under the tools configuration. Run against the paired corpus branch the check passes — every lens goal-routable or pipeline-internal, every named lens resolving.

The new resource declares `type: reference` in its own frontmatter, which the check's existing non-lens test already excludes, so the resource is not itself held to a goal route.

## Merge order

This is one of **two** server-side changes the corpus branch needs, and it must merge **after** `fix/catalogue-prescribes-and-flags` — until that tree is in place the resource does not exist and this check cannot read it.

Its sibling is the reference-predicate fix on the same corpus branch. Running the full guard suite from either server branch alone fails on the guard the other one carries; with both applied the suite is clean at 46 of 46, which I verified by combining them locally before opening either.

author: ryanjosephkamp
body:
## What changed and why

The provider-outage quarantine (`live_quarantine.json`) excuses a live failure only when the case recorded **exactly one** `source_outcome` property, and exactly one naming the entry's source. Of resmon's two OAPEN live cases, only `test_api_tier4.py::test_oapen_live_search` recorded one. The other — `test_entity_search_live.py::test_a_real_source_answers_a_real_author_query[oapen]` — recorded none, so an entry naming it would have printed in the weekly run summary as a quarantine and excused nothing.

- **Every** parametrised author-query case now records `source_outcome_property(slug, outcome)`, from the same `search_outcome().snapshot()` it already takes, on the answered path and on the raised path (recorded before the exception continues), before any assertion. A keyed source that skips before the client call still records nothing.
- The precondition is written down where the next person adding a quarantine entry will read it: in the `quarantine_disposition` docstring and in the reader-facing policy in `docs/source-response-reliability.md`. An excuse needs exactly one recorded outcome in total and exactly one for the entry's source, so it fails closed both ways — a case that records none, and a case that records two and cannot say whose outage the failure was.
- Two additive hermetic guards in `test_live_suite.py`.

## How it was verified

All hermetic. No live request is made by anything on this branch.

| Check | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Full backend suite | `python -m pytest -q` | 2991 passed, 2 skipped, 108 deselected (6 min, Python 3.11.5 locally) |
| Live-suite partition, selection and evidence guards | `pytest -q test_live_suite.py test_source_response_reliability.py test_api_tier4.py` | 171 passed, 2 deselected |
| Scheduled selection unmoved | `python live_suite.py --summary` | `92 of 108 live_network tests`; `91 of 92 asserted; 1 quarantined (oapen, since 2026-09-18, http_500, expires 2026-10-18)` — unchanged |

The two new guards:

- `test_a_recorded_author_query_outcome_is_what_lets_the_quarantine_excuse_it` drives the **real** `quarantine_disposition` over a real entry read back through `load_quarantine` and a real recorded property built through `SearchOutcome`'s own `note_attempt` / `note_retried_failure` / `note_failure`. With the property: `excused`. Without it (today's behaviour): `unmatched`. With a second source on the same report: `unmatched`. No hand-written dicts.
- `test_every_author_query_case_records_one_source_outcome_for_its_own_slug` runs the real author-query module in a child process against a client double and reads the recorded properties back out of the durable live evidence: **20 of 20** askable sources, the denominator taken from `_askable()` over the capability table rather than a list in the test. `validate_evidence` puts each property through `_canonical_source_outcome`, refuses one recorded outside the call phase, and the evidence writer refuses a second `source_outcome` on one report — so a passing run is also the proof that each case records exactly one.

Both guards were made to go red. Deleting the answered-path recording turns the second into `0 of 20 askable sources recorded a source outcome naming themselves` with all twenty nodeids named. Making the double open a non-loopback socket turns the child run into twenty-one failures reading `Blocked outbound connection to example.invalid` — that is `conftest.py`'s socket guard, which the child plugin deliberately shuts again after the production conftest opens it for `live_network` items, so the hermetic run's boundary is enforced rather than assumed.

## What it deliberately does not do

- **It adds no quarantine entry for the author-query case.** There is no admissible evidence for one: the case passed on both 2026-09-18 runs and in the run where only OAPEN's dated search failed. An entry is added when the case actually fails with the signature from two vantages. This change only makes such an entry capable of doing anything.
- **It does not make an OAPEN outage on the author-query case excusable today.** `quarantine_disposition` excuses only an `AssertionError` in the call phase. The strict-source branch of that case calls `pytest.fail` when the source answers with nothing, which is the shape an OAPEN outage takes there, and `pytest.fail` raises `Failed`, not `AssertionError` — so that path would still be `unmatched`. The new guard pins this with `assert not issubclass(pytest.fail.Exception, AssertionError)` and says so in a comment. Converting that branch, or widening the gate, is a separate decision and is not made here.
- No connector change, no schema change, no new dependency, nothing under `implementation_scripts/`. `live_quarantine.json` is untouched.

## Limitations

- The client double answers every source identically. It establishes that each case records a well-formed `source_outcome` for its own slug; it establishes nothing about any real provider's behaviour. That remains the weekly live run's job.
- The recorded property was verified over a simulated outage snapshot and over hermetic successful calls. No real OAPEN 500 was observed during this change.
- Local counts were taken on this workstation's interpreter; CI's Python 3.10/3.11/3.12 columns are the gate.

author: asherwilson
body:
Two things the first real deploy of the API found.

The deploy raced the images. Both started on `release: published`, so the server was told to pull 0.0.19 about a second after the build began and it failed on `provisioner:0.0.19: not found`. The deploy now runs after the Images workflow and only when it succeeded, and it refuses to run for anything that is not a released version.

The provisioner watched the signer's port. Its Dockerfile was started from the signer's and kept `EXPOSE 4200` and a healthcheck on `127.0.0.1:4200`, while the service listens on 4400. On the server it reported unhealthy forever while answering every request perfectly. `scripts/checks/service-ports.test.mjs` now reads each service's config and its Dockerfile and refuses a mismatch, so a copied Dockerfile cannot keep its neighbour's port again. It fails on the old file and passes on the new one.

Closes #608
Closes #609

author: miciav
body:
## Il bump: quattro siti, non tre

| File | Da | A |
|---|---|---|
| `pyproject.toml` | `0.6.1` | `0.6.2` |
| `src/sonata_engine/__init__.py` | `__version__` | `0.6.2` |
| `packages/sonata-tasks/pyproject.toml` | `0.6.1` | `0.6.2` |
| `packages/sonata-tasks/pyproject.toml` | `sonata-engine==0.6.1` | `==0.6.2` |

Il terzo è guardato dal test `test_dunder_version_matches_the_pyproject`; il quarto è
il pin lockstep, quello che si dimentica e che rompe l'allineamento della coppia.
`sonata_tasks` non ha una `__version__`, quindi non c'è un quinto sito scoperto.
`uv.lock` rigenerato: due righe, nessun rumore del resolver.

## Il workflow: da matrix a due job

`tasks` ha `needs: engine`. Un matrix esegue le gambe in parallelo e non può
esprimere una dipendenza, e questa coppia ne ha una — verificata nel wheel costruito,
non nei sorgenti:

```
sonata_tasks-0.6.2-py3-none-any.whl
  Requires-Dist: sonata-engine==0.6.2
```

Un upload di `tasks` che sopravvive a un upload di `engine` fallito lascia su PyPI una
distribuzione **che non si installa**, e una versione caricata si yankera, non si
riusa. `fail-fast: false` garantiva solo che entrambe le gambe venissero tentate, non
che la seconda aspettasse.

## La guardia del tag diventa una composite action

È lo stesso controllo due volte, e due copie divergono. Spostandola guadagna
`nullglob`: senza, una `dist/` vuota espande il glob nel letterale `dist/*.whl`, che
conta come un wheel — quindi il controllo "esattamente uno" passava sul nulla e il
fallimento veniva riportato come nome che non corrisponde.

Testata come bash estratto dall'action, quattro casi:

| Caso | Esito |
|---|---|
| wheel giusto | rc=0, `tag v0.6.2 matches ...` |
| `dist/` vuota | rc=1, `expected exactly one wheel in dist/, found 0` |
| due wheel | rc=1, `found 2` |
| tag sbagliato | rc=1, `does not match the built ...` |

## Verifica

- 227 test sonata + 348 sonata-tasks, coverage 96.17% e 90.75% contro la soglia 90.
- Coerenza delle quattro sedi e del lock letta dai file: `sonata-engine 0.6.2`, `__version__ 0.6.2`, `sonata-tasks 0.6.2`, pin `sonata-engine==0.6.2` → lockstep coerente: True.
- I due wheel costruiti portano il metadata giusto, `Requires-Dist: sonata-engine==0.6.2` incluso.
- ruff, basedpyright (entrambi i progetti), pre-commit: verdi. Controlli strutturali sul workflow: `needs` punta a un job esistente, `./.github/actions/check-release-tag/action.yml` esiste, lo step della composite ha `shell:`.

## Una nota su cosa manca

Il workflow di release gira **solo su tag**, quindi nessuna CI lo esercita: la sua
prima esecuzione sarebbe la release vera. Se vuoi, prima di tagliare la 0.6.2 posso
spingere un tag usa-e-getta su questo branch (es. `v0.0.0-test`): la guardia fallisce
per costruzione, non viene caricato nulla, e si osserva che `engine` gira e `tasks`
viene **saltato** — cioè esattamente la proprietà che questa PR introduce. Il tag si
cancella subito dopo. Dimmi se lo vuoi.

En el cuadro de roles (`/roles-permisos`) las 14 pantallas FLITO vivían en un grupo aparte, «FLITO (SOAT e Impuestos)», lejos de las acciones de su módulo. author: carloswonmore
body:
Fixes #686.

## What

#679 hid the console window on the child launches it could reach. A run-time audit of the released
**0.24.0** build — every `child_process` launch instrumented, **101 launches** across `init` /
`import --from-repo` / `doctor` / `packages` — found three more `git` launches on a code path #679
did not touch. This PR fixes those three plus the siblings that reading the same two files turns up.

| file | function | before |
|---|---|---|
| `src/providers/git/index.ts:28` | `gitIdentity()` | `spawnSync('git', ['config','--get','user.name'], …)` — no `windowsHide` |
| `src/providers/git/index.ts:72` | `ensureInstalled()` | `spawnSync('git', ['--version'], …)` — no `windowsHide` |
| `src/providers/git/index.ts:85` | `cloneRepo()` | `spawnSync('git', ['clone','--',…], …)` — no `windowsHide` |
| `src/wiki-engine/code-knowledge/code-collector.ts:146` | `gitCommit()` | `execFileAsync('git', ['-C', root, 'rev-parse','HEAD'])` — no options object at all |
| `src/wiki-engine/code-knowledge/code-collector.ts:162` | `isWorkingTreeClean()` | `execFileAsync(…)` — no options object |
| `src/wiki-engine/code-knowledge/code-collector.ts:183` | `gitDiffNameStatus()` | `execFileAsync(…)` — no options object |

The first two are `GenericGitProvider`, which is selected only when the repository host is not one
we recognise — so #679's `provider` / `gitHub` / `gitLab` branches never reached them. The
code-collector three run on every `teamai import --from-repo` / wiki scan.

The code-collector change hoists one module-level constant so the three call sites stay in sync:

```ts
const GIT_EXEC_OPTIONS = { windowsHide: true } as const;
```

`cloneRepo()` is not in the audit table (the `git` provider never reached a clone in that run) but
shares its second-argument shape with `ensureInstalled()` and flashes once per clone, so it is
fixed here too.

## Why it matters

A parent with no console of its own — a GUI host or a hook host — makes Windows give the child a
new one, which flashes a visible window. Before this change a single `teamai init <git-url>` plus a
single `teamai import --from-repo` starts four such children: the audit recorded 4 launches with
`windowsHide=None` out of 101, three of them on these branches.

## Tests

- `src/__tests__/generic-git-provider.test.ts` — new `GenericGitProvider — windowsHide` block drives
  `ensureInstalled()` → `authenticate()` → `cloneRepo()` and asserts all three `spawnSync` calls
  carry `windowsHide: true`.
- `src/__tests__/code-collector-windowshide.test.ts` (new) — mocks `node:child_process`, drives the
  three helpers, asserts the same on the options object handed to `execFile`.

Both assert on the options object on purpose: **CI has no Windows runner**
(`os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest]`), so nothing else can catch a missing `windowsHide`.

Verified locally on Windows 11 25H2 / Node 22.22.2:

| step | result |
|---|---|
| `tsc --noEmit` | clean (0 lines) |
| those two files, patch applied | `Test Files 2 passed (2)` / `Tests 19 passed (19)` |
| those two files, patch reverted | `Test Files 2 failed (2)` / `Tests 2 failed \| 17 passed` |

The revert run fails on exactly the two new assertions, i.e. the tests do guard the change:

```
expected { encoding: 'utf-8', …(2) } to deeply equal ObjectContaining {"windowsHide": true}
expected 'function' to be 'object' // Object.is equality
```

## Real-CLI end-to-end verification on this build

The 101-launch audit above was measured against released **0.24.0**. It documents what those branches
did *before* this PR; it is not evidence about this build. Here is the same instrument re-run on the
built output of the branch head.

**Build.** `npm run build` → `dist/index.js` **1,804,627 B** (head `3cb1b28`, Windows 11 25H2,
Node 22.22.2, tsup 8.5.1).

**Harness.** The `git` provider channel from the #679 audit: a bare fixture repo exported by
`git daemon` on `127.0.0.1:9418`, reached as `https://127.0.0.1:9418/group/fixture.git` so the host
is unknown and `resolveHostProvider` selects `GenericGitProvider`. `USERPROFILE` / `HOME` and
`GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` are redirected into a scratch directory, and the credential guards are the same
(`GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, `GCM_INTERACTIVE=never`, `GCM_GUI_PROMPT=0`, `GIT_ASKPASS=`,
`SSH_ASKPASS=`). Every `child_process` entry point is wrapped by a CJS `--require` shim.

**Commands and results.**

| # | command | exit | launches | missing `windowsHide` |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| 1 | `init <url> --scope user --agent codebuddy --force` | 0 | 31 | **0** |
| 2 | `import --from-repo <url> --skip-enrich --all --output <out>` | 0 | 14 | **0** |
| 3 | `import --from-repo <url> --incremental --skip-enrich --all --output <out>` | 0 | 18 | **0** |
| | **total** | | **63** | **0** |

All six call sites this PR touches were reached on the real paths:

| call site | launch shape | reached by | launches |
|---|---|---|---:|
| `providers/git/index.ts` `ensureInstalled()` | `spawnSync('git', ['--version'], …)` | `init` | 1 |
| `providers/git/index.ts` `gitIdentity()` | `spawnSync('git', ['config','--get','user.name'], …)` | `init` | 1 |
| `providers/git/index.ts` `cloneRepo()` | `spawnSync('git', ['clone','--',…], …)` | `init` | 1 |
| `code-collector.ts` `gitCommit()` | `execFile('git', ['-C',<cache>,'rev-parse','HEAD'], …)` | `import` | 3 |
| `code-collector.ts` `isWorkingTreeClean()` | `execFile('git', ['-C',<cache>,'status','--porcelain'], …)` | `import --incremental` | 1 |
| `code-collector.ts` `gitDiffNameStatus()` | `execFile('git', ['-C',<cache>,'-c','core.quotePath=false','diff','--name-status','-M','-C',<old>,<new>], …)` | `import --incremental` | 1 |

Raw records, showing the options object arrived at the three `execFile` shapes:

```json
{"fn":"execFile","cmd":"git","args":["-C","…\\cache\\repos\\git\\group\\fixture","rev-parse","HEAD"],"hasOptions":true,"windowsHide":true,"stdio":null,"shell":null}
{"fn":"execFile","cmd":"git","args":["-C","…\\cache\\repos\\git\\group\\fixture","status","--porcelain"],"hasOptions":true,"windowsHide":true,"stdio":null,"shell":null}
{"fn":"execFile","cmd":"git","args":["-C","…\\cache\\repos\\git\\group\\fixture","-c","core.quotePath=false","diff","--name-status","-M","-C","0b3a193cde29fb05acc38eff2ce90103ae0e9986","0cfb450976422a9a03591a81eaf2003b875342ee"],"hasOptions":true,"windowsHide":true,"stdio":null,"shell":null}
```

The incremental run fetched a real new fixture commit and acted on the diff, so the code-collector
paths were live rather than skipped:

```
ℹ [incremental] cache hit …\cache\repos\git\group\fixture, syncing from 0b3a193c
ℹ [incremental] Fetch complete: SHA=0cfb4509
[extract] incremental: 1 files changed, 0 deleted
```

For comparison, the #679 run recorded `windowsHide=None` on 4 of 101 launches under these same
commands — three of them on the branches this PR fixes. On this build: 0 of 63.

**The instrument had to be fixed before it could be trusted.** The first shim replaced the six
`child_process` entries with a plain `function (...args) { record(...); return original.apply(this, args); }`,
which drops `util.promisify.custom`. `promisify(execFile)` then degrades from `{ stdout, stderr }` to
a bare string, so `code-collector`'s `const { stdout } = …` received `undefined`, `stdout.trim()`
threw, and each function's own `catch` swallowed it — the shim was manufacturing a silent failure
and hiding the very incremental path it was meant to observe. `spawn-audit.cjs` now re-attaches the
symbol after wrapping, and the unfixed original is kept next to it so the #679 numbers stay
reproducible.

**What this does not cover.** The five clone functions added in `3cb1b28` (`ghRepoClone`,
`gitlabRepoClone`, `gitcodeRepoClone`, `cnbRepoClone`, `gfRepoClone`) run only when the host matches
`github` / `gitlab` / `gitcode` / `cnb` / `tgit`, which needs a live instance and a token per
provider, so the `git` channel cannot reach them. They are covered by
`src/__tests__/provider-clone-windowshide.test.ts` ins

body:
## What changed

Replaced the custom midi-writer-js TypeScript workarounds with the library's actual type definitions.
Updated MIDI recording to track note start times and calculate note durations correctly.
Updated tests for the corrected MIDI behavior.
Connected MIDI recording to the UI for start, stop, and export.

## Why

The previous TypeScript workaround hid issues with how MIDI note events were being created. Using the real types required updating note duration handling.

The MIDI functions also needed to be connected to the existing recording and export UI.

Closes #65
Closes #91 

#88 will remain open until pause functionality and filepath selection are implemented. 

## How it was tested

Ran the MIDI Vitest tests.
Verified TypeScript checking passes.

## RCA (defect fixes only)

<!-- rca:start issue=91 -->

### Root cause

The custom MidiWriter TypeScript declarations hid required note event fields, allowing `noteOff` events to be created without the required duration information.

### Discovery

The defect was discovered when the custom type workarounds were removed and TypeScript began using MidiWriter's actual declarations.

### Exposing test

No test originally exposed the issue. It was found during development when TypeScript reported errors in `noteOff`.

### Fix verification

`npx tsc --noEmit` completed successfully and the MIDI unit tests passed. (https://github.com/Kakrl/MakeShift/actions/runs/35526610489/job/106119766417?pr=92)

### Regression test

`tests/frontend/midiUtils.test.ts` — `creates a note event using the note start time and duration`. This test is not currently run in CI.

### Remaining risk

The MIDI subsystem is the only part of the codebase that uses MidiWriter, so the same issue was not found elsewhere.

### Process improvement

Use library-provided TypeScript declarations instead of recreating external library types.

<!-- rca:end -->

author: pfenerty
body:
ScriptLanguage was documented as an extension point but was only half open.
A third party could construct `new Script(myLanguage, body)` and nothing
else: the name union and the extension map were both closed, so a language
from outside the core could not reach scriptFromFile, the {language, body}
object form, task or project defaultLanguage, or `tektonic lint`'s file
discovery.

registerLanguage(lang, { extensions }) opens it and returns the language's
tagged-template helper, so registration and use are one step and no
stringly-typed name is needed at the call site. The four built-ins register
through the same function at import time — there is no privileged path into
the registry, which is the only way the seam stays honest.

LanguageName becomes KnownLanguageName | (string & {}): any registered name
type-checks where a built-in does, and 'nushell' still autocompletes.
A name may be registered once (a second registration throws rather than
overriding at a distance); a conflicting extension warns and the last one
wins. `tektonic lint` now walks the registry's extensions instead of a
hard-coded list, so a registered language's files are linted by its own
lintCommand.

The exit-code contract stays closed, because a wrap() that ignores
captureExitCode reports a failed step as green — silently. The new
assertExitCodeContract in @pfenerty/tektonic/testing renders a body, runs it
with the real interpreter and asserts both the process exit code and the
contract file, so an out-of-tree language can prove it complies; the static
checks run even when the interpreter is absent.

Build robust, capable decompiler output that reads like developer-authored C# while retaining exact semantic ownership.

- Advances #3218
- Advances #5876
- Omits extension-method type arguments inferred directly from a raised lambda result when receiver inference, target-container overloads, and final expression natural type prove the recorded binding.
- Card revision: `e6ce392d402ae2033c9e5143c25b33c612d85c2d`

## Demo

`dotnet-inspect.any@0.14.0` contains the real
`DotnetInspector.CommandLine.HelpWriter::FormatOptionEntry` witness.

Before:

```csharp
IOrderedEnumerable<string> names =
    S_0.OrderBy<string, int>(a => a.TrimStart('-').Length)
       .ThenBy<string, string>(a => a);
```

After:

```csharp
IOrderedEnumerable<string> names =
    S_0.OrderBy(a => a.TrimStart('-').Length)
       .ThenBy(a => a);
```

Neighboring direct output inference also becomes idiomatic:

```csharp
values.Select(value => value.Length)
```

Explicit arguments remain for method groups, typeless or narrowing lambda
results, expression trees, custom delegates, nested result templates, multiple
output sources, unfixed delegate inputs, and competing same-arity sibling
shapes.

## Change

**Conclusion: PASS** - the decompiler now omits lambda-result-inferred generic
arguments only under typed import-time and final-IR proofs; exact compile-back
and fixed-population evidence show no binding or fidelity regression.

### Raise contract

| Obligation | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Lowering shell | A selected generic extension `MethodSpec` whose receiver fixes some method type parameters and whose remaining parameter occurs as the direct result of exactly one trusted core-library `Func<..., T>`. |
| Consumed ownership | No IR or control-flow region is consumed. Import records typed receiver/output inference provenance; printing removes only the explicit generic argument list. |
| Control flow | Not applicable: the call, receiver, arguments, and evaluation order are unchanged. |
| Replacement | The recorded method instantiation must survive exact target-container sibling analysis, and each output obligation must still be a one-expression raised lambda whose natural type exactly matches the recorded type argument. |
| Decline boundary | Method groups, expression-tree output inference, custom delegates, block/multi-return lambdas, narrowing or typeless results, nested result templates, duplicate output sources, unfixed delegate inputs, unresolved metadata, and ambiguous same-arity siblings retain explicit arguments. |
| Falsifier | A bare emitted call binds to a different member/instantiation, fails to compile when the explicit form compiled, or recompiles to a different method body. |

### Evidence map

| Lens | Scope | Compared | Held constant | Answers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Method validity | `HelpWriter::FormatOptionEntry` | Base `1f6d53483` -> head `e6ce392d4` | `dotnet-inspect.any@0.14.0` bytes | Both spellings bind. |
| Method correctness | Same method | Explicit -> inferred generic arguments | Selected extension methods and arguments | Calls preserve the recorded `OrderBy<string, int>` and `ThenBy<string, string>` instantiations. |
| Method IL fidelity | Compiler-produced fluent fixture | Raised and lowered views | Original fixture IL | Both views recompile Exact. |
| Structural review | `HelpWriter::FormatOptionEntry` | Exact base/head product documents | Same method token `0x060019E7` | Two supported invocation rows changed; gaps remain explicit. |
| PDB Source -> After | Same logical method in the package PDB | Authored source -> head product | SHA256-verified PDB document | The inferred calls now match authored spelling. |
| Render A/B | 12,637 methods in `dotnet-inspect.any@0.14.0` | Exact base/head products | Same package bytes and sampling | 70 methods changed; all changes are generic argument elision. |
| Fixture activation | Compiler-produced extension fixtures | Accepted and declined shapes | Release compiler output | Positive cases elide and boundary cases stay explicit. |

### Shared judgment

| Lens | Evidence kind | Direction | Comparison |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Method validity | Product quality | **Same** | Valid -> valid. |
| Method correctness | Product quality | **Same** | Recorded generic instantiations are preserved. |
| Method IL fidelity | Product quality | **Same** | Exact -> Exact in raised and lowered views. |
| Structural review | Evidence coverage | **Same** | Partial on both revisions; two claimed invocation changes have supported rows. |

## What

Release **0.24.0**: comq takes its AMQP connection from
[`@toa.io/amqplib`](https://github.com/toa-io/amqplib), and the write batching it carried for
amqplib's sake is gone.

Per message answered, measured with comq's own `npm run benchmark` against the same broker: CPU
11.2 → 7.2 µs at 20 000 messages/s and 12.6 → 7.0 µs at 64 requests in flight, saturation
90 000 → 97 000 messages/s, p50 latency 0.79 → 0.63 ms.

It also carries what has been on `dev` since 0.23.0: a request waits for its reply, comq's own
queues no longer scale with the application's, and one queue each for parked messages and replies.

## Breaking

**Node.js 24 or newer**, which `engines` now states. CI has run on 24 all along.

## Merging

With a merge commit, as always — semantic-release reads the version out of the commit messages.
