author: ilovepixelart
body:
Four git checkpoint defects, each of which ended in a silent loss or a wrong restore that `/rewind` still reported as success, and the background subagent registry. Each fix is paired with a test that fails without it; the checkpoint tests run real git.

## Wrong restores

- **A provider retry no longer corrupts the run's checkpoint** (`git-checkpoint.ts`). A provider error or an overflow recovery continues the same prompt through `agent.continue()`, which fires `agent_start` and `turn_start` again. The pre-run snapshot taken there staged every tracked file at its mid-run content and was only discarded at `turn_end`, after the shared index had changed. A file first edited later in the run then moved the recorded checkpoint onto that index: `/rewind` restored `a mid-run` where `a before` was expected, and a file first edited in the retry turn was not restored at all. Only a prompt fires `before_agent_start`; a run re-entering without it, whose last user message already has a checkpoint and with nothing queued, reuses that checkpoint's ref. A queued follow-up still gets its own snapshot.
- **A forked session can restore the checkpoints it inherited** (`git-checkpoint.ts`). `/fork` copies the branch's checkpoint entries into a new session file, while the shadow repository is keyed to the session file, so those refs lived only in the parent's shadow: "Code restore failed: fatal: invalid reference". `session_start` with reason `fork` now fetches them, a local bare-to-bare fetch.

## Checkpoints that silently stopped

- **One path git refuses no longer ends checkpointing for the session** (`git-checkpoint.ts`). git fails the whole `add` on a single refused pathspec: a file edited through a symlinked directory ("beyond a symbolic link") or an unreadable one failed every later pre-run snapshot, for every file, with no notification. An edit is tracked by the real directory its file sits in, mapped back under the work tree as the session spells it, and when the bulk add still fails each path is added alone and the refused one dropped.
- **Files inside a nested repository are checkpointed** (`git-checkpoint.ts`). With cwd a workspace of clones, a monorepo with submodules, or `$HOME`, `git add` exits 0 for a path under another repository and stages nothing, so the edit was never snapshotted while `/rewind` answered "Rewind complete". Such a path is hashed and written to the index directly, which `checkout` restores like any other entry.

## Background subagents

- **The background run registry survives a module re-import** (`subagent/background.ts`). `/reload`, and `/resume` into a session recorded in another directory, clear pi's extension cache and evaluate the module again. The registry was module state, so it restarted empty while the children kept running: `/tasks` said "No background subagent runs", cancel said "Unknown background run", and at quit nothing was signalled, so the detached child outlived pi.

*Behavior change: a retry of the same prompt no longer takes a second pre-run snapshot. The test that pinned two snapshots now pins one.*

- [x] `npm run check` passes (Biome, strict tsc, Vitest)
- [x] Tests cover the change

author: franchb
body: ## The bug `delete_handler` validates the cookie by reading the needle with `EcVolume::read_ec_shard_needle`, which reads **only locally-mounted shards**. For any interval that lives on a peer it errors `"ec shard N not available locally"`, and the handler mapped *every* `Err` to 500 without appending to `.ecj`. On a standard 10+4 spread over 14 servers, no node holds every shard, so **every HTTP DELETE of an EC needle failed 500 and left the needle live.** The GET path (`get_or_head_handler_inner`) already uses `read_ec_shard_needle_distributed`; only the delete path was left behind. ## The fix Route the delete's read through the same distributed reader. It does a local-first pass in its snapshot phase, so the all-shards-local case costs what it did before. No store guard is held across the `.await` — the reader takes and releases its own, and `RwLockReadGuard` is `!Send`. Two smaller corrections fall out of the new return type: - The reader reports both *"needle not in the index"* and *"volume vanished between the `has_ec` check and the snapshot"* as `Ok(None)`, which collapses the old `Some(Ok(None))` and `None` arms into a single 404. - An `io::ErrorKind::NotFound` now answers **404 instead of 500**, matching the GET path. Telling a caller to retry a delete that can never succeed was half the bug. The cookie check and its ordering before the journal append are unchanged — I deliberately left the HTTP path's own check alone rather than trying to unify it with the gRPC `BatchDelete` work from #11348. ## Reproducing it on one node The reason this survived is that it looks like it needs a 14-server fixture. It doesn't: the distributed reader seeds its Reed-Solomon buffers from locally mounted siblings (Phase 0 in `store_ec.rs`), so with ≥ 10 survivors it reconstructs **without any peer fan-out**. The regression test mounts 13 of 14 shards, leaving out the one holding the needle's interval — so the local-only read fails while the distributed read succeeds. Against the unfixed handler it fails exactly as reported: ``` assertion `left == right` failed: DELETE of an EC needle must reconstruct through the distributed reader instead of failing 500 on a non-local shard left: 500 right: 202 ``` It also asserts the tombstone actually landed (a later GET is 404), not merely that the handler answered 202. ## Not addressed here Rust journals the tombstone **locally**, while Go routes it to the primary shard holder. That is a separate behaviour change with its own failure modes (who is primary, what happens when they are unreachable, whether the local `.ecj` row is still written), so it belongs in its own PR. Tracked against the same checkbox in the umbrella issue. Adjacent but out of scope: `VolumeNeedleStatus` (`grpc_server.rs`) also reads EC needles local-only. It is a status query rather than a mutation, so I left it alone. ## Verification - `cargo clippy --all-targets` — clean, 0 warnings - `cargo test` — **636 pass, 0 fail** (integration suite 28 → 29) - `cargo fmt --check` — clean for both touched files (Unrelated: `cargo fmt --check` reports one pre-existing diff in `remote_storage/mod.rs` introduced by #11390. Left alone.) 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by CodeRabbit - **Bug Fixes** - Fixed deletion of erasure-coded needles stored on peer or unmounted shards. - DELETE and batch-delete operations now validate erasure-coded needle data consistently. - Missing needles or volumes return 404, while unexpected failures return 500. - Existing deletion markers are handled safely, and successfully deleted needles no longer remain accessible through GET requests. - Batch deletion now reports absent needles appropriately. - **Tests** - Added coverage for deleting needles when the relevant shard is not mounted locally.

body:
…rker

Signing in from northflow.adamlacasse.dev failed with Google's redirect_uri_mismatch because the app sent a *.up.railway.app callback. The Worker fetches the Railway origin URL and forwards the public host in X-Forwarded-Host, but Railway's edge proxy overwrites that header with its own hostname before it reaches gunicorn, so ProxyFix rebuilt every external URL on the wrong domain. Confirmed by sending a spoofed X-Forwarded-Host directly to the Railway domain and still getting a Railway redirect_uri.

- worker.js now also sends the browser-facing host in a private header, X-Northflow-Host, which nothing in between rewrites.
- New PublicHostMiddleware copies that header into the request host, but only when the value is in the PUBLIC_HOSTS allowlist, so a spoofed header on the publicly reachable Railway hostname cannot steer OAuth redirects.
- ProxyFix keeps x_proto but drops x_host, which only ever carried the wrong value here.
- Document PUBLIC_HOSTS in README, .env.example and DEPLOYMENT_ACTIVE.md.

Deploy requires: `wrangler deploy` for the Worker and PUBLIC_HOSTS=northflow.adamlacasse.dev on the Railway web service.

author: joaquindecima
body:
> Necesita Vasak-OS/vasak-desktop#95 para que aparezcan filas. Sin él la lista
> viene vacía y el resto del lanzador funciona igual, así que se puede mergear
> antes.

Si Firefox ya está abierto, escribir «firefox» ofrece **esa ventana** antes que
abrir otro. Es la diferencia entre volver a lo que estabas haciendo y empezar de
nuevo, y por eso una ventana abierta pesa más que la aplicación que la abriría.

## Por qué por D-Bus y no del compositor

En Wayland, enumerar ventanas es un protocolo privilegiado —`foreign_toplevel`—
y `permisos-globales` lo reparte por programa. Pedirlo para el lanzador sería
pedir también **los títulos de todo lo que hay abierto**; el escritorio ya los
tiene, y en #95 pasa a poder contestarlos.

Traerla al frente va por el mismo camino, con `PresentWindow`, que a diferencia
del botón del panel **nunca minimiza**: elegir una ventana en una lista de
resultados no puede esconderla.

## Se pregunta cada dos segundos, no en cada tecla

Un viaje por D-Bus por letra es trabajo en el camino crítico, y lo que se abre y
se cierra no cambia en medio de una palabra. Dos segundos es más de lo que tarda
alguien en escribir y menos de lo que se nota.

Si el escritorio no contesta —una sesión donde el lanzador arrancó solo— no hay
filas y todo lo demás sigue.

## Lo que dejé afuera, y por qué

**El prefijo `w `** que decía el issue. Las ventanas aparecen **sin prefijo**,
que es la mitad que importa: con prefijo habría que acordarse de escribirlo justo
cuando uno busca algo que ya tiene abierto.

Listar todas sin escribir nada sí querría un prefijo, y ahí hay que elegir: los
que hay son de un carácter (`>`, `?`, `:`) y ninguno sobra para esto. Un prefijo
de palabra —`w ` y un espacio— es una segunda gramática para un solo proveedor.
Si te parece que vale, lo agrego; es una línea.

## Comprobado

- `cargo test` — 204 pruebas, 0 fallos (8 nuevas)
- `bun test` — 96 pruebas, 0 fallos
- `cargo clippy --all-targets`, `cargo fmt`, `bun run lint`, `vue-tsc`: limpios
- Los campos que faltan en la respuesta no descartan la ventana: el escritorio
  puede agregar o sacar campos, y lo que hace falta acá es el identificador y el
  título

Closes #9

author: yanzhao77
body:
## 本次改动（T03-01 第一批：配对载荷与信任上下文）

新建 T03-01 任务卡，并把状态由「阻塞」改为「进行中」——网络绑定部分仍阻塞于 B02，但**配对逻辑本身未被阻塞**，且它是 B02 无法替代的部分。B02 那一行保持「阻塞」，网络缺口仍在台账里可见。

### 1. 把「先比对再发令牌」做成结构性保证

协议 §2：

> 采用每连接隔离的信任上下文；**必须在发送令牌、HTTP 请求及文件内容之前完成指纹比对**。
> 即使证书受系统 CA 信任也必须比对 pin，不能只在"不可信证书回调"中比对。

这类规则的问题不是难写，而是**写错了也不报错**：一个先发令牌、后比对指纹的实现，**对着诚实的服务端照样工作**，所有功能测试照样通过。所以令牌在这里不是一个字段：

```dart
/// Refuses until the certificate has been compared and matched.
String get pairingToken { ... }   // 未比对 → ProtocolViolation(PAIR_REJECTED)
```

调用方**没有顺序需要记住**。配套不变量：

| 不变量 | 依据 |
| --- | --- |
| 比对失败**关闭**连接，不得在同一上下文上重新协商 | §2「比较失败关闭连接」；在对端身份校验已失败的连接上重试，正是重试循环变成攻击的方式 |
| **每连接隔离**：一个连接的失败不泄漏到另一个 | §2「采用每连接隔离的信任上下文」 |
| **除非比对显式返回 trusted，否则关闭** | 本次主动收紧：初版在「证书编码不可用」时抛异常但**不关闭**，改为统一关闭——不变量越简单越不容易被绕过 |

### 2. 指纹的三种写法，形状相同、语义不同

§2 把 pin 定义为 `SHA-256(叶证书完整 DER)`，并明确**不是** PEM 文本摘要、**不是** SPKI 摘要。弄错会得到一个**看起来完全合理、但永远匹配不上**的 pin。

- `serverFingerprintOf(List<int> leafCertificateDer)` 的参数类型是**字节**，没有接受 PEM 字符串的重载，传错是**编译错误**；
- 测试直接断言它与 PEM 文本摘要不同、与对 DER **一部分**求摘要也不同。

**比较刻意不是常数时间**：指纹发布在用户扫描的二维码里，**不是秘密**，时序信道不泄漏任何攻击者尚未拥有的东西；手写常数时间比较等于为不存在的问题发明密码学代码（`AGENTS.md` §5）。这一点写进了代码注释。

### 3. QR 载荷：严格解析

载荷是客户端从不受信来源读到的第一个东西，决定「连到哪里」和「信任谁」。§4 要求未定义字段**拒绝**而非忽略。

52 项测试里绝大多数是负例：非 JSON / 数组 / 纯文本 / URL；超 4096 字节（**在解析之前**检查）；顶层与 candidate 内的多余字段；`kind` 与版本错误；指纹 63/65 位、**大写**、非 hex、base64 形状；`sessionId` 大写或去掉连字符；令牌带填充、长度不符、**非规范写法**、标准字母表；候选空列表、超 8 个、端口 0/65536/写成字符串；`host` 带 scheme、凭证、路径、查询、空白、方括号、主机名、IPv4 越界与**前置零**、IPv6 双省略与组超 4 位。

三个值得单独说明的判定：

- **大写指纹被拒绝**——它被用于**相等比较**，正是最不该有两种拼写的地方；
- **IPv4 前置零被拒绝**——`10.0.0.01` 在某些解析器里按八进制解释，一个字符串可能意味着两个地址；
- **方括号地址被拒绝**——端口是独立字段，不需要方括号消歧；同时接受两种写法等于给同一地址两个名字。这是**有意的严格**，已在任务卡与运行汇总中写明。

### 4. base64url：为什么专门写一个解码器

§4 要求「解码后重新编码必须相同」。无填充 base64 的末位字符含空闲比特，**多个字符串可以解码到同一批字节**——而被当作凭证使用的值，最不该有「同一令牌两种拼写」。

## 验证

| 检查 | 结果 |
| --- | --- |
| `dart format lib test tooling` | 通过 |
| `flutter analyze` | `No issues found!` |
| `flutter test` | **426 passed**（358 → 426） |
| `check_links.py --strict` / `check_secrets.py` / `check_ci_workflow.py` | 全部通过 |

## 未完成 / 限制（T03-01 保持「进行中」）

- **没有真实 TLS 引擎**：`PairingHandshake` 接收调用方给出的叶证书 DER；真正取 DER、以及离线 pin 模式下的**证书日期与主机名策略**（§2 要求由目标引擎原型明确）未实现。
- **没有网络绑定与可达性验证（B02 阻塞）**：本次只做词法校验，**不声称**任何候选地址可达或在本地链路上。多网卡与指定 Network 完全未涉及。
- **没有配对令牌的服务端生命周期**：单次消费、300 秒单调计时、服务重启失效、统一 `PAIR_REJECTED`、限流（§3）全部未实现。
- **没有 `POST /v1/pair`**：请求体、`sessionAccessToken` 签发与交付、`Authorization: Bearer`、恢复凭证与 receipt 未实现。
- **没有二维码生成与扫描 UI**，也**没有平台权限路径**（相机 / 本地网络）。
- **没有被任何生产调用方使用**。

**需人工重点复核**：① `expiresInSeconds` 只是提示（§3 以服务端状态为准），当前只校验为正数、**不**当过期时间，后续不得改成信任它；② 候选地址的信任语义——本次只保证「拿到令牌必须先比对」，**选哪个候选**仍由调用方决定，网络层必须确保 pin 来自二维码本身而非连接结果；③ `abandon()` 的调用时机（取消/超时/切换候选），目前无调度代码因而无端到端验证；④ 比较非常数时间是有意选择，若要改应先说明威胁模型变化。

证据：[`docs/testing/evidence/2026-09-20/t03-01-01/summary.md`](https://github.com/yanzhao77/NearSend/blob/feat/t03-01-pairing-trust/docs/testing/evidence/2026-09-20/t03-01-01/summary.md)

author: dtumad
body:
## Summary

Adds `--lean-module-system` to the Lean backend. With the flag, every generated file is a Lean [module](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Source-Files-and-Modules/): it starts with `module`, imports the support library and its sibling files with `public import`, and opens an `@[expose] public section` right after its imports. The hand-written files the backend copies into the project (`Sail/{Real,FakeReal,SpecializationV1,SpecializationArchSem}.lean` and `--lean-import-file`s) get the same spelling. Without the flag the output is byte-identical to today's.

## Context: what we use the backend for and what blocks us

We maintain a Lean verification of a RISC-V zkVM's AIR against the Sail RISC-V model, generated by this backend (`sail-riscv` at `61266bd4`, this compiler at `41694abd`, lean-sail v5). The generated model is ~160 Lean files; our tree on top of it is ~1 000 modules that unfold the generated `execute_*`/register definitions in proofs.

We want to move our own files to Lean's module system, mainly so that editing a proof does not rebuild every importer (module-mode oleans separate the public interface from proof bodies; a proof-only change no longer changes the interface hash). The blocker is a rule of the module system: a `module` file may only import `module` files. Our lowest layer imports the generated model and, through it, lean-sail — so until both are module libraries, none of our files can be. The companion change on lean-sail is rems-project/lean-sail#13 (migrate the library to the module system); this PR is the generator side.

## Why exposed and public everywhere

The generated code is all definitions, and downstream proofs unfold them by `rfl`/`simp`. Under the module system a definition body is visible to importers only when it is exposed, and a re-exported name only through `public import`. Making the whole model exposed and public reproduces exactly what a non-module importer sees today, so consumers can switch their own files to module mode with no change in what elaborates. A finer public/private split would be a policy decision for the backend that this PR does not make.

## Why a flag rather than the default

Module-mode output can only be built against a module-mode support library, so consumers on lean-sail v5/v6 need the current spelling. The flag keeps every existing test's expected output unchanged.

## Implementation

`src/sail_lean_backend/sail_plugin_lean.ml` only (+75/−15):
- `opt_lean_module_system` and the `--lean-module-system` option;
- `module_header`, `import_line`, `expose_section` helpers used by `print_function_file_prelude`, the `Defs.lean` header and `file_prelude`;
- the copy of static/imported Lean files now runs in OCaml (`copy_lean_file_to_project`, replacing the `sed` invocation) so it can prepend the header, make the `import`s public and insert the section after the last import under the flag. `THE_MODULE_NAME` substitution is unchanged.

The generated `lakefile.toml` is unchanged.

## Verification

- `test/lean/run_tests.py --lean-local-support-library <module-mode lean-sail>`: 36 golden tests pass unchanged (the unflagged output is byte-identical) and the runnable self-tests pass.
- With the flag: `append.sail` generates a project whose files start with `module` / `public import` / `@[expose] public section`; it builds against the module-mode lean-sail on v4.29.0 (`lake build`, 16 jobs).
- Full RISC-V model (`sail-riscv` `61266bd4`, `rv64d` config) generated with the flag: the diff against the unflagged generation is the headers only (161 files), and the model builds against lean-sail#13.
- `dune build @fmt` clean (ocamlformat 0.29.0).

A follow-up could add a `--lean-module-system` mode to `run_tests.py` once lean-sail's default branch is a module library; the golden files would then differ only in their headers.

author: seonghobae
body:
* 🚨 Severity: Medium
* 💡 Vulnerability: Possible SQL injection vector through string-based query construction (Bandit B608) where string interpolation was used for building dynamic IN clauses instead of safe query parameters.
* 🎯 Impact: While the identifiers are currently sourced from schema validations, using unsafe string interpolation establishes a bad pattern that can lead to SQL injection vulnerabilities down the line if validations change or input sources expand.
* 🔧 Fix: Implemented native psycopg array adaptation using `ANY(%s)` and a Python `list` argument, completely avoiding dynamic string interpolation for the `IN` clause.
* ✅ Verification: Verified with `bandit -r src/` yielding zero B608 errors and verified full test suite coverage (`100%`) using `coverage run`.

author: fatal10110
body:
Refs #2362.

Folds the two remaining unblocked items from #2362 — the `AttackType` / `creature.FormulaActor` asserts and the manor seed-state return-type drift. **#2362 must stay open after this merges** — deliberately no closing keyword anywhere in this description: four of its five scope bullets (REAL_DAMAGE, GET_PLAYER, the skill-condition parser asserts, GIVE_SP and extraction) are unported — GIVE_SP now split out to #2387, the rest blocked on systems Go does not have, and the remaining gate sites still reference that issue from the code.

## Behavior delivered

None. This is a type-level fold with no observable change: no packet, persistence, lifecycle, formula or constant is touched.

### Formula caster surface

`creature.ResolvePhysicalSkillInput`, `ResolveMagicDamageInput`, `ResolveBlowInput`, `ResolveManaDamageInput` and `ResolveSkillSuccessInput` took an `attackable.Combatant` caster and immediately re-asserted it to `creature.FormulaActor`; so did `Character`/`Hostile`/`summon.Actor`'s `LethalInput`, `Hostile.PhysicalSkillInput` and `player.attackerUsesBow`. Those asserts were dead: `*player.Character`, `*npc.Hostile` and `*summon.Actor` are the only production `attackable.Combatant` implementations and all three already satisfy `FormulaActor` (verified by temporary `var _ creature.FormulaActor = (*T)(nil)` assertions in each package, which compiled clean on `main`).

The caster parameter is now typed `creature.FormulaActor` through the whole chain, including `FormulaActor.ShieldDefense` and the `PhysicalSkillInput` / `MagicDamageInput` / `BlowInput` / `ManaDamageInput` / `LethalInput` / `SkillSuccessInput` / `EffectSuccessInput` methods on `handler/skill.Creature`, which now embeds `creature.FormulaActor` instead of `attackable.Combatant`. `combatantOf` becomes `formulaCasterOf` and keeps its job unchanged: a door or signet effect point is not a creature, so it yields nil and the formula treats it as a caster that cannot roll.

Each resolver's `!ok` branch rejected a nil caster as well as a non-formula one. The nil rejection is preserved as an explicit `== nil` check, so a nil caster still returns `false` rather than panicking.

### Manor seed state

`handler/skill` declared its own `seedState` interface plus a `seedableTarget` that required `SeedState() seedState`. `*npc.Hostile` returns `*npc.SeedState`, which has all six methods but not that exact signature, so no live target ever matched and both handlers were dead in production. The `NPC` cast cluster now requires `SeedState() *npc.SeedState` and the handlers use `asNPC`; the duplicate interface is deleted.

SOW and HARVEST remain inert, for the reason that was always the real blocker: nothing implements `seedItem`, so no item resolves to a `manor.Seed`, so SOW never sows and HARVEST never finds a sown target. That is stated at the handler.

## Sites deliberately left

The Phase C gate (`docs/actor-model-degoifying-plan.md:526`) goes **9 → 7**. Every remaining site is commented where it occurs and is blocked on a system Go has not ported:

| Site | Blocked on |
|---|---|
| `handler/skill/resources.go` (REAL_DAMAGE) | per-kind death sequence; summons have none (#2361) |
| `handler/skill/resources.go` (GIVE_SP) | tracked on **#2387** — reachable now through datapack skills **2167** (Scroll of SP) and **2306** (Primeval Crystals), both of which consume their item and grant nothing. The level-table blocker holds for players only; `summon.Actor.AddExpAndSp` is live and needs no table, so the pet half is a contract-shape mismatch (`AddExpAndSP`/`int` vs `AddExpAndSp`/`int64`). |
| `handler/skill/teleport.go` (GET_PLAYER) | `TeleportTo` carries a scatter radius; no datapack skill uses GET_PLAYER |
| `handler/skill/extractable.go` | no actor exposes an inventory capacity check |
| `skill/conditions/target.go` ×3 | the skill-condition parser does not build `TargetNpcID` / `TargetRaceID` yet |

Three `creature.FormulaActor` asserts also stay, in `MakeAttackHit` on each of the three kinds, now documented at the site. Folding them needs the world known-list to hand out formula operands: `CreatureActor.ForEachKnownCombatantInRadius` (`attack/controller.go:47`) yields `attackable.Combatant`, narrowed from `world.Tracked`, and `world` cannot name `creature.FormulaActor` because `creature` already depends on `world`. The pole and split paths draw their extra targets from that callback, so this is a separate refactor.

`creature.RaidCurseTarget`'s three asserts stay too. They are not capability drift: `SkillSeeTargetOf` receives `target.Actor` values that include doors, and `TestCursesOnAttack` receives any attack target, so the assert is the kind narrowing that selects an attackable NPC. Erasing it would mean putting a meaningless `NpcID()` on players and summons.

## Verification

- `gofmt -l` — no output
- `go vet ./...` — clean
- `go build ./...` — clean
- `make test-unit` — pass
- `make test` — pass
- `make test-race` — pass

The manor handler tests now drive the real `*npc.SeedState` instead of a hand-written spy, so `AllowedToHarvest` and `HarvestedCrop` are asserted against the production lifecycle rather than a restatement of it.

## Gap audit

- Manor SOW/HARVEST activation — seed items resolving to `manor.Seed`, the Player-only caster gate, the Monster-only target gate, the sow/harvest system messages, the party harvest broadcast and the manor production rate: **#240** (OPEN, milestone *M12 - Territory: sieges, castles, clan halls, manor*, comments checked; specifics recorded there in a new comment rather than a duplicate issue).
- Party-shared harvest eligibility: **#863** (OPEN, milestone *M12 - Territory: sieges, castles, clan halls, manor*, comments checked — none).
- The seven remaining gate sites and the three `MakeAttackHit` narrowings: **#2362** (OPEN, milestone *M14 - Hardening, parity sign-off, release*, comments checked — none), which this PR deliberately leaves open.

author: ahmad-luqman
body:
## Summary

Broadens the M3 eleven-instruction slice to all of RV32I plus the M2 trap subset, and runs the M1 C self-check on the RTL.

- **Memory port**: the strobe (`mem_strb`, renamed from `mem_wstrb`) names the byte lanes of reads as well as writes, so a byte load of the console status is distinguishable from a word load; the contract records this in `docs/rv32.md` ("Behavior fixed in M4"). The emulator is unchanged.
- **Core**: `lb/lh/lbu/lhu/sh` with lane muxes and sign or zero extension; the eight ALU operations with a barrel shifter and one 33-bit subtractor whose `eq/lt/ltu` flags serve `slt*` and all six branches; PC-relative targets from a separate adder; `jalr`, `fence`; the four CSRs, `csrr*` in all six forms, `mret`.
- **Traps vector** through `mtvec` and report on a `trap` pulse of the retirement port; a trap before the previous handler retires an instruction halts as `double-fault`, the emulator's rule. Every trace, trap lines included, is now identical on both backends; the M3 `unsupported` halt is gone.
- **Self-check on hardware**: `make run-rv32-rtl` / `run-rv32-rtl-verilator` run `build/rv32/selfcheck.bin` to `PASS 807d9fad` with the emulator's 32,610-line trace; 138,495 cycles unstalled (4 × 24,555 + 5 × 8,055), 40,665 more per stall cycle. Both join `make test-rv32`.
- **Harness**: `$fatal` on a trap after an accepted write; the runner takes `--program loop|full`, `--image`, `--expect-console`, prints and checks the cycle relation.
- **Docs**: `docs/rv32-rtl.md` is the M4 record with the coverage/limitations table; `docs/rv32-to-gates.md` adds the comparator, shifter, lanes, trap path, three waveforms (stalled `sb`, sign vs zero extension, a discarded `x0` write), and the new synthesis table; roadmap, README, PLAN updated; the M5 session is listed.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `make test-rv32-rtl` / `-verilator` | 29 tests, both simulators |
| `make run-rv32-rtl` / `-verilator` | `PASS 807d9fad`, 32,610 identical lines, cycle formula holds |
| `make lint-rv32` | clean (`--Wall --language 1364-2005`) |
| `make synth-rv32` | 8,175 cells, 1,457 flip-flops, no latches (M3: 5,777 / 1,331) |
| `make test-rv32` end to end, `make test`, `test-alu`, `test-sap8`, `test-simd4` | pass |
| Pre-push review pass (code, tests, comments, silent failures) | findings fixed in the last commit; a 700-program random differential fuzz found no divergence |

body:
The delay was mine, added last round. Chasing a scroll-derived target at a rate that rises with scroll speed sounds like "it moves as fast as you scroll" and is not the same thing: a chase is always behind, and on a slow deliberate scroll — where the rate is lowest and you are watching most closely — it lagged the page visibly.

The scroll is the animation. The slot's centre meeting the viewport's is upright, every position between is a fixed angle, and the word is simply put there. It still turns at the speed you scroll and still lies back down on the way up, because both of those were always properties of the position mapping rather than of the chase. Lenis has already smoothed the scroll; smoothing what is derived from it only added delay.

The pointer tilt stays damped — the pointer jumps, and easing toward it is the whole effect — and the entrance is added on top of it undamped.

Measured against where the scroll puts it: stepping down 1 → 0.974 → 0.520 → 0.065 → 0, back up 0.292 → 0.974 → 1, and sampled 150ms, 400ms and 800ms into a flick. The gap between where it should be and where it is reads 0.0000 at every one.

The hero's `hello` is untouched — an earlier read of this had me change its exit tumble, and that is reverted.

author: carlosdanyell
body:
## O que muda

O Neon Words vai de 25 para 50 fases, o catálogo antigo passa por uma revisão de palavras e cada fase ganha palavras bônus que saem das mesmas letras mas não entram na grade.

**Fases 26 a 50** — rodas de 6 a 8 letras e 9 ou 10 palavras por cruzadinha, um degrau acima das anteriores. Cada fase parte de uma palavra-base (CAVALO, FLORESTA, GUITARRA, MAGNETO, ESTRELA...) e usa só palavras do português corrente, sem acento na grafia correta, porque a grade mostra as letras sem acento.

**Revisão das fases já publicadas** — nove fases repetiam a mesma palavra no singular e no plural, e quatro palavras só cabiam na grade perdendo o acento ou a cedilha:

- 07 LETRAS → RESTA · 08 CANTOS → COSTA e CONTAS → SACO · 09 AMIGOS → GOSMA · 13 HORAS → ROSNA · 16 ALTOS → ESTALO · 17 CAMPOS → PASMO · 18 VIOLAS → AVISO e OLIVAS → LISO · 20 PONTES → TENSO · 24 VARAS → SALVA
- 15 BRACO → BROCA · 17 MACO → MOSCA · 19 ARDUA → AGUDA e AGUA → RUGA

Nome, cor, letras e desbloqueios dessas fases continuam os mesmos; só a lista de palavras mudou e a grade foi remontada a partir dela. Quem já tinha essas fases salvas perde apenas as palavras trocadas.

**Palavras bônus** — 189 palavras em 49 das 50 fases (a primeira é tutorial). Valem 5 pontos por letra, aparecem no placar e no diálogo, e não são necessárias para completar a cruzadinha. Dão uma saída para quem travou sem precisar gastar dica.

## Como testei

- [x] Abri no celular (emulação em 320×568, 340×640, 360×640, 390×844 e paisagem 760×420) na orientação que o jogo usa
- [x] `play.html?game=neon-words&debug=1` sem erro no console

Verificações no navegador: fase concluída pelo teclado abre a tela certa, bônus pontua e entra no chip, bônus repetido é recusado, palavra de fora continua recusada, seletor com as 50 fases, e a tela de conquista cabe sem rolar de 340×640 para cima.

## Checklist

- [x] Arquivo novo ou alterado em `core/`, `games/`, `assets/` ou nas páginas: está em `ASSETS` e `VERSION` subiu no `sw.js` (v38 → v39)
- [x] Jogo novo: não se aplica — o Neon Words já está no catálogo; atualizei a contagem de fases no `core/registry.js` e no `README.md`
- [x] Testes passando: 76 testes, incluindo `tests/neon-words.test.mjs`, que passa a conferir o catálogo inteiro (letras que formam cada palavra, ausência de singular e plural juntos, desbloqueios que chegam depois de palavras suficientes, cruzamentos válidos, nenhuma sequência na grade fora da fase, ligação entre todas as palavras, fase vencível do começo ao fim e o fluxo das palavras bônus)

author: yehor-design
body:
Slice 28's composer task. The Notion shape ADR-0028 delivered is unchanged — the
708 px column, the 56 px gutter, the flat `/` menu, the input rules, the
shortcuts. What changed is everything the composer used to keep to itself.

## The cover stated its value as a fill

One of four buttons was rendered `primary` and that was the whole signal:
colour alone (WCAG 1.4.1), announced to nobody, and two of the four dispatched
the same `{ mode: "automatic" }`. The section now prints "Обрано: Фото 2",
every toggle carries `aria-pressed`, a thumbnail is labelled with the
photograph's own name rather than with an instruction to do what has already
been done, and the duplicate is gone. The focal point gained the same visible
readout beside the `aria-valuetext` only a screen reader could hear.

## Leaving with unpublished work warns once

`beforeunload` covered a reload, a close and an address typed into the bar, and
none of the ways a reader actually leaves: a press on a link in the shell is a
client-side navigation that fires no unload event at all, so the composer
unmounted and the writing was gone without a word. `UnpublishedWorkGuard`
watches clicks in the capture phase, stops only a same-origin link that leads
somewhere else — never one the gardener wrote into the entry — and re-issues
the navigation they pressed once they have chosen. In the product's dialog, not
the browser's.

## The input rules are on the screen

`## `, `[x] `, `~~` and the rest were findable only by a reader who already
knew Markdown. `JournalShortcutSheet` lists every rule and every key and
**generates every row from the module that implements it**, so it cannot teach
a key that does nothing.

## Two more

- **The composer's files left the shadcn bridge**: 116 legacy class names
  retired across fifteen files, and three hand-rolled dialog buttons became
  `Button`. The names were aliases of the same colours, so nothing moved;
  `text-xs` at 12 px became `text-caption` at 13, which DESIGN.md §3 requires.
- **The receipt after publishing said "Збережено приватно"** — saved privately
  — on a product with no drafts and no private entries, three lines under a
  control that says an entry is public and indexable at once. It now says so,
  and names the entry it published.

## Proof

Run in a real browser, which is the only place three of these are visible.
`tests/journal-notion-composer.spec.ts` gained a keyboard-only pass: the column
and gutter measured, a block moved by ArrowUp on the focused handle and its
announcement read back, the sheet opened and checked against the rule modules,
the cover's value changed by key, and the leave dialog both cancelled and
confirmed — with axe over the whole document while the sheet is open.

That axe pass found two things: the sheet's scroller was reachable by pointer
and not by keyboard (`scrollable-region-focusable`), and `base-ui`'s focus
guards report `aria-hidden-focus` wherever any overlay is open — the library's
standard focus-lock sentinels, excluded by selector with the reason beside it.
`tests/catalog-picker.spec.ts` gained the result-count announcement.

- Full browser gate: **164 passed, 1 skipped**
- 3,757 unit tests, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, every mechanical gate green

## Two notes for the reader

- **708 px is a cap, not a width.** ADR-0028's column is a `max-width`; inside
  the shell's 704 px content column the canvas renders at 656 — 70–75 Cyrillic
  characters, inside DESIGN.md §3's measure. A proof that asserts a rendered
  708 asserts something true on no screen the product has.
- **The card's "40 px gutter" is a slip.** ADR-0028 D3 says 56, and 56 is what
  ships and what the proof measures.

author: apage224
body:
Closes #143, #135, #136.

## What changes

- `stripEsm` tracks a multi-line `import` or `export` statement from its opening line to the line that closes it, with inline code held out and quoted or template spans consumed rather than counted. It enters that state only for a declaration shape (a binding followed by `=`, `(`, `{`, or `export {` / `export *` / `export default` forms), and if a statement never closes before the run ends the lines are kept, so prose that starts with "import" or "export" survives.
- MDX comments and bare `{expression}` lines are dropped from MDX renditions (fenced code exempt); plain Markdown pages are untouched.
- `reduceTags` parses tags into a tree and renders prop-bearing parts to Markdown instead of dropping them: components with `title` and `href` become `- [title](href): children` list items in source order, a titled `Card` becomes a heading over its body, an `AsciiTerminal` with inline `lines` becomes a fenced text block. HTML anchors are excluded from the link rule. Titles are escaped for link syntax and targets with whitespace or parentheses use the pointy form, so text from another repository cannot forge a link.
- JSON-LD is serialized through `serializeJsonLd`, which escapes `<`, `>` and `&`.
- `renderMarkdown` gains an `mdx` option (default `false`); both plugin call sites pass the page's extension.

## Why

Renditions and llms output are what agents read. A site with data arrays in MDX shipped the array source as page text, card grids lost every title and link, and generated pages arrived nearly empty. neuralspotx measured 94 of 149 routes gutted before working around it site-side (AmbiqAI/neuralspotx#256).

## Consumer-visible changes on the next alpha

- Renditions grow where components carried content and shrink where they carried source; `llms-full.txt` moves with them.
- JSON-LD strings are escaped.
- New exports from `starlight/discoverability.ts`; `renderMarkdown` accepts `mdx`.
- A site that composes its own renditions from generated models should keep doing so and drop only component-link recovery; stacking produced no duplication in the neuralspotx consumer test.

## Validation

`npm run validate` (240 tests, 31 new for the rendition pass), `npm run docs:build` (gallery assertions: card links and transcript fence present, no MDX source), `npm run docs:test` (148 passed on a quiet machine; earlier failures were spread across unrelated suites while another Playwright run shared the machine). Gallery renditions diffed line by line against main: the only removals are MDX comments, MDX expressions and card descriptions that moved into their list items. Hardening commit produced byte-identical gallery output to the first commit. Consumer test (run by the reviewer): packed tarball installed into a copy of the neuralspotx site; with the site's own rendition composer disabled, generated CLI pages still need it because their argument tables live in component props, and stacking that composer on this branch produced no duplicated links.

## Release note

Next pre-release, 0.1.0-alpha.16: additive exports and a consumer-visible change in rendition output.

author: teaspoonai
body:
## What

Closes the one residual #49's formal model left open. `stt.py` pairs the engine's dones with the commits it sent **by order**, because the wire did not say which done answers a client commit and which is the engine's own endpointer closing a segment. When an engine close is already on the wire as a commit goes out, that close takes the commit's stamp and the commit's real answer — the rest of the sentence — lands as nobody's. `SttCommit.tla` keeps that as the shipped design's single counterexample (`sc_final_stop`), proves the turn never ends stale any other way (`sc_final_stop_residual`), and proves the property holds outright once the engine marks its dones (`sc_final_stop_marked`).

teagram-engine #36 (deployed on .234 since 2026-09-20 14:28) makes `transcription.done` carry `"reason": "commit" | "vad"`. This PR reads it:

- a done marked `vad` is placed as the engine's own close whatever the commit queue holds — the queue keeps the commit for its own answer;
- no `reason` (an older engine, the streaming backend's synthesized done) → the queue pairs as before.

**Assumes an engine that never skips a final commit's done.** The pre-#36 engine's "start generation" guard (`!audio_received`) could silently drop a final commit landing right after its own VAD close with no audio chunk grabbed in between — no done at all; with the brain now waiting on that commit's answer that would be a turn stranded to the 5 s watchdog. #36 closes it (`!audio_ever && !commit_final`), and #36 is what .234 runs; on an engine without the field this PR is inert anyway.

Trust in the marker is total and the drift is one-sided: a done marked `commit` with nothing queued is logged at WARNING (cannot happen on a correct engine) and taken as the engine's own close; an engine that labelled a commit's answer `vad` would leave that stamp queued for the next done to inherit, which only the engine can prevent — said so in the `_commits` comment.

Stamping is unchanged: a marked-vad close with words is the next stop's, wordless the last commit's, and it still keeps a held segment. The formal README now says the marked rows are the shipped configuration on that engine.

## Tests

`test_a_marking_engines_close_in_the_stops_silence_leaves_the_commit_its_answer`: the ceiling path on the new engine, in the order the turn's end rides on — the engine's own close in the stop's silence marked `vad` (stamped as the next stop's), then the ceiling's commit answered EMPTY marked `commit` (stamped with the stop): `[("final", 2), ("done", 1)]`, the turn ending on the `SegmentDoneFrame`. `test_a_done_the_engine_marks_as_its_own_never_takes_a_commits_place`: commit 1 out, the engine's own close lands first marked `vad` → the commit is not popped and its real answer keeps stamp 1 (`[("final", 2), ("final", 1)]`); the same wire unmarked pairs by the queue as before; a `commit`-marked done with nothing queued warns. Formal rows relabelled: the unmarked rows describe the engine before #36, the marked row the one .234 runs. Suite 53 passed / 2 skipped; `config_schema --check` clean.

## Verified on .234

The deployed engine (#36 @ dfd718c, since 2026-09-20 14:28) emits the field on every done — its journal: `done (3.0s audio, 16 chars, 1140 ms trailing silence credited, commit)`, `done (3.2s audio, 0 chars, 1500 ms trailing silence credited, vad)`.

## Deploy

Brain package only (pip recipe). Safe against either engine; the mispairing it closes only exists with the new one, which is what .234 runs now.

author: darthrater78
body:
Three commits, independent of each other.

### 1. `fix(eod)`: the end-of-day summary reported an intraday price

`_eod1_summary` read whatever the last poll left behind. The market-hours gate stops polling at the close, so with a 300s interval the day's final poll landed up to five minutes early — and a refresh requested at 16:00 or later was refused by the gate and handed back cache. The sensors then held that intraday value until the next open.

Observed on 2026-09-18: `sensor.ha_stock_app_voo_stock_price` last updated at **15:56:20 with 701.94** and stayed there all weekend. The settled close was **701.78** — the integration only picked it up after a restart left the coordinator with no cached data to return, which is the accidental proof that the provider serves the right number once asked after the close.

- New `StockCoordinator.async_force_refresh_now()` — sets the force flag and **awaits** `async_refresh()`. The existing `async_force_refresh()` is untouched: it goes through the debounced `async_request_refresh()`, so a caller reading `.data` immediately afterwards can still be handed the previous poll. Fine for the Refresh button, not for this.
- Summary moves **16:00 → 16:05**. The official close isn't settled the instant the bell rings; `_eod2_start_watch` already waits the same five minutes for the same reason.
- A failed refresh keeps the summary rather than losing it, and logs which way it failed — `async_refresh` signals through `last_update_success` rather than raising, so both paths are handled.

**Known limitation:** on an early-close day the summary still fires at 16:05, ~3h late, because the schedule is a fixed time rather than derived from `market_close_time()`. The forced fetch means the price it reports is the correct close even then. Deriving the schedule per-date needs date-aware arming inside `_schedule_daily`; not worth it for ~2 days a year.

**Not unit-tested:** the suite is deliberately HA-free (`market.py` only, per `tests/test_market.py`), and both changed paths need a `hass`. Verification is Monday's 16:05 — the price sensors should update then and match the official close.

### 2. `ci`: stop filtering pushes

A path-skipped workflow produces **no run at all**, not a skipped one, so `release.yml`'s gate — which queries `runs?head_sha=` and refuses to publish a tag with no passing CI run — reports "CI has never run for this SHA" for any commit CI skipped. Filtering pushes put a trap on the release path, reachable by tagging a docs-only commit, surfacing at exactly the wrong moment.

The filter stays on `pull_request` and comes off `push`. Every taggable commit now always has a run, and the coupling between the two workflows is removed rather than documented. PR churn is where the repeated runs were being spent, so the saving is largely kept — this costs one run per merge.

### 3. `chore`: ignore all of `.claude/`

Only `.claude/dev-skills-gates.md` was ignored, so `handoff.md` kept showing as untracked and `gh` warned about an uncommitted change on every PR.

---

No version bump — `2.7.13` will carry the `monarchmoneycommunity>=1.6.0` floor bump, and the EOD fix releases separately after it.

body:
Fixes #1537

Checklist for Pull Requests

- [x] Is there a related issue or pull request in [winget-pkgs](https://github.com/microsoft/winget-pkgs)? If so, add the link(s) below.
  - Relates to microsoft/winget-pkgs#438131

Manifests

- [x] Have you checked that there aren't other open [pull requests](https://github.com/pl4nty/winget-extras/pulls) for the same manifest update/change?
- [ ] Have you [validated](https://github.com/microsoft/winget-pkgs/blob/master/doc/Authoring.md#validation) your manifest locally with `winget validate --manifest <path>`?
- [ ] Have you tested your manifest locally with `winget install --manifest <path>`?
- [x] Does your manifest conform to the [1.28 schema](https://github.com/denelon/winget-pkgs/tree/docs/manifest-schema-1.28.0/doc/manifest/schema/1.28.0)?

Note: `<path>` is the directory's name containing the manifest you're submitting.

---

The download ships a single self-contained .NET executable in a ZIP, so it's a
`zip` installer with a `portable` nested installer. The ARP publisher is unusable
here — the binary's `CompanyName` is the product name, and a portable carries no
ARP entry at all — so the locale manifest names Qualcomm Technologies, Inc.

Qualcomm Software Center renders its catalog client-side and its product API
needs an account, so the shard is a script: the public Snapdragon enterprise
site hardcodes the current download URL in its bundle, and the bundle name
carries a build hash, so it reads the bundle out of the page before matching the
version. The download path carries a four-part file version (1.0.4.0) while the
release is named with three, matching the version in winget-pkgs#438131.

author: copilot
body:
PakistanLawSite’s `#archivedpatientGrid` surface could hang on large responses because `_capture_html()` still had paths that depended on full-page serialization. This change makes citation-grid capture always go through the compact snapshot path, avoids `page.content()` on that surface entirely, and limits citation-grid detail expansion to the run budget.

- **Capture path**
  - Detect `#archivedpatientGrid` up front and immediately render synthetic compact HTML.
  - Remove the oversized-only dependency for grid compaction so large and small grid pages follow the same safe path.
  - Preserve existing metadata (`content_guard`, row count, row cap, content length) on compact captures.

- **Snapshot cost**
  - Reduce DOM work during grid capture by reading table structure directly (`tHead`, `tBodies`, `rows`, `cells`) instead of broader selectors.
  - Use `textContent`-based previews and narrower fallback parsing for `casetypeid` extraction.

- **Citation-grid fan-out**
  - Bound detail-page fetches in citation-grid mode with `max_queries`, preventing a single oversized grid from expanding into unbounded downstream detail requests.

- **Regression coverage**
  - Add coverage for archived-grid compaction even when the page is not oversized.
  - Add coverage that citation-grid detail fetches stop at the configured run budget.

```python
async def _capture_html(self, *, resp=None) -> tuple[str, Dict[str, Any]]:
    content_length = self._header_int(resp, "content-length")
    if await self._has_archivedpatient_grid():
        snapshot = await self._capture_archived_grid_snapshot()
        html_compact = self._render_compact_archived_grid_html(snapshot or {})
        return html_compact, {
            "content_guard": "archivedpatientGrid_compact",
            "content_length": content_length,
        }
```

author: narumiruna
body:
## Outcome

Consolidate duplicated domain behavior across Backend, Web, Android, and validation tooling without changing supported HTTP contracts, storage formats, or UI copy/layout.

- Backend: one route-revision codec and narrow library sort-order/sync-event persistence helpers; retain transaction orchestration and event order; remove unused SharingService forwarding aliases.
- Web: one share-link hook with the existing distinct control surfaces; one password form and state hook preserving each account menu's original lifetime.
- Android: typed library route modes with unchanged Room TEXT names and legacy Once fallback; shared cloud conversion, random-route rules, and presentation helpers that retain fractional-format differences.
- Tooling: replace the obsolete Nest prerequisite, run canonical Just recipes from hooks, and untrack/ignore TypeScript build info.

Signed commit: `8409707`. Existing plan/index work was preserved and updated. No dependency, lockfile, schema, migration, CSS, image, release, tag, deployment, or publication changes.

## Evidence

- Backend on Node.js 22.23.2: lint, **139 unit tests (21 suites)**, **8 E2E cases (3 suites)**, typecheck, build, and changed-file Prettier check pass.
- Web on Node.js 22.23.2: Biome (**69 files**), **13 tests**, typecheck and production build pass. Typecheck ran twice; the local build-info cache is ignored and untracked.
- Android on Java 26: Spotless, Detekt, **154 JVM tests**, and debug APK build pass using the installed Homebrew SDK. No connected-device operations.
- Room generated version/identity remain `2` / `ca31ac6542d7f35fc7552b09839c5db4`; `routes.mode` remains `TEXT NOT NULL`.
- Chrome DevTools Protocol against a local production build: all four Map/Library × places/routes share flows pass GET error/404, rejected/successful create/update, clipboard failure/success, disable/re-enable, close/reopen focus restoration, and public-page navigation. Both password menus pass rejected/successful submissions, exact payloads, field clearing, and original close/reopen state behavior. **67 intercepted fixture requests; no real account/database writes.** This is UI validation, not a live database integration.
- Non-writing configuration hooks, canonical Android/Web hooks, complete diff review, and `git diff --check` pass. No binary/image files in the commit.

## Open gates / risks

**Draft: not ready to claim the saved plan complete.**

1. `just android-ui` executes but **all 12 cases fail with `ScreenshotImageNotFoundException` because reference images are absent**. Baselines were not created, updated, or committed. Existing references or explicit user disposition are required.
2. The saved plan requires explicit user acceptance before closure. It remains active, with all blocked/aggregate acceptance items unchecked; the separate Android workflow plan is untouched.
3. Browser fixtures do not replace live PostgreSQL integration or Android screenshot comparison.
4. Existing `npm ci` audit findings remain: Backend 2 moderate/5 high, Web 1 moderate. No out-of-scope dependency remediation.
5. A broad hook probe encountered an existing missing final newline in `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`; its automatic edit was reverted. Focused non-writing hooks pass, and the unrelated workflow is unchanged.

Full task-by-task evidence: [`docs/plans/2026-09-21_repository-simplification-plan.md`](docs/plans/2026-09-21_repository-simplification-plan.md).

## Summary

author: naek56
body:
## Ce qui change

Le titre passe de Gloria Hallelujah à **Roboto Mono**. Trois réglages devaient être repris à zéro, parce qu'une chasse fixe est l'inverse d'une manuscrite sur chacun des trois :

**La chasse est fixe, donc la ligne est longue.** Chaque glyphe avance de 0,6 em, espaces et points compris : « Créer. Échouer. Évoluer. » fait 24 caractères, soit **14,4 em bruts** là où la manuscrite en faisait 11,5. La même ligne au même corps serait 25 % plus large. Le corps maximal redescend donc de 4,6rem à **3,3rem**, et l'approche repasse en **négatif (−0,035 em)** : sur une chasse fixe, resserrer ne fait pas se cogner les lettres, ça reprend une partie de l'air que la grille impose entre elles. C'est exactement l'inverse de la règle qui valait pour des lettres détachées à terminaisons obliques.

**L'interligne redescend de 1,28 à 1,14** — le 1,28 logeait l'accent aigu de Gloria Hallelujah, qui montait très au-dessus de la capitale. Roboto Mono a des métriques ordinaires.

**La graisse remonte à 500** — une chasse fixe dessine des fûts plus fins à corps égal, et le 400 s'effaçait sous le champ de lames. 500 est le dernier cran avant que les contreformes du « é » et du « É » ne commencent à se fermer.

Gloria Hallelujah n'a plus de porteur et quitte le projet (lien Google Fonts et préchargement compris). Roboto Mono est chargée en 300..700 : c'est un seul fichier variable, demander une graisse de plus ne coûte pas un octet.

## Une conséquence inattendue de la chasse fixe

Le centrage optique n'a plus besoin d'être conditionné au nombre de lignes. Mesuré au scan des colonnes d'encre, l'encre tombait à gauche de :

| corps | lignes | décalage mesuré |
|---|---|---|
| 52,8 px | 1 | 0,0663 em |
| 36,1 px | 1 | 0,0693 em |
| 27,2 px | 2 | 0,0735 em |

Trois valeurs quasi identiques — et c'est une propriété de la chasse fixe : tous les glyphes partagent la même gouttière, donc le défaut ne dépend plus de *quelles* lettres commencent et finissent la ligne, seulement de l'approche qui traîne derrière la dernière. **La media query qui conditionnait la correction disparaît.** Résidus après correction : +0,20 px, +0,03 px, −0,10 px.

## Vérifications

- **Symétrie** au scan des colonnes d'encre à 320 / 390 / 768 / 1280 / 1440 px : titre, chapô et mot-marque à **0 px du centre**, nav à 0, aucun débordement horizontal.
- **Contraste** remesuré sur le pixel rendu, quatre instants répartis sur quinze secondes d'animation du fond : bande du titre **15,76:1**, bande du chapô **7,14:1**. Le titre monte un peu plus haut que la manuscrite et se pose donc sur un champ plus vide — c'est meilleur qu'avant (11,41:1).
- **Bascule 1 → 2 lignes** mesurée entre 390 et 420 px. Jamais 3 lignes, aucun débordement de 320 à 1920 px.
- L'écart d'encre entre le titre et le chapô vaut 40 px pour une hauteur de capitale de 37 px — la respiration est conservée malgré l'interligne plus serré.
- `prefers-reduced-motion` intact, `tsc` et `vite build` passent.

Le reste de la page ne bouge pas : l'intro, le fond en lames de verre, le bouton et le chapô sont inchangés.

author: baristaze
body:
## What changed

Two sections land in `architecture.md`, and a new lens group judges them.

**Operations.** People steer, agents maintain. Every operational task is a skill a person runs with an agent, and the boundary is the credential the skill holds, never the prompt. The section makes that concrete:

- **Operator Roles**: administrator (a person; creates and destroys, nothing else), deployer (the pipeline, the only role that writes; production split into plan and apply), investigator (every signal and every description, read-only, no secret value, no data-bucket object, no database row), supporter (the investigator plus a named tenant's rows through the operator plane, with a read allowlist entry). Roles named `<product>-<role>-<environment>`, fenced by tag; the agents' principal is one user that can only assume the read-only roles.
- **Operator Credentials**: a skill names its profile, verifies it holds that one and no wider, reads the rest from one owner-only file per environment; the local stack is an environment every skill runs against.
- **Operational Skills**: the built-in nine (`ops-investigate`, `ops-watch`, `ops-root-cause`, `ops-infra-as-code`, `ops-cloud-deployment-create`, `ops-cloud-deployment-nuke`, `ops-simulate-traffic`, `stress-test-create-or-update`, `stress-test-run`); the watch is spawned and burst-resistant; the first responder is an agent that reads the platform's size before it escalates.
- **Dashboards and Alarms as Code**, **Scale-Out as a Lever** (one root variable, off by default, every lever below it on), **Cost Boundaries** (a budget and an anomaly monitor from the first apply), **Creating and Destroying an Environment** (two scripted, dry-runnable administrator runs; production destroyed only behind a typed name and a merged change), **Traffic and Stress** (one generator drives the edge; the stress test is the same generator with a scenario and a target; the gate proves the wiring in thirty seconds), **The Telemetry Round Trip** (one test reads every signal back by request id through one reader interface with a local and a cloud impl).

**Documentation as Code.** A README at every abstraction level in its own language; `om/README.md` for a reader with no code; `llms.txt` at the root names what each audience is served, and exposure is by listing; every document speaks product, technology, or service.

**Lenses.** `lenses/ops.md`, 27 lenses (`OPS-01` to `OPS-27`), 229 in all; `arch-review-ops` generated; `arch-review-full` fans out to eight.

**Skills.** Nine project-local skill templates under `skills/_shared/ops-skills/`; `arch-scaffold-new` copies them into a new tree and its skeleton gains the ops distribution, the READMEs, the map, the scripts, the roles, the budget, the alarms, the dashboard, the switches, and a wiring-check step. `docs/adopting.md` gains "Operate with the built-in skills".

**Narrowed.** "Load testing" leaves "What This Document Does Not Cover" as a shape; its numbers stay there. Alerting narrows to the thresholds of the alarms.

Minor: rules added, none removed or reversed. Version 0.19.0 in `plugin.json`, the marketplace manifest, the changelog, and `docs/adopting.md`.

## Evidence

`make check`: lint 0 issues in 53 files; lenses ok, 229 lenses in 8 groups; leaks ok, 45 files; links ok, 53 files; toc ok; version ok 0.19.0; generated skills ok; skills ok, 19 skills, 8 review groups; agents ok. `uvx pytest tests -q`: 80 passed (the Makefile's `python3` has no pytest, as before).

The reference implementation adopts this release in a tadas pull request the same day, where the nine skills are run against the local stack; template defects found there land here before this is marked ready.

author: lbedner
body:
`app.cli.migrate_gen` passes `include_object`, `compare_type` and
`render_as_batch` through `config.attributes["configure"]`. That's the
contract. `env.py` was the half that never read it — it called
`context.configure()` with a fixed keyword list:

```python
context.configure(
    connection=connection,
    target_metadata=target_metadata,
    include_schemas=True,
)
```

So every option a caller set was dropped. `render_as_batch` among them,
which is the one that hurts: without batch mode autogenerate emits

```sql
ALTER TABLE agent ALTER COLUMN memory_modules DROP NOT NULL
```

and SQLite has no such statement. Every generated revision is invalid.

Found while adding the auth service: the generator wrote a revision and
then **failed replaying its own output**.

## The silence is the defect

An option that is dropped looks exactly like an option nobody set.
Nothing fails at the point of the mistake; it surfaces much later as
invalid SQL inside a migration nobody hand-wrote.

## The shape is upstream's, on purpose

One options dict, merged with the caller's, and no default passed as
its own keyword beside `**options` — that raises
`TypeError: got multiple values for keyword argument` the moment a
caller overrides the same option, i.e. exactly when it matters.

Matching upstream also keeps the next `aegis update` from conflicting
here.

## Not a backport

aegis-stack's `env.py.jinja` already has this. Steward's predates it,
and `add-service` had no reason to touch `env.py` since auth doesn't
change it — so the project ended up with **today's `migrate_gen` and a
0.11.0 `env.py` that could not hear it**. That mismatch is its own
upstream finding and is filed separately.

## Test

Two guards, both cheap:

- the online path actually consults `config.attributes["configure"]`
- no default is passed as a second keyword beside `**options`, which
  would collide precisely when a caller overrides it

`uv run poe check`: 5302 passed, 11 skipped.

author: jajjer
body:
## What & why

The #137 echinocandin verdict-accuracy arm posted a **measured Rung-A FAIL** (VME 4/40 = 10.0% [4.0, 23.1]; `work/RESULTS_diagnostic_accuracy.md`). `docs/DIAGNOSTIC_GO_NO_GO.md` left the **Rung C decision open** — "document a narrow panel vs. extend coverage" — because the *mechanism* behind each miss was uncharacterised, and framed the ceiling as **off-panel / efflux**.

This PR characterises the misses from data already on disk and turns that open decision into an evidence-backed one. The finding corrects the doc: **the ceiling is FKS1-hotspot-shaped, not efflux.**

## Findings (reproducible — `scripts/characterize_coverage_ceiling.py` reproduces the measured confusion exactly)

- **All 4 VME misses are FKS1 HS3**: B19617/B19618 W691L, B22769 W691C, B21978 M690I (unresolved even by the source paper) — a hotspot the caller has **no window for** (it reads only HS1 635–643, HS2 1350–1358).
- **The 11 abstentions are mostly HS1 subs the caller already reads but never panel-tags**: 9× D642Y/F635, 1× HS2 R1354S.
- **Projection:** an HS3 window (688–698, anchor W691, reference-verified) → **VME 1/40 = 2.5% [0.4, 12.9]**, clears the bar; widening the HS1/HS2 panel converts abstentions→detections.

## Changes (all additive; measured artifacts untouched, relevant tests green)

- `scripts/characterize_coverage_ceiling.py` — reproducible join, reuses the run's Wilson math
- `work/RESULTS_diagnostic_coverage_ceiling.md` — mechanism table + projection
- `docs/DIAGNOSTIC_GO_NO_GO.md` — corrected C2 / Rung A / Rung C / §6 (were "efflux/off-panel"); Rung C now favours *extending the FKS1 panel*
- `work/PREREGISTRATION_diagnostic_accuracy_v2.md` (+ pinned sha) — freezes the exact caller change and the unchanged re-measure bar

## Two integrity guardrails (both in the prereg)

1. **Anti-circularity:** panel mutants must be pinned from literature **independent of** PMC12323592, or "recovering" them on the same isolates is overfitting.
2. **Projection, not a re-claim:** the measured post-extension VME needs the caller change **+ a GCP re-run**. Rung A stays a measured NO-GO until then.

## Scope note

The caller edit is **deferred to its own PR** — a panel-bearing HS3 window ripples into `_FKS1_PANEL_WINDOWS`, `format_call` source strings, prevalence resolution, stored snapshots, and 6 test files. This PR is analysis + decision + frozen prereg only.

author: mattleyit
body:
Closes #5

Applica il lavoro consegnato da Claude Code / Cowork sul progetto Google Cloud. Nessun codice eseguibile: solo configurazione nel manifest e documentazione.

## Cosa contiene
- `manifest.json`: campi `key` (chiave pubblica) e `oauth2` (`client_id` + scope `calendar.readonly`).
- `.env.example`: riferimenti progetto GCP, Client ID, Extension ID, percorso della chiave privata.
- `docs/google-cloud-setup.md`: setup completo, derivazione dell'ID dalla chiave, procedura di ricostruzione da zero, limiti della modalita' Test, modello di sicurezza.
- `README.md`: sezione setup OAuth con la tabella dei valori.

## Decisione chiave: Extension ID fissato con una chiave RSA
La issue chiedeva di registrare l'extension ID come origine autorizzata, ma quell'ID non esisteva ancora: un'estensione unpacked deriva l'ID dal percorso della cartella (cambi cartella, cambia l'ID) e l'ID definitivo lo assegna il Web Store al primo upload. Legare il client OAuth a un ID provvisorio avrebbe significato rifare le credenziali dopo.

Con il campo `key` nel manifest, Chrome deriva l'ID dalla chiave pubblica: **un solo Extension ID valido in locale e in produzione**.

## Verifica fatta
Derivazione dell'ID ricalcolata dalla chiave nel manifest: `ghoaagpljnphhilolmhpbndjhabpfcbo`, combacia con l'Item ID registrato sul client OAuth. La chiave pubblica nel manifest corrisponde alla chiave privata generata.

## Cosa non ho potuto verificare io
- Che il consent screen e il client OAuth siano configurati come documentato (accesso alla console Google: solo Cowork / Matteo).
- Il flusso di auth end-to-end: arriva con la issue #3.

## Nota per la issue #3
In stato *Test* il refresh token scade dopo **7 giorni**. Il flusso di auth deve gestire la riautenticazione senza rompere il polling: `getAuthToken({ interactive: false })` va trattato come fallimento atteso, non come errore, con fallback a un prompt interattivo.

## Sicurezza
Il `.pem` con la chiave privata non entra nel repo (coperto da `.gitignore`). Client ID e campo `key` sono valori pubblici per definizione: il flusso Chrome Extension non ha client secret e Google lega il client all'Extension ID.

author: nicolaschan
body:
## Summary

Windows users on 1.7.x reported choppy audio plus stream errors printed over the TUI. Two separate causes, both addressed here.

### Pacer removal
- The input hub throttled every chunk with a `tokio::time::sleep_until` on a 10ms cadence, re-anchoring the deadline whenever it woke late.
- tokio timers on Windows fire ~15ms late ([tokio #5021](https://github.com/tokio-rs/tokio/issues/5021)), which is past the 10ms period, so the re-anchor branch ran on alternate chunks and the sender ran at ~80% of real time. Peers heard the Windows user starve every fifth fill, and the sender's outgoing delay grew without bound.
- The pacer was introduced in #50 alongside `Fixed(480)`, most likely to smooth the 2s capture fragments that the PulseAudio backend (#47) delivered under `BufferSize::Default`. `Fixed(480)` fixed that at the source, leaving the pacer with nothing to do on a real microphone.
- Synthetic sources in tests are now paced by a `Paced` wrapper in `tests/common/sine.rs` using anchored deadlines, so test hubs still stream at real time without the slow-down.
- `bursty_source_is_paced_to_10ms` tested the pacer and is removed (same deletion as #76, which can be closed if this merges first).

### Buffer size
- `Fixed(480)` is now requested only when cpal's default host is PulseAudio, clamped to the range it reports. Every other host gets `BufferSize::Default`.
- PulseAudio is the one backend where the request matters: unset attributes mean a 2s fragment and 2s target length. On WASAPI the callback period is always the device period regardless, and [Microsoft's docs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/audioclient/nf-audioclient-iaudioclient-initialize) say shared-mode event-driven streams should pass 0. CoreAudio and ALSA defaults are within a few ms of 480 frames.
- Host detection uses `HostId::name()` so there is no `cfg` branching.

Not included: the `eprintln!` in the two cpal error callbacks still writes to stderr under the TUI. That is a separate small change.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test --workspace` (adds three unit tests for `callback_buffer_size`)
- [ ] Windows user confirms peers hear them cleanly for a multi-minute call

author: svollmi1
body:
## At `instances: 1` there is nothing to promote

A single-instance CNPG cluster is not a database that fails over — a node reboot is a full outage for it. Today's k8sworker04 reboot demonstrated this with a clean control: same node, same event, three databases, outcome determined entirely by this one field.

| cluster | instances | outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `authentik-db` | **1** | **~6 minute outage** (19:18:04 → 19:23:58) |
| `harbor-db` | 2 | `READY 1`, kept serving |
| `vollmint-db` | 2 | `READY 1`, kept serving |

The authentik pod rescheduled to k8sworker02 and then sat on a `Multi-Attach error` while its Longhorn volume detached from the rebooting node and reattached to the new one. SSO was unavailable for every service behind authentik forward-auth for that window.

This changes `instances: 1` → `2` for the three clusters still at one: `authentik-db`, `jellystat-db`, `shlink-db`.

## Capacity, checked before committing

Per the Longhorn rule in `.claude/rules/storage.md` — never size a PVC without verifying Longhorn can schedule it:

```
aggregate headroom (max − scheduled, over-provisioning 100%):  493.5 GiB
  k8sworker01  38.8    k8sworker04 215.8
  k8sworker02  55.8    k8sworker05  43.7
  k8sworker03 115.8    k8sworker06  23.7

cost: 10Gi + 5Gi + 5Gi = 20 GiB of PVC
      × 3 replicas     = 60 GiB scheduled   (12.2% of headroom)
```

Every node has room for the largest new replica (10Gi); the tightest is k8sworker06 at 23.7 GiB. Pod overhead is +250m CPU and +1.3 GiB of memory requests across six workers.

## What happens on reconcile

CNPG bootstraps each new replica with a base backup from its primary, so expect brief I/O on the primary of each cluster while it clones — 10Gi, 5Gi and 5Gi respectively. Worth landing when the cluster is otherwise quiet rather than alongside other churn, since for these three the primary is currently the only copy.

No other field changes. The two clusters already at 2 set no `affinity`, PDB or `primaryUpdate` config, so CNPG's defaults are what is actually in use here and are inherited unchanged. All three validated with `kubectl apply --dry-run=server`.

## Noted, not fixed here

Velero is FSB-backing-up every CNPG `pgdata` volume today (94–190 PodVolumeBackups each across the five clusters). Per `.claude/rules/velero.md` those copies are torn — FSB walks a directory postgres is actively writing — and CNPG is already backed up properly by barman to MinIO with a B2 mirror. This change takes that from 5 torn copies a night to 8.

That is pre-existing and a separate concern, so it is not mixed in here. Worth its own issue to exclude `pgdata` from FSB.

author: chrisflav
body:
Closes taxis #500 ("No CI gate for the frontend"), and folds in taxis #504 (the async timeout).

## What was ungated

No workflow in `.github/workflows/` mentioned `npm`, `node`, `vitest`, `tsc` or `eslint`. `build-fork.yml` and `build-internal.yml` both call `build-test-shared.yml`, which is backend-only, and the one place the SPA is touched at all is the `docker/production/spa` image build — which runs `vite build`, and `vite build` strips types rather than checking them.

So ~58k lines of TypeScript and 33 vitest files were gated by nothing, while ~12k lines of Python carry a hard 100 % coverage gate.

This is not hypothetical: **PR #305** was pushed with `npm run typecheck` failing on its own new test code (two `TS2322` errors), every CI check went green, and only a reviewer running `tsc` by hand caught it. This job would have failed that PR.

## What the job runs

New standalone workflow `.github/workflows/check-frontend.yml`, shaped like `check-translations.yml` / `pre-commit.yml`: triggers on `pull_request` and on pushes to `main`, one job, `working-directory: frontend`.

- `actions/setup-node@v4`, Node **22** — the same major `docker/production/spa/Dockerfile` builds the SPA with (`FROM node:22-alpine`). There is no `engines` field and no `.nvmrc` anywhere in the repo, so the Dockerfile is the only statement of intent; pinned rather than guessed.
- npm cache keyed on `frontend/package-lock.json`.
- `npm ci` (not `npm install`), then `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test`, `npm run build`.

## Fork safety

`build-fork.yml` uses `pull_request_target` because the backend build needs secrets (GHCR push, PR comments), and that forces the `check-source` dance in `build-fork.yml`/`build-internal.yml` so the two do not both run.

The job also declares `permissions: contents: read` rather than relying on the repository default staying read-only — it executes fork-authored code, so the token it gets should not depend on a settings toggle. (Verified on the run: `GITHUB_TOKEN Permissions — Contents: read, Metadata: read`.)

A typecheck/test/build job needs **no secrets** and no write permissions. So a plain `pull_request` trigger is correct here, and safer: it checks out the fork's code in an unprivileged context, which is exactly what you want when you are about to run that code's `npm ci` and test suite. It also means the `check-source` split does not apply — there is only one workflow, it runs the same way for forks and internal PRs, and nothing needs to be de-duplicated.

## Why the `asyncUtilTimeout` change is in the same PR (#504)

`frontend/src/test/setup.ts` never called `configure({ asyncUtilTimeout })`, so every `findBy*`/`waitFor` ran on testing-library's own **1000 ms** default — the generous `testTimeout: 20000` in `vitest.config.ts` does not raise it. That produced intermittent failures (observed three times, always `Unable to find role="button" and name "Bearbeiten"` in `src/features/finance/statements.integration.test.tsx`). The mechanism is proven: forcing the budget to 1 ms reproduces the exact error on the exact tests, and the file passes 69/69 in isolation and survives a 14× mean slowdown — what kills it is a single scheduler stall over a second.

CI runners are precisely the loaded machines where that bites, and a gate that flakes on its first loaded run gets ignored or reverted. So the fix ships with the gate rather than after it. The budget is now 5 s, still well inside the 20 s test timeout.

Verified rather than assumed: a throwaway test asserted `getConfig().asyncUtilTimeout === 5000` and that a `waitFor` resolving only after 2 s now succeeds (it would have failed at the old default). Both passed; the throwaway file is not part of this diff.

## Coverage — deliberately *not* in the gate

`npm run test:coverage` **already fails on `main`**, and still fails on this branch. `vitest.config.ts` asks for `statements: 100, lines: 100, branches: 97, functions: 98`; the measured reality is:

| metric | threshold | actual |
| --- | --- | --- |
| statements | 100 | **99.32** |
| lines | 100 | **99.32** |
| branches | 97 | **96.34** (96.34–96.35 across runs) |
| functions | 98 | **97.43** |

131 of 19,303 statements are uncovered, and **115 of those 131 (88 %) are in one file**, `src/features/finance/StatementFlow.tsx` (86.29 % statements, 12 uncovered functions including `ErstattungStep` and `PayoutPreview`, which are never rendered by any test). The rest: `StatementReview.tsx` (8), `components/FeedbackButton.tsx` (6), `Statements.tsx` (1), `components/ui.tsx` (1 — line 74, the "open the dropdown upwards" branch, which needs faked viewport geometry since jsdom reports zero-sized rects).

I did **not** add coverage to this job and did **not** lower the thresholds. Lowering a standard quietly is worse than the gap it hides. The typecheck/test/build gate is the issue's stated goal and the thing that would have caught the real bug; the coverage question deserves its own decision on the numbers above. Closing the gap is a real piece of work on `StatementFlow.tsx`, not a trivial top-up.

## Verification

Run locally from a clean `npm ci`, in the same order the job runs them:

- `npm run typecheck` — clean, exit 0.
- `npm run test` — **33 files, 1054 tests, all passing**, 38.9 s.
- `npm run build` — succeeds in 3.0 s (emits the pre-existing >500 kB chunk-size *warning*, which does not fail the build).
- `src/features/finance/statements.integration.test.tsx` in isolation — **69/69**.
- `actionlint 1.7.7` on the new workflow — clean, exit 0.
- `pre-commit run --files .github/workflows/check-frontend.yml frontend/src/test/setup.ts` — all hooks pass (`check-yaml` parsed the workflow).

Resolves taxis issues #500 (this gate) and #504 (the async timeout).
