body:
PR 3a of the Discover sequence (DECISIONS #31, `docs/discover/schema-v2.md`). No model API, no client change, nothing a user sees. **All 139 works are `reviewed: false`** â€” no flag is flipped.

## What landed

- **`registry.py`** â€” `load()` validates all three registries and raises one `RegistryError` listing every problem, not the first. It owns `AXES`, the four closed axis lists the tagger will import. `resolve_work` / `resolve_track` / `resolve_person` are methods on the loaded object, keyed by the work slug without a leading "the".
- **`data/registry/works.json`** â€” 139 entries, sorted by id. **`tracks.json`** â€” all 54 tracks, 26 with axes, sorted by id. **`people.json`** â€” `[]`, PR 3b.
- **`registry_report.py`** â†’ `docs/discover/registry-2026.md`, the review document.

Two optional fields, neither changing what an existing field means, so no DECISIONS entry: works gain **`terms`** (words that lead a searcher to a work but are not names for it â€” they never resolve, so one term sits on several works) and tracks gain an **`audience`** default.

## Track axes, before and after

Recomputed: each v1 topic maps to its v2 home, `Gaming` reads as the medium the track plays in, and a track takes a value where **one value covers â‰¥80% of its tagged events**. Six rows changed:

| track | before | after | why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `group-cosplay-photoshoot` | `craft: photography` | **none** | the rule offers 100% and the track declines it: 186 meetups are not "the craft of photography" |
| `high-fantasy` | none | **`genre: fantasy`** | 80% exactly â€” the census's "over 80%" excluded it |
| `sci-fi-literature` | none | **`genre: sci-fi`** | 80% exactly, same boundary |
| `miniatures-games` | none | none | **tabletop 73%** â€” does not clear |
| `video-gaming` | none | none | **video-games 69%** â€” does not clear |
| `nsdmg-war-college` | none | none | **history 52%, tabletop 28%** â€” nowhere near |

The last three are the ones item 1 expected to clear. Merging Gaming into tabletop raised them but not to 80%, so they take nothing; the report shows every track's best candidate per axis whether or not it clears, so the gap is visible rather than inferred. `live-action-roleplaying-games` also declines the value the rule offers it (tabletop 100%), as decided earlier.

## Works

- `type` **is where the work started** â€” it picks a shelf and nothing more. `pokemon` â†’ `game`/`video`, `yu-gi-oh` â†’ `franchise` (one began on a Game Boy, the other as a manga). `fallout`, `halo`, `the-last-of-us`, `battletech`, `critical-role` keep what they were drafted with. The rule is now in schema-v2.md's `type` row and settles all seven, so they leave UNSURE.
- `warhammer` is a work of its own (`game`/`miniatures`), the **parent** of `warhammer-40000`; "Warhammer" is no longer an alias of the child, and now resolves to the parent.
- `the-avengers` â†’ id **`avengers`**, name "Avengers", leaving the name free for BritTrack's.
- **`ponies` stands.** Its one event reads: *"â€¦the Peacock show Ponies. We're gathering in the situation room to discuss the fabulous femalesâ€¦ their antics in Moscow, and our hopes for a season 2."* Not My Little Pony, so no other id is minted.
- `angel`, `dragon-ball-z`, `predator` and the ten character-led children stay as drafted.

## Labels

Nothing is dropped for lacking a registry home. 256 distinct phrases: **26** a work's own name, **37** alias, **20** child, **28** term, **132** elsewhere, **13 search-only** (kept in `src/search.js`, with the 28 concept groups), **0 dropped** â€” no phrase in CANON or SYNONYMS is wrong.

**`genre: romance` is now an axis value**, added on the evidence below; `romance`, `romantasy` and `paranormal romance` moved from search-only to elsewhere. The other three words got no value - `kind` already carries a karaoke night, a dance and a wrestling show - and stay in `src/search.js`. The track recomputation moves nothing, since no v1 topic maps to romance.

| words | events | of those, in the title | its v2 home |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| romance, romantasy | **13** | 8 | `genre: romance` |
| wrestling | **5** | 2 | the kind `performance`; search-only |
| karaoke, sing-along | **29** | 20 | the kind `performance`; search-only |
| dance, dancing | **43** | 21 | the kind `party`; search-only |

## UNSURE â€” 4

1. `angel` â€” child of Buffy; a bare "Angel" is an ambiguous name to resolve, and the only entry whose name is an everyday word.
2. `dragon-ball-z` â€” child of Dragon Ball rather than merged; the census flags them as a prefix pair.
3. `predator` â€” seeded on two 2026 mentions, one of which is `D&D 5.5E: Crowning The Apex Predator`, not the film.
4. Character-led children (`batman`, `superman`, `wonder-woman`, `justice-league`, `spider-man`, `x-men`, `avengers`, `wolverine`, `deadpool`, `daredevil`) â€” seeded as child works after the brief's own "batman under dc-comics". A character is not a franchise; a reviewer may want some folded into the parent.

## Verification

- **`registry.load` passes on the real files:** 139 works, 54 tracks, 0 people. All 139 `reviewed: false`.
- **Each rule's fixture fails** â€” 20 rules, one specific problem each, e.g. `works.json: the key 'serenity' resolves to more than one entry: 'Serenity' (firefly), 'Serenity' (serenity)`; `a game needs a family, one of rpg, ccg, board, miniatures, video, not None`; `works.json: firefly -> firefly is a parent cycle`; `axes.medium has 3 values, at most 2`.
- **Coverage: 0 unresolved fandom names, 0 unresolved tracks**, 0 of 256 phrases unlabelled, and **0 tracks whose axes the evidence does not support**.
- **Two runs of the report give the same bytes**, and again under a different `PYTHONHASHSEED`.
- **`git status`: nothing under `data/2026/`.**
- `npm run lint`, `npm test` (844 passed, 4 skipped) and `python -m pytest tests/` (104 passed) green.

## Docs

`schema-v2.md` records the work slug, the resolution key, the label set, `terms`, the track `audience` default, the `type` rule and `genre: romance` on the axis list. On terms it says they reach the client inside the resolved data the pipeline writes, never by the client reading a registry â€” and leaves whether that is a per-event field or an index the pipeline builds to the client switch.

author: svyable
body:
## What changed

Added one bounded primary-source audit for **THE POSITIVE RESULT**, stacked on #2294 rather than editing its active manuscript concurrently. No manuscript prose, README/TOC, catalog, rights, or tooling files changed.

## Research added or checked

- Recovered the LR experiment's prospective logic from 1972/1976 primary descriptions: labelled-gas evolution after nutrient addition plus strong attenuation in a heat-treated duplicate was established before Mars as a biologically meaningful metabolic pattern.
- Checked the December 1976 LR report and the broader Viking biology-team report: Mars matched important parts of that pattern, but both records stopped short of concluding that life had been demonstrated.
- Added the later second-nutrient-injection result and the 1979 flight-like simulation showing that its abrupt gas decline has a plausible physical CO2/water/soil-equilibrium explanation.
- Added the 1981 hydrogen-peroxide analog work as counterevidence: even LR's biological advocates produced an abiotic system matching important kinetic/thermal features, then challenged it on independent Martian plausibility.

Primary sources:
- https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/19770035046
- https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/19720040720
- https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/19770033065
- https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/19760062481
- https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/19780027540
- https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/19800051898
- https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/19810053555

## Strongest counterargument

`Positive result` can still overstate the historical protocol if it implies one preflight rule whose satisfaction should have compelled a life announcement. Viking's team explicitly distinguished prima facie biological criteria from a definitive answer, and cross-instrument contradiction plus nonbiological chemistry were legitimate interpretive constraints rather than necessarily post-hoc goalpost moving. If the deeper flight protocol contains mandatory discriminators the simplified heat-control account omits, the chapter should narrow further.

## Why this improves the book

It sharpens the opening's best idea. The interesting historical fact is not that Mars passed a `life test` and scientists refused the answer. It is that Mars produced a response matching important **prospective metabolic criteria** while the causal interpretation remained non-unique. The later second-injection behavior then gives the narrative a genuine reversal: the same instrument that initially looked biological generated a feature its own designers could model physically.

Scope: **1 research file / 1 commit**, stacked on #2294. Nothing is merged.

author: ivananikin
body:
**Found in production, by the rule V3.17.9.2 added.** With the price book configured and correct, the proof run still reported a cost of `None` — and named exactly why:

```
unpriced_units: ['model_input_tokens[deepseek:cache_unreported]']
```

The research-provider leg reported its split (384 cached of 590 input). The **six routing calls did not**, so the AND across that vendor's calls was False and all 21,482 input tokens stayed unpriceable.

## The defect

`DeepSeekModelProvider` accumulated `_prompt_tokens` and `_completion_tokens` and dropped `cached_tokens` — which its own transport has parsed since it was written.

Its class docstring already records the same shape of defect one field over: `consume_usage` did not exist at all until a run reported an empty `model_by_vendor` while genuinely spending tens of thousands of tokens.

## The fix

- Accumulate `_cached_prompt_tokens`, and `_cache_reported` as an **AND** across calls (`None` until the first call).
- Reset both on `consume_usage` with everything else, so a second run cannot inherit the first's cached tokens.
- `cache_reported` comes from key **presence** in the response body, so `cached_tokens: 0` from a body that never mentioned caching stays *unreported* rather than becoming a zero billed at the $0.3/M miss rate.

This is what the V3.17.9.2 rule is for: it did not produce a plausible wrong number, it refused and pointed at the producer.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `pytest` with `V3_TEST_POSTGRES_URL` at head 040 | **6695 passed, 39 skipped, 0 failed** |
| `ruff check app/ tests/` | clean |
| `mypy app` | **71 errors in 10 files — unchanged baseline** |

No migration.

body:
## Summary

This PR migrates the closure editor form integration to support Waze Map Editor's (WME) new Zustand-based architecture while maintaining seamless backward compatibility with legacy Backbone-based WME versions. 

It introduces `ZustandClosureEditorForm`, defines the WME closure store schema, implements an `AUTO` fallback mechanism in `ClosureEditorFormContextProvider`, and updates `ClosureEditorPanel` to utilize this auto-detection.

Fixes #111

---

## Motivation & Problem (Reason for Change)

The WME team is gradually migrating editor state management away from legacy BackboneJS collections/models in favor of React hooks and Zustand stores (`useSyncExternalStore`). 

As part of this rollout, the WME closure edit tab was migrated to a Zustand store. The existing `ClosureGroupModelBasedEditorForm` relied on inspecting Backbone models attached to the DOM, causing closure presets to fail when attempting to apply closure details on newer WME versions.

---

## Changes Made

### 1. `ZustandClosureEditorForm` Implementation
* Added `ZustandClosureEditorForm`, implementing the `ClosureEditorForm` interface:
  * Uses `findParentStore` from the Fiber hooks engine to extract the WME closure Zustand store (`StoreApi<WmeClosureStoreState>`) from the form's React Fiber tree.
  * Implements getters and setters for start/end dates, description/reason, direction, event ID, permanent status, and provider partner details via `store.getState()` and `store.getState().updateAttribute(...)`.
  * Extracts available closure partner providers directly from the form DOM options.

### 2. WME Closure Store Schema & Type Guard
* Added `wme-closure-store-schema.ts`:
  * Defined `WmeClosureStoreState` and `WmeClosureItemState` interfaces.
  * Implemented `isWmeClosureStoreState` type guard predicate to reliably match and validate the closure store shape on the Fiber tree.

### 3. Dual-Compatibility with `AUTO` Context Provider Type
* Updated `ClosureEditorFormContext.tsx`:
  * Added `type?: 'AUTO' | 'CLOSURES_GROUP_MODEL_DOM_FORM' | 'ZUSTAND_STORE_DOM_FORM'`.
  * Implemented an auto-detection strategy under `'AUTO'`: attempts to instantiate `ZustandClosureEditorForm` first, and gracefully falls back to `ClosureGroupModelBasedEditorForm` if the store cannot be extracted.
* Updated `ClosureEditorPanel.tsx` to use `type="AUTO"` in `ClosureEditorFormContextProvider`.

### 4. Unit Tests
* Added `zustand-closure-editor-form.spec.ts` covering:
  * Store extraction and error handling when the store is missing.
  * Form getters and setters (dates, description, direction, event ID, permanent, provider editing restrictions).

Adds independent local face recognition on selected camera frames, using checksum-pinned OpenCV YuNet and SFace CPU models. Opt-in profiles can be named, merged and forgotten in Settings. Images remain in memory; unnamed profiles expire after seven days. Ambiguous matches remain unidentified.

Stacked on #41 for camera selection; this is separate from scene descriptions and speaker diarization. It introduces no GPU workload, allows one bounded inference request with no backlog, and cancels pending work when the camera stops.

Validation: 83 Node tests pass, including matching ambiguity, disable/delete/cancel invalidation and persistent profiles; branded AsciiDoc PDF builds; Chromium rendered synthetic profiles. Real CPU inference on blank/generated-avatar fixtures took 0.23–0.27 seconds. This is pipeline validation, not family-recognition accuracy testing.

Draft acceptance work remains:
- Typed face observations into Unmute, without adding image-derived content to system instructions.
- Conversational naming with unambiguous face selection and model-worded unfamiliar-person notifications.
- Thumbnail-based profile disambiguation, household calibration and end-to-end camera/voice load testing.

Settings explicitly states that voice notifications and conversational naming are not yet connected. This branch has not been deployed or enabled in the running assistant.

author: martianoff
body:
Closes the last gap from the ratatui comparison that is a **defect rather than
a missing feature**: `markdown.gala` dropped all inline styling the moment a
paragraph wrapped to a second row.

## The bug

Wrapping was computed on the joined plain text and re-emitted as rows of
unstyled `Text`. A paragraph that fit on one line kept its bold, italic, code
spans and links; the same paragraph one column narrower rendered completely
flat. A width threshold, not a gradual degradation — the shape that makes a
bug hard to believe when someone reports it.

`text.gala`'s own header has described this defect since Wave A. Now it's fixed.

## What changed

**`WrapSpans(spans, width) -> Array[Line]`** — wraps styled text, preserving
each character's style across breaks and coalescing neighbours that share one
(otherwise a wrapped line carries a Span per character).

**`wrapParagraph` delegates to it.** This is the part worth reviewing. The two
were independent implementations of the same greedy algorithm, and
`MarkdownLineCountAt` pre-computes block heights through one path while the
renderer lays out rows through the other. Drift between them mis-sizes every
layout that asked for an exact height, so a single engine is a correctness
property rather than tidiness. `TestWrappedRowCountStillMatchesTheHeightOracle`
pins the agreement across widths 12–40.

**The engine counts cells, not runes.** The plain wrapper counted runes, so a
CJK paragraph broke at `width` glyphs and rendered twice that many columns,
overflowing whatever sat beside it. ASCII is unaffected — the metrics are
identical there, and all 1072 prior tests pass unchanged.

**Markdown links carry their URL as an OSC 8 hyperlink.** The parser already
had the target and `Style` gained `Link` in 0.12.0. Terminals without OSC 8
ignore the sequence and still show underlined blue.

## Verification

- 1080 tests, 0 failures
- Verified non-vacuous: restoring the plain-text wrap fails
  `TestBoldSurvivesAWrapOntoTheSecondRow` and
  `TestBoldOnTheFirstRowIsUnaffectedByWrapping`
- Renderer-level assertions (`buf.StyleAt`), not unit tests on the wrap
  function alone — `TestPlainTextAroundAStyledRunStaysPlain` guards the
  opposite direction so the fix isn't "make everything bold"

author: jarnodegreve-ui
body:
## Vraag
"Kan je als de ruil openklapt duidelijk per chauffeur tonen wie er al geaccepteerd/geweigerd heeft?"

## Wat je ziet
Eén blok **Verloop**, overal waar een ruil openklapt: per persoon avatar, naam, rol, een stille statuspil en het moment (dd/mm uu:mm).

- **Aanvrager**: Aangevraagd, of Ingetrokken.
- **Collega**: Wacht op antwoord (aan zet), Geaccepteerd, Geweigerd, of "Antwoord niet afgewacht" als een admin rechtstreeks goedkeurde. Na de doorvoer: "Wissel bevestigd" of "Wissel nog niet bevestigd".
- **Planner**: Wacht op collega, Te beoordelen (aan zet), Goedgekeurd, Geweigerd, Geannuleerd, plus "Afgehandeld".
- Bij een 1-op-1-ruil staat per persoon wat hij krijgt; de losse regels "Aan:", "In ruil:" en "Jij geeft:" zijn daardoor weg. Ging de ruil niet door, dan staat er "Zou … krijgen".
- Overname: zelfde stappen (de collega moet wel akkoord geven). Handmatige wissel door de planning: geen akkoordstap, dus "Ingevoerd door de planner", "Geen akkoord nodig", en de nieuwe rijder "Nog niet bevestigd" of "Bevestigd".
- Wie aan zet is draagt een pil met klokje, gebeurd en goed een stille pil met groen puntje, geweigerd rood, de rest een kale regel. Geen goud.

Plekken: de uitklaprij van de aanvrager, de kaart van de collega, de staflijst (mobiel het volledige blok, in de desktoptabel een compacte versie onder de status), het beoordelingspaneel, en de rijen onder Afgehandeld, die nu uitklappen (daar stond "Afgewezen" zonder door wie).

## Bron
Het activiteitenlog (`entity_type = 'swap'`). De swaps-tabel kent maar één `decidedAt` en zegt niet wie weigerde; de logregel draagt de rol van de actor en de overgang ("pending → rejected"). Niet-staf die afwijst = de collega, staf = de planner. Op productie nagekeken: elke statuswissel is gelogd met rol en ruil-id, ook voor de oudste ruilen, en de nachtcron ruimt ruil-logregels bewust nooit op. **Geen migratie, geen nieuwe kolom, geen wijziging aan de ruilflow.**

- `GET /api/swaps` hangt `verloop` aan elke ruil: één logquery voor alle ruilen (staf: parallel met de ruilen zelf; chauffeur: alleen de id's van zijn eigen ruilen). `PATCH /api/swaps/:id` geeft het bijgewerkte verloop terug, want de client voegt dat record lokaal in.
- Privacy: een chauffeur krijgt alleen het verloop van ruilen waar hij aanvrager of collega is, nooit de naam van de planner en nooit de vrije logtekst. Staf krijgt wel de naam van wie besliste.
- Het veld is afgeleid: het telt niet mee in de collectie-revisie en wordt bij een array-save weggegooid.
- Mislukt de logquery, dan komen de ruilen gewoon zonder verloop terug; het blok toont dan wat de ruil zelf zegt en gokt niet wie weigerde.

## Let op
`target_seen_at` is de bevestiging van de nieuwe rijder NA de doorvoer ("Begrepen, ik rijd deze dienst"), niet "de collega heeft de aanvraag gezien". Dat laatste wordt nergens bijgehouden, dus het blok toont geen "gezien / niet gezien" bij een wachtende aanvraag.

## Tests
- `shared/ruilVerloop.test.ts`: elke status × soort, ontbrekende logregels, privacy, en een drift-test tegen de log-acties in `api/index.ts`.
- `src/apiIntegration.test.ts`: chauffeur krijgt geen verloop van andermans ruil en geen stafnaam, staf wel; revisie en array-save ongemoeid; mislukte logquery; PATCH.
- `src/lib/format.test.ts`: `formatMomentKort`, onder UTC, Europe/Brussels en America/Los_Angeles.
- `e2e/ruil.spec.ts`: het blok vóór en na accepteren.

body:
## Summary
- Editing a fixed-price contract failed with **"A time-based contract needs a rate."** even though Fixed Price was selected and a price entered. Switching an existing time-based contract to fixed price failed the same way.
- Root cause: `CrudIntent.save_from_dict` coerces payload values through `model_validate` on **create**, but on **update** it `setattr`s the raw payload onto the tracked entity. `ContractType` is a plain `enum.Enum`, so the string `"fixed_price"` never equals `ContractType.fixed_price` and `validate_pricing` fell through to the time-based branch. SQLAlchemy accepts enum names on flush, which is why other edits appeared to work while every validator that compares enum members before flush saw strings.
- Fix: the update path now copies the coerced values from the validated copy it already builds (`tuttle/app/core/abstractions.py`), so every enum field on every entity is a member before validators run — not just `Contract.type`.

## Test plan
- [x] New `tuttle_tests/test_contract_edit_enum_coercion.py`: editing a fixed-price contract, switching time-based → fixed price, and enum members (`type`, `unit`, `billing_cycle`) present after an edit. All three fail on `main` with exactly the reported message and pass with the fix.

author: danielscholl
body:
## What

`KEELSON_NODE_<id>_OUTPUT_FILE` is now set for every upstream node, not only
when the output passed the 16 KiB env cap, so a bash or script node can read
the file unconditionally instead of guarding every read with a
`[ -n "${..._FILE:-}" ]` conditional. `KEELSON_NODE_<id>_OUTPUT_TRUNCATED=1`
marks a capped value, so a consumer that must use the variable can fail with a
cause instead of on a parse error. `keelson workflow validate` warns when a
shell body hands the capped variable straight to `jq`, `JSON.parse` or
`json.loads`, and the env channel is now documented in both authoring guides
rather than only the node reference. Closes #865.

`plan-act-evaluate`'s `report` node was the one bundled workflow the new
warning fired on; it now reads the spill file. Out of scope: the `_OUTPUT`
fallback branches in `fix-issue` and `resolve-pr` still work and are left
alone.

## Why now

The failure this came from looked like nothing changed: a JSON bundle had been
under the cap for a dozen runs, grew past it as the project accumulated state,
and the last node of a run died on
`JSONDecodeError: Invalid control character at: line 1 column 8193` after every
model node had already succeeded. The cap is doing its job — the problem is
that the escape hatch was conditional and undocumented, so authors could not
reach for it before they had been bitten.

It also unblocks #872, #873 and #874, which all declare a dependency on this
and read `_OUTPUT_FILE` from a persist step.

## Test plan

- `bun run check` — 613 files, clean
- `bun --filter '*' typecheck` — 8/8 workspaces, exit 0
- `bun --filter '*' test` — 4386 pass, 0 fail
- `bun --filter '*' build` — exit 0
- `cd docs && bun run build` — 52 pages
- Parsed all 9 bundled workflow assets through the real loader: 1
  `json_parse_on_capped_env_output` hit on `origin/main`
  (`plan-act-evaluate` / `report`), 0 after the fix. Checked both sides so a
  zero could not be a scan that never matched.

The warning is a heuristic scoped to a single logical line. An earlier
whole-body version flagged 10 nodes across 4 bundled workflows, 4 of them false
positives where `_OUTPUT` is read as plain text and an unrelated `jq` reads a
file — precision matters more than recall for something that fires at validate
time.

## Risk & rollback

- Blast radius: every `bash` and `script` node's environment. Existing bodies
  are unaffected; the change only adds variables.
- Compatibility: none. No schema, config or migration change; `_OUTPUT` keeps
  its current shape and cap.
- Rollback: revert the commit.

author: theioz
body:
## Why

Oura has deprecated Personal Access Tokens. The stored PAT now returns **401** on `/v2/usercollection/sleep`, confirmed live:

```
[run-syncs] oura: FAILED for 1 user(s)
    bed84e8e-...: Oura sleep returned 401
```

Recovery data (sleep, readiness, HRV, RHR) stopped arriving. `recovery_metrics` for 2026-09-19 is entirely NULL apart from `steps: 0`, and there is no row at all for 09-20.

## What changed

Mirrors `api/auth/google-health/*` rather than inventing a second shape.

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `api/auth/oura/start/route.ts` | **new** — CSRF cookie, redirect to `cloud.ouraring.com/oauth/authorize` |
| `api/auth/oura/callback/route.ts` | **new** — state check, code exchange at `api.ouraring.com/oauth/token`, `storeIntegration` |
| `lib/sync/oura.ts` | refresh-token exchange before each sync; persists rotated refresh tokens; honest row count; 401/403 split |
| `components/settings/integrations-settings.tsx` | PAT input → Connect button |
| `(protected)/settings/page.tsx` | drops the now-unused `saveOuraToken` server action |

**Scopes** default to `daily spo2`, overridable via `OURA_SCOPES`. `daily` is load-bearing — it carries `/sleep`, `/daily_readiness`, `/daily_sleep`, `/daily_activity` and `/vo2_max`, the four endpoints the sync treats as required. The env override exists because Oura's developer console offers scopes (Stress, Heart Health, Ring Configuration) that its published docs page does not list, and requesting an unrecognised scope fails the whole authorize round-trip.

**Refresh-token rotation** is persisted rather than swallowed. Oura returns a new refresh token on every exchange; a failure to store it throws, because the rotation has already happened server-side and reporting success would leave the next cron run to fail with a misleading error.

## The part that isn't the auth

This was invisible for two days, and that's a separate defect worth fixing.

`sync_log` recorded `status: ok, records_written: 3` on both 09-19 and 09-20 while writing all-NULL rows. `records_written` counted rows **upserted**, and Oura keeps emitting `daily_activity` stubs (`steps: 0`) for days the ring never recorded — so a total outage satisfies that counter exactly as well as a healthy sync. A failure and a success produced an identical log line.

Now:
- `records_written` counts rows actually carrying `total_sleep_hrs` or `readiness`.
- A window where none do is logged `partial`, which falls outside `lastSyncAgeSecs()`'s `status = 'ok'` filter — so a degraded window is retried on the next run instead of being skipped for 30 minutes.
- 401 (dead authorisation) and 403 (scope never granted) now report distinct, actionable errors instead of a bare status code.

## Deploy

New env keys in `~/docker/mr-bridge/.env` on compute-core:

```
OURA_CLIENT_ID=...
OURA_CLIENT_SECRET=...

author: superalvi1
body:
## Root cause (Hassan)

User Management lists `users`. Sales CRM Clients / Target Clients lists `leads`.
Self-registration created a Customer **user** (and sometimes a `customers` row) but **never created a `leads` row**, and `users.customer_id` could stay empty. Hassan therefore appeared in User Management and not in CRM Clients. An empty `users.customer_id` also made portal APIs treat the user as unlinked.

Correct relationship:

`users.customer_id` → `customers.id` → `leads.customer_id`

## This branch

- Registration, login, and admin-create now create or reuse a customer, never steal one already linked to another user, set `users.customer_id`, and create or reuse a CRM lead.
- Additive SQL: `scripts/client-crm-link-schema.sql` then `scripts/backfill-client-crm-profiles.sql` then `scripts/interactive-proposals-schema.sql`.
- Client login lands on the dashboard. Solar Wizard is optional. Missing profile shows **Profile setup pending** instead of a blank page or wizard loop.
- Staff **Open Client Portal / Manage Client** opens only the selected lead (details, proposals, interactive links, warranties, invoices/payments, tickets, documents, notes).
- Interactive proposals: staff share a WhatsApp link from a saved quotation. Client opens it without CRM login. Server-side catalog pricing. Original quotation is immutable. Token stored as SHA-256 hash only. Sent / Viewed / Modified / Accepted / Revoked / Expired.

## Do not

- Merge to main
- Deploy production
- Apply the SQL on production without staging review
- Commit or expose service-role keys / JWT secrets

## Tests run in this pass

Passed: `npm run test:client-crm-link`, `npm run test:interactive-proposal`, `npm run test:authorization`, `npm run test:phase-1b2a`, `npm run test:mobile-disclosure`, `npm run test:ai-quote-mobile`, `npx vite build`.

`npm run lint` (`tsc --noEmit`) still fails on **pre-existing** errors in files this PR does not touch.
`npm test` smoke-server-start failed in this sandbox because production WhatsApp inbox wiring requires live Supabase.

## Remaining blockers

1. Apply the three SQL scripts on **staging** (not production) in order.
2. Confirm Hassan appears under CRM Clients and can open the client dashboard.
3. Human review of unique `customers.user_id` index if duplicate `user_id` rows already exist.
4. Do not merge until that staging check is signed off.

author: siterelenby
body:
Two bugs found in 1.4.0 before it went to Play. **1.4.0 is already tagged and its GitHub release is published with signed `open` APKs**, so these want a 1.4.1 rather than a re-cut: anyone who has installed `sheaf-1.4.0-open.apk` holds versionCode 104000, and re-issuing different bytes under that same code leaves them with no upgrade path.

## "Don't show again" never survived a restart

`ClientSettingsResponse` names the field `clientId`; the server sends `client_id`; Moshi does not convert snake_case. Non-null with no default, so the missing field failed the **whole response**, and both callers wrap the call in `runCatching` - so every read of client settings threw, silently, for the life of the feature.

The write path was fine throughout. The dismissal reached the server and was stored; it just could never be read back, which is why this looked like a persistence bug rather than a parse one.

```
JsonDataException: Required value 'clientId' missing at $
```

A contract test now decodes the shape the server actually sends. It uses the app's own Moshi rather than a bare one, because this type is handled by `KotlinJsonAdapterFactory` and a plain builder cannot read it at all - which is also why the existing model tests never caught it.

I swept every model for the same mistake. The only other camelCase-without-`@Json` properties are on `FrontUpdate`, whose hand-written adapter writes the snake_case names itself, and on the watch's local-storage models, which never touch the wire.

Anything dismissed permanently before this stays dismissed - the data was always there.

## Sharing was reachable only through Settings

It's where you go to take something down, which is not a thing to go hunting through Settings for, and web has had it as a top-level destination all along. It now joins the drawer with the rest of the system, and can be pinned to the bottom bar.

- The entry appears when the instance serves public profiles, **or** when it doesn't but this account still has grants on file. Grants outlive the instance switch, so hiding the entry in that case would leave somebody published with no way to reach the button that unpublishes them.
- Availability is re-asked whenever the drawer opens, so publishing a first link doesn't need a relaunch to reveal the entry.
- A pinned Sharing slot on a server that later turns sharing off keeps its place, dimmed, and says why when tapped, rather than disappearing from somebody's bar over a setting they don't control.
- The Settings > System row stays. A second way in costs nothing, and #79 put it there deliberately.

author: fabian20xv
body: ## Summary Preview JWT verify no longer hard-fails on **develop ES256** access tokens from `https://bkwhqfkosxnoffpsjcug.supabase.co`. Tess QA: `verifyWithJwtSecret()` always called `jwtVerify(token, TextEncoder.encode(SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET))`. Develop Auth issues ES256 (JWKS EC) tokens, so jose threw `Key for the ES256 algorithm must be one of type CryptoKey, KeyObject, or JSON Web Key. Received an instance of Uint8Array` and `GET /v1/session` returned `401 invalid_token` without falling through to Auth-server verify. ## Behavior `src/server/jwt.js` now: 1. Decodes the JWT header `alg`. 2. **HS256** (symmetric): verifies with `SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET` as before. 3. **ES256 / RS256** (asymmetric, including develop JWKS): verifies with `createRemoteJWKSet(new URL(\`${SUPABASE_URL}/auth/v1/.well-known/jwks.json\`))`. 4. On jose **key-type / alg mismatches**, falls through to `GET ${SUPABASE_URL}/auth/v1/user` instead of hard-failing. Develop ES256 user JWTs are therefore supported on Preview/staging. Invalid signatures still 401. ## E0 locks (unchanged) Auth verify only. Parent (`krcwpupbdizzjyydzaqp`) and develop (`bkwhqfkosxnoffpsjcug`) project allowlists are not weakened. No parent-project, Tess-seed, or split-screen UI changes. ## Tests - HS256 still works when `SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET` is set (no JWKS fetch). - ES256 path uses mocked JWKS at `/auth/v1/.well-known/jwks.json`. - Key-type TypeError falls through to Auth-server verify. - `GET /v1/session` accepts a develop ES256 Bearer token. `npm run ci` passes locally (148 tests).

author: dcodish
body:
Measured while fixing #1012 in round #1200, which named this as the third member of the arc family and left it for its own look. On «ABC משולש ישר זוית» · «AC=15» · «BC=10» · «O על AC» · «D על CB»:

```
רבע מעגל ODC   ->  centre O, ends D and C, span 90    ✓
גזרה ODC       ->  centre O, ends D and C, span free   ✓
חצי מעגל ODC   ->  not-handled                         ✗
חצי עיגול ODC  ->  not-handled                         ✗
```

Both siblings read a three-letter run as *centre, then the two ends*. The semicircle read no 3-run at all, so a spelling a student would naturally try was answered «לא הבנתי» while the family was two-thirds consistent. **A family with two conventions is one a student cannot learn.**

## Why this needed no ruling

For a semicircle, centre-first + two ends ON the circle + a span of 180° says **`O` is the midpoint of `DC`**. That is what the sentence means rather than an extra assumption, and it is exactly what the two-letter spelling already builds.

It also lowers to **constraints**, not to an assertion: both ends are members of a free-radius circle centred at `O` (so |OD| = |OC|) and `set-collinear(D, O, C)` closes it. So a figure that cannot honour it is refused honestly — and measured, your own over-constrained figure now refuses **with the same message its quarter sibling gives**, which is the parity this is about.

**The fix is the run reading and nothing else.** The general branch already produced the right geometry; it had simply never been reached with a named centre and two ends.

## Play it — `http://localhost:5175/`

**The gap, on your own figure:**
```
ABC משולש ישר זוית
AC=15
BC=10
O על AC
D על CB
חצי מעגל ODC
```
**Look for:** the last line is now *understood* — it is refused for a geometric reason (O cannot sit on AC and be equidistant from D and C), **exactly as «רבע מעגל ODC» is refused on the same figure**. **Before:** «לא הבנתי» — the tool did not read the sentence at all.

**And where it can build — start from a clean canvas:**
```
חצי מעגל ODC
```
**Look for:** a half circle with `O` sitting at the **midpoint** of `DC`, the diameter drawn. **Before:** not handled.

**The contrast that shows the span is real — clean canvas:**
```
רבע מעגל ODC
```
**Look for:** equal radii as before, but `O` is *not* between D and C — a 90° arc, not a half. **Before:** unchanged.

**The re-reading still applies to it — clean canvas:**
```
נקודה D
נקודה C
O אמצע DC
חצי מעגל DCO
```
**Look for:** it builds. You wrote the letters in the wrong order; the tool re-read the run and adopted the one that works, and the step row shows the spelling it used. **Before:** not handled.

## Evidence

- `src/__tests__/issue-1204-semicircle-run.test.ts` (11) — the lowering asserted **against the quarter's skeleton** rather than written out, so the family cannot drift; the geometry read off the **built figure** with the quarter as the counter-case (equal radii alone would pass for both — what distinguishes a semicircle is that its centre lies *between* its ends); the previously-working spellings pinned to lowerings **measured on the pre-change tree in the same context**; and #1012's re-read **driven through the real submit path**, not assumed from where the code sits.
- 2-D lane green: **408 files / 7113 tests**. `tsc -b` clean, `build` clean, doc gate 757 green.
- `catalog.ts` updated — it is the user-facing reference and the coverage map at once, so it now teaches the 3-run and says what it means.
- **ADR-534** · Requirements 02 (the arc family's letter run) · Design none (the rule's own reading, no new seam).

Closes #1204

author: jianmliu
body:
Follows #69. The mirror is now real, and it is on Cloudflare Pages.

Pages refuses any file over 25 MiB — measured, not assumed:

```
✘ Error: Pages only supports files up to 25 MiB in size
  aigg-brains/flywire-fafb-v783-min2.bin is 73.5 MiB in size
```

…and R2 is not enabled on the account (`Please enable R2 through the Cloudflare Dashboard`). So a mirror there publishes **parts** and a manifest beside them, and the page puts them back together.

**Nothing about that is trusted.** The parts are concatenated and the worker recomputes `model_id` over the result, which the chain pins: a missing part, a reordered part or a hostile part fails exactly as a wrong whole file does. The manifest is not signed and says nothing but where to look next. The whole object is tried first, so a mirror that *can* hold a brain just holds it.

```
node js/mirror_pack.mjs <payload.bin> <dir>/<bucket>/<object> [partMiB=20]
```

It refuses a part size Pages would reject, and reassembles what it wrote before saying it is done — a packer that produces a mirror nobody can use is worse than no packer.

### One thing only a real host teaches
Cloudflare Pages answers a **missing** path with `200` and its `index.html`, not a 404.

The first version of this fell back to the parts on a 404, and so never fell back at all: the page took a web page for a brain and failed three steps later with `bad payload magic`. A response whose content-type is html is now read for what it is — *the file is not there, whatever the status line says* — and the test's mirror answers the same way, because that is what the host being targeted really does.

### Live
73.5 MB in four parts on `aigg-brains.pages.dev`, fetched by a browser tab holding founder #0 on BSC testnet:

```
fly #1: its base (…the founders' base (≥ 2 synapses)): served by aigg-brains.pages.dev
fly #1: 77.1 MB base downloaded, checking its model_id…
fly #1: model_id 0xbd6fbedc8734… matches the MEP
```

**12.7 seconds, and the storage provider whose quota is spent was never touched.**

To turn it on for everyone, the relayer wants `PORW_BRAIN_MIRRORS=https://aigg-brains.pages.dev`; until then the page can still be pointed at any source by hand.

body:
Closes #272. Part of #281.

## What

`track_fingerprints`, keyed on `(track_id, friend_id, fingerprint_type, fingerprint_version)` so several engines — and several versions of one engine — can index the same track at once. Swapping engines becomes an insert, not a destructive migration.

No companion `fingerprint_hashes` table, per #271's conclusion: Chromaprint measured 8.2 KiB/track, so the whole library is ~31 MB and rebuilds its postings index in memory in 2.3 s. One `bytea` blob per track is enough.

## The one decision worth reviewing

`tracks` is keyed `(track_id, username)` and had **no unique key on `(track_id, friend_id)`**, so fingerprints could not carry a real foreign key — which is why `track_embeddings` leaves orphans behind when a track is hard-deleted.

`friend_id` is written from the same friend row as `username` (`trackRepository.ts:128`), and `friends.username` is unique, so the pair is already unique in practice. This migration declares that (`tracks_track_id_friend_id_key`) and hangs a composite FK off it, which is what makes "deleting a track cascades" true in the database rather than by convention.

⚠️ **Before deploying:** that `ADD CONSTRAINT` fails if prod holds any duplicate `(track_id, friend_id)`. I reasoned it can't, but couldn't check prod data:

```sql
SELECT track_id, friend_id FROM tracks GROUP BY 1, 2 HAVING count(*) > 1;
```

## Repository

`fingerprintRepository.ts` + `src/types/fingerprint.ts`:

- `upsertFingerprint` — conflicts on the full four-column key, so engines and versions never clobber each other
- `findFingerprint`, `findFingerprintsByAudioSha256` — lookup by identity and by source-audio hash
- `listFingerprintsForIndex` — with payload, for #278's in-memory index
- `listFingerprintStatus` — *without* payload, for #277's skip decisions; reading thousands of blobs to compare hashes would be wasteful
- version listing, count, scoped deletes

## Verification

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `just migrate-test` | up / down / up clean ✅ |
| unit tests (mocked `dbQuery`) | 23 ✅ |
| DB integration tests (real Postgres) | 7 ✅ |
| `just lint-all` / `just typecheck` / web suite | ✅ (1405 passed) |

The integration tests cover every acceptance criterion directly: Panako + Chromaprint on one track, two versions of one engine, upsert-by-version leaving siblings untouched, lookup-by-hash, the same `track_id` under two friends staying separate, and both cascades.

Also adds `just fingerprint-test` (throwaway pgvector, mirrors `redis-test`) and a CI step on the existing `migrate-test` job, reusing the container it already spins up.

author: dbabsy
body:
The batter's name rendered oversized and ran straight through the count badge and the runner text beside it.

## Cause

The at-bat block was given `class="ab"`. That class already existed in this stylesheet as the **team abbreviation** in the matchup rows:

```css
.ab{font-family:var(--mono);font-size:13px;font-weight:700;width:42px;flex:0 0 auto}
```

So the at-bat span inherited a fixed 42px width (36px under the mobile breakpoint) and a 13px bold font. The content is wider than that, nothing clipped it, and it spilled over the top of the runner list.

Nothing errored. The page was only wrong on games that were **actually live** — which is how it got past a preview built from a frozen fixture.

## Fix

Renamed to `.atbat`, with the block allowed to shrink and its name ellipsised rather than overflow, and the runner list given `flex-grow` so it yields space first as originally intended.

## Regression test

Adds a check that fails on any class defined by two standalone rules in `games.py` or `ledger.py`. Descendant and modifier selectors (`.bd .bg`, `.tag.ok`, `.lv.on .lv-tag`) are scoped and don't count; `@media` overrides are skipped, since re-declaring a class there is the point.

Verified both directions: the test flags `.ab` on the shipped commit, and passes here.

```
duplicates on origin/main: ['.ab']  -> test would have FAILED: True
```

`test_ledger.py` at 33 assertions, all passing; runs in CI before the build.

body:
## Summary

Adds top-level `permissions:` blocks to 4 workflows following GitHub's security best practice (STEPSAR — set top-level permissions with least privilege).

## Changes

| Workflow | Permissions | Rationale |
|----------|-------------|-----------|
| `ci.yml` | `contents: read` | Read-only CI/build/test |
| `compliance-check.yml` | `contents: read` | Read-only CI/build/test |
| `qodana.yml` | `contents: read` | Read-only CI/build/test |
| `codeql.yml` | `actions: read,   contents: read,   security-events: write` | CodeQL/SARIF upload |

## Security Impact

- **Before**: Workflows ran with default `contents: write` permission (GitHub org default)
- **After**: Each workflow has minimum permissions needed for its function
- Reduces blast radius of compromised workflow tokens

## Compliance

- SOC 2 CC6.1 — Logical access controls
- GitHub security best practice (STEPSAR)
- Aligns with existing workflows in the fleet that already have permissions blocks

## Rollback

Revert the merge commit to restore previous state (no permissions = org default).

## Summary
- Projects native solver contact callbacks into bounded, copied Horo contact and trigger lifecycle records.
- Publishes immutable fixed-tick event buffers with canonical pair ordering, duplicate-manifold coalescing, lifecycle reconciliation, overflow policy, telemetry, and diagnostics.

## Motivation
- Solver callbacks are concurrent and manifold storage is transient; consumers need stable begin, persist, end, enter, and exit records without callback reentrancy or native pointer leakage.

## Implementation Notes
- The native adapter copies typed endpoint, subshape, material, filter-generation, contact, and sensor evidence while the callback is active.
- The owner thread sorts and reconciles copied observations after the solver joins. Solid pairs emit begin/persist/end; sensor pairs emit enter/exit without physical response.
- `DropNewest` preserves a deterministic canonical prefix and reports drops; `FailTick` preserves the prior publication and fails the world.
- Public settings identity advances to schema 2. Richer impulse/manifold reader APIs remain deferred to the neighboring follow-up issues.

## Validation
- [x] Build passed
- [x] Relevant tests passed
- [ ] Manual smoke tested if applicable

Commands run:
```bash
cmake -S . -B build/issue872 -DBUILD_TESTING=ON -DHORO_BUILD_PHYSICS_NATIVE=ON
cmake --build build/issue872 --target HoroPhysicsTests --parallel 2
./build/issue872/tests/HoroPhysicsTests "[physics][events][projection]"
git diff --check
sonar analyze --project horocore_horo-engine --format json --depth STANDARD
```
The targeted projection suite passed: 5 test cases and 50 assertions. The local Sonar secrets scan was clean, but Agentic/Vortex returned 403 with all 20 changed files skipped; hosted CI analysis remains required.

## Risks
- Event buffer and callback evidence ceilings are intentionally bounded; overflow behavior is explicit and visible through telemetry and diagnostics.
- Full CTest, GPU smoke tests, and hosted quality gates were not run locally in this worktree.

## Issue Links

- Jira: HORO-872
- GitHub: Closes #872

## Reviewer Notes
- Review the native callback ownership boundary first, then `PhysicsEventProjection` lifecycle reconciliation and overflow tests.
- `PhysicsWorld.cpp` owns fixed-tick integration and publication metadata; `PhysicsEvents.h` is the backend-neutral copied evidence contract.

author: cadlira
body:
## Contexto

A configuração de provedores de IA (TF-010) permitia apenas verificar a credencial com o envio fixo de `ping`. Esta entrega dá o primeiro uso real a essa infraestrutura, com a ação opcional "Sugerir subtarefas" no formulário de tarefa do Side Panel. É o primeiro caminho em que conteúdo de tarefa sai do dispositivo, por isso o desenho prioriza pré-visualização literal, consentimento próprio por origem e validação da saída pelas mesmas regras da digitação manual.

## Alterações realizadas

- Nova ação "Sugerir subtarefas" em `TaskForm.vue`, oferecida somente no Side Panel com provedor configurado; indisponível com motivo legível quando o título está vazio ou o limite de subtarefas foi atingido.
- Pré-visualização do texto exato a enviar (título e descrição atuais do formulário mais instruções fixas), com origem de destino, aviso de corte da descrição e recomposição quando título ou descrição mudam antes de confirmar.
- Consentimento próprio para conteúdo de tarefa, em memória e por origem, independente do teste de conexão; troca de origem exige novo consentimento e recusa não envia nada nem altera o formulário.
- Permissão de host solicitada a partir do gesto do usuário quando ausente; sem concessão, nenhum conteúdo é enviado.
- Domínio puro com `buildSubtaskSuggestionContent`, parser tolerante de linhas (remove marcadores e repetições) e `buildSubtaskSuggestionProposal` submetido a `validateSubtaskDrafts`, respeitando vagas restantes de `MAX_SUBTASKS`.
- Caso de uso com requisição única por acionamento, limite de tempo de 30 segundos, cancelamento por `AbortController` e bloqueio de acionamento concorrente; sem repetição automática.
- Executor de geração separado do `runAiProbe`, com leitura limitada do corpo, extração pelo caminho mínimo do formato do provedor, descarte de erros capturados e defesas de transporte (`redirect: error`, `no-store`, `omit`, `no-referrer`).
- Adapters de geração para OpenAI/CUSTOM (`OpenAiCompatibleSubtaskSuggester`) e Anthropic (`AnthropicSubtaskSuggester`), montados em `chrome-ai-service.ts` e fornecidos apenas no Side Panel; popup do Quick Add permanece sem qualquer elemento de IA.
- Proposta revisável em estado local: seleção item a item, edição do título antes de aceitar, aceite que apenas acrescenta itens não concluídos a `subtaskItems` e descarte sem tocar na lista; nada é persistido pela IA.
- Falhas em conjunto fechado (`EMPTY_RESPONSE`, `UNREADABLE_RESPONSE`, `NO_VALID_ITEM` além dos motivos de conexão), exibidas com no máximo origem e código de estado, sem expor credencial, URL completa, cabeçalhos ou corpo bruto.
- Cobertura por suítes de domínio, aplicação, infraestrutura, composição, componentes (`TaskFormAiSuggestion`, `QuickAdd` sem IA), integração e garantias de `background-no-ai`, `layer-boundaries` e Manifest.

## Melhorias

- Tarefa com título e descrição passa a gerar rascunhos de subtarefa revisáveis sem sair do formulário.
- Igualdade entre texto pré-visualizado e texto transmitido vira propriedade da construção, reduzindo risco de envio divergente.
- Reutilização do validador manual impede que a IA produza o que o usuário não poderia digitar.
- Ausência total do recurso sem provedor configurado mantém o funcionamento principal idêntico e sem rede adicional.

## Como validar

- Revisar o diff de produto com foco em `TaskForm.vue`, `ai-subtask-suggestion-service.ts`, `ai-subtask-suggestion.ts`, `ai-generation.ts` e adapters.
- Conferir os testes novos e ajustados: `ai-subtask-suggestion-service.test.ts`, `ai-subtask-suggestion.test.ts`, `TaskFormAiSuggestion.test.ts`, `ai-generation.test.ts`, `ai-subtask-suggestion.test.ts` de integração e `QuickAdd.test.ts` sem IA.
- Validar manualmente no Side Panel: sem configuração nenhum elemento aparece; com provedor, pré-visualização idêntica ao enviado, recusa preserva o digitado, troca de origem exige novo consentimento, permissão ausente/recusada não envia, cancelamento não altera o formulário, aceite parcial e descarte comportam-se como descrito, e salvar oferece desfazer.
- Evidências visuais não capturadas neste fluxo: mudanças visuais existem (`TaskForm.vue`), mas o servidor/extensão não estava disponível para captura; prosseguido sem screenshots por opção explícita.

## Impactos e riscos

- Nenhuma permissão nova no Manifest; acesso segue como permissão de host opcional por origem.
- Nenhuma dependência nova de runtime; requisições usam `fetch` direto nos adapters, fora do service worker.
- Nenhuma chave nova de armazenamento; backup e formato de tarefa inalterados.
- Risco residual: qualidade das sugestões varia por modelo; mitigado por confirmação item a item e recurso estritamente opcional.

author: zenmanage-brk
body:
## Summary

Audited the .NET SDK against the PHP reference SDK for feature parity and .NET best practices (ZEN-399), fixed what came up, and bumped both packages to the first stable `1.0.0` release.

**Correctness / parity fixes**
- `FlagManager.AllAsync()`/`SingleAsync()` now fall back to configured defaults when rule loading fails outright, instead of throwing past a caller-supplied default — previously a failed load also permanently poisoned the manager into an empty flag list with no retry.
- `AllAsync()` now merges `DefaultsCollection` keys missing from the loaded flags, matching PHP's `all()`.
- Rule engine: added the missing `regex` operator (previously silently always `false`), fixed multi-value clauses only ever comparing the first condition value, and fixed `not_in` using inverted aggregation logic vs. PHP.
- `ApiClient`: CDN URLs must now be HTTPS (fails closed, like PHP); usage reporting checks the HTTP status and retries with backoff instead of treating any response as success; rule fetch no longer retries on malformed/invalid data.

**Release-blocking fix**
- `dotnet pack` was actually broken for `Zenmanage.AspNetCore` (missing packaged README), and CI only ever packed the other package — so a tagged release would have silently published only half the SDK to NuGet. Fixed the csproj and updated `ci.yml`/`release.yml` to pack and publish both packages.

**Other best-practice fixes**
- Added `CacheException` for cache I/O failures.
- `ApiClient`/`Zenmanage` now implement `IDisposable` (disposing the `HttpClient` only when the SDK created it itself).
- `SdkInfo.Version` now derives from the assembly's informational version at runtime instead of a hand-maintained constant that could drift from the shipped version.
- Fixed the `IFagManager.cs` filename typo and the ASP.NET Core example (`examples/aspnet-core.cs` called APIs — `Context.Single(userId)`, `AddAttribute(string,string)` — that don't exist).
- Confirmed `Zenmanage`/`Zenmanage.AspNetCore` are both unclaimed on nuget.org.

**Repo hygiene**
- Added a `.gitignore` and untracked `bin`/`obj` build output (297 files), which had been committed with no `.gitignore` in place. Left on disk, just untracked — separate commit from the SDK fixes.

## Test plan
- [x] `dotnet test` (unit): 106/106 passing
- [x] Live parity/integration suite (`sdks/debuggers/sdk-integration-tests/zenmanage-dotnet`, hits the production API): 49/50 passing, 1 intentionally skipped pending unrelated backend work (ZEN-637/ZEN-649)
- [x] `dotnet pack` succeeds for both `Zenmanage` and `Zenmanage.AspNetCore` at `1.0.0`, README included in both

author: crypticswarm
body:
The split into `docs/` moved the README's prose near-verbatim, which carried its repetitions along with it. This is the pass that takes them out: where a fact was stated in two places, the page that owns the subject keeps it and the other copy goes.

Most of it is the reference pages doing their job. The `*_HOME_DIR` defaults, the `~/.gitconfig` mount, `install.sh`'s host variables, the `harness-runtime` build stage and the skill-eval knobs were each stated on a page and in a reference table both. `docs/ollama.md` was four lines of targets the make-target reference already tabulates, so it is gone and the one thing only it carried — why you would serve a model locally — is the reference's § Ollama intro now.

Three fixes ride along, because leaving a wrong statement standing while shortening the page around it is worse than either.

Assets order user, org, checkout, workspace, so a skill in the workspace beats the checkout's — the configuration page promised the opposite. The commands page offered `.opencode/command/` as the repo-local alternative, which is OpenCode's own project-local discovery and no layer of this pipeline; the workspace layer it reads is `<workspace>/.agents/commands`. And `AGENTS.md` described an alias `install.sh` does not write.

The Claude harness's module header restated four things its page already says. It is one line now, like the other three harnesses, and the two arguments a person editing the spec needs sit beside the code they explain — the allowlist that fails safe, and the rename that makes a symlink useless for a credential store. The page picks up the one piece of reasoning that was only in the header, and stops resting on "container-local", which says nothing on its own when every harness runs in a container.

`~/.gitconfig` was documented as `run_opencode` behavior. It is mounted by the run macro every harness target goes through.

author: antonio-ramon
body:
Estende o realtime dos comentários para os outros três casos. Front: Antonio-Ramon/front-pensacomigo#7.

## Realtime

- Quatro eventos novos: `CurtidasAtualizadas` e `PostVisualizado` no grupo `post:{id}`, `PostPublicado` e `PostRemovido` em `Clients.All` — quem está no feed não abriu post nenhum e por isso não está em grupo algum.
- Os dois contadores empurram o **valor**, não um aviso: o `GET` do post é o `AbrirPostCommand`, que **incrementa visualização**, então refetch a cada curtida corromperia o outro contador.
- Hub renomeado `ComentariosHub` → `TempoRealHub`, rota `/hubs/tempo-real`. Um hub só: cada hub é uma conexão WebSocket por aba.
- Despublicar pela edição emite `PostRemovido` — para quem olha o feed é o mesmo fato que deletar.

## Curtidas

- `AjustarCurtidasAsync` passou a usar SQL cru com `RETURNING qtd_curtidas`: `ExecuteUpdateAsync` devolve linhas afetadas, não valores, e o push precisa do número já somado. Mesma ida ao banco, sem a corrida entre `UPDATE` e `SELECT`. Interpolação em `FormattableString` vira parâmetro.
- O `null` (nenhuma linha casou) virou o sinal de "o contador não mudou, não há o que anunciar".

## ADR

Duas afirmações corrigidas no [ADR 0001](docs/adr/0001-realtime-signalr-mediatr.md): o número empurrado pelo WS **não** diverge do `GET` (os dois leem a mesma coluna — o drift real é `qtd_curtidas` × `COUNT(likes)`, e existe com ou sem realtime), e a curtida nunca esteve bloqueada para realtime por esse motivo.

## Verificação

Build verde, **68 testes unitários verdes** (+4). O teste que trava o `null` foi **verificado falhando** ao trocar o `if` por `qtd ?? 0`.

**Não verificado:** nada rodou ponta a ponta (o e2e exigiria a API local contra o Supabase de produção), e o `RETURNING` não passou por banco real — o teste unitário usa fake de repositório e os de integração não rodam sem Docker. É o ponto mais frágil da fatia.

## Fica de fora, de propósito

Agendado que vence não emite nada (entra no ar pela data, sem comando — precisaria de job); quem está lendo um post deletado não é avisado; visualização empurra 1 mensagem por leitor que abre (`ponytail:` no handler, upgrade = agregar num `PeriodicTimer`).

## `.teach`

Aula 0025 (sinal vs valor, `RETURNING`, `Clients.All`, conexão única no front) + registro 0023, em commit próprio.

author: samchon
body:
## Summary

Stacked on #2524. `appendMeshTopology` keyed its incidence maps by concatenated welded key strings — 1.9 million string allocations and hashes per face export. Each distinct welded position now gets a dense integer id, an edge is the packed pair, and incidence is the length of a run in a numerically sorted `Float64Array`. Only offending runs are looked up again, in traversal order, so every violation message and its order are unchanged. Meshes at 2^26 vertices are refused with the limit named rather than aliased.

## Measurement

Merged face mesh of `generated-korean-girl-01` (208,053 vertices, 314,352 triangles), min of 7 runs:

| | before (#2524) | after |
|---|---|---|
| `validateMeshTopology` | 5,255 ms | 485 ms |

One editor edit runs this check three times (build `validateModel`, export `validateModel`, export Float32 `validateMeshTopology` per material); the CPU profile put 5.2 s of a 15 s edit here.

## Proof

- Golden: 166 validations on two subjects (merged mesh open/closed, 40 parts each open/closed, `validateModel`), 41 MB of results — byte-identical digest before and after.
- `test_validation_mesh_topology` (+ scenario 10 for the capacity refusal), `test_validation_model_*`, `test_geometry_procedural_closure`, `test_subject_gltf_precision`: 27/27 green with plugins on.
- Red under: aliasing pair code (`from + to`), flipped canonical order, off-by-one guard (`>` for `>=`). The ordering pass caught a real early-stop bug mid-rewrite.
- `ttsc --noEmit` with plugins on engine and test: 0 errors.

author: gallegohp
body:
Escanear el QR no siempre es viable (requiere una imagen accesible, y en pruebas fallaba en silencio con codigos ya vencidos sin avisar). WhatsApp Web tambien soporta vincular con un codigo de 8 caracteres ingresado en el telefono, que ahora se expone en POST /codigo.

- El codigo se lee del atributo `data-link-code` del DOM, no de una captura de pantalla, para evitar errores de lectura (O/0, I/1, etc).
- WhatsApp resuelve el pais por defecto de forma asincrona al abrir la pantalla y por un instante muestra uno transitorio incorrecto, asi que se espera a que se asiente y se selecciona el pais explicitamente en vez de confiar en el default.
- Se quitan los endpoints /debug/click, /debug/type y /debug/text: con /codigo ya no hacen falta, y permitian controlar arbitrariamente el navegador (alto riesgo si este puerto llegara a exponerse). Se dejan /debug/screenshot y /debug/html por ser de solo lectura.
- El loop de fondo que revisa el QR ahora tambien usa el lock de la sesion de Selenium: sin esto competia por la misma conexion con cualquier otra operacion (se veian "Connection pool is full" y clics que no surtian efecto).

author: enricosaito
body:
## 1. Grand Champion wins the automatic pick

World Champion stays **fully selectable** — anyone who would rather show it can. It just no longer wins by default for a player who holds both.

Done with `sort` (15 vs 20), in `BUILTIN_FLAIRS` and the live row. This is where `sort` stops being pure rarity and becomes **display precedence**: there are more $50,000 earners (15) than world champions (7), so rarity alone would order them the other way round. The field's doc now says that outright, so the next person doesn't "fix" it back.

Verified against the real catalogue:

| case | result |
|---|---|
| holds both, no selection | **grand-champion** |
| holds both, selects world-champion | world-champion |
| world champion under $50k | world-champion |

## 2. Tooltips off the chips that repeated themselves

`1v1 PR #3`, `$63,250`, `Ranked #4` and `US-E #2` each had a hover that restated the chip as a longer sentence. Gone.

**The legend titles keep theirs**, and that's the distinction: "The Traveler" genuinely doesn't say which legend it came from, and the tooltip is the only place that appears. Screenshot confirms the ice-blue ladder chips lost theirs while the periwinkle legend titles kept them.

`RegionRankTag` lives on the profile only, so dropping its tooltip affects nothing else.

## 3. Tracking stops glowing once it's tracked

A tracked player sat in a permanently gold-bordered, gold-tinted box. On a profile full of cards that reads as an alert about something that had already gone right.

Gold on a border means *"you could press this"*, so it belongs to hover. Tracked now rests exactly as neutral as untracked, and the **filled gold star is the whole of the state**. Hovering a tracked control still turns red rather than gold, because there the affordance is "click to remove" and that has to look like what it is.

## 4. The card is one component again

Inside the card, the star and its word lose their outline. A bordered pill inside a bordered card is a box in a box, and the card is already the button — that chip is content, not a second control.

The standalone chip keeps its edge, because alone in a table row it needs one to read as a control at all. Both still render through the same `shell`, so the two skins can't drift.

## Verified

- Flair precedence exercised against the live catalogue, all four cases above.
- Header screenshotted: chips intact, tooltips gone from the right ones.
- `tsc`, `eslint`, `next build` clean; two dead symbols the refactor orphaned (`chipCls`, an unused `InfoTip` import) removed.

**Not visually verified:** the tracked and hover states of the tracking control, which need a signed-in session I can't drive headlessly. The change is confined to class strings on existing branches and typechecks, but the first click on a real profile is worth a look.

author: mominbinshahid
body:
Four of eighteen. `T15` names the order and the reason for it: **the manifest first, on its own, because its failure is the one that reaches a phone.**

## The manifest

It held `/MealUnits/` three times — `id`, `start_url`, `scope` — in `public/`, which the build copies verbatim. Nothing rewrote them and nothing compared them to anything.

**A wrong `scope` orphans an app somebody has already installed.** The home-screen icon stops matching the site it came from, the install quietly stops being the install, and nobody is told. It survives a green build, a passing suite and a successful deploy.

It is emitted from `BASE` now, by the `sitemap` plugin rather than one of its own — and that placement is load-bearing rather than tidy. `serviceWorker` walks `outDir` for its precache, so the manifest has to exist before that runs; `sitemap` is ahead of it in the plugin array and both write at `closeBundle`. Verified in the built `sw.js`: **the manifest is in the precache, `robots.txt` is not**, which is what each should be.

Icon paths stay **relative**. A manifest resolves them against its own URL, so they are already right under any base — writing the base in would be three more copies to keep in step, which is the defect rather than the fix.

## robots.txt

Same treatment for its one `Sitemap:` address. Quieter failure — a stale URL is a 404 a crawler reports to nobody — but the same unguarded copy.

And generating it is rather the point of keeping it at all: it is **inert where it currently ships** (T16), kept only for the day this moves to its own domain. A file kept for a move is precisely a file whose addresses must survive one.

## One knock-on, and the checker found it rather than a person

Moving `robots.txt` out of `public/` dropped it from `PUBLIC_CRAWLER_ONLY` — the same set that validates `src/sw.ts`'s `NOT_THE_APP` — so the worker was suddenly excluding a file nothing vouched for. Its job had not changed; only where it is written had. There is a `GENERATED_CRAWLER_ONLY` set now, holding it and the sitemap.

## check-plan.py

`check_generated_manifest`: the hand-written files must not come back to `public/`, the three base-carrying fields must read `BASE`, the icon paths must stay relative, and `robots.txt`'s `Sitemap:` line must build from `SITE_URL` and `BASE`. Three seeded mutations, all caught.

## Still to go

Fourteen: `index.html`'s eight (cheap — already transformed at build time) and `src/ui/fonts.css`'s three, which are the real work because the idiomatic fix turns them into hashed filenames the worker's precache manifest then has to pick up.

## Verification

790 tests · check-plan clean · self-test 146/146 · `smoke: clean` · manifest and robots.txt fetched from the served build.

author: danielggordon
thomas-waters
body:
**1.16.0** — four commits.

**A save that fails is no longer lost.** It used to show a toast, live in memory, and disappear on the next reload. Failed ops now wait in an outbox on the device, are re-applied over whatever the database returns so they stay on screen, and drain on the next open, when the connection returns, when the tab is shown again, or after any other save succeeds.

**The shape of his days** — Insights → Overview. A row a day drawn against the clock, following the period toggle. Rows run night-end to night-end, the same stretch `sleepDayKey` counts as a day, and sleep is drawn at the time it happened so a night carries over to the row below. Tap a row to open that day.

**What was going on** — Insights → Calendar. Teething, unwell, away, nursery, vaccinations: a first and last day plus a note. Marked days get a dot on the calendar, a chip in the day, and an "All day" row in the consultant log. Stored in one `app_state` row, so no migration.

**The HSE comes first in the sleep model.** Night sleep and naps now use the HSE's per-age figures — 10 to 12 hours a night and two naps of 1 to 2 hours at nine months — with the AASM consensus supplying 24-hour totals it does not state. This widens most bands, because the model had been built from the middle of parenting charts and those are tighter than published guidance: days that read as short will now read as ordinary. An info button beside "Usual for his age" and the month grid lists every source with a link, and says plainly that wake windows are chart convention rather than guidance.

No database change.

author: sauso
body:
## What

The nightly "memories" timelapse sampler (`captureChildFrame`) selected a child's camera with no
`disabled` filter at all — a disabled camera (streaming/detection legs off, source possibly stale or
gone) could still be selected, and could be picked ahead of a working enabled sibling purely by sort
order. Full mechanism and severity are in a separate private security advisory; this PR states effect
only.

## Fix

- Camera selection now filters `disabled = 0`, matching an existing precedent for the identical
  "primary camera for a child" query already used in `sleepAnalysis.js`/`sleepReviews.js`.
- Eligibility is re-checked again right before the captured frame is written to disk — the snapshot
  fetch in between is async (an HTTP request, or an ffmpeg grab with its own 8s timeout), during
  which the camera could be disabled, reassigned to a different child, or deleted outright.

## Testing

- 10 new tests in `backend/test/timelapse-capture.test.js`, covering: disabled-only child (no
  request at all), a disabled camera excluded even when sorted first **and** sort_order still
  respected among the remaining enabled cameras (fixture deliberately inserted out of sort_order
  order, so it can't pass by insertion-order coincidence), mid-capture disable/reassign/delete of
  the camera, mid-capture deletion of the **child** (confirmed against the actual `ON DELETE SET
  NULL` FK behavior, not just inferred), and the same re-check on the RTSP fallback path (not only
  the HTTP snapshot_url path).
- Every "★ THE FIX" test was confirmed to fail on the pre-fix code by temporarily reverting each
  piece of the fix locally — not just written and left unverified.
- Full backend suite: 1246/1246 passing, `npm run test:core` coverage gate clean, no regression.
- **Deliberately not adding `lib/timelapse.js` to the core-logic coverage-include list**: the file
  sits at ~11% line coverage today (assembly, pruning, retention — all untested, pre-existing and
  unrelated to this fix). Adding it would either fail the gate outright or require writing tests for
  all of that unrelated surface area, well beyond this fix's scope. `captureChildFrame` itself is now
  thoroughly covered by the new file.

## Review

Adversarially reviewed by Codex (`gpt-6-astra`) and an independent Claude subagent in parallel, each
running the real suite. Both held the fix itself sound; two real process/precision findings were
fixed before this PR: one test's name claimed to verify sort-order precedence between two disabled
and enabled cameras but couldn't actually discriminate that (only one candidate row survived the
`WHERE` filter, so `ORDER BY` had nothing to compare) — rewritten with a fixture that genuinely
tests it; and the child-deletion case was previously only inferred from the FK schema, not directly
exercised — now has its own test.

author: jonnyeclectic
body:
## What and why

A catalog cache outlives the clone it was built from. `catalog.load_tap` serves a stale cache when the clone is gone, **deliberately**, and `rag.read_body` then degrades that entry to its name and description, also deliberately. Each is right on its own. Stacked under a gate that read neither, they let `make eval` index the same entry count, across the same tap count, under the same `BM25 full-content` label, and floor four metrics on a corpus that is frontmatter only.

Measured on the pinned 20-tap corpus, with `$BOOST_HOME/repos` moved aside and the cache and sentinel intact (the `main` behaviour):

| state | entries | mean doc len | body-less docs | recall@k / hit@1 / MRR / nDCG@k | exit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| intact clones | 10,731 / 20 taps | 862.2 tok | 0 | 0.841 / 0.484 / 0.607 / 0.655 | 0 (4× PASS) |
| `repos/` moved aside | 10,731 / 20 taps | 41.4 tok | **10,731** | **0.852 / 0.582 / 0.684 / 0.717** | **0 (4× PASS)** |

95.2% of the scored text is absent, and the run scores **higher**, so the loss reads as an improvement. This has a simple cause. BM25 normalises by `avg_len`, which falls with the documents, so a corpus that shrinks uniformly nearly keeps its rank *set*: recall@10 moves by one query while hit@1 moves by nine. What the loss really costs is the ordering, and ordering is what the three newer floors cover.

The same corpus copy, re-run on this branch:

| state | what happens | exit |
|---|---|---|
| `repos/` emptied, sentinel/config/caches intact (the card), plain `make eval` sequence | `holds no clone — re-tapping`, all 20 re-cloned and pinned in 58 s, then 0.841 / 0.484 / 0.607 / 0.655 | 0, then 0 |
| one clone (`minio/skills`) removed | refused: `4 of 10731 indexed documents carry no body … 457 of the index's 9250218 tokens` | **66** |
| … then the printed `Fix:` command, run verbatim | re-clones `minio/skills`, rewrites the sentinel; gate back to the intact numbers | 0, then 0 |
| one `SKILL.md` deleted inside a clone | refused: `1 of 10731 … 111 of the index's 9252439 tokens` | **66** |
| … then the printed `Fix:` command, run verbatim | file restored at the pin, `minio/skills 4 entries`; gate back to the intact numbers | 0, then 0 |
| one clone removed, run with no floor and no `--save-baseline` | `warning: CORPUS INCOMPLETE — scoring anyway`, then scored | 0 |

**Three layers, each for a different state:**

- `corpus_refusal()` runs before anything is scored. It is gated on the **document count**, not `body_share`: `body_share` is a share of the tokens this index *does* hold, and it reads 0.0 for an empty index as well as a body-less one. The run **refuses with exit 66** (`EX_NOINPUT`) when it binds anything, meaning a floor (`--fail-under` / `--floor`) or a baseline pin (`--save-baseline`). Any other run (`make eval-ai`, `--stats`, a natural-language `--golden` run) gets the same diagnosis as a warning and is scored. The refusal names the count of body-less documents, gives their stand-in tokens as a count, and prints a `Fix:` line that interpolates the resolved `BOOST_HOME`, `PYTHON` and the absolute script path. There is **no flag of its own**: a flag would give `make eval` and `ci.yml` a way to disagree about what the required gate checks, and `tests/unit/test_eval_corpus.py` already exists to catch that disagreement on the floors. Because `--save-baseline` counts as binding, `eval-corpus-refresh.yml`'s bare re-baseline step cannot pin a baseline over a body-less corpus either.
- `ensure_eval_corpus.sh` honours its sentinel only when `repos/` holds at least one clone **directory**, so a stray `.DS_Store` does not count as a corpus. It also deletes the sentinel **before** every `--ensure`, so only a clean run can vouch for the corpus again.
- `eval_corpus.py --ensure` repairs what the refusal catches. It re-clones a configured tap whose clone directory is gone, through `registry.update`, which is core's existing answer to a missing clone. It also checks every row out with `--force`, so a deleted tracked file inside the sparse cone is restored rather than counted short.

Also `flush=True` on the "indexed N entries" line. Piped stdout is block-buffered while stderr is not, so in a `make eval | tail` log the build line landed *after* the refusal.

Fixes docs/roadmap/items/eval-gate-scores-a-body-less-corpus.md

## Floors and baseline: unmoved, by construction

**No `boost_cli/core` line changed.** `rag` already counted what it could not read (`read_body_full`, the `build` stats, `index_completeness()`), and the missing-clone path already existed in `registry.update`; nothing in `scripts/` had ever asked either one. So the intact-corpus numbers are identical before and after (0.841 / 0.484 / 0.607 / 0.655, re-measured on this branch). `tests/eval/baseline.json` and all four floors are untouched, and the mutation gate sees an unchanged tree.

Two incidental findings. First, `metadata_only == 0` on the intact corpus, so the sparse cone and `catalog.scan_dir` do **not** interact badly here: BM25 indexes 100% of the bodies. Second, the card's "10,152 entries" predates a pin refresh. These numbers match `docs/roadmap.html`'s own `0.840659 / 0.483516 / 0.606517 / 0.655233` to the digit.

## Tests

`tests/unit/test_eval_corpus_bodies.py` has 20 tests, and `tests/unit/test_eval_corpus.py` gains 6. Measured by running both files against clean `git archive` copies of each tree:

- **Against the reviewed PR tip (`aac6849`): 17 fail.** They cover exit 66, the interpolated remedy, the refusal landing before any score, `--save-baseline` refusing, a floorless run warning and still scoring, the partial case under a floor, the token count and the conditional HIGHER, the refresh workflow's refusal handling, `.DS_Store`, the sentinel lifecycle, re-pinning restoring a deleted file, `--ensure` re-cloning (one clone, and all of them), `--ensure` restoring a deleted `SKILL.md`, and the card scenario through the real wrapper.
- **Against pre-PR `main` (`c0c7690`): 23 fail.** Seven of those call `corpus_refusal` directly, which does not exist there.
- The 9 that pass on `aac6849` do so on purpose. Three are controls that also pass on `main`: a complete corpus is still scored, an intact corpus is still skipped, and a clone that cannot be re-made still exits **75**. The other six pin behaviour the reviewed tip already got right: "no index", "empty index" and "complete index" are not refusals, a high token share still refuses, one missing document in 10,731 refuses, and a sentinel over an emptied `repos/` calls `--ensure`.

The card-scenario test runs the **real** `ensure_eval_corpus.sh` and the real `--ensure`, with no stub interpreter, against two local fixture taps whose clones were deleted while `config.json` survived.

One existing-file edit is carried over from the reviewed commits: the sentinel wrapper's stub interpreter creates `$BOOST_HOME/repos/owner__repo`, as a real `--ensure` does. No assertion was weakened.

## What is not established

How far the four metrics move on a *partially* materialised corpus. The refusal counts unreadable documents rather than estimating metric drift, so the partial case is covered by construction, not calibration. The message now says exactly that ("How far a partial loss moves them has not been measured") and claims HIGHER only for the fully body-less case, where it was measured.

## Follow-up after review

An adversarial review returned FAIL. It found three defects and five nits. All are addressed here, and none is declined.

- **Defect: the card's own scenario did not re-tap.** With `repos/` reclaimed but `config.json` intact, `--ensure` found every tap configured, skipped `registry.add`, and ran `git -C` in a missing directory. All 20 rows then read "the pin in tests/eval/taps.txt is stale" and exited 75 as CORPUS UNAVAILABLE.
